有罪判決が出た日、被害者の家族に深く頭を下げられた。: On the day of the guilty verdict, the victim's family bowed deeply to me.
検事正の決裁で、書類に赤ペンを17箇所入れられた。: At the chief prosecutor's approval review, 17 red-pen corrections were made on my document.
在外公館に赴任し、3年でアフリカと中東と南米を転々とした。: Posted to overseas missions, I moved through Africa, the Middle East, and South America in three years.
レセプションで1晩に名刺を80枚交換した。: At a reception, I exchanged 80 business cards in one evening.
大臣の外遊の随行で、48時間寝なかった。: Accompanying the minister on an overseas trip, I went 48 hours without sleep.
現地の治安悪化で、日本人の退避支援のため空港に3日間詰めた。: As local security worsened, I stayed at the airport for three days helping Japanese nationals evacuate.
英語とフランス語に加え、アラビア語の研修を2年受けた。: Besides English and French, I took two years of Arabic training.
子どもが日本語より現地の言葉を先に覚えた。: My child learned the local language before Japanese.
条約交渉で、1つの単語をめぐって5時間協議した。: In treaty negotiations, we spent five hours discussing a single word.
現地で逮捕された日本人旅行者の面会に、拘置所に行った。: I went to a detention center to visit a Japanese tourist who had been arrested abroad.
天皇誕生日のレセプションで、寿司を握ってもらうため日本から料理人を呼んだ。: For the Emperor's Birthday reception, I had a chef flown in from Japan to make sushi on the spot.
帰国したら、日本のコンビニの品揃えに感動して20分店内にいた。: After returning to Japan, I was so moved by the selection at a convenience store that I stayed inside for 20 minutes.
羽田のレーダー室で、1時間に40機をさばいた。: In the radar room at Haneda, I handled 40 aircraft in an hour.
夜勤明けで目がチカチカし、帰りの電車で寝過ごした。: After a night shift my eyes were flickering, and I slept past my stop on the train home.
英語の交信で、パイロットのなまりが強すぎて3回聞き返した。: In radio communication, the pilot's accent was so strong that I asked him to repeat three times.
台風で着陸待ちの機体が上空に10機たまった。: Because of a typhoon, 10 aircraft ended up circling overhead waiting to land.
資格取得まで、訓練で2年かかった。: It took two years of training to get certified.
「管制官って、手旗振る人？」と親戚に言われた。: A relative said, “Air traffic controller? The person who waves the little flags?”
緊急事態宣言をした機体が無事着陸し、交信の最後に「サンキュー」と言われた。: An aircraft that declared an emergency landed safely, and at the end of the radio call, the pilot said, “Thank you.”
年に1回の英語試験と身体検査で、毎回緊張した。: The annual English exam and medical checkup made me nervous every single time.
新人のころ、先輩に交信を止められて真っ白になった。: As a rookie, my senior cut off my radio transmission and my mind went blank.
正月も交代制で、空港で年を越した。: Even on New Year's, we worked shifts, and I welcomed the new year at the airport.
学芸員の公募に100人応募があり、採用は1人だった。: A curator opening drew 100 applicants, and only one was hired.
展覧会の準備で、借用作品の梱包に1日中立ち会った。: While preparing for an exhibition, I stood by for a whole day as loaned artworks were packed.
収蔵庫の温湿度管理で、湿度計を1時間おきに確認した。: For humidity and temperature control in the storage room, I checked the hygrometer every hour.
企画展の来場者が目標の3万人を超え、館長が珍しく笑った。: Visitors to the special exhibition exceeded the target of 30,000, and the director rarely smiled.
子ども向けのワークショップで、恐竜の骨の模型を作った。: At a workshop for children, I made a model of dinosaur bones.
「学芸員は雑芸員」と先輩に言われ、本当に雑用ばかりだった。: A senior said, “Curators are really ‘miscellaneous-duty staff,’” and it was truly nothing but odd jobs.
年収は非常勤時代200万円台で、常勤になって350万円になった。: My annual income was in the 2-million-yen range as a part-timer, and rose to 3.5 million yen after I became full-time.
論文を書きたいのに、展示の準備で3年書けていない。: I want to write papers, but I haven't been able to for three years because of exhibition preparation.
作品の解説パネルを50字に縮めるのに半日かかった。: Cutting an artwork's description panel down to 50 characters took half a day.
見学に来たおじいさんが、展示を見て昔の話を30分してくれた。: An elderly man who came to visit looked at the exhibit and told me stories from the old days for 30 minutes.
会議で企画を30本出し、通ったのは1本だった。: I pitched 30 ideas in a meeting, and one got approved.
深夜番組の台本を、収録の2時間前に書き直した。: I rewrote a late-night show script two hours before taping.
ナレーション原稿で「果たして…」を1日に5回書いた。: In narration scripts, I wrote “Could it be...” five times in one day.
レギュラー番組が4本あったのに、改編期に3本終わった。: I had four regular shows, and three ended during the program reshuffle.
芸人さんに台本を無視されたが、そのアドリブの方が面白かった。: A comedian ignored my script, but his ad-lib was funnier.
ギャラは1本3万円で、拘束は12時間だった。: The pay was 30,000 yen per episode, with 12 hours on call.
自分の考えたコーナーが、SNSのトレンドに入った。: A segment I came up with made it onto social media trends.
エンドロールの名前が一瞬すぎて、親に「見えなかった」と言われた。: My name in the end credits flashed by so quickly that my parents said, “We couldn't see it.”
ネタ帳がスマホのメモで2000件になった。: My gag notebook grew to 2,000 entries in my phone's notes app.
YouTubeチャンネルの構成作家の仕事が増え、テレビより稼ぐようになった。: Work as a writer for YouTube channels grew, and I started earning more than from TV.
機材に総額400万円かかり、ローンが残っていた。: The equipment cost a total of 4 million yen, and the loan was still outstanding.
結婚式の撮影で、新郎の父親の涙をアップで撮った。: Shooting a wedding, I took a close-up of the groom's father in tears.
七五三シーズンは1日に15家族を撮った。: During the Shichi-Go-San season, I photographed 15 families in one day.
雨の屋外撮影で、レンズに水滴がつき続けた。: During an outdoor shoot in the rain, water droplets kept landing on the lens.
子どもの写真撮影で、笑わせるために変顔を1時間続けた。: For a children's photo shoot, I made silly faces for an hour to get them to laugh.
クライアントに「スマホで撮った方が良くない？」と言われた。: A client said, “Wouldn't it be better to just shoot it on a smartphone?”
撮影データのSDカードを紛失しかけて、全身から汗が出た。: I nearly lost the SD card with the shoot data and broke out in a sweat all over.
自分の写真が、駅の広告ポスターになった。: One of my photos became an advertising poster at a train station.
報道の現場で、被災地の写真を撮りながら手が震えた。: On a news assignment, my hands shook as I photographed the disaster area.
10年前に撮った家族から、「おじいちゃんの遺影に使わせてもらった」と連絡が来た。: A family I photographed 10 years ago got in touch: “We used it for Grandpa's memorial portrait.”
子ども食堂の運営で、1日に60食を作った。: Running a children's cafeteria, I cooked 60 meals in a day.
助成金の申請書を1か月に5本書いた。: Wrote five grant applications in one month.
給料は月18万円で、「やりがい搾取だよ」と友達に言われた。: Pay was 180,000 yen a month, and a friend said, “That's exploitation disguised as fulfillment.”
クラウドファンディングで、目標300万円に対して320万円集まった。: In a crowdfunding campaign, we raised 3.2 million yen against a goal of 3 million.
ボランティアのシフト調整で、LINEグループが10個になった。: Arranging volunteer shifts, I ended up with 10 LINE groups.
支援していた若者から、就職が決まったと電話が来た。: A young person I had been supporting called to say they'd gotten a job.
寄付者向けの年次報告書を作り、写真の許可を一人ずつ取った。: Making the annual report for donors, I got photo permission from each person one by one.
行政との協働事業で、書類の様式が毎年変わった。: In a joint project with the local government, the document format changed every year.
活動がテレビで紹介され、翌週に寄付が200件届いた。: Our activities were introduced on TV, and 200 donations arrived the following week.
代表が燃え尽きて、半年休んだ。: The director burned out and took half a year off.
選挙で、駅前に朝6時から立って毎日あいさつをした。: During the election campaign, I stood in front of the station from 6 a.m. every day to greet people.
当選ラインまであと87票の差で当選した。: Won the election by a margin of just 87 votes above the cutoff.
議会の一般質問の原稿を、3日かけて書いた。: Took three days to write my script for the general questioning session in the assembly.
地域の夏祭り、運動会、葬式に週末が全部消えた。: Local summer festivals, sports days, and funerals ate up all my weekends.
報酬は月50万円だが、選挙費用の借金を返すと手元に少ししか残らなかった。: The pay was 500,000 yen a month, but after repaying election campaign debts, very little was left.
住民から「側溝の蓋が割れている」と電話が来て、役所に伝えた。: A resident called saying, “The drain cover is cracked,” and I passed it on to the city office.
自分の提案で、小学校にエアコンが入った。: Because of my proposal, air conditioning was installed in elementary schools.
政務活動費の領収書を1枚ずつ公開した。: I made every receipt for political activity expenses public, one by one.
議会で居眠りしている議員をSNSで批判され、自分も写り込んでいた。: I was criticized on social media for a councilor dozing off in the assembly, and I was in the photo too.
落選した夜、選挙事務所で支援者に頭を下げた。: On the night I lost the election, I bowed my head to supporters at the campaign office.
お盆の棚経で、1日に40軒の檀家さんを回った。: During the Obon sutra-reading rounds, I visited 40 parishioner households in a day.
修行時代、朝3時半に起きて座禅を組んだ。: During my training years, I woke at 3:30 a.m. to practice seated meditation.
お布施の額を聞かれて「お気持ちで」と答え、困った顔をされた。: When asked how much the donation should be, I answered, “Whatever you feel is right,” and they looked troubled.
檀家の減少で、寺の収入が10年で半分になった。: With fewer parishioner families, the temple's income halved in 10 years.
葬儀でお経を読みながら、故人と将棋を指した日を思い出した。: While chanting sutras at a funeral, I remembered the day I played shogi with the deceased.
副業で、平日は中学校の先生をしていた。: On the side, I worked as a middle school teacher on weekdays.
お寺のYouTubeを始めたら、登録者が1万人になった。: I started a YouTube channel for the temple, and it reached 10,000 subscribers.
除夜の鐘をついていたら、近所から「うるさい」と苦情が来た。: While ringing the New Year's Eve bell, I got complaints from the neighbors that it was too loud.
小さな子どもに「お坊さんって髪ないの？」と聞かれ、触らせてあげた。: A small child asked, “Don't monks have hair?” and I let them touch my head.
お寺の屋根の修繕費に2000万円かかると言われた。: I was told repairing the temple roof would cost 20 million yen.
正月三が日で、お守りが3000体売れた。: During the first three days of the New Year, 3,000 amulets sold.
地鎮祭で、施主の工務店の社長に毎回同じ冗談を言われた。: At the groundbreaking ceremony, the owner, a construction company president, told me the same joke every time.
七五三の祈祷で、泣き叫ぶ3歳児を前に祝詞を読んだ。: During a Shichi-Go-San blessing, I read the ritual prayer in front of a screaming three-year-old.
兼務している神社が12社あり、移動だけで1日終わった。: I served 12 shrines concurrently, and travel alone took up the whole day.
神社の収入だけでは食べられず、平日は市役所で働いた。: The shrine's income alone couldn't support me, so I worked at city hall on weekdays.
台風で御神木が倒れ、氏子さんたちと片付けた。: A typhoon knocked down the sacred tree, and I cleaned up with the parishioners.
夏祭りの準備で、テントを50張り立てた。: Preparing for the summer festival, we put up 50 tents.
結婚式の神前式で、新郎が緊張して誓詞を噛んだ。: At a Shinto wedding, the groom was so nervous that he stumbled over the vows.
お賽銭泥棒を防犯カメラで見つけた。: I caught an offertory box thief on the security camera.
子どものころから遊んでいた境内を、自分が守る番になった。: The shrine grounds where I played as a child—now it was my turn to protect them.
新人賞に応募すること7回目で、最終選考に残った。: On my seventh submission to the new writers' award, I made the final selection.
デビュー作の初版は5000部で、印税は約75万円だった。: My debut novel's first print run was 5,000 copies, and royalties came to about 750,000 yen.
締め切りの前日、編集者からのLINEに既読をつけられなかった。: The day before the deadline, I couldn't bring myself to read my editor's LINE message.
書店で自分の本が平積みされているのを見つけ、こっそり1冊表向きに直した。: I found my book stacked flat in a bookstore and secretly turned one copy face-out.
Amazonのレビューで星1をつけられ、3日引きずった。: I got a one-star Amazon review and dwelled on it for three days.
取材のために、1か月間漁船に乗せてもらった。: For research, I was allowed to board a fishing boat for a month.
2作目が売れず、重版がかからなかった。: My second book didn't sell, and it never got a reprint.
深夜のファミレスで、ドリンクバーだけで6時間書いた。: At a family restaurant late at night, I wrote for six hours on just the drink bar.
自分の小説がドラマ化され、エンドロールに名前が出た。: My novel was adapted into a TV drama, and my name appeared in the end credits.
読者から「この本に救われました」と手紙が届いた。: A reader sent me a letter: “This book saved me.”
CMの15秒の曲を、40パターン作った。: I made 40 variations of a 15-second commercial jingle.
ゲーム音楽の仕事で、ループ部分のつなぎ目を何度も聞き直した。: On a game music job, I listened over and over to the seam of the loop.
JASRACからの分配金明細を見て、カラオケで歌われた回数を知った。: Seeing my royalty distribution statement from JASRAC, I learned how many times my song had been sung at karaoke.
コンペで提出した曲が、100曲中で採用された。: My song submitted to a competition was picked out of 100.
アイドルの曲が採用され、ライブで数万人が歌っているのを客席から見た。: An idol group used my song, and I watched from the audience as tens of thousands sang it at a concert.
DTMのソフトとプラグインに、合計300万円使った。: I spent a total of 3 million yen on DTM software and plugins.
夜中に浮かんだメロディーを、スマホに鼻歌で録音した。: I recorded a melody that came to me in the middle of the night by humming into my phone.
「これ、なんか違うんだよね」というクライアントの一言で、1週間の作業が消えた。: One comment from a client, “Something about this just feels off,” wiped out a week of work.
自分の曲が、何年か後に地元の小学校の運動会で流れていた。: Years later, my song was playing at my hometown elementary school's sports day.
初配信の同時接続が12人で、そのうち2人は友達だった。: At my first stream, there were 12 concurrent viewers, and two of them were friends.
Live2Dのモデル制作に、合計80万円かかった。: Making the Live2D model cost a total of 800,000 yen.
10時間耐久配信で、喉が完全につぶれた。: During a 10-hour endurance stream, my voice gave out completely.
登録者1万人の記念配信で、泣いてしまった。: At the 10,000-subscriber celebration stream, I cried.
スパチャで1晩に50万円入ったが、事務所と分けて手元には3割だった。: I received 500,000 yen in Super Chats in one night, but after splitting with the agency I kept only 30%.
コラボ相手の配信で、本名を言われかけた。: During a collab partner's stream, they almost said my real name.
機材トラブルで、モデルが固まったまま30分しゃべり続けた。: Because of equipment trouble, I kept talking for 30 minutes while my model was frozen.
中の人の年齢を詮索するコメントを、NGワードに登録した。: I registered comments prying into the person behind the avatar's age as blocked words.
アンチのコメントを見すぎて、1週間配信を休んだ。: I read too many hater comments and took a week off from streaming.
リアルイベントで、ファンの顔を初めて見た。: At an in-person event, I saw my fans' faces for the first time.
やまと学校の訓練で、1年間スマホを使えなかった。: During training at the Yamato school, I couldn't use my smartphone for a year.
体重を52キロにキープするため、毎日サウナに入った。: To keep my weight at 52 kg, I went to the sauna every day.
デビュー戦で、6艇中6着だった。: In my debut race, I came in 6th out of 6 boats.
初勝利の日、水神祭で仲間に水面に投げ込まれた。: On the day of my first win, my fellow racers threw me into the water in the Suijin-sai ritual.
フライングをして、30日間の出場停止になった。: I jumped the start and was suspended from racing for 30 days.
全国のレース場を転々とし、1年の半分以上は宿舎生活だった。: Moving from track to track across the country, I spent more than half the year living in lodging quarters.
A1級に昇格し、年収が2000万円を超えた。: Promoted to the A1 class, my annual income exceeded 20 million yen.
転覆して、モーターに水が入った。: I capsized, and water got into the motor.
賞金でローンなしで家を建てた。: I built a house with prize money, without taking out a loan.
レース後、ファンから「お前の舟券で負けた」と怒鳴られた。: After a race, a fan yelled at me, “I lost my bet on you!”
競輪学校の入試で、自転車の適性試験に2回落ちた。: I failed the bicycle aptitude test twice in the entrance exam for the keirin school.
太ももの太さが62センチになり、スーツのズボンが入らなくなった。: My thighs reached 62 centimeters, and I could no longer fit into suit trousers.
ラインを組んだ先輩の番手で、最後に差し切って勝った。: Riding behind a senior in our line, I came from behind at the end and won.
落車して鎖骨を折り、3か月レースに出られなかった。: I crashed, broke my collarbone, and couldn't race for three months.
年間の賞金が1500万円を超えた。: My annual prize money exceeded 15 million yen.
雨のレースで、バンクがツルツルだった。: In a race in the rain, the banked track was slick.
競輪場のファンのヤジが、毎回同じおじさんだった。: The jeers from the keirin fans were always from the same old guy.
練習で毎日100キロ走った。: I rode 100 kilometers every day in training.
ガールズケイリンの選手と同じ練習場で、自分より速かった。: At the same practice track as the Girls Keirin racers, they were faster than me.
S級に昇格した日、地元の練習仲間と焼肉に行った。: On the day I was promoted to S class, I went out for yakiniku with my practice buddies from back home.
競馬学校に、身長と体重の基準ぎりぎりで入った。: I got into the jockey school barely meeting the height and weight requirements.
毎朝4時から調教に乗った。: Every morning from 4 a.m., I rode in training workouts.
斤量に合わせるため、レース前日は水も控えた。: To meet the weight allowance, I even held back on water the day before races.
デビュー年に年間30勝を挙げ、新人賞をもらった。: In my debut year, I won 30 races and received a rookie award.
落馬して、ヘリで病院に運ばれた。: I fell from my horse and was taken to the hospital by helicopter.
G1の騎乗依頼が来たのは、デビュー8年目だった。: The offer to ride in a G1 came in my eighth year since debut.
勝った馬の馬主さんに、口取り写真に呼ばれた。: The owner of the winning horse invited me to the winner's circle photo.
騎乗停止で、2週間レースに乗れなかった。: Got a riding suspension and couldn't race for two weeks.
引退した馬に会いに、北海道の牧場まで行った。: Went all the way to a ranch in Hokkaido to see a retired horse.
賞金の5%が騎手の取り分だと説明すると、みんな驚いた。: Everyone was surprised when I explained the jockey gets 5% of the prize money.
入門して、ちゃんこの1日2食で体重が40キロ増えた。: Joined the stable and gained 40 kilos on two chanko meals a day.
序ノ口の給料はなく、場所手当が年に数十万円だった。: No salary at the lowest rank, just a tournament allowance of a few hundred thousand yen a year.
兄弟子の付け人として、浴衣の洗濯から靴並べまでした。: Served a senior wrestler as his attendant, from washing his yukata to lining up his shoes.
初めて大銀杏を結った日、鏡を何度も見た。: The day I first had my ooichou topknot tied, I kept checking the mirror.
十両に昇進し、月給が110万円になった。: Promoted to Juryo; monthly salary became 1.1 million yen.
巡業で、子どもを抱っこして泣かせる「泣き相撲」をした。: On a regional tour, did “crying sumo,” holding babies until they cried.
膝の怪我で休場し、番付が10枚下がった。: Sat out a tournament with a knee injury and dropped ten ranks.
ファンからの差し入れの米が、部屋に30俵あった。: Fans sent so much rice that the stable had 30 bales of it.
新幹線の座席が狭く、2席分の切符を買った。: The Shinkansen seats were too narrow, so I bought two tickets.
引退相撲で、断髪式に親が来て泣いていた。: At my retirement ceremony, my parents came to the hair-cutting and cried.
奨励会で26歳の年齢制限まで残り2年だった。: Two years left before the age-26 limit in the shogi apprentice league.
四段に昇段してプロになった日、師匠に電話した。: The day I reached 4-dan and turned pro, I called my master.
対局で12時間考え、夕食の注文に迷った。: Thought for 12 hours in a match, then agonized over what to order for dinner.
AIの評価値が自分の手を「悪手」と示し、テレビ中継のコメントに叩かれた。: The AI evaluation called my move a “blunder,” and I got slammed in the TV broadcast comments.
順位戦でC級2組を抜けるのに5年かかった。: It took five years to climb out of Class C2 in the Meijin ranking league.
対局の勝敗で月の収入が大きく変わった。: My monthly income swung wildly depending on wins and losses.
将棋教室で、小学生に飛車落ちで負けた。: At a shogi class, lost to an elementary schooler in a rook-handicap game.
タイトル戦の挑戦者になり、和服をあつらえた。: Became a title match challenger and had a kimono tailored.
「棋士って何食べてるの？」と聞かれ、勝負メシを答えた。: Asked “What do shogi pros eat?”, I answered with my match-day meals.
研究会で、後輩の新手に感心した。: At a study group, was impressed by a junior's novel move.
選抜試験の応募者は4000人で、合格者は2人だった。: 4,000 applied to the selection exam; 2 passed.
ロシア語の訓練を、1日6時間受けた。: Had six hours of Russian training a day.
水中訓練で、宇宙服を着て6時間潜った。: In underwater training, spent six hours submerged in a spacesuit.
打ち上げの瞬間、体に4Gがかかった。: At liftoff, my body felt 4 G.
ISSから見た地球が、写真で見るよりずっと青かった。: Earth seen from the ISS was far bluer than in photos.
宇宙で食べたラーメンは、地上の味とは違った。: The ramen I ate in space didn't taste like it does on the ground.
帰還後、地上で歩けず、しばらく車椅子だった。: After returning, I couldn't walk on the ground and used a wheelchair for a while.
小学校で講演し、子どもたちに質問攻めにされた。: Gave a talk at an elementary school and was bombarded with questions.
宇宙ステーションのトイレの修理を担当した。: Put in charge of repairing the space station toilet.
打ち上げが延期になり、また半年待つことになった。: The launch was postponed, and I had to wait another six months.
時給2000円に、ドリンクバックが1杯200円ついた。: 2,000 yen an hour, plus a 200 yen commission per drink.
客から「LINE教えて」と言われ、営業用のアカウントを教えた。: A customer asked for my LINE, so I gave them my work account.
終電後の閉店で、タクシー代が自腹だった。: Closing after the last train meant paying for the taxi myself.
常連さんの誕生日にシャンパンを入れてもらい、売上で1位になった。: A regular ordered champagne on their birthday, and I ranked first in sales.
昼の大学の授業中、眠くて寝てしまった。: Fell asleep in my daytime university lecture.
酔ったお客さんにずっと説教され、笑顔でうなずき続けた。: A drunk customer lectured me forever, and I kept nodding with a smile.
同じ店の子が無断で辞め、シフトが週5になった。: A coworker quit without notice, and my shifts went up to five a week.
毎日、ドリンクで3〜4杯飲み、肝臓が心配になった。: Drinking three or four drinks every day made me worry about my liver.
親には「カフェでバイトしてる」と言っていた。: Told my parents I was working part-time at a café.
辞めた後、就活で「接客経験」とだけ書いた。: After quitting, I wrote only “customer service experience” for job hunting.
月に1回、自費で性病検査を受け、1回1万円かかった。: Once a month I paid out of pocket for an STD test, 10,000 yen each time.
源氏名を使い、本名は誰にも教えなかった。: Used a stage name and never told anyone my real name.
1か月で100万円稼いだが、税金をどう申告すればいいか分からなかった。: Earned 1 million yen in a month, but had no idea how to report the taxes.
親には「派遣で事務をしている」と言っていた。: Told my parents I was doing office work as a temp.
写メ日記を毎日3回更新した。: Updated my photo diary three times a day.
知り合いの客が来たらどうしようと、毎日不安だった。: Every day I worried about what I'd do if an acquaintance came in as a customer.
お金が貯まって、奨学金を一括で返した。: Saved enough to pay off my student loan in one lump sum.
クレジットカードの審査に落ち、職業欄に何を書くべきか悩んだ。: Got rejected for a credit card and agonized over what to put in the occupation field.
スタッフの男性が、帰りの送迎で家の近くまで送ってくれた。: A male staff member drove me home after work, dropping me near my place.
辞めた後、空白期間の説明に困り、面接で「家業の手伝い」と言った。: After quitting, I struggled to explain the gap and told interviewers I'd been “helping with the family business.”
教授から「来年アメリカに留学しないか」と声がかかった。: My professor asked, “Want to study in the U.S. next year?”
ボストンで2年研究した。論文が1本通って、帰国後に講師になった。: Did research in Boston for two years. One paper got accepted, and I became a lecturer after returning home.
実験がうまくいかず、2年で貯金が600万円減った。でも家族と過ごす時間は人生で一: Experiments went badly, and my savings dropped by 6 million yen in two years. But I spent more time with my family than ever before.
留学先の研究室で隣の席だった同僚と、10年後に共同で創薬ベンチャーを立ち上げた。: Ten years later, I co-founded a drug discovery startup with the colleague who sat next to me in the lab abroad. Our shares were valued at 200 million yen.
英語が上達しないまま2年が過ぎた。帰国して一番役に立ったのは、現地で覚えたパンケ: Two years passed without my English improving. The most useful thing I brought home was how to make pancakes, learned over there.
臨床を続けて、地域で「あの先生なら」と言われるようになった。: Kept up clinical work, and locals began saying, “If it's that doctor, it's fine.”
医局での立場が微妙になり、3年後に市中病院へ移った。: My standing in the department became awkward, and three years later I moved to a community hospital.
5年後、医局の教授選で票を集める側に回り、自分が副院長になった。: Five years later, I ended up rounding up votes in the department's professor election, and became deputy director myself.
臨床一筋で年間1200件の内視鏡をこなすうちに腰を痛め、半年間リハビリに通った。: Devoted to clinical work, I performed 1,200 endoscopies a year, hurt my back, and went to rehab for six months.
開業医の父が倒れ、クリニックを継ぐか迫られた。: My father, a private-practice doctor, collapsed, and I was pressed to take over his clinic.
院長になった。患者の半分は父の代からの常連で、毎日「お父さんは元気？」と聞かれる: Became the director. Half the patients have been coming since my father's day, and every day they ask, “How's your dad?”
借金ごと継いだ。機械の更新に3000万円かかった。: Inherited the clinic along with its debt. Replacing the equipment cost 30 million yen.
父が3か月で復帰し、親子で診療を分担することになった。待合室で親子喧嘩をして患者: My father returned in three months, and we split the patients between us. We argued in the waiting room and patients had to stop us.
電子カルテを導入したら、80代の看護師さんが一斉に辞めた。1か月、受付も自分でや: When I introduced electronic records, the nurses in their 80s all quit at once. For a month I even manned the reception desk myself.
クリニックは閉院した。父は寂しそうだったが「好きにしろ」と言った。: The clinic closed. Father looked lonely, but said, “Do as you like.”
後継の医師が見つかり、譲渡金で2000万円入った。: A successor doctor was found, and the transfer fee brought in 20 million yen.
大学に残って研究を続け、7年後に教授になった。父は退院後、毎年の学会に聴きに来た: Stayed at the university to keep researching, and became a professor seven years later. After leaving the hospital, Father came to hear me at the conference every year.
閉院の日、50年分のカルテを整理していたら、自分の出生記録の写しが出てきた。: On closing day, while sorting 50 years of patient charts, I found a copy of my own birth record.
隣の駅に大手の歯科チェーンが開院した。: A big dental chain opened a branch at the next station over.
「精密治療」で評判になり、遠方からも患者が来るようになった。: Became known for “precision treatment,” and patients began coming from far away.
ローンが月40万円になった。患者は思ったほど増えなかった。: The loan payments hit 400,000 yen a month. Patients didn't increase as much as I'd hoped.
導入したマイクロスコープの動画をSNSに上げたら、歯科学生のフォロワーが2万人に: I posted videos from the new microscope on social media, gained 20,000 followers among dental students, and got three speaking requests a month.
大手チェーンが2年で撤退した。投資した設備のおかげで、残った患者を全部引き受けら: The big chain pulled out within two years. Thanks to the equipment I'd invested in, I could take in all the remaining patients.
施設を週3回回るようになった。「先生が来る日が楽しみ」と言われた。: Began visiting care facilities three times a week. They told me, “We look forward to the days you come.”
移動ばかりで体力が持たず、1年でやめた。: All the travel wore me out, and I quit after a year.
訪問先の施設で出会った90代の元大工さんが、医院の看板を無料で彫ってくれた。: A retired carpenter in his 90s, whom I met at one of the facilities, carved the clinic's sign for free.
訪問歯科の実績が評価され、市から在宅医療の委員に選ばれた。会議が月4回増えた。: My home-visit work was recognized, and the city appointed me to a home-care committee. Four more meetings a month.
患者に「保険でいいから一番いいのにして」と言われた。: A patient told me, “Insurance coverage is fine, just give me the best one.”
納得して自費のセラミックを選んでくれた。10年後も割れていない。: They understood and chose the self-paid ceramic. Ten years later, it still hasn't cracked.
口コミに「金儲け主義」と書かれた。星1つだった。: A review called me “money-hungry.” One star.
その患者が地元企業の社長で、社員300人の歯科健診をまとめて任されることになった: That patient turned out to be the president of a local company, and I was entrusted with the dental checkups for all 300 employees.
自費の詰め物が1年で欠けた。無償でやり直し、材料代を18万円自腹で払った。: A self-paid filling chipped within a year. I redid it for free and paid 180,000 yen for materials out of pocket.
保険の範囲で精一杯やった。採算は合わないが、患者さんは満足して帰った。: Did everything I could within insurance coverage. It didn't pay, but the patient went home satisfied.
口コミで「誠実な先生」と広まり、患者が月に30人増えた。: Word spread that I was an “honest doctor,” and I gained 30 more patients a month.
保険診療の限界を研究し続けて学会で発表したら、厚労省の検討会に呼ばれた。: I kept studying the limits of insured treatment and presented at a conference, which got me invited to a Ministry of Health panel.
同じことを言う患者が月に40人来るようになり、売上が前年比で15%落ちた。: Forty patients a month started saying the same thing, and sales dropped 15% from last year.
海外の大学から、今の倍の給料でポストのオファーが来た。: A university abroad offered me a position at double my current salary.
シンガポールに移った。研究費も時間も増え、論文が3年で10本出た。: Moved to Singapore. With more funding and time, I published 10 papers in three years.
言葉と文化の壁で家族が馴染めず、2年で帰国した。: My family couldn't adjust to the language and cultural barriers, so we returned home after two years.
シンガポールで立ち上げた研究室から特許が出て、ライセンス料が年に800万円入るよ: A patent came out of the lab I set up in Singapore, and licensing fees began bringing in 8 million yen a year.
現地の屋台料理にはまりすぎて、2年で体重が12kg増えた。健康診断で初めて引っか: I got so hooked on the local street food that I gained 12 kg in two years. For the first time, I was flagged at my health checkup.
残って教授に昇進した。会議が倍になった。: Stayed and was promoted to professor. The meetings doubled.
ずっと「あのとき行っていれば」と思っている。: I've always wondered, “What if I had gone back then?”
学部長選挙に担ぎ出され、5年間ほぼ研究ができなかった。: Was drafted into the dean election and could barely do research for five years.
地元の高校で出前授業をしたら、10年後にその中の3人が自分の研究室に入ってきた。: I gave a guest lecture at a local high school, and ten years later three of the students joined my lab.
ゼミ生が博士課程に進みたいと相談してきた。: A seminar student came to me wanting to go on to a doctoral program.
5年後、その子は助教になった。最初の論文の謝辞に名前が載っていた。: Five years later, that student became an assistant professor. My name was in the acknowledgments of their first paper.
ポスドクを3年転々とした末に民間へ行った。「後悔はしてません」と言われたが、少し: After drifting through postdoc positions for three years, they went into industry. They said, “I have no regrets,” but it stung a little.
その教え子が20年後にノーベル賞候補と報じられ、取材で自分の名前を出してくれた。: Twenty years later, that student was reported as a Nobel Prize candidate and mentioned my name in an interview.
博士課程の3年間で、教え子は研究より料理配信で有名になった。たまに研究室で振る舞: During the three years of the doctoral program, my student became more famous for cooking streams than for research. Sometimes they cook for the lab.
就職も考えろ: Think about getting a job too
その子は企業研究所に就職し、毎年年賀状をくれる。: They got a job at a corporate research lab and send me a New Year's card every year.
「先生に夢を潰された」とSNSに書かれた。: They posted on social media that I “crushed their dream.”
現実を話したら、その子は逆に燃えた。海外の大学院に奨学金で進み、5年後に教授とし: When I told them the reality, they got fired up instead. They went to a graduate school abroad on a scholarship and, five years later, surpassed me as a professor.
「先生の話で踏ん切りがついた」と起業し、3年後に研究室へ1000万円を寄付してく: Saying, “Your words gave me the push I needed,” they started a company and, three years later, donated 10 million yen to the lab.
監査先の売上計上に不自然な点を見つけた。上司は「今回はいい」と言う。: Found something unnatural in a client's revenue recognition. My boss said, “Let it go this time.”
調査の結果、架空売上が見つかった。新聞に載り、事務所内で一目置かれた。: The investigation uncovered fictitious sales. It made the newspapers, and I earned respect within the firm.
クライアントが怒って監査契約を切った。上司との関係が冷え切った。: The client got angry and terminated the audit contract. My relationship with my boss turned ice cold.
業界誌で「若手監査人の良心」と紹介され、独立した後の顧客が初年度で20社集まった: A trade magazine called me “the conscience of young auditors,” and after going independent I gained 20 clients in the first year.
指摘の対応で3か月、毎晩22時まで資料をめくった。結局ただの計上ミスだった。: Following up on my flag took three months of poring over documents until 10 p.m. every night. It turned out to be a simple booking error.
何も起きなかった。ただ、ときどき夢に出る。: Nothing happened. It still shows up in my dreams now and then.
3年後に粉飾が発覚した。監査人として金融庁に呼ばれた。: Three years later, the accounting fraud came to light. As the auditor, I was summoned by the Financial Services Agency.
同じ担当先が翌年、別の監査法人に移った。自分のことは誰も覚えていなかった。: The same client switched to another audit firm the next year. Nobody remembered me.
上司が退職し、引き継ぎで同じ問題を自分で是正することになった。半年かかった。: My boss resigned, and in the handover I ended up fixing the same problem myself. It took six months.
事業会社のCFO候補として、上場準備中のベンチャーから誘われた。: A startup preparing to go public approached me as a CFO candidate.
会社が上場した。ストックオプションで5000万円になった。: The company went public. My stock options were worth 50 million yen.
上場準備中のベンチャー: A startup preparing to go public
上場は延期を繰り返し、資金が尽きて会社は解散した。: The IPO was postponed again and again, and the company ran out of money and dissolved.
上場当日の鐘を鳴らす役を社長に譲られ、手が震えて2回空振りした。: The president let me ring the bell on listing day. My hands shook and I missed twice.
社長と大喧嘩して1年で辞めたが、その後に出した本が会計士の間で3万部売れた。: After a huge fight with the president I quit within a year, but the book I published afterward sold 30,000 copies among accountants.
パートナーに昇進した。年収が1500万円を超えた。: Promoted to partner. Annual income topped 15 million yen.
昇進レースに負けて、40代で地方事務所に回された。: Lost the promotion race and was sent to a regional office in my 40s.
法人の不祥事で業務停止となり、半年間の自宅待機の間に料理教室へ通った。: The firm was hit with a business suspension over a scandal, and during six months at home I attended cooking classes.
後輩を20人育てた。その中の1人が上場企業のCFOになり、毎年お中元が届く。: Trained 20 juniors. One of them became CFO of a listed company, and sends me a midsummer gift every year.
大企業から高額な顧問契約の話が来た。ただし相手は以前訴えた会社だった。: A big company offered a lucrative retainer contract. But it was a company I had once sued.
月50万円の顧問料で事務所の経営が安定した。: A 500,000 yen monthly retainer stabilized the firm's finances.
昔の依頼者に知られ、「裏切り者」と言われた。: Former clients found out and called me a “traitor.”
顧問先の社内体制を一から作り直し、5年で同社の訴訟が年12件から1件に減った。: I rebuilt the client's internal systems from scratch, and in five years their lawsuits dropped from 12 a year to 1.
顧問先の社長と釣り仲間になり、毎月第2土曜は船の上で法律相談をするようになった。: I became fishing buddies with the client's president, and every second Saturday we hold legal consultations out on a boat.
弱い立場の人の事件を続けた。お金はないが、紹介で依頼が途切れない。: Kept taking cases for the vulnerable. No money, but referrals keep the work coming.
事務所の家賃が払えなくなり、知り合いの事務所に間借りした。: Could no longer pay the office rent and moved into an acquaintance's office as a tenant.
断った件がネットで話題になり、「筋を通す弁護士」として講演が年20本来た。: The case I turned down became a hot topic online, and as “the lawyer who stands on principle,” I got 20 speaking invitations a year.
司法修習の同期が受けた。10年後に年収で8倍の差がついたが、同窓会では向こうがず: A classmate from the legal training institute took it. Ten years later, his income was eight times mine, but at the reunion he complained the whole time.
無罪を主張する被告人の弁護。証拠は不利だ。: Defending a defendant who claims innocence. The evidence is against him.
一審で無罪判決が出た。テレビで報道され、依頼者が泣いた。: Acquitted at the first trial. It was on TV, and my client cried.
有罪だった。控訴審の準備をしながら、半年で体重が6kg落ちた。: Found guilty. While preparing for the appeal, I lost 6 kg in six months.
冤罪事件として映画化された。主役の俳優が自分より20歳若くて少しだけ腹が立った。: It became a movie as a wrongful-conviction case. The lead actor was 20 years younger than me, which irritated me slightly.
控訴審で逆転無罪になるまで4年かかった。その間に髪の半分が白くなった。: It took four years to win a reversal and acquittal on appeal. Half my hair turned white in the meantime.
情状弁護に切り替える: Switch to a plea for leniency
執行猶予がついた。本人は「納得してない」と言った。: Got a suspended sentence. He said, “I'm not convinced.”
結果に本人も家族も感謝してくれた。: Both he and his family thanked me for the result.
10年後、被告人が再審請求で無罪を勝ち取った。自分は何もできなかったと、新聞を読: Ten years later, the defendant won acquittal through a retrial. Reading the newspaper, I thought I hadn't been able to do anything.
被告人の母親から毎年、家で漬けた梅干しが1瓶届くようになった。: Every year the defendant's mother sends me a jar of homemade pickled plums.
クラスでいじめの兆候を見つけた。管理職は「様子を見よう」と言う。: Noticed signs of bullying in my class. The administrators said, “Let's wait and see.”
早めに介入して収まった。被害の子が卒業式で笑っていた。: Intervened early and it settled down. The child who was targeted was smiling at graduation.
加害側の保護者が教育委員会に乗り込んできた。毎晩胃が痛かった。: The parents of the bully stormed into the board of education. My stomach hurt every night.
対応を記録した資料が市内の全小学校のマニュアルになり、研修講師に呼ばれるようにな: My records of how I handled it became the manual for every elementary school in the city, and I started getting invited as a training instructor.
加害側だった子が6年生で学級委員に立候補し、演説で「去年の自分を変えたい」と言っ: The child who had been the bully ran for class representative in sixth grade and said in the speech, “I want to change who I was last year.”
自然に収まった。でも本当によかったのか今もわからない。: It settled down on its own. But I still don't know if that was really the right call.
不登校になってしまった。ずっと自分を責めた。: The child stopped coming to school. I blamed myself for a long time.
様子を見ている間に、子どもたち自身が話し合いの場を作った。自分は最後まで何もして: While I was waiting and watching, the children set up a discussion on their own. I did nothing to the very end.
3年後、被害の子の親から訴えられた。和解金の一部を自分も負担することになった。: Three years later, the parents of the child who was targeted sued. I ended up paying part of the settlement myself.
過労で心が限界。年度途中だ。: Overwork has pushed me to my limit. And it's the middle of the school year.
半年休んで復帰した。子どもたちが「おかえり」と手紙をくれた。: Took six months off and came back. The kids gave me letters saying, “Welcome back.”
復帰できず、そのまま退職した。: Couldn't return and ended up resigning.
休職中に始めた陶芸が楽しくなり、2年後に退職して工房を開いた。年収は半分になった: The pottery I took up during leave became so enjoyable that I quit two years later and opened a studio. My income was cut in half.
休職中に勉強した心理学を活かし、復帰後は学校カウンセリングの担当になった。: Putting to use the psychology I studied during leave, I became the school counseling lead after returning.
年度末まで踏ん張る: Hang on until the end of the year
なんとか3月を迎えた。修了式のあと、職員室で1時間動けなかった。: Somehow made it to March. After the closing ceremony, I couldn't move in the staff room for an hour.
4月に倒れて入院した。: Collapsed in April and was hospitalized.
修了式の日、クラス全員が描いた似顔絵の黒板アートで送り出された。そこで泣き崩れた: On closing day, the whole class sent me off with a chalkboard art of portraits they'd drawn. I broke down in tears.
3月に退職届を出した。翌月から学習塾を開き、教え子が10人通ってくれた。: Handed in my resignation in March. The next month I opened a cram school, and 10 students came.
素行の悪い生徒の退学が職員会議で議論されている。: The staff meeting is debating whether to expel a student with bad conduct.
その子は卒業した。10年後、自分の店を開いて招待してくれた。: That student graduated. Ten years later, they opened their own shop and invited me.
また問題を起こした。他の先生から「あなたのせい」と言われた。: They caused trouble again. Other teachers said, “It's your fault.”
その子が教員になり、同じ職員室で働くことになった。初日の職員会議で居眠りしていた: That student became a teacher and ended up working in the same staff room. On the first day, they dozed off in the staff meeting.
その子が文化祭でたった1人で劇の大道具を作り上げ、賞を取った。職員室の空気が変わ: At the school festival, that student built the play's entire set alone and won an award. The mood in the staff room changed.
その子は学校を去った。その後どうしているかは知らない。: That student left the school. I don't know what became of them.
5年後、その子が「あのとき辞めてよかった」と働く姿を見せに来た。: Five years later, that student came to show me their working life and said, “I'm glad I left back then.”
同窓会で、その子の話になった。誰もその後を知らず、全員がしばらく黙った。: At the reunion, that student came up. Nobody knew what became of them, and everyone fell silent for a while.
10年後、その子が地元のヤンキー漫画でベストセラー作家になった。担任のモデルは自: Ten years later, that student became a bestselling author of a local delinquent manga. The homeroom teacher character was modeled on me.
強豪私立から、野球部監督として引き抜きの話が来た。: A powerhouse private school offered to recruit me as head coach of their baseball team.
3年目に甲子園に出た。アルプススタンドで泣いた。: In the third year, we made it to Koshien. I cried in the stands.
結果が出せず、OB会に叩かれて2年で解任された。: Couldn't produce results, got slammed by the alumni association, and was fired after two years.
甲子園で負けた試合が名勝負と言われ、高野連の記念DVDに収録された。: The game we lost at Koshien was called a classic, and it was included in the high school baseball federation's commemorative DVD.
寮生活の世話まで24時間任され、3年で体重が10kg減った。: Being in charge around the clock, even of dorm life, I lost 10 kg in three years.
公立で地道に教えた。大会では毎回2回戦負けだが、生徒たちは楽しそうだった。: Taught steadily at the public school. We lose in the second round at every tournament, but the students seemed to be enjoying themselves.
10年後、教え子がプロ野球のドラフトで指名された。テレビの前で泣いた。: Ten years later, a former student was picked in the pro baseball draft. I cried in front of the TV.
野球部が部員9人ぎりぎりになり、自分が打撃投手を毎日200球投げた。肩を壊した。: The baseball club shrank to the bare minimum of nine members, and I threw 200 batting-practice pitches a day. I wrecked my shoulder.
21世紀枠で甲子園に出た。初戦は0対12で負けたが、町中が旗を振って迎えてくれた: We reached Koshien through the 21st Century Slot. We lost the first game 0–12, but the whole town welcomed us home waving flags.
処方の量がおかしい気がする。医師は不機嫌で忙しそうだ。: The prescribed dose seems off. The doctor is grumpy and looks busy.
やはり10倍量の誤記だった。医師から後日、缶コーヒーが届いた。: Sure enough, it was a 10x dosage typo. The doctor later sent me a can of coffee.
「合ってる」と怒鳴られた。合っていた。: The doctor yelled, “It's correct!” And it was.
疑義照会がきっかけで病院の処方チェック体制が見直され、薬剤部から講演を頼まれた。: My query led the hospital to overhaul its prescription-checking system, and the pharmacy department asked me to give a talk.
その医師が10年後に院長になり、病院の薬剤師としてスカウトされた。: Ten years later, that doctor became hospital director and recruited me as a hospital pharmacist.
患者が副作用で救急搬送された。眠れない日が続いた。: The patient was rushed to the ER with side effects. I had sleepless nights afterward.
数年後、同じ医師の処方ミスが別の薬局で見つかった。自分の店でも出していたことが分: Years later, the same doctor's prescription error was found at another pharmacy. I realized my store had dispensed it too, and couldn't sleep.
患者が「この薬で元気になった」と毎月手作りのクッキーを持ってくる。量は合っていた: A patient says, “This medicine made me well,” and brings homemade cookies every month. The dose was right.
ドラッグストア本部から、店長への昇格を打診された。: Drugstore headquarters asked if I'd be promoted to store manager.
年収が120万円上がった。ただ、トイレットーパーの売上目標にも追われるようになっ: My annual income rose by 1.2 million yen. But I also started being chased by sales targets for toilet paper.
シフトの穴を自分で埋め続け、月の休みが4日になった。: I kept covering the gaps in the schedule myself, and my days off dropped to four a month.
売り場作りがはまり、担当した店の売上が全国1位になった。表彰で5万円の商品券をも: My shelf layouts hit the mark, and my store ranked first in sales nationwide. I received a 50,000 yen gift certificate as an award.
店長として2年働いたあと、エリアマネージャーに昇格し、担当店舗が12店舗になった: After two years as a store manager, I was promoted to area manager, overseeing 12 stores.
患者の顔と薬歴を覚え、「あなたに聞くと安心」と言われるようになった。: I memorized patients' faces and medication histories, and people started saying, “Asking you puts me at ease.”
給料は上がらず、同期の店長たちと差がついた。: My pay didn't rise, and a gap opened up with my peers who became store managers.
在宅医療に関わるようになり、訪問先のおばあちゃんから毎回お茶と羊羹を出された。: I got involved in home care, and the old lady I visited served me tea and yokan every time.
管理薬剤師として独立開業の誘いを受け、3年後に自分の薬局を開いた。: As a managing pharmacist, I was invited to go independent, and three years later I opened my own pharmacy.
企業の研究所から、任期なしで年収1.5倍のオファーが来た。: A corporate research lab offered me a permanent position at 1.5 times my salary.
研究テーマは選べないが、生活が安定し、子どもを持つ決心がついた。: I can't choose my research topics, but life is stable, and I made up my mind to have a child.
3年後に事業撤退で研究所ごと閉鎖された。: Three years later, the business was withdrawn and the whole research lab was shut down.
企業で開発した技術が家電に採用され、社内表彰で報奨金300万円をもらった。: A technology I developed at the company was adopted in home appliances, and I received a 3 million yen bonus at the internal awards.
企業でも結局論文を書き続け、5年後に大学から教授として呼び戻された。: Even in industry I kept writing papers, and five years later a university called me back as a professor.
成果が大きな雑誌に載り、准教授のポストを得た。: My results appeared in a major journal, and I got an associate professor post.
任期が切れ、また次の任期付きポストへ移った。: My term ran out, and I moved on to yet another fixed-term post.
科研費が3年連続で不採択になった。研究室の電気代を自分で払った月があった。: My research grant was rejected three years in a row. Some months I paid the lab's electric bill myself.
自作の実験装置の動画がSNSでバズり、テレビの科学番組に月1回出るようになった。: A video of my homemade experiment rig went viral on social media, and I started appearing on a TV science show once a month.
共同研究者が、データを少し「整えた」形跡がある。: There are signs that my co-researcher had “tidied up” the data a little.
論文は取り下げになったが、研究室の信頼は守られた。: The paper was withdrawn, but the lab's credibility was protected.
告発者として居づらくなり、研究室を出た。: As the whistleblower, I became uncomfortable staying and left the lab.
指摘の過程で作った不正検知ツールが学会で評価され、全国の大学に配布された。: The fraud-detection tool I built while pointing out the problem was praised at an academic conference and distributed to universities nationwide.
当の共同研究者が泣いて謝り、次の論文は2人で一から全データを取り直した。2年かか: My co-researcher apologized in tears, and for the next paper the two of us retook all the data from scratch. It took two years.
何事もなく論文は出た。ずっと心に引っかかっている。: The paper came out without incident. It has weighed on my mind ever since.
2年後に不正が発覚し、共著者として巻き込まれた。: Two years later the fraud came to light, and I was dragged in as a co-author.
共同研究者が他の大学に移った。そこで同じことをして、全国ニュースになった。: My co-researcher moved to another university, did the same thing there, and made the national news.
ずっと気になって再実験したら、データは整える前の方が面白い結果だった。: It kept bothering me, so I reran the experiment, and the data before it was tidied up turned out to be more interesting.
炎上案件のPMを任された。納期まであと2か月。: I was put in charge of a troubled project as PM. The deadline is two months away.
毎晩終電で何とか納めた。社長賞で金一封5万円をもらった。: I got it delivered somehow, working until the last train every night. The president's award came with a ¥50,000 cash bonus.
納期に間に合わず、顧客に詰められ続けた。: I missed the deadline and the client kept grilling me.
納品後の打ち上げで、顧客の部長が「次も君で」と言い、次の案件が5000万円で決ま: At the party after delivery, the client's department head said, “You again next time,” and the next project was settled at ¥50 million.
2か月で体重が8kg減った。納品の翌日から1週間寝込み、家族に心配された。: I lost 8 kg in two months. The day after delivery I was bedridden for a week, and my family was worried.
断って転職活動: Decline and look for a new job
Web系の自社開発企業に移った。私服で出社でき、年収も80万円上がった。: I moved to a web company with in-house development. I could go to work in casual clothes, and my salary rose by ¥800,000.
転職先もSESだった。: My new employer was an SES (contract engineering) company too.
転職先で炎上案件の前任PMと同じチームになった。話してみたら気が合い、2年後に一: At my new job I ended up on the same team as the previous PM of the troubled project. We hit it off, and two years later we started a company together.
面接で炎上経験を話したら面白がられ、年収が180万円上がった。: When I talked about my troubled-project experience in the interview, they found it fascinating, and my salary rose by ¥1.8 million.
社内ツールを勝手に作ったら、業務時間が半分になった。上司は「誰の許可で？」と言う: I built an internal tool on my own, and work time was cut in half. My boss said, “Who gave you permission?”
全社展開され、部署の残業が月20時間減った。: It was rolled out company-wide, and my department's overtime dropped by 20 hours a month.
「前例がない」と却下された。こっそり使い続けている。: It was rejected with “there's no precedent.” I keep using it in secret.
その上司が人事部長になり、自分を新設のDX推進部の課長にした。: That boss became head of HR and made me a section chief in the newly created DX Promotion Department.
ツールが他社に評判になり、引き抜きの話が年に3件来た。: The tool gained a reputation at other companies, and I got three poaching offers a year.
副業で売る: Sell it as a side business
SaaSにしたら月30万円の売上になった。: I turned it into a SaaS, and it brought in ¥300,000 a month.
大手企業にSaaSごと4000万円で買収された。: A major company acquired the whole SaaS for ¥40 million.
副業がバレて就業規則違反で減給になった。ツールはそのまま社内で使われ続けている。: My side business was discovered, and I got a pay cut for violating company rules. The tool is still in use inside the company.
大口顧客に、不利な条件を隠して売るよう上司に言われた。: My boss told me to sell to a major client while hiding the unfavorable terms.
契約は取れなかったが、半年後にその客が別の大口を紹介してくれた。: I didn't get the contract, but six months later that client introduced me to another major account.
ノルマ未達で賞与が30万円減った。: I missed my quota, and my bonus was cut by ¥300,000.
その顧客が転職先でも指名してくれ、10年で取引額が累計3億円になった。: That client requested me even after I changed jobs, and over ten years our total transactions reached ¥300 million.
正直さが社内で浮き、2年後に同じ考えの同僚3人と独立した。: My honesty made me stand out awkwardly at work, and two years later I went independent with three like-minded colleagues.
売上トップになった。でも客の顔が見られなくなった。: I became the top seller. But I could no longer look my customers in the eye.
後でクレームになり、担当を外された。: It later turned into a complaint, and I was taken off the account.
その上司が後で別件で処分された。自分は何も言われなかったが、しばらく眠れなかった: That boss was later disciplined over a different matter. Nothing was said to me, but I couldn't sleep for a while.
1年後にその客が倒産した。自分の売った条件が原因の1つだと新聞記事で知った。: A year later that client went bankrupt. I learned from a newspaper article that the terms I sold them were one of the causes.
ライバル会社からトップ営業として引き抜きがあった。顧客ごと来てほしいと言う。: A rival company tried to recruit me as a top salesperson. They wanted me to bring my clients with me.
年収が300万円上がった。古巣の上司とは二度と口をきかなくなった。: My salary rose by ¥3 million. I never spoke to my old boss again.
移った先で3年連続トップを取り、営業部長になった。年収が1300万円を超えた。: At the new company I took the top spot three years running and became sales director. My salary exceeded ¥13 million.
古巣から競業避止で訴えられ、和解金を100万円払った。: My old company sued me over a non-compete clause, and I paid ¥1 million in settlement.
残ったことを知った部長が、次の人事で課長にしてくれた。: The department head, learning that I had stayed, made me a section chief in the next personnel reshuffle.
引き止めの約束は守られず、課長の席は別の人に回った。: The promise made to keep me was broken, and the section chief post went to someone else.
同期のトップ営業が引き抜きに乗って移った。2年後、その人がお菓子を持って帰ってき: A fellow top salesperson from my cohort took a poaching offer and left. Two years later, that person came back with a box of sweets.
残った代わりに後輩の育成を任され、3年で部署の売上が1.4倍になった。: In return for staying I was put in charge of training juniors, and in three years the department's sales grew 1.4 times.
師長から、来月からICU配属を打診された。: The head nurse asked if I'd be assigned to the ICU starting next month.
必死で勉強し、2年後には後輩に教える側になった。: I studied desperately, and two years later I was the one teaching juniors.
重症患者の緊張に耐えられず、眠れなくなった。: I couldn't bear the tension of critical patients and started losing sleep.
ICUの経験を活かし、5年後に急性・重症患者看護の専門看護師になった。: Drawing on my ICU experience, five years later I became a certified nurse specialist in acute and critical care nursing.
ICUで出会った同僚と結婚した。夜勤明けに2人で牛丼を食べるのが定番デートだった: I married a colleague I met in the ICU. Our usual date was eating gyudon together after night shifts.
慣れた病棟で、患者さんの話をゆっくり聞ける日々を選んだ。: I chose days on a familiar ward, where I could listen to patients unhurried.
病棟の人手不足が悪化し、夜勤が月10回になった。: The ward's staffing shortage got worse, and I ended up on night shifts ten times a month.
病棟で患者さんの話を聞くうちに書き留めた記録が本になり、5000部売れた。: The notes I jotted down while listening to patients on the ward became a book, and it sold 5,000 copies.
病棟の後輩10人が全員辞めずに残った。師長会議で「あなたの病棟だけ」と言われた。: All ten junior nurses on my ward stayed on. At the head nurses' meeting I was told, “Yours is the only ward.”
美容クリニックから、日勤のみ・年収600万円で誘われた。: A cosmetic clinic offered me a day-shift-only job with a ¥6 million salary.
夜勤がなくなり、肌の調子が良くなった。ただ、ノルマがあった。: With no more night shifts, my skin improved. But there were quotas.
「人を看る」実感がなくなり、2年で病院に戻った。: I lost the sense of truly “caring for people” and returned to a hospital after two years.
カウンセラーとして指名が増え、月の売上インセンティブが20万円を超えた。: As a counselor I got more client requests, and my monthly sales incentive topped ¥200,000.
美容業界で知った人脈で起業し、訪問看護と美容を組み合わせた事業で年商5000万円: Using connections from the beauty industry, I started a business combining home-visit nursing and beauty care, reaching annual sales of ¥50 million.
主任になった。夜勤は減らないが、チームが好きだ。: I became a unit chief. The night shifts haven't decreased, but I love my team.
燃え尽きかけたが、同期と行った温泉旅行で持ち直した。: I was close to burning out, but a hot-spring trip with my cohort set me right again.
美容クリニックに移った同期が、2年後に看護部長として戻ってきた。上司になった。: A colleague who had moved to a cosmetic clinic came back two years later as director of nursing. She became my boss.
夜勤中に急変した患者を救った。家族から病院宛に手紙が届き、院内報に載った。: During a night shift I saved a patient whose condition suddenly worsened. The family sent the hospital a letter, and it was printed in the hospital newsletter.
新しい子育て支援事業を企画した。前例がないと上が渋っている。: I planned a new childcare support program. Upper management is reluctant because there's no precedent.
事業が始まり、地元紙に載った。利用者が年1000人を超えた。: The program launched and was covered in the local paper. Users exceeded 1,000 a year.
根回し不足で議会で叩かれ、出先機関に異動になった。: For lack of groundwork I was attacked in the city council and transferred to a branch office.
他の市から視察が年に30件来るようになった。視察対応だけで毎週1日が消えた。: Other cities began sending 30 study visits a year. Handling the visitors alone ate up one day every week.
事業を通じて知り合ったNPOに、退職後の再就職が決まった。: After retirement I landed a new job at an NPO I got to know through the program.
何も起きなかった。定時で帰れた。: Nothing happened. I got to leave on time.
翌年、隣の市が同じ事業を始めて全国ニュースになった。: The next year, the neighboring city started the same program and made the national news.
前例に従って空いた時間で、地域のママさんバレーのコーチを始めた。: With the free time that following precedent gave me, I started coaching a local moms' volleyball team.
何も起きないまま定年を迎えた。退職の挨拶は3行で終わった。: I reached retirement age with nothing ever happening. My farewell speech ended in three lines.
地元の有力者から「便宜を図ってくれ」と頼まれた。: A local bigwig asked me, “Do me a favor.”
角が立ったが、上司は「よく断った」と言ってくれた。: It caused friction, but my boss said, “Good thing you refused.”
嫌がらせの投書が何度も庁内に届いた。: Harassing letters were sent to the office again and again.
数年後、その有力者の不正が発覚した。断った記録が残っていて、自分だけ無傷だった。: A few years later, that bigwig's misconduct came to light. The record of my refusal remained, and I alone came out unscathed.
その有力者の孫が新人として配属された。驚くほど真面目だった。: That bigwig's grandchild was assigned to my section as a new hire. The kid was surprisingly diligent.
お歳暮が毎年届くようになった。: Year-end gifts started arriving every year.
監査で発覚し、懲戒処分になった。: It was discovered in an audit, and I was disciplined.
融通した件が報道され、半年間毎朝役所の前に記者が10人いた。: The favor was reported in the news, and for six months ten reporters stood in front of city hall every morning.
融通はバレなかった。有力者の紹介で、娘の就職先が決まった。: The favor was never found out. Through the bigwig's introduction, my daughter got a job.
会社がRPAを導入し、業務の半分がなくなると言われた。: The company introduced RPA, and I was told half of my duties would disappear.
社内のDX担当として評価され、主任になった。: I was recognized as the company's DX lead and became a unit chief.
慣れない仕事で毎日残業になった。: The unfamiliar work meant overtime every day.
RPAの経験を買われて、IT企業に転職した。年収が150万円上がった。: My RPA experience was valued, and I moved to an IT company. My salary rose by ¥1.5 million.
ロボットが月末に止まり、手作業で300件処理した。結局自分しか直せなかった。: The robot stopped at month-end, and I processed 300 items by hand. In the end, I was the only one who could fix it.
人手がまだ必要で、そのまま残れた。: Manpower was still needed, so I was able to stay put.
1年後、部署が縮小されて関連会社に出向になった。: A year later my department was downsized, and I was sent on secondment to an affiliate.
RPAが3回暴走し、そのたびに自分の手作業で救った。社内で「最後の砦」と呼ばれた: The RPA ran amok three times, and each time I saved the day by hand. I came to be called the company's “last bastion.”
空いた時間で始めた社内報作りが評判になり、広報部に異動した。: The company newsletter I started making in my spare time became popular, and I was transferred to the PR department.
簿記2級の勉強を始めるか迷っている。: I'm wondering whether to start studying for the Level 2 bookkeeping exam.
半年で合格し、経理部に異動して手当が月1万円ついた。: I passed in six months, moved to the accounting department, and got an allowance of ¥10,000 a month.
2回落ちて心が折れた。: I failed twice and lost heart.
簿記の勉強をきっかけに税理士を目指し、8年かけて5科目に合格した。: Studying bookkeeping led me to aim for tax accountant, and it took eight years to pass all five subjects.
簿記2級の勉強仲間とSNSで知り合い、オフ会で15人の友達ができた。: I met fellow Level 2 bookkeeping students on social media and made 15 friends at offline meetups.
平日の夜はヨガ教室に通い始めた。: I started going to a yoga class on weeknights.
ヨガ教室で出会った人と、2年後に結婚した。: Two years later I married someone I met at the yoga class.
ヨガにはまりインストラクター資格を取った。週末だけで月8万円の副収入になった。: I got hooked on yoga and earned an instructor certification. Weekends alone brought in ¥80,000 a month on the side.
特に何もせず1年が過ぎた。毎晩見ていたドラマが全部で200話を超えた。: A year passed without doing anything in particular. The dramas I watched every night added up to over 200 episodes.
親方が引退し、一人親方として独立しないかと言われた。: My master is retiring and suggested I go independent as a sole-proprietor craftsman.
元請けから仕事が途切れず、年収が200万円上がった。: The general contractors kept the work coming, and my income rose by ¥2 million.
支払いが3か月遅れる元請けに当たり、資金繰りに苦しんだ。: I got a general contractor who paid three months late, and I struggled to keep cash flowing.
独立して5年で従業員6人の会社になった。最初に雇ったのは昔の親方の孫だった。: Five years after going independent, I had a company with six employees. The first person I hired was my old master's grandchild.
独立1年目に資材を盗まれ、150万円分を自腹で買い直した。: In my first year on my own, materials were stolen, and I paid ¥1.5 million out of pocket to replace them.
安定した給料で、職長になった。: With a steady paycheck, I became a foreman.
会社が倒産し、退職金はほとんど出なかった。: The company went bankrupt, and almost no severance pay came out of it.
会社員のまま技能五輪の指導員になり、若手が全国大会で金メダルを取った。: Staying with the company, I became a coach for the Skills Olympics, and a young trainee won a gold medal at the national competition.
腰を痛めて現場に出られなくなり、事務所の積算担当に回った。: I hurt my back and couldn't work on-site anymore, so I was moved to cost estimating at the office.
工期が遅れていて、安全帯なしで作業しろと言われた。: The schedule was behind, and I was told to work without a safety harness.
揉めたが、所長が間に入ってくれた。: We argued, but the site manager stepped in.
「使えない」と言われて別の現場に回された。: I was called “useless” and sent to a different site.
断ったのを見ていた新人の母親から、会社に感謝の手紙が届いた。所長が朝礼で読んだ。: The mother of a new recruit who had seen me refuse sent the company a thank-you letter. The site manager read it aloud at the morning assembly.
断ったことがきっかけで現場の安全大会で発表することになり、県から表彰された。: Refusing led to my presenting at a site safety conference, and I received a commendation from the prefecture.
足を滑らせて落ち、骨折で3か月休んだ。: I slipped and fell, and was off work for three months with a fracture.
同じ現場の仲間が、安全帯なしで落ちた。自分は見ていることしかできなかった。: A coworker on the same site fell without a harness. All I could do was watch.
労基署の抜き打ち検査が入り、現場が1週間止まった。自分も指導を受けた。: The labor standards office made a surprise inspection, and the site was shut down for a week. I received a warning as well.
第一種電気工事士と電験三種の勉強を始めるか迷っている。: I'm wondering whether to start studying for the First-Class Electrician and Third-Class Chief Electrical Engineer qualifications.
3年かけて電験三種に合格した。ビル管理会社から引く手あまたになった。: It took three years, but I passed the Third-Class Chief Electrical Engineer exam. Building management companies were competing for me.
仕事と両立できず、途中でやめた。: I couldn't balance it with work and gave up partway.
電験三種を取ったあと独立し、太陽光発電所の保安管理で年収が900万円になった。: After earning the qualification, I went independent, and managing safety at solar power plants brought my income to ¥9 million.
勉強のノートをSNSで公開したら、参考書の出版の話が来た。: I shared my study notes on social media, and a publisher offered to turn them into a study guide.
腕で勝負した。若手から「師匠」と呼ばれるようになった。: I let my skills do the talking. The young workers began calling me “Master.”
50歳を過ぎて膝を痛め、高所作業ができなくなった。: After I turned fifty, I hurt my knee and could no longer work at heights.
地元の祭りの電飾を毎年1人で仕上げるようになり、市長から感謝状をもらった。: I began finishing the lights for the local festival by myself every year, and the mayor gave me a letter of appreciation.
現場一本の腕が見込まれ、照明デザイナーの会社に職人として引き抜かれた。: My field-honed skills were recognized, and a lighting design firm recruited me as a craftsman.
知り合いから、資格なしの友人にやらせた工事の手直しを格安で頼まれた。: An acquaintance asked me to fix, at a bargain price, electrical work done by an unlicensed friend.
文句を言われたが、安全な配線に直した。: They complained, but I rewired it safely.
丁寧な仕事が評判になり、近所の工務店から仕事が回ってくるようになった。: My careful work earned a reputation, and local builders began sending me jobs.
直した配線の写真を見た不動産会社から、アパート30棟の点検をまとめて頼まれた。: A real estate company saw photos of my rewiring and asked me to inspect 30 apartment buildings in one go.
手直しの最中に壁の中から前の住人の昭和の宝くじが出てきた。外れていた。: While doing the repairs, I found a Showa-era lottery ticket from a previous resident inside the wall. It was a loser.
格安で受ける: Take it at a bargain price
感謝され、知り合いから仕事が増えた。: They were grateful, and more jobs came in from acquaintances.
他の箇所から漏電し、責任を問われた。: Current leaked from another spot, and I was held responsible.
格安で受けたことが業界に広まり、「安い人」と思われて単価が上がらなかった。: Word got around the industry that I took jobs cheap, and I was seen as “the cheap guy,” so my rates never went up.
頼んできた知り合いが、3年後に大手ハウスメーカーの購買担当になった。大口の仕事が: The acquaintance who made the request became a purchasing manager at a major homebuilder three years later, and big jobs came my way.
中古の4tトラックを買って、個人で独立するか考えている。: I'm thinking of buying a used 4-ton truck and going independent as an owner-operator.
いい荷主がついて年収が700万円になった。: I landed good shippers, and my income reached ¥7 million.
燃料高騰で赤字が続き、2年で会社員に戻った。: Soaring fuel prices kept me in the red, and after two years I went back to being an employee.
個人で運送会社を立ち上げ、10年でトラック15台の会社になった。: I started my own trucking company, and in ten years it grew to a fleet of 15 trucks.
トラックのエンジンが半年で壊れ、修理に200万円かかった。: The truck's engine broke down within six months, and the repair cost ¥2 million.
運行管理者の資格を取り、内勤に移った。: I earned my transport manager qualification and moved to an office job.
会社の大型車が自動運転の実験に使われ、運転席に座るだけの日が来た。: The company's large trucks were used for self-driving trials, and the day came when all I did was sit in the driver's seat.
会社の配車システムを作り直す担当になり、ドライバーの残業が月20時間減った。: I was put in charge of rebuilding the company's dispatch system, and drivers' overtime dropped by 20 hours a month.
定年まで無事故で走り、表彰で金時計をもらった。: I drove accident-free until retirement and received a gold watch as an award.
配車係から、休憩を削れば今日中に終わると言われた。: The dispatcher told me that if I cut my breaks, I could finish today.
翌日に回したが、事故なく帰れた。: I pushed it to the next day, but made it home without an accident.
配車係に嫌われ、割のいい便を回されなくなった。: The dispatcher took a dislike to me and stopped giving me the well-paying runs.
同じ日に休まず走った同僚が事故を起こした。配車係が以後、休憩を削れと言わなくなっ: A coworker who drove without a break that same day had an accident. After that, the dispatcher stopped telling people to cut their breaks.
休憩中に寄った道の駅でラーメンにはまり、全国120か所の道の駅を制覇した。: I got hooked on the ramen at a roadside station I stopped at during a break, and ended up visiting 120 roadside stations nationwide.
なんとか間に合った。: I just barely made it on time.
居眠りで追突事故を起こした。: I dozed off and rear-ended another vehicle.
間に合った報酬として、翌月から長距離便を任された。月収が8万円上がったが、家にほ: As a reward for making it, I was given long-haul runs from the following month. My monthly pay rose by ¥80,000, but I barely got home anymore.
3年続けた結果、睡眠時無呼吸症候群と診断され、乗務停止になった。: After three years of this, I was diagnosed with sleep apnea syndrome and suspended from driving.
介護福祉士を取ったら、主任に推薦すると言われた。: I was told that if I earned my certified care worker qualification, they'd recommend me for unit chief.
合格して主任になった。手当で月2万円上がった。: I passed and became a unit chief. The allowance added ¥20,000 a month.
不合格だった。来年また受ける。: I failed. I'll take it again next year.
主任として新人研修を作り直し、施設の離職率が3割から1割に下がった。: As unit chief I redesigned the new-hire training, and the facility's turnover rate fell from 30% to 10%.
試験勉強中に書いたノートを後輩にあげたら、5人全員が合格した。: I gave the notes I wrote while studying for the exam to my juniors, and all five of them passed.
現場で利用者さんと向き合うのが好きなので、そのままにした。: I like working face to face with the residents on the floor, so I left things as they were.
新しく来た主任と合わず、現場の雰囲気が悪くなった。: I didn't get along with the newly arrived unit chief, and the atmosphere on the floor turned bad.
現場一筋でいたら、利用者の家族から「この人がいるから預けられる」と指名が増えた。: Staying on the floor paid off: more residents' families began requesting me, saying, “We can leave them here because of this person.”
腰を痛めて現場に立てなくなり、相談員に転向した。給料は少し下がった。: I hurt my back and could no longer work on the floor, so I switched to being a care counselor. My pay dropped a little.
同僚が利用者に乱暴な言葉を使っているのを見た。: I saw a coworker speaking roughly to a resident.
指導が入り、施設の空気が少しよくなった。: Guidance was given, and the atmosphere at the facility improved a little.
告げ口したと言われ、職場で浮いた。: I was accused of tattling and became an outcast at work.
報告がきっかけで施設全体の研修が始まり、自分が講師になった。: My report led to facility-wide training, and I became the instructor.
施設長から「波風を立てるな」と言われ、半年後に別施設へ異動になった。: The facility director told me, “Don't make waves,” and six months later I was transferred to another facility.
「疲れてて、ごめん」と言われた。2人で飲みに行った。: They said, “I'm tired, sorry.” The two of us went out for a drink.
逆ギレされ、関係が最悪になった。: They blew up at me, and our relationship hit rock bottom.
その同僚と10年後に共同でグループホームを開いた。: Ten years later, that coworker and I opened a group home together.
話したあとも同僚の態度は変わらず、結局自分が辞めた。: Even after we talked, my coworker's attitude didn't change, and in the end I was the one who quit.
保護者から理不尽なクレームが続いている。園長は「相手を立てて」と言う。: A parent keeps making unreasonable complaints. The director says, “Let them save face.”
園長が間に入り、なんとか収まった。: The director stepped in, and things somehow settled down.
結局自分が謝らされ、悔しかった。: In the end I was made to apologize, and I was frustrated.
園長が守ってくれた恩を感じ、その園で20年勤め上げた。: Grateful that the director had protected me, I worked at that school for twenty years.
クレームの保護者が、翌年PTA会長として園の行事を全面的に手伝ってくれた。: The complaining parent became PTA president the next year and helped with all of the school's events.
保護者が冷静になり、最後は「先生ありがとう」と言った。: The parent calmed down and in the end said, “Thank you, teacher.”
役所に通報されて調査が入った。問題なしだったが疲れた。: I was reported to the city office and an investigation followed. No problems were found, but I was exhausted.
記録を取る習慣が評判になり、市の保育士研修で講師を頼まれた。: My habit of keeping records earned a reputation, and I was asked to teach at the city's childcare worker training.
保護者が転園し、その親の別の子の担任が自分になった。気まずかった。: The parent moved their child to another school, and then I became homeroom teacher for that parent's other child. It was awkward.
企業内保育所から、給料を月3万円上げると誘われた。: A company-run daycare offered me a ¥30,000 monthly raise to join.
少人数で、子ども一人ひとりと向き合えるようになった。: With small groups, I could finally give each child my full attention.
園の運営会社が撤退し、1年で職を失った。: The company running the daycare pulled out, and I lost my job within a year.
企業内保育所の利用者だった社員が、自分の講演を社内で企画した。: An employee who had used the company daycare organized a talk by me inside the company.
企業の社長の子どもを担当し、気に入られて保育事業の責任者に抜擢された。: I looked after the company president's child, won his favor, and was promoted to head of the childcare business.
主任になり、新人の育成を任された。: I became a head teacher and was put in charge of training newcomers.
園の運営が別法人に変わり、方針がまるで変わった。: The school came under a different operator, and its policies changed completely.
園の元卒園児が保育士になって戻ってきた。自分のことを「先生」とまだ呼ぶ。: A former student of the school came back as a childcare worker. They still call me “teacher.”
結局給料は変わらないまま、10年が過ぎた。: In the end my pay stayed the same, and ten years went by.
ディーラーから、営業職への異動を勧められた。給料は上がる。: The dealership suggested I move into sales. The pay would go up.
整備の知識が活きて、販売台数が店舗トップになった。: My mechanical knowledge came in handy, and my unit sales became the best in the store.
ノルマに追われ、工具を握りたくなった。: Hounded by quotas, I longed to hold my tools again.
営業成績で表彰され、ハワイ旅行に招待された。旅行中もずっと車の話をしていた。: I was honored for my sales record and invited on a trip to Hawaii. I talked about cars the entire time.
営業の傍ら自分の整備ブログを始めたら、月10万PVになり、広告収入が月3万円入っ: Alongside sales I started my own car-maintenance blog, which reached 100,000 page views a month and earned ¥30,000 a month in ad revenue.
検査員の資格を取り、工場の要になった。: I earned my inspector qualification and became the linchpin of the shop.
工場長になった。若手が「工場長みたいになりたい」と言ってくれた。: I became shop manager. A young mechanic told me, “I want to be like you.”
国家1級の整備士を取り、メーカーの技術コンテストで全国3位になった。: I earned the national Grade 1 mechanic certification and placed third in the nation at a manufacturer's technical contest.
EVの普及で仕事が半減し、50歳で職業訓練を受け直した。: As EVs spread, work was cut in half, and at fifty I went back for vocational retraining.
昔からのお客さんの車、修理代が車の価値を超えている。: A longtime customer's car would cost more to repair than it's worth.
お客さんは納得し、次の車もうちで買ってくれた。: The customer understood and bought their next car from us.
「思い出の車なのに」と怒って来なくなった。: They got angry, saying, “But it's a car full of memories,” and never came back.
そのお客さんの孫が整備士になり、うちの工場に就職してきた。: That customer's grandchild became a mechanic and came to work at our shop.
買い替えを勧めたら、お客さんが旧車として売りに出し、なんと300万円で売れた。: After I recommended replacing it, the customer put it up for sale as a classic car, and it actually sold for ¥3 million.
部品を探し回り、3週間かけて直した。お客さんは泣いて喜んだ。: I hunted everywhere for parts and fixed it over three weeks. The customer wept with joy.
部品代がかさみ、請求額でお客さんと揉めた。: Parts costs piled up, and I got into a dispute with the customer over the bill.
直した車が旧車イベントで賞を取り、雑誌に載った。: The car I fixed won a prize at a classic car event and was featured in a magazine.
直した翌月にエンジンも壊れた。お客さんは笑って「寿命だね」と言った。: The month after I fixed it, the engine broke down too. The customer laughed and said, “Guess it's its time.”
本部から、新店舗の立ち上げ店長を頼まれた。: Headquarters asked me to be the launch manager of a new store.
オープンから半年で黒字化した。エリアマネージャーに昇進した。: The store turned a profit six months after opening. I was promoted to area manager.
人が集まらず、半年間ほぼ休みなく働いた。: Staff wouldn't come, and I worked almost without a day off for six months.
新店のスタッフから3人が店長に育ち、自分は本部の人事部長に引き抜かれた。: Three of the new store's staff grew into store managers, and I was tapped to become HR director at headquarters.
新店のオープン初日に停電し、ろうそくで接客した。それが話題になった。: A blackout hit on the new store's opening day, and we served customers by candlelight. It became the talk of the town.
今の店で、スタッフと楽しく働き続けた。: I kept working happily with my staff at the current store.
新店に行った同期が先に昇進した。: A colleague of my cohort who went to the new store got promoted before me.
今の店で育てたバイトが、5年後に本部の社員として自分の上司になった。: A part-timer I trained at my current store became a headquarters employee five years later and ended up as my boss.
断った翌年、今の店が閉店になり、結局新店に行くことになった。: The year after I declined, my current store closed, and I ended up going to the new store anyway.
万引きを目撃した。中学生だった。: I witnessed a shoplifting. The culprit was a middle schooler.
泣きながら謝った。親に連絡して、警察には言わなかった。: They apologized in tears. I contacted their parents and didn't tell the police.
その中学生が数年後に高校生になり、アルバイトとしてうちの店に応募してきた。: A few years later that middle schooler became a high schooler and applied to work part-time at our store.
その子の親が乗り込んできて「うちの子がそんなことするわけない」と30分怒鳴った。: The kid's parent stormed in and yelled for 30 minutes: “My child would never do that.”
警察が来た。少し胸が痛んだが、それが仕事だった。: The police came. It hurt a little, but it was the job.
数年後、その子が親と一緒に謝りに来た。高校に受かったと言っていた。: Years later, the kid came to apologize with a parent. Said they'd gotten into high school.
防犯カメラの設置を提案し、店のロス率が半分になった。本部から表彰された。: Proposed installing security cameras, and the store's loss rate was cut in half. Commended by headquarters.
通報の件で地元の中学校から講演を頼まれ、全校生徒の前で話した。: Because of the reporting incident, a local junior high asked me to give a talk, and I spoke in front of the whole school.
自分の店を出すため、物件を見つけた。: Found a property to open my own shop.
地元の人気店になり、行列ができるようになった。: It became a popular local spot, with lines out the door.
2年で閉店した。借金が800万円残った。: Closed after two years. Left with 8 million yen in debt.
地元の人気店になったあと、大手外食チェーンから業務提携の話が来て、3店舗に広がっ: After becoming a popular local spot, a major restaurant chain offered a partnership, and it grew to three locations.
隣にチェーン店が開店し、客が半分になった。メニューを全部入れ替えて半年で持ち直し: A chain store opened next door and customers dropped by half. Replaced the entire menu and recovered in six months.
オーナーが店を畳むことになり、急に職を失った。: The owner decided to close the restaurant, and I suddenly lost my job.
雇われ料理長として作った新メニューがテレビで紹介され、月売上が200万円増えた。: A new menu item I created as an employed head chef was featured on TV, and monthly sales rose by 2 million yen.
オーナーの息子が厨房に入ってきて、口出しが毎日続いた。2年耐えて辞めた。: The owner's son came into the kitchen and meddled every day. Endured it for two years, then quit.
料理番組の取材依頼が来た。: A cooking show asked to feature me.
放送翌日から予約が3か月先まで埋まった。: From the day after the broadcast, reservations were booked three months out.
放送後の客足は2週間で元に戻った。: Foot traffic went back to normal two weeks after the broadcast.
番組で作った料理がSNSでバズり、レシピ本が5万部売れた。: The dish made on the show went viral on social media, and the recipe book sold 50,000 copies.
放送で「店主の口癖」がネタにされ、半年間近所の子どもに真似された。: My “catchphrase as owner” was made fun of on air, and neighborhood kids imitated it for half a year.
常連さんが「テレビに出なくてよかった」と笑った。: A regular laughed, “Glad you didn't go on TV.”
断ったのに、常連客が勝手に投稿した写真がバズり、行列が3か月続いた。: Even though I declined, a photo a regular posted on their own went viral, and lines lasted three months.
断った番組の代わりに出た隣の店が大繁盛した。少し悔しかった。: The shop next door, which appeared in place of the show I turned down, became hugely successful. It stung a little.
期間工の満了が近い。社員登用の試験を受けるか、満了金をもらって辞めるか。: My fixed-term factory contract is about to end. Take the permanent-employee exam, or collect the completion bonus and leave?
正社員になった。ボーナスが出た日、実家に電話した。: Became a full-time employee. The day the bonus came in, I called home.
正社員になって5年後、工場の改善提案で社長賞を受賞し、報奨金50万円をもらった。: Five years after becoming a full-time employee, won the President's Award for a factory improvement proposal and received a 500,000 yen prize.
試験に受かった直後、工場の閉鎖が発表された。遠方の工場に異動した。: Right after passing the exam, the factory's closure was announced. Transferred to a faraway plant.
満了金と貯金で300万円を手に、半年かけて日本一周した。: With 3 million yen from the bonus and savings, spent half a year traveling around Japan.
次の仕事がなかなか決まらなかった。: It took a long time to find the next job.
日本一周の途中で立ち寄った港町が気に入り、そこで漁師の見習いになった。: Fell in love with a port town I stopped at during the trip around Japan, and became an apprentice fisherman there.
