満了金で中古車を買って友達と始めた便利屋が、3年で月商80万円になった。: Bought a used car with the bonus and started an odd-jobs service with a friend. Within three years it was making 800,000 yen a month.
現場をまとめる立場になった。手当が月2万円。: Became the one who keeps the floor together. The allowance was 20,000 yen a month.
上と下の板挟みで胃が痛い毎日になった。: Caught between those above and below, my stomach hurt every day.
班長として作った手順書が全工場で採用され、課長への昇進が決まった。: The procedure manual I wrote as team leader was adopted at every plant, and I was promoted to section manager.
班のメンバーと毎年行くキャンプが恒例になり、10年続いた。: The yearly camping trip with the team became a tradition and lasted ten years.
作業に集中し、定時で帰れる日々を続けた。: Focused on the work and kept going home on time.
後輩が先に班長になり、指示を受ける立場になった。: A junior became team leader before me, and I ended up taking his orders.
定時で帰って始めたプラモデル作りがはまり、全国コンテストで入賞した。: Took up model-building after getting home on time, got hooked, and placed in a national contest.
班長を断ったことで上司の評価が下がり、昇給が3年止まった。: Turning down the team leader post lowered my boss's opinion of me, and raises stopped for three years.
施設警備の隊長への昇格を打診された。: Was asked to become captain of the facility security team.
シフト管理と報告書に追われるようになった。給料は月3万円上がった。: Got buried in shift scheduling and reports. Pay rose by 30,000 yen a month.
隊員が次々に辞め、自分が穴を埋め続けた。: Team members quit one after another, and I kept filling the gaps myself.
隊長として防災訓練を取り仕切り、施設が消防署から優良表彰を受けた。: As captain I ran the disaster drills, and the facility received a commendation from the fire department.
隊長になって半年で、施設が閉鎖され契約が終わった。: Six months after becoming captain, the facility closed and the contract ended.
代わりに隊長になった後輩が、シフトで気を遣ってくれた。: The junior who became captain in my place was considerate with my shifts.
現場で落とし物を届け続けたら、施設のテナント店長から仕事を紹介され、転職した。: After diligently returning lost items on the job, a tenant store manager at the facility offered me a job, and I changed careers.
夜勤の巡回中に見つけた漏水を報告し、被害を防いだ。施設から金一封3万円をもらった: Reported a water leak found on a night patrol and prevented damage. The facility gave me a 30,000 yen cash award.
イベント警備で、明らかに危険な混雑が起きている。主催者は入場を止めない。: At an event I'm guarding, the crowd is clearly dangerous. The organizer won't stop admissions.
独断で入場を止める: Stop admissions on my own call
事故は起きなかった。後日、主催者から感謝状が届いた。: No accident occurred. Later, the organizer sent a letter of thanks.
主催者に怒られ、契約を切られた。: The organizer got angry and terminated the contract.
入場を止めた判断がニュースで報じられ、業界の安全マニュアルに採用された。: The decision to stop admissions was reported in the news and adopted into the industry's safety manual.
主催者から損害賠償を請求されかけたが、警備会社の社長が全部かばってくれた。: The organizer nearly demanded damages, but the security company's president shielded me from everything.
なんとか事故なく終わった。: Somehow it ended without an accident.
将棋倒しが起き、けが人が出た。ずっと夢に出る。: A crowd crush happened and people were injured. It haunts my dreams.
混雑が収まったあと、迷子になった5歳の子を2時間かけて親のもとに届けた。: After the crowd settled, I spent two hours taking a lost five-year-old back to the parents.
指示に従ったことを後から悔い、翌年から防災士の資格を取った。: Regretted following orders afterward, and the next year went on to earn a disaster-prevention specialist qualification.
独立して自分のサロンを持つか迷っている。: Torn between going independent and opening my own salon.
常連さんがついてきてくれて、3年で2店舗目を出した。: My regulars followed me, and I opened a second salon in three years.
内装に1200万円かけたが客が定着せず、苦しい経営が続いた。: Spent 12 million yen on the interior, but customers didn't stick, and business stayed tough.
開業2年目、店のインスタが2万フォロワーを超え、予約が半年先まで埋まった。: In the second year, the salon's Instagram passed 20,000 followers and appointments were booked six months out.
開業したら毎月の家賃と人件費で手元に残るのは10万円だった。3年後に閉店した。: After opening, rent and labor costs left me with just 100,000 yen a month. Closed after three years.
売上の6割が手元に残るようになり、自由に働けた。: Kept 60% of sales and could work freely.
集客を全部自分でやる大変さを知った。: Learned how hard it is to find every customer on your own.
面貸しで出会った別の美容師と、5年後に共同でサロンを開いた。: Five years later, opened a salon together with another stylist I met while renting a chair.
フリーになった途端、常連客が引っ越しで3人減った。月の売上が半分になった。: The moment I went freelance, three regulars moved away. Monthly sales were cut in half.
お客さんが、明らかに似合わない髪型を強く希望している。: A customer is insisting on a hairstyle that clearly won't suit them.
正直に止める: Honestly talk them out of it
別の提案を気に入ってくれ、ずっと通ってくれるようになった。: They liked my alternative suggestion and became a long-time regular.
機嫌を損ねて、二度と来なかった。: They took offense and never came back.
そのお客さんが結婚式の髪型も任せてくれ、式で新郎のご両親にも気に入られた。: That customer also entrusted me with their wedding hairstyle, and the groom's parents liked it too at the ceremony.
正直に止めたのがSNSで評判になり、「本音で言ってくれる美容師」として新規客が月: Talking them out of it honestly got buzz on social media, and as “the stylist who tells it straight,” I gained 20 new customers a month.
口コミに「下手」と書かれた。: A review called me “bad at this.”
希望の髪型がSNSでバズり、真似したい客が月30人来た。: The requested hairstyle went viral on social media, and 30 customers a month came wanting to copy it.
本人は大満足だったが、翌日その人の家族が店に来て「どうしてこうした」と1時間責め: They were thrilled, but the next day their family came to the salon and scolded me for an hour: “Why did you do this?”
大手企業から、会社を買収したいという話が来た。: A major corporation offered to acquire the company.
3億円で売却した。しばらく何をしていいかわからなかった。: Sold for 300 million yen. For a while I didn't know what to do with myself.
売却後、社員が大量に辞めたと聞いて胸が痛んだ。: After the sale, I heard that many employees had quit, and it hurt.
売却益で始めたエンジェル投資の1社が上場し、さらに5億円が入った。: One of the companies I backed as an angel investor with the sale proceeds went public, bringing in another 500 million yen.
売却した会社の元社員たちが、自分を慕って新会社を一緒に立ち上げてくれた。: Former employees of the company I sold looked up to me and joined me in founding a new one.
自分で続けて10年、会社が業界2位になった。: Ten years of running it myself, and the company became number two in the industry.
続けたが、働きすぎで倒れ、半年社長業から離れた。復帰したら会社が自分抜きで回って: Kept going, but overwork made me collapse and I stepped away from the presidency for six months. When I returned, the company was running fine without me.
資金ショート寸前。個人保証で追加融資を受けるか迫られた。: On the verge of running out of cash. Pressed to take additional financing backed by a personal guarantee.
なんとか持ち直し、5年で借金を返した。: Somehow recovered and paid off the debt in five years.
結局会社は倒産し、自宅を手放した。: In the end the company went bankrupt and I lost my home.
借金を返し終えた日、社員全員で焼肉を食べに行った。会計は32万円だった。: The day I finished paying off the debt, the whole staff went out for yakiniku. The bill was 320,000 yen.
個人保証で資金をつないだが、2年後に結局また資金ショートした。: Bridged the funding gap with a personal guarantee, but two years later ran short of cash again.
社員一人ひとりの再就職先を探して、会社を閉じた。: Found a new job for each employee, then closed the company.
数年後、元社員たちが集まって「また一緒にやりましょう」と言ってくれた。: Years later, former employees gathered and said, “Let's work together again.”
会社をたたんだ経験を本に書いたら、経営者向けに3万部売れた。: Wrote a book about closing a company, and it sold 30,000 copies to business owners.
会社をたたんだあと、1年間何もできなかった。: After closing the company, I couldn't do anything for a year.
バイト先から正社員登用の話が来た。: My part-time workplace offered me a full-time position.
ボーナスと社会保険がついた。親が安心した。: Got a bonus and social insurance. My parents felt relieved.
責任が増えたのに、給料はあまり変わらなかった。: Responsibilities grew, but the pay barely changed.
正社員になって3年後、店舗の運営を任され、年収が450万円になった。: Three years after becoming full-time, I was put in charge of running the store, and my annual income reached 4.5 million yen.
正社員になった途端、会社が業績不振で給料を1割カットした。: Right after I became full-time, the company's results slumped and it cut salaries by 10%.
夢のために使う時間を守った。: Protected the time I spend on my dream.
30代になり、選べる仕事が減っていった。: Entering my 30s, the jobs I could choose from kept shrinking.
自由な時間で続けたバンドがCMソングに採用され、30万円の使用料が入った。: The band I kept going in my free time had a song picked for a commercial, earning a 300,000 yen licensing fee.
同じバイト先で30年働いた。社員より店のことを知っていた。: Worked at the same part-time job for 30 years. Knew the store better than the staff did.
友達から「一緒にキッチンカーやらない？」と誘われた。: A friend asked, “Want to run a food truck together?”
イベント出店で人気になり、月収40万円になった。: Became popular at event stalls and reached a monthly income of 400,000 yen.
半年で友達と揉めて解散した。: Fell out with my friend within six months and we split up.
キッチンカーがテレビで紹介され、3台に増えた。: The food truck was featured on TV and grew to three trucks.
キッチンカーの車検代と修理費で、1年目の利益が全部消えた。: Vehicle inspection and repair costs for the food truck wiped out all of the first year's profit.
いつものバイト生活を続けた。: Kept up the usual part-time life.
友達のキッチンカーが繁盛しているのを、SNSで見た。: Saw on social media that my friend's food truck was thriving.
断ったが、その友達が繁盛店のノウハウを本にまとめ、自分の名前を謝辞に入れてくれた: I declined, but that friend compiled the know-how of a thriving business into a book and put my name in the acknowledgments.
誘ってきた友達がキッチンカーで失敗し、借金を抱えた。相談されて50万円貸した。: The friend who invited me failed with the food truck and fell into debt. When asked for help, I lent 500,000 yen.
太客から「店を辞めて一緒に暮らそう」と言われた。: A big-spending customer said, “Quit the club and live with me.”
関係はこじれたが、仕事は続けられた。: The relationship soured, but I was able to keep working.
しつこく付きまとわれ、店に相談して出禁にしてもらった。: Was persistently stalked, so I consulted the club and had them banned.
断ったあと、その太客が他の店で同じことを言っていたと知った。: After I refused, I learned that the same customer was saying the same thing at other clubs.
断った太客が、5年後に会社の経営を成功させ、自分の店の開店祝いに100万円分の花: The big spender I turned down became a successful business owner five years later and sent 1 million yen worth of flowers for my shop's opening.
思ったより穏やかな暮らしになった。: Life turned out more peaceful than expected.
半年で別れて、行くあてもなく店に戻った。: Broke up within six months and, with nowhere else to go, went back to the club.
一緒に暮らし始めたら、相手が料理が下手で、毎日自分が作ることになった。2年後に結: After we started living together, my partner turned out to be a bad cook, so I ended up cooking every day. We married two years later.
同居を始めたが、相手の借金が800万円あると発覚した。: We started living together, then it came out that my partner had 8 million yen in debt.
資格を取って事務職に就いた。給料は激減したが夜眠れるようになった。: Earned a qualification and took an office job. Pay dropped sharply, but I could sleep at night.
昼の職場になじめず、半年で夜に戻った。: Couldn't fit in at the daytime workplace and went back to nights within six months.
昼の仕事で知り合った同僚と、お金の勉強会を始めた。参加者が月50人になった。: Started a money study group with a coworker I met at the daytime job. Attendance reached 50 people a month.
資格を取って経理に入ったら、夜の世界より人間関係が複雑で、3年で2回転職した。: Got a qualification and joined accounting, where relationships were more complicated than in the night world. Changed jobs twice in three years.
女の子が集まらず、1年で閉店した。: Couldn't gather any hostesses, and closed after a year.
自分の店が人気になり、3年で2店舗目を出した。: My place became popular, and I opened a second one in three years.
店を出したが、ママ業は思ったより地味な仕事で、毎晩の帳簿付けに追われた。: I opened the place, but being a mama was more mundane than expected, and I was chased by bookkeeping every night.
ナンバー1のお客さんが、売掛を払えなくなった。: My number one customer could no longer pay their tab.
お客さんは少しずつ返してくれた。: The customer paid it back little by little.
連絡が取れなくなり、200万円が残った。: Lost contact, and 2 million yen was left unpaid.
立て替えたお客さんが、5年後に会社を立ち上げ、店の常連として戻ってきた。: The customer whose tab I covered started a company five years later and came back as a regular.
立て替えた200万円が戻らず、ローンを組んで返した。: The 2 million yen I covered never came back, and I took out a loan to pay it off.
売上は下がったが、気持ちが楽になった。: Sales dropped, but I felt lighter.
店長に「甘い」と言われ、居づらくなった。: The manager called me “naive,” and it became uncomfortable to stay.
売掛をやめたことが店内で評判になり、他のホストも追随した。店の売上はかえって伸び: Dropping tabs became the talk of the club, and the other hosts followed. Sales actually grew.
売掛をやめたら、その噂がSNSで広がり、新規のお客さんが月20人増えた。: After I dropped tabs, the word spread on social media, and new customers rose by 20 a month.
肝臓の数値が悪いと健康診断で言われた。: My health checkup said my liver numbers were bad.
営業の経験を活かし、不動産会社で売れっ子になった。: Made use of my sales experience and became a top performer at a real estate company.
昼の世界の給料の低さに驚いた。: Was shocked at how low daytime pay was.
引退後、トーク力を活かして婚活イベントの司会を始め、月50万円稼げるようになった: After retiring, I used my conversation skills to start emceeing matchmaking events, earning 500,000 yen a month.
引退後に始めた居酒屋が、元客と元同僚で毎晩満席になった。: The izakaya I opened after retiring filled up every night with former customers and former colleagues.
ノンアル営業を始めた。意外と指名が増えた。: Started working alcohol-free. Surprisingly, requests for me went up.
数値がさらに悪化して入院した。: The numbers got even worse and I was hospitalized.
ノンアル営業のノウハウを本にしたら、1万部売れた。: Turned my alcohol-free hosting know-how into a book, and it sold 10,000 copies.
飲み続けた結果、40歳で肝硬変の手前と言われた。: After years of drinking, at 40 I was told I was on the verge of cirrhosis.
組を抜けたい。だが簡単にはいかない。: I want out of the gang. But it's not easy.
支援団体の助けで離脱した。5年後、ようやく自分名義の口座が作れた。: Got out with help from a support organization. Five years later, I could finally open a bank account in my own name.
離脱したが、仕事が見つからず生活に苦しんだ。: Got out, but couldn't find work and struggled to get by.
離脱した経験を講演で話すようになり、全国の少年院から年30回呼ばれた。: Began talking about my experience of leaving in lectures, and was invited to juvenile training schools across the country 30 times a year.
離脱後に働いた配送会社で、10年後に配車主任になった。: At the delivery company I worked for after leaving, I became dispatch supervisor ten years later.
組の中で地位が上がった。だが居場所は狭まっていく。: Rose in rank within the gang. But my place to belong kept shrinking.
抗争に巻き込まれて重傷を負った。: Got caught up in a gang war and was seriously injured.
組長が引退し、組が穏やかに解散した。みんなで最後に焼肉を食べた。: The boss retired and the gang disbanded peacefully. We all had one last yakiniku meal together.
組の中で事務方になり、帳簿をつけていたら、警察に押収された。: Became the gang's paperwork guy, and the ledgers I kept were seized by the police.
上から、危ない仕事の「身代わり」を頼まれた。: Those above asked me to be the “fall guy” for a risky job.
指を詰めさせられた。: Was made to cut off a finger.
断ったあと組を抜け、地方の工場で働き始めた。同僚に過去を話したら、黙って弁当を分: After refusing, I left the gang and started working at a factory in the countryside. When I told a coworker about my past, he silently shared his lunch with me.
断った自分の代わりに後輩が身代わりになった。ずっと引っかかった。: A junior became the fall guy in place of me after I refused. It weighed on me for good.
刑務所で4年過ごした。出所の日、迎えに来たのは組の人間だけだった。: Spent four years in prison. The day I was released, the only ones who came to meet me were gang members.
出所したら組は解散していた。迎えはなかった。: When I got out, the gang had disbanded. No one came to meet me.
刑務所で調理師免許を取った。出所後、定食屋を開いて15年続いた。: Earned a cook's license in prison. After release, opened a diner that lasted 15 years.
服役中、手紙をくれたのは小学校の時の担任だけだった。出所後に会いに行った。: While serving time, the only person who wrote to me was my elementary school homeroom teacher. After release, I went to see them.
グループの人気が落ち、卒業を考えている。: The group's popularity has slipped, and I'm thinking about graduating.
女優に転身して、ドラマの脇役が決まった。: Switched to acting and landed a supporting role in a drama.
芸能界を離れ、普通の会社員になった。: Left show business and became an ordinary office worker.
卒業後、地元の観光大使になり、町のイベントの司会を年40回するようになった。: After graduating, became a local tourism ambassador and emceed town events 40 times a year.
卒業ライブのチケットが500枚しか売れなかった。最後のMCで泣いた。: Only 500 tickets sold for the graduation concert. I cried during the final MC.
楽曲がバズって、武道館公演が決まった。: A song went viral and a Budokan concert was set.
グループは2年後に解散した。: The group disbanded two years later.
グループに残って10年、最後の1人として冠番組が始まった。: Ten years after staying, as the last remaining member I got my own TV show.
グループに残ったが、メンバーが次々卒業し、自分が最年長になった。: Stayed with the group, but members graduated one after another and I became the oldest.
ソロデビューの話が来た。だがメンバーとの関係が悪くなりそうだ。: An offer for a solo debut came. But it might sour things with the other members.
ソロ曲がヒットした。: My solo song became a hit.
売れずに、グループにも戻れなかった。: It didn't sell, and I couldn't go back to the group either.
ソロ曲がドラマ主題歌になり、紅白歌合戦に出場した。: My solo song became a drama theme, and I appeared on Kohaku Uta Gassen.
ソロデビューしたが、メンバーが応援コメントをくれた。関係は悪くならなかった。: Made my solo debut, and the members gave messages of support. Our relationship didn't sour.
メンバーと一緒に、もう一度上を目指すことにした。: Decided to aim high once more together with the members.
グループが解散し、ソロの話は二度と来なかった。: The group disbanded, and no solo offer ever came again.
断ったら、メンバーの1人が泣いて「ありがとう」と言った。翌年ドームライブが決まっ: When I declined, one of the members cried and said, “Thank you.” The next year, a dome concert was set.
断ったが、メンバーの一人が裏でソロの話を受けていた。: I declined, but one of the members had secretly accepted a solo offer.
相方から「解散したい」と言われた。: My comedy partner told me, “I want to break up the duo.”
説得する: Try to talk them out of it
続けた。翌年、賞レースで準決勝に進んだ。: We kept going. The next year, we reached the semifinals of a comedy competition.
説得できず、解散した。: Couldn't persuade them, and we broke up.
説得して続けたコンビで、10年目に賞レースで優勝した。賞金1000万円だった。: The duo I persuaded to continue won a comedy competition in its tenth year. The prize was 10 million yen.
説得で相方が残ったが、ネタ合わせのたびに喧嘩した。: My partner stayed after I persuaded them, but we fought every time we rehearsed our routines.
ピン芸人としてネタ番組で注目された。: Gained attention on comedy shows as a solo comedian.
芸人を引退し、放送作家になった。: Retired from comedy and became a TV writer.
解散後、元相方がYouTubeで売れ、自分を何度もゲストに呼んでくれた。: After the breakup, my former partner made it big on YouTube and invited me as a guest many times.
解散したら、元相方がすぐに別の人と組んで、テレビに出始めた。: After the breakup, my former partner quickly teamed up with someone else and started appearing on TV.
YouTubeを始めるか、劇場一本でいくか。: Start YouTube, or stick to the theater alone?
企画動画がバズり、登録者が50万人を超えた。: A themed video went viral, and subscribers passed 500,000.
YouTubeで作った企画がテレビで番組化され、自分が司会になった。: A concept I created on YouTube was turned into a TV show, and I became the host.
YouTubeで炎上し、劇場の出番も一時的に減らされた。: Got caught in an online firestorm on YouTube, and my theater slots were temporarily cut.
劇場で磨く: Hone my act at the theater
劇場での評判が上がり、テレビに呼ばれた。: My reputation at the theater grew, and I got called to TV.
何も変わらないまま3年が過ぎた。: Three years passed with nothing changing.
劇場で磨いたネタが賞レースで決勝に進み、翌月からテレビ出演が週5本になった。: The routine I honed at the theater reached the finals of a comedy competition, and from the next month I was on TV five times a week.
劇場の楽屋でできた後輩たちが売れ、自分を番組に呼んでくれるようになった。: The juniors I got to know in the theater dressing room made it big and began inviting me onto their shows.
ドラマの大きな役が決まりかけたが、事務所を移籍しないといけない。: A big drama role was nearly mine, but I'd have to switch agencies.
その役がハマり、翌年は主演が決まった。: The role suited me perfectly, and the next year I was cast as the lead.
役は別の人に決まり、前の事務所とも気まずくなった。: The role went to someone else, and things got awkward with my old agency too.
移籍先の社長と気が合い、10年後には自分が事務所の副社長になった。: Hit it off with the new agency's president, and ten years later I became the agency's vice president.
移籍したら、新事務所でマネージャーが半年で3回変わった。: After switching, my manager at the new agency changed three times in six months.
社長が「恩は忘れない」と言い、次の舞台の主役を回してくれた。: The president said, “I won't forget what you've done,” and gave me the lead in the next stage play.
事務所が経営難で倒産した。: The agency fell into financial trouble and went bankrupt.
残った事務所で、後輩の俳優が育ち、自分が演技指導を頼まれた。: At the agency I stayed with, junior actors grew up, and I was asked to coach acting.
残ったことで社長と信頼関係ができ、10年後に事務所を継いだ。: Staying built trust with the president, and ten years later I took over the agency.
映画のために体重を15kg落とす役が来た。: Got offered a role that required losing 15 kg for a film.
体当たりの演技が評価され、映画賞の新人賞を取った。: My all-out performance was praised, and I won a newcomer award at a film festival.
撮影後に体調を崩して、3か月寝込んだ。: Fell ill after filming and was bedridden for three months.
減量が話題になり、ダイエット本の出版依頼が来た。5万部売れた。: The weight loss became a talking point, and I was asked to publish a diet book. It sold 50,000 copies.
撮影は無事終わったが、リバウンドで体重が20kg増えた。: Filming wrapped up safely, but I rebounded and gained 20 kg.
その映画は大ヒットし、役を受けた俳優はブレイクした。: The film was a huge hit, and the actor who took the role broke out.
断った役の代わりに受けた舞台が、思わぬロングランになった。: The stage play I took instead of the role I turned down unexpectedly became a long run.
断った分、空いた時間で始めた料理配信が話題になり、レシピ本が出た。: With the time freed up by declining, I started cooking streams that caught on, and a recipe book came out.
週刊誌に、事実と違う記事を書かれそうだ。: A weekly tabloid looks set to run an article that gets the facts wrong.
ファンが味方してくれて、好感度が上がった。: Fans took my side, and my likability went up.
反論が火に油を注ぎ、CMを2本降ろされた。: My rebuttal added fuel to the fire, and I was dropped from two commercials.
SNSの反論がきっかけで、名誉毀損の訴訟を起こし、勝訴して300万円の賠償を得た: My social media rebuttal led me to file a defamation suit, which I won, receiving 3 million yen in damages.
反論に疲れてSNSを1年休んだら、ファンが逆に増えた。: Worn out from the rebuttals, I took a year off social media, and my fans actually increased.
事務所に任せて沈黙: Leave it to the agency and stay silent
騒ぎは1か月で収まった。: The uproar died down in a month.
沈黙が「認めた」と取られた。: My silence was taken as an admission.
沈黙していたら、半年後に週刊誌が訂正記事を出した。: I stayed silent, and six months later the tabloid ran a correction.
沈黙のあと、事務所のスタッフが辞め、マネージャーがいなくなった。: After the silence, agency staff quit and I was left without a manager.
独立して個人事務所を作るか迷っている。: Torn between going independent and setting up my own agency.
YouTubeと自分の企画で、収入が3倍になった。: With YouTube and my own projects, my income tripled.
テレビの仕事がほぼなくなった。: TV work almost completely dried up.
独立後、自分のYouTubeで始めた料理企画が書籍化され、10万部売れた。: After going independent, a cooking series I started on my own YouTube became a book and sold 100,000 copies.
独立1年目に税金の計算を間違え、追徴課税で800万円払った。: In my first year of independence I miscalculated my taxes and paid 8 million yen in back taxes.
事務所の方針で仕事を絞られ、レギュラーが1本になった。: The agency narrowed my work down, leaving me with one regular show.
事務所に残って10年、後輩タレントのブレイクを支える立場になった。: Ten years after staying at the agency, I became the one supporting a junior talent's breakout.
事務所の社長が代替わりし、新社長と方針が合わず、結局独立した。: The agency's president changed, and I clashed with the new one and ended up going independent.
大企業の不正を示す内部資料を入手した。上層部は掲載に慎重だ。: Got hold of internal documents exposing a major corporation's wrongdoing. The top brass is wary of running the story.
記事が大反響を呼び、社長が辞任した。新聞協会賞を取った。: The article caused a huge stir and the company president resigned. Won the Japan Newspaper Association Award.
訴訟を起こされ、2年間法廷に通った。: Got sued and spent two years going to court.
報道後、他の記者から「よくやった」と連絡が100通来た。: After the story ran, 100 messages from other reporters came in saying “Well done.”
掲載後、取材源が特定されてしまい、取材源が会社をクビになった。ずっと後悔した。: After publication, my source was identified and fired from the company. I regretted it for years.
記事はボツになった。他社が半年後に報じた。: The article was killed. A rival outlet ran it six months later.
その判断が正しかった。資料は偽造だった。: The call turned out to be right. The documents were forged.
ボツになった記事を、10年後に書籍として出版した。ベストセラーになった。: Ten years later, I published the killed article as a book. It became a bestseller.
ボツの判断に納得できず、1年後に独立してフリーになった。: Unable to accept the decision to kill it, I went freelance a year later.
ネットメディアから、年収1.5倍で引き抜きの話が来た。: An online media outlet offered to poach me with 1.5 times my salary.
PV重視の記事に疲れたが、自由に企画できた。: Worn out by page-view-driven articles, but I could pitch freely.
1年でメディアが閉鎖された。: The outlet shut down within a year.
ネットメディアで作った連載がドラマ化された。: A series I created at the online outlet was adapted into a TV drama.
ネットメディアに移ったが、上司が元新聞社の先輩だった。: Moved to the online outlet, only to find my boss was a former senior colleague from the newspaper.
デスクになった。原稿を直す側になった。: Became a desk editor. Now I was the one fixing other people's copy.
部数減で支局が統合され、地方に飛ばされた。: Circulation fell, branch offices were merged, and I was sent off to the provinces.
デスクになって育てた若手記者が、新聞協会賞を取った。: A young reporter I trained as desk editor won the Japan Newspaper Association Award.

制作会社と組んで、配信向けの番組を作らないかと誘われた。: A production company invited me to team up and make a show for streaming.

再生は伸びず、社内で「テレビを裏切った」と言われた。: Views never took off, and people at the station said I had “betrayed TV.”

配信の制作会社に転職し、年収が1.5倍になった。: Switched to a streaming production company, and my salary rose 1.5 times.
局内での出世コースを順調に歩んだ。: Moved steadily along the promotion track inside the station.
担当番組が改編期にまとめて終わった。: All the shows I handled ended at once in the schedule overhaul.

地上波のバラエティ部長になったが、視聴率で毎週詰められた。: Became head of variety at the broadcaster, but was grilled over ratings every week.
出演者がロケで危険な目にあう企画を、上が押し通そうとしている。: The higher-ups are trying to force through a segment that puts the performers in danger on location.
企画が修正され、安全に収録できた。: The plan was revised and we shot it safely.
「空気が読めない」と言われ、番組を外された。: Told I “can't read the room,” I was taken off the show.
反対したことで出演者の事務所から信頼され、看板番組を任された。: Objecting earned the trust of the performers' agency, and I was put in charge of a flagship show.
反対したら、上から「お前がやれ」と言われ、自分がロケに出ることになった。: When I objected, my superior said “Then you do it,” and I ended up going out on the shoot myself.
放送は話題になった。: The broadcast became a talking point.
出演者がけがをして、BPOで問題になった。: A performer got injured, and it became an issue at the BPO (broadcasting ethics watchdog).
放送は話題になったが、自分は企画書を見るたびに胸が痛んだ。: The broadcast got people talking, but every time I saw the proposal, my chest ached.
企画が通って視聴率が18%を取り、局長賞で金一封10万円をもらった。: The plan went through and hit an 18% rating, earning a ¥100,000 cash award from the station head.
クライアント企業から、事業部長として引き抜きの話が来た。: A client company offered to hire me away as a division head.
現場を動かす面白さを知った。: Discovered the thrill of running things on the ground.
社内政治に疲れ、1年でコンサルに戻った。: Exhausted by office politics, I went back to consulting after a year.
事業会社で立ち上げた新規事業が年商50億円になり、取締役になった。: A new business I launched at the operating company hit ¥5 billion in annual sales, and I became a director.
事業会社の部下100人の名前を覚えられず、1年で全員の顔写真カードを作った。: Unable to remember the names of the 100 staff at the operating company, I made photo flash cards of everyone within a year.
パートナーに昇進した。年収3000万円になった。: Promoted to partner. Annual income reached ¥30 million.
昇進できず、ずっとマネージャー止まりだった。: Never got promoted and stayed stuck at manager.
コンサルのパートナーとして、10年で売上300億円の部署を作った。: As a consulting partner, built a division with ¥30 billion in sales over ten years.
コンサルに残ったが、AIの導入で若手の仕事が半分になり、部署が縮小された。: Stayed in consulting, but AI adoption halved the junior staff's work and the division shrank.
クライアントの経営陣が、どう見ても無理な戦略を推している。: The client's management is pushing a strategy that is plainly unworkable.
契約を切られ、社内で詰められた。: The contract was terminated, and I got grilled internally.
反対意見を通したら、5年後に業界で「止めたコンサル」と評判になり、指名が年10件: My objection won out, and five years later I was known in the industry as “the consultant who stopped it,” getting 10 requests by name a year.
反対したが、社長が戦略を強行し、2年後に事業撤退。自分は「止められなかった」と言: I objected, but the president forced the strategy through and the business pulled out two years later. I was told I “failed to stop it.”
意向に沿ってまとめる: Compile it to match their wishes
戦略が失敗し、自分の名前も業界で汚れた。: The strategy failed, and my name was tarnished in the industry too.
戦略は失敗したが、その後の再建の仕事で報酬が2倍になった。: The strategy failed, but the rebuilding work that followed paid me twice as much.
意向に沿ったまとめの資料が、思わぬ形で社長に気に入られ、3年の長期契約になった。: The report compiled to match his wishes unexpectedly won the president's favor, leading to a three-year contract.
リストラの噂がある。社外からヘッドハンターの電話が来た。: Rumors of layoffs are going around. A headhunter called from outside the company.
ヘッジファンドに移り、年収が倍になった。: Moved to a hedge fund, and my income doubled.
移った先のファンドが1年で解散した。: The fund I moved to was dissolved within a year.
ヘッジファンドで年収が5000万円を超えたが、睡眠が4時間になった。: My income at the hedge fund topped ¥50 million, but I was down to four hours of sleep.
転職先で同じヘッドハンターから2年後にまた電話が来た。: Two years after changing jobs, the same headhunter called me again.
リストラを免れて、マネージングディレクターに昇進した。: Escaped the layoffs and was promoted to managing director.
翌月、自分がリストラの対象になった。: The next month, I was on the layoff list.
リストラの波を乗り越え、10年後にアジア統括の責任者になった。: Weathered the waves of layoffs and, ten years later, became head of Asia operations.
残ったが、リストラで同僚が半分に減り、業務量が倍になった。: I stayed, but layoffs cut my colleagues in half and my workload doubled.
30代でFIREできるだけの資産ができた。: Built enough assets to FIRE (retire early) in my thirties.
沖縄に移住して、海の見える家で暮らし始めた。: Moved to Okinawa and started living in a house with an ocean view.
1年で暇に耐えられなくなった。: Within a year, I couldn't stand the idleness.
沖縄で始めたカフェが地元の人気店になった。: The cafe I opened in Okinawa became a local favorite.
FIREしたが、株価暴落で資産が4割減った。結局働きに戻った。: I FIREd, but a stock market crash cut my assets by 40%. In the end I went back to work.
数字を追う日々を続けた。: Kept on chasing numbers day after day.
40歳で心臓に不安が見つかり、医者に止められた。: At 40, a heart concern turned up and my doctor told me to stop.
続けた結果、40代でマネージングディレクターになった。年収が1億円を超えた。: By carrying on, I became a managing director in my forties. My income topped ¥100 million.
続けていたら、子どもに「パパはいつも電話してる」と言われた。: As I kept at it, my child said, “Dad is always on the phone.”
外資系コンサルから、年収2倍で転職の誘いが来た。: A foreign-owned consulting firm offered me a job at double the salary.
政策の知識を活かして活躍した。: Put my policy knowledge to good use and thrived.
「公のために」という感覚を失って、虚しさを感じた。: Lost the sense of working “for the public good” and felt empty.
コンサルで政策提言のプロジェクトを率いて、元の省庁と協働することになった。: Led a policy-proposal project at the consultancy and ended up working with my old ministry.
転職後、元の省庁の後輩から相談が毎月来るようになった。: After changing jobs, juniors from my old ministry started coming to me for advice every month.
課長に昇進し、大きな制度改正を担当した。: Promoted to section chief and put in charge of a major system reform.
心身をすり減らし、休職した。: Worn down in body and mind, I took leave.
課長として担当した制度改正が国会で可決され、記念に議場の写真を撮った。: The system reform I handled as section chief passed the Diet, and I took a commemorative photo of the chamber.
残ったが、10年後に局長になり、深夜の国会答弁作成が週3回になった。: I stayed, became a bureau director ten years later, and found myself drafting Diet answers late at night three times a week.
政治家から、筋の悪い要望をねじ込まれた。: A politician pushed an improper request on me.
次の人事で、地方に飛ばされた。: In the next personnel shuffle, I was sent off to the provinces.
押し返した記録が、後に政治家の不正を暴く証拠になった。: The record of my pushback later became evidence exposing the politician's misconduct.
押し返したら、上司ごと異動になった。上司とは今でも年に1回飲む。: After I pushed back, both my boss and I were transferred. We still go out for a drink once a year.
大きな問題にはならなかった。: It didn't become a big problem.
後に問題化し、国会で追及された。: It later blew up and I was questioned in the Diet.
受け入れた要望が後に大問題となり、自分の名前が国会の議事録に残った。: The request I accepted later became a major scandal, and my name ended up in the Diet minutes.
受け入れたが、政治家が次の選挙で落選し、要望自体がなくなった。: I accepted it, but the politician lost the next election and the request simply vanished.

会社が立ち直り、社長が「あなたのおかげ」と言った。: The company recovered, and the president said, “I owe it to you.”
会社が倒産し、貸し倒れの責任を問われた。: The company went bankrupt and I was held responsible for the bad loan.
立ち直った会社の社長が、銀行の退職後に顧問として迎えてくれた。: The president of the recovered company welcomed me as an advisor after I retired from the bank.
融資を続けた会社が業界の再編で大手に買収された。社長から高級日本酒が届いた。: The company I kept lending to was acquired by a major player in an industry reshuffle. The president sent me a bottle of premium sake.
会社は倒産した。融資部では評価された。: The company went under. The loan department thought well of me for it.
その社長が別の銀行から融資を受けて復活し、二度と口をきいてくれなかった。: That president got a loan from another bank, bounced back, and never spoke to me again.
貸し剥がした会社の社長が、10年後に地元の商工会議所会頭になった。: The president of the company I pulled the loan from became head of the local chamber of commerce ten years later.
貸し剥がした件で、本部から融資部長に昇進した。: For pulling that loan, headquarters promoted me to head of the loan department.
50歳を前に、関連会社への出向を打診された。: Approaching 50, I was asked about a secondment to an affiliate company.
給料は下がったが、定時で帰れるようになった。: My pay dropped, but I could leave on time.
出向先になじめなかった。: Couldn't fit in at the new workplace.
出向先で始めたシニア向けの資産相談が人気になり、本社に戻って担当役員になった。: The asset consultations for seniors I started at the affiliate became popular, and I returned to headquarters as the executive in charge.
出向先で趣味の囲碁仲間ができ、定年後も週1回集まっている。: Made Go-playing friends at the affiliate, and we still meet once a week after retirement.
地元の中小企業の財務部長になった。: Became finance director at a local small business.
なかなか転職先が見つからなかった。: Couldn't find a new job for a long time.
断って転職した会社が上場し、ストックオプションで3000万円を得た。: The company I joined after declining went public, and my stock options brought in ¥30 million.
転職先が見つからず、1年後に結局元の銀行の関連会社に入った。: Found no new job, and a year later ended up joining an affiliate of my old bank anyway.
アフリカの新規事業の立ち上げ責任者に指名された。: Named to lead the launch of a new business in Africa.
事業が軌道に乗り、帰国後に部長になった。: The business got on track, and I became a department head after returning to Japan.
アフリカの事業で現地の学校を建て、名誉村民の称号をもらった。: Through the African business, built a local school and was given the title of honorary villager.
マラリアにかかり、2か月入院した。: Caught malaria and was hospitalized for two months.
本社勤務を続けた。出世は少し遅れた。: Kept working at headquarters. My promotion came a little later.
同期がアフリカで成功して、先に部長になった。: A peer succeeded in Africa and became department head before me.
本社勤務で育てた部下が、アフリカ事業の責任者になって成功した。: A subordinate I trained at headquarters became head of the African business and succeeded.
本社勤務中にAI関連の新規事業を任され、子会社の社長になった。: While at headquarters, I was entrusted with a new AI-related business and became president of a subsidiary.

会社が上場して、大きなリターンを得た。: The company went public and I earned a large return.
資金繰りに苦しみ、ベンチャーの厳しさを学んだ。: Struggled with cash flow and learned how harsh the startup world is.

本社の部署が再編され、窓際に近い部署に回された。: My department at headquarters was reorganized and I was moved to a near-sidelined unit.
本社で投資部門の責任者になり、出資先の上場で社長賞をもらった。: Became head of the investment division at headquarters and received the President's Award when an investee went public.
窓際に近い部署で、趣味の盆栽が社内報に連載された。: In the near-sidelined unit, my bonsai hobby got its own column in the company newsletter.

競合に勝った。翌年、チームリーダーに昇進した。: Beat the competition. The next year, I was promoted to team leader.
負けた。帰りの電車で寝過ごし、終点の高尾まで行った。: Lost. On the train home I fell asleep and rode all the way to the terminus at Takao.
プレゼン中に寝落ちしかけたが、その様子が「本気度が伝わった」と評価され年間2億円: I nearly nodded off mid-pitch, but it was praised as showing how serious I was, and we landed a ¥200 million-a-year account.
3日目に倒れて点滴を打った。代わりに出た後輩が勝ち、翌年の昇進は後輩だった。: Collapsed on day three and was put on an IV drip. The junior who took my place won, and the next year's promotion went to that junior.
なぜかクライアントに刺さって勝った。誰にも言えない。: For some reason it resonated with the client and we won. I can't tell anyone.

お酒を水に替えて乗り切った。: Swapped their drink for water and got through it.

なだめている間に別の乗客の具合が悪くなり、2人同時対応で足がつった。: While I was calming them, another passenger fell ill; handling both at once gave me a leg cramp.

控えめな予報が的中し続け、「当たる気象予報士」としてバラエティ番組に呼ばれた。: My low-key forecasts kept coming true, and I was invited onto variety shows as “the weather forecaster who gets it right.”
控えめに伝えた日、自分の家の床下が浸水した。: On the very day I kept the message low-key, the crawl space under my own house flooded.

顔が出なくなり、少し寂しさを感じた。: My face no longer appeared on screen, and I felt a little lonely.
予報モデルを改良し、スーパーの食品ロスを年1億円削減して社長賞を取った。: Improved the forecast model, cut supermarkets’ food waste by 100 million yen a year, and won the President’s Award.
転職先がテレビ局と提携し、結局ほぼ毎日画面に出ることになった。: My new company partnered with a TV station, and I ended up on screen almost every day anyway.
お天気キャスターとして全国放送の枠をもらった。: Got a nationwide broadcast slot as a weather presenter.
番組改編で担当枠がなくなった。: My slot disappeared in a programming overhaul.

生放送中に雹が降り始め、中継先で傘ごと飛ばされる映像が年末特番で使われ続けた。: Hail started falling during a live broadcast, and the footage of me being blown away along with my umbrella at the remote site kept getting replayed in year-end specials.

おはなし会に毎回30人が集まり、地域紙に載った。: Thirty people came to every storytelling session, and it was featured in the local paper.

給料が上がり、ボーナスも出るようになった。: My pay went up, and I started getting bonuses too.

採用され、選手の体重管理を任された。チームが優勝した。: Got hired and was put in charge of the players’ weight management. The team won the championship.

状況が悪化し、早く動けばよかったと悔やんだ。: The situation got worse, and I regretted not acting sooner.

営業職が合わず、結局福祉の世界に戻った。: Sales didn’t suit me, and I ended up back in the welfare field.

燃え尽きそうになり、1か月休職した。: Nearly burned out and took a month of leave.

整体院を開業しないかと、先輩に誘われた。: A senior colleague invited me to open a chiropractic clinic together.
口コミで予約が埋まり、病院勤務時代の倍稼いだ。: Word of mouth filled the appointment book, and I earned double what I did at the hospital.
集客に苦戦し、1年で店を閉めた。: Struggled to attract customers and closed the clinic within a year.
プロスポーツチームのトレーナー契約が取れ、選手が店の常連になった。: Landed a trainer contract with a pro sports team, and the players became regulars at the clinic.
先輩と経営方針で揉め、共同経営を解消。看板は先輩に残った。: Clashed with my senior over management policy and dissolved the partnership. The clinic’s name stayed with the senior.
リハビリ科の主任になった。: Became head of the rehabilitation department.
後輩の指導に追われ、患者さんと向き合う時間が減った。: Swamped with mentoring juniors, I had less time to face patients.
開発した歩行訓練の方法が学会で賞を取り、全国から見学が来た。: The gait training method I developed won an award at an academic conference, and visitors came from all over the country.
院内の運動会で無双し、「本気出しすぎ」と言われた。: Dominated the hospital sports day and was told, “You’re trying way too hard.”
火災現場。逃げ遅れた人がいるとの情報があるが、建物は崩れかけている。: A fire scene. There are reports of someone trapped inside, but the building is about to collapse.
子ども1人を救出した。表彰を受けた。: Rescued one child. Received a commendation.
天井が落ち、全治2か月のケガを負った。: The ceiling fell, and I suffered injuries that took two months to heal.
救出した子どもが18年後、消防士になって同じ署に配属されてきた。: Eighteen years later, the child I rescued became a firefighter and was assigned to the same station.
突入したところ、逃げ遅れていたのは飼い猫1匹だった。新聞に載り、感謝状が2枚届い: When I rushed in, the one left behind was a single pet cat. It made the newspaper, and I received two letters of appreciation.
中には誰もいなかったと後で分かった。: We later learned there was no one inside.
救助は間に合わなかった。長い間その現場を夢に見た。: The rescue came too late. For a long time I dreamed of that scene.
隊長の判断が正しかったとわかり、3年後、自分が隊長として同じ判断をした。: Realized the captain's call had been right. Three years later, as captain myself, I made the same call.
後日、救助された別の隊員から「待ってくれて助かった」と言われた。退路が崩れる寸前: Later, another rescued crew member told me, “Thank you for waiting.” The way out had been about to collapse.
救急救命士の資格を取るよう、上司に勧められた。: My boss urged me to get the emergency medical technician license.
救急隊長になり、多くの命をつないだ。: Became an ambulance team captain and saved many lives.
救急出動の多さに疲弊した。: Worn out by the sheer number of ambulance calls.
自分が救命した男性が、1年後に元気な姿で娘の結婚式の写真を送ってきた。: A man I had saved sent me photos from his daughter's wedding a year later, healthy and well.
資格取得の勉強中、自宅で倒れた父を自分で処置し、命をつないだ。: While studying for the license, I treated my father when he collapsed at home and kept him alive.
特別救助隊（レスキュー）に選抜された。: Selected for the Special Rescue Team.
年齢とともに体力が落ち、現場の第一線から外れた。: My strength faded with age, and I was taken off the front lines.
全国消防救助技術大会で優勝し、署の壁に写真が飾られた。: Won the National Fire Rescue Skills Competition, and my photo went up on the station wall.
退職後、地元の自主防災組織の会長になり、毎月の訓練に100人集まった。: After retiring, became head of the local volunteer disaster-prevention group; 100 people turned up to the monthly drills.
職務質問をした若者が、家庭の事情で家に帰れないと言っている。規則上は保護者に連絡: A young person I stopped for questioning says they can't go home because of family problems. By the rules, I should contact their guardian.
虐待の事実が判明し、その子は保護された。後日手紙が届いた。: Abuse was confirmed and the child was taken into protection. A letter arrived later.
本人が拒否して逃げ出し、行方が分からなくなった。: They refused, ran off, and disappeared.
15年後、その若者から「警察官になりました」と連絡があった。: Fifteen years later, that young person got in touch: “I became a police officer.”
規則違反として始末書を書かされたが、署長は個人的に缶コーヒーをくれた。: I was made to write a letter of apology for breaking the rules, but the station chief privately handed me a can of coffee.
規則通り保護者に連絡する: Contact the guardian as per the rules
親が迎えに来て、何事もなく帰っていった。: The parent came to pick them up, and they went home without incident.
数か月後、その子が再び補導されてきた。: A few months later, the same kid was brought in again.
保護者は涙ながらに感謝し、親子関係のカウンセリングに通い始めたと聞いた。: The guardian thanked me in tears, and I heard they started parent-child counseling.
規則通りに対応したことを、後で本人から「あの時は本気で恨んだ」と言われた。: Later the kid told me, “I really hated you back then” for going by the rules.
刑事課への異動の打診が来た。花形だが激務だ。: Offered a transfer to the Criminal Investigation Division. Glamorous, but brutal hours.
大きな事件の捜査本部に入り、犯人逮捕に貢献した。: Joined the task force on a major case and helped arrest the culprit.
捜査本部で1か月家に帰れず、家族との関係が冷えた。: Stuck at the task force for a month without going home; things cooled with my family.
未解決の詐欺事件を解決し、警視総監賞を受けた。: Solved a cold fraud case and received the Superintendent General's Award.
刑事になったが、張り込みの退屈さに耐えきれず、2年で地域課に戻った。: Became a detective, but couldn't stand the boredom of stakeouts and went back to the Community Affairs Division after two years.
地元に顔見知りが増え、町の人に頼られた。: Got to know more people in the neighborhood, and the townsfolk relied on me.
同期が出世していき、少し焦った。: My peers kept getting promoted, and I felt a little anxious.
交番の前で毎朝あいさつしていた小学生が、20年後に自分の部下として赴任してきた。: A schoolkid I used to greet every morning in front of the police box was posted to my unit as my subordinate twenty years later.
迷子の犬を年間40匹保護し、地元で「犬のお巡りさん」と呼ばれた。: Took in 40 lost dogs in a year and became known locally as “the dog cop.”
任期制の満了が近い。継続するか、民間に出るか決めなければならない。: My fixed-term enlistment is nearly up. I have to decide whether to continue or go civilian.
陸曹に昇任し、部下を持つようになった。: Promoted to sergeant and got subordinates of my own.
体力の衰えを感じ、訓練がきつくなった。: Felt my strength declining; training got harder.
定年まで勤め上げ、退職金2000万円を受け取った。: Served until mandatory retirement and received a ¥20 million severance payment.
海外派遣部隊に選ばれ、半年間の任務を終えて帰国した。: Chosen for an overseas deployment, and came home after a six-month mission.
満了金を元手に、運送会社に就職した。: With the completion bonus as a nest egg, I got a job at a trucking company.
体力以外のアピールポイントがなく、就活に苦戦した。: With no selling point other than stamina, the job hunt was a struggle.
民間で立ち上げた防災用品の会社が自治体と契約を結んだ。: The disaster-supply company I started in the private sector signed a contract with a local government.
就職先で、体力を買われ社内運動会の全種目に駆り出された。: At my new job, they valued my stamina and drafted me into every event at the company sports day.
災害派遣中、上官の命令より目の前の救助を優先したい場面になった。: During a disaster relief deployment, I faced a moment when I wanted to put the rescue in front of me ahead of my superior's order.
部隊の安全が守られた。後で判断の正しさを知った。: The unit stayed safe. I later learned the decision was right.
その人を助けられなかったことが、ずっと胸に残った。: Not being able to save that person stayed with me for years.
命令に従った結果、その後の大規模救助を担い、200人を救出した。: Having followed orders, I took part in the large-scale rescue that followed and saved 200 people.
上官が後日、「あの場で俺も迷った」と打ち明けてくれた。関係が変わった。: My superior later confessed, “I was torn there too.” Our relationship changed.
目の前の人を助ける: Save the person in front of me
1人を救い出したが、上官に厳しく叱責された。: Got one person out, but was severely reprimanded by my superior.
二次災害に巻き込まれ、ケガをした。: Got caught in a secondary disaster and was injured.
救った人がのちに部隊を訪問し、全員にお礼の手紙を書いてくれた。: The person I saved later visited the unit and wrote thank-you letters to everyone.
命令違反の記録が残り、昇任が2年遅れた。: The record of disobeying orders stayed on file, and my promotion was delayed by two years.
運転中、遅延が3分出ている。次の駅でなんとか取り戻したい。: While driving, I'm running three minutes late. I'd like to make it up at the next station.
安全運転で遅延を受け入れる: Drive safely and accept the delay
指令所から問い合わせが来た。: The control center called with an inquiry.
遅延を受け入れた運転が「安全運行の模範」と社内報に載った。: My decision to accept the delay was featured in the company newsletter as “a model of safe operation.”
遅延の影響で乗客から苦情が10件来たが、全員に丁寧に謝った。: The delay brought 10 complaints from passengers, and I apologized politely to every one of them.
オーバーランをして、日勤教育を受けた。: Overran the platform and was sent to day-shift retraining.
遅延回復の記録が社内で話題になり、運転技術の講師に選ばれた。: My delay-recovery record became the talk of the company, and I was picked as a driving-skills instructor.
急ブレーキで乗客が転倒し、新聞に小さく載った。: A sudden brake made a passenger fall, and it made a small item in the newspaper.
鉄道会社の新幹線運転士への登用試験の話が来た。: The railway company offered me a chance to take the Shinkansen driver promotion exam.
合格し、時速300kmの世界に入った。: Passed and entered the world of 300 km/h.
不合格だった。来年また挑戦することにした。: Failed. Decided to try again next year.
新幹線運転士として、皇族の乗る臨時列車を担当した。: As a Shinkansen driver, I was put in charge of a special train carrying members of the Imperial Family.
試験は落ちたが、勉強仲間の後輩3人は全員合格し、結婚式に呼ばれた。: I failed the exam, but all three junior colleagues I studied with passed, and I was invited to their weddings.
指導運転士になり、後輩を育てた。: Became an instructor driver and trained juniors.
ワンマン化で仕事の負担が増えた。: Conversion to one-man operation increased my workload.
地元の鉄道ファンの間で有名になり、引退日にはホームに200人が集まった。: Became famous among local rail fans, and 200 people gathered on the platform on my retirement day.
路線が廃止になり、最後の列車を自分が運転した。: The line was discontinued, and I drove the last train.
天候が怪しいが、今日は大漁の予感がする。: The weather looks dicey, but I have a feeling about a big catch today.
大漁で、1日で50万円の売上になった。: A huge catch: ¥500,000 in sales in a single day.
時化に遭い、命からがら港に戻った。: Hit a storm and barely made it back to port alive.
一網で300万円分の本マグロが獲れた。港で語り継がれた。: One haul brought in ¥3 million worth of bluefin tuna. It became a legend at the harbor.
漁は空振り、燃料代8万円だけかかった。帰りにイルカの群れを見た。: Came up empty, and all I had to show for it was ¥80,000 in fuel costs. On the way back I saw a pod of dolphins.
結局海は荒れた。判断は正しかった。: The sea did turn rough. It was the right call.
翌日、仲間が大漁を自慢してきた。: The next day, a fellow fisherman bragged about his big catch.
港で待つ間に始めた魚料理のSNSがバズり、通販で月50万円売れるようになった。: The fish-recipe social media account I started while waiting at the harbor went viral, and mail-order sales reached ¥500,000 a month.
時化の日に網の修理をしていたら、隣の船の漁師と30年ぶりに和解した。: Mending nets on a stormy day, I made up with the fisherman on the next boat after thirty years.
若い漁師が減り、自分の船を継ぐ人がいない。: Young fishermen are disappearing, and no one is left to take over my boat.
都会から移住してきた若者が弟子入りした。: A young person who moved from the city became my apprentice.
観光客の相手は向いてなかった。: Dealing with tourists wasn't for me.
体験に来た子どもの一人が10年後、本当に漁師になって船を継いでくれた。: One of the kids who came for the experience actually became a fisherman ten years later and took over my boat.
漁業体験が旅行サイトで人気1位になり、本業より稼げた。: The fishing experience hit No. 1 on a travel site and earned more than my actual job.
船を売り、のんびり釣りをする余生を送った。: Sold the boat and spent the rest of my days fishing leisurely.
海を見るたびに寂しくなった。: Every time I looked at the sea, I felt lonely.
引退後、海の家を開いた。夏だけで100万円売れた。: After retiring, I opened a beach shack. It made ¥1 million in the summer alone.
船を売った翌年、魚価が高騰して近所の漁師が軒並み儲かった。: The year after I sold the boat, fish prices soared and the fishermen nearby all made good money.
院長が不要な自費治療を患者に勧めるよう指示してくる。: The clinic director orders me to push unnecessary out-of-pocket treatments on patients.
売上が上がり、院長の機嫌がよくなった。: Sales went up and the director was in a good mood.
患者さんに不信感を持たれ、口コミが荒れた。: Patients grew distrustful, and the online reviews turned ugly.
院長が売上で歯科医院を2つ増やし、自分は分院のチーフに抜擢された。: With the revenue, the director opened two more dental clinics, and I was promoted to chief of a branch.
指示に従ったことが患者のSNSで晒され、医院ごと保健所の指導を受けた。: A patient exposed my compliance on social media, and the whole clinic received guidance from the public health office.
院長に睨まれたが、患者さんからは信頼された。: The director glared at me, but patients came to trust me.
居づらくなり、転職した。: It became uncomfortable to stay, so I changed jobs.
断ったことを知った患者が地域の口コミで医院を紹介し、新患が月30人増えた。: A patient who heard I'd refused recommended the clinic in local reviews, and new patients rose by 30 a month.
院長が自分の方針を聞き入れ、医院の方針が変わった。: The director took my stance on board, and the clinic's policy changed.
ブランク明けで復職するか、別の道に進むか迷っている。: After a career break, I'm torn between returning to work and taking another path.
手が感覚を思い出し、すぐ戦力になった。: My hands remembered the feel, and I was useful right away.
新しい機器についていけず苦労した。: Struggled to keep up with the new equipment.
復職先で予防歯科のセミナーを始めたら、地域の企業から講演依頼が来た。: I started a preventive dentistry seminar at my new workplace, and local companies began asking me to give talks.
ブランク明けの初日、患者さんの口に指を噛まれた。でも1か月で慣れた。: On my first day back, a patient bit my finger. But I got used to it within a month.
医療事務として働き始めた。: Started working as a medical clerk.
結局、歯科の仕事が恋しくなった。: In the end, I missed dental work.
医療事務の経験を活かして、歯科医院向けのコンサル会社を起業した。: Drawing on my medical clerk experience, I founded a consulting firm for dental clinics.
新しい職場で出会った人と結婚した。歯並びをよく褒められた。: Married someone I met at my new workplace. They often complimented my teeth.
不動産決済の当日、売主の本人確認書類に不審な点がある。地面師の可能性もある。: On the day of the real estate settlement, something looks off in the seller's ID documents. It could be a land-swindling impostor.
偽物だった。数億円の詐欺被害を防いだ。: It was a fake. Prevented hundreds of millions of yen in fraud losses.
本人だった。依頼者に怒られ、取引が1週間遅れた。: It was the real owner. The client was furious and the deal was delayed a week.
地面師グループが逮捕され、テレビ局から取材を受けた。: The land-swindler ring was arrested, and TV stations interviewed me.
決済を止めた件が業界内で評判となり、大手不動産会社から指名が来た。: Stopping the settlement earned me a reputation in the industry, and a major real estate company asked for me by name.
問題なく決済が終わった。: The settlement went through without a hitch.
詐欺だった。賠償責任を問われた。: It was fraud. I was held liable for damages.
決済後、売主の正体が判明。保険で賠償はされたが、資格停止3か月になった。: After settlement, the seller's true identity came out. Insurance covered the damages, but my license was suspended for three months.
その日の決済は無事に終わり、帰りに買った宝くじで3万円当たった。: The settlement that day went smoothly, and the lottery ticket I bought on the way home won ¥30,000.
ベテランの司法書士事務所から、事務所を継がないかと声がかかった。: A veteran judicial scrivener's office asked if I'd take over the practice.
顧客を引き継ぎ、安定した経営ができた。: Inherited the clients and ran the practice stably.
古い慣習が多く、改革に苦労した。: There were many old customs, and reform was a struggle.
前所長の顧客の孫が事業を始め、法人登記の仕事を毎年頼まれた。: The grandchild of a former director's client started a business and hired me for corporate registrations every year.
継いだ事務所に古い書類が山のようにあり、整理に1年かかった。: The practice I took over had mountains of old documents, and sorting them took a year.
相続特化のWeb集客が当たり、2年で黒字化した。: Web marketing focused on inheritance cases paid off, and I turned a profit in two years.
集客に苦しみ、2年間赤字だった。: Struggled to attract clients and ran at a loss for two years.
遺言書のYouTube解説が10万再生され、問い合わせが殺到した。: My YouTube explainer on wills hit 100,000 views, and inquiries flooded in.
独立初年度、依頼人がゼロの月が3回あり、駅前でチラシを配った。: In my first year on my own, there were three months with zero clients, so I handed out flyers in front of the station.
フリーアナウンサーへの転身を事務所に誘われた。局の看板番組を手放すことになる。: A talent agency invited me to go freelance as an announcer. It would mean giving up the station's flagship show.
バラエティ番組に引っ張りだこになり、年収が3倍になった。: Became a hot commodity on variety shows, and my annual income tripled.
仕事が続かず、1年後には司会の仕事が月1本だけになった。: The work dried up, and after a year I was down to one hosting gig a month.
フリー2年目に冠番組を持ち、全国ネットで放送された。: In my second year as a freelancer, I got my own show, broadcast nationwide.
フリーになった途端、局の後輩がかつての看板番組を引き継ぎ、大人気になった。: The moment I went freelance, a junior at the station took over my old flagship show and it became hugely popular.
報道番組のメインキャスターに抜擢された。: Picked as the main anchor of a news program.
管理職になり、マイクの前に立つ機会が減った。: Moved into management, and got fewer chances to stand at the mic.
定年まで局に残り、伝説のアナウンサーとして特番が組まれた。: Stayed at the station until retirement, and a special program was made about me as a legendary announcer.
局の新人研修の講師を10年務め、教え子が5人もキー局のエースになった。: Taught the station's new-hire training for ten years, and five of my students became aces at major networks.
生放送中、ゲストが明らかに不適切な発言をした。: During a live broadcast, a guest made a clearly inappropriate remark.
「よく止めた」と局内外で評価された。: Praised both inside and outside the station: “Good thing you stopped that.”
ゲストの事務所と揉め、番組が気まずくなった。: Clashed with the guest's agency, and things got awkward for the show.
その場面が切り抜かれ、「理想の司会者」として雑誌の表紙を飾った。: The scene was clipped and shared, and I made a magazine cover as “the ideal host.”
ゲストがその後、自分の番組に謝罪に来て、なぜか仲良くなった。: The guest later came to my show to apologize, and somehow we became friends.
流して次へ進める: Let it slide and move on
放送後に炎上し、局として謝罪することになった。: It blew up online after the broadcast, and the station had to apologize.
流したことで番組プロデューサーから責められ、担当を外された。: The producer blamed me for letting it slide, and I was taken off the show.
放送後、局に抗議の電話が300件来た。その対応をしたのは自分だった。: After the broadcast, the station got 300 protest calls. I was the one who handled them.
人気作のメイン役のオーディション。指定のキャラ像と、自分の解釈が違う。: Audition for the lead role in a hit series. My take on the character differs from the specified portrayal.
落ちたが、音響監督に名前を覚えてもらえた。: Didn't get it, but the sound director remembered my name.
そのキャラがアニメ化され、イベントで5000人の前に立った。: The character got an anime adaptation, and I stood before 5,000 people at an event.
指定通りに演じた別作品で、監督から「次はあなたの解釈で」と言われ主演が決まった。: In another work where I played it as specified, the director said, “Next time, do it your way,” and I landed the lead.
「それだ」と言われ、役が決まった。作品は大ヒットした。: They said, “That's it,” and I got the part. The series became a huge hit.
落ちた。帰りに一人でラーメンを食べた。: Didn't get it. On the way home I ate ramen alone.
そのキャラの解釈が業界で評判になり、声優アワードの新人賞を取った。: My interpretation of the character got talked about in the industry, and I won the Rookie Award at the Seiyu Awards.
落ちた役の代わりに、通行人役で3年間毎週出演した。ファンが付いた。: Instead of the role I lost, I played a passerby every week for three years. I picked up fans.
30歳を前に、バイト生活が続いている。: Approaching thirty, I'm still living off part-time jobs.
ソシャゲのキャラで人気が出て、声優一本で食べられるようになった。: Became popular through a mobile game character and could finally make a living as a voice actor alone.
状況は変わらず、焦りだけが増えた。: Nothing changed, and only my anxiety grew.
40歳で大ブレイクし、紅白の応援ゲストに呼ばれた。: Broke out big at forty and was invited as a guest supporter on Kohaku Uta Gassen.

就職した会社の取引先に声優事務所の社長がいて、副業で月1本ずつ仕事をもらえた。: A client of my new company was the head of a voice-acting agency, and I got one side gig a month from him.

人気が回復し、連載が続いた。: Popularity recovered and the serial continued.
中途半端になり、結局打ち切りになった。: It ended up half-baked and got cancelled anyway.

最終回が話題になり、単行本が重版した。: The final chapter got people talking, and the volumes went back to press.
打ち切りになった。でも悔いはなかった。: It was cancelled. But I had no regrets.
打ち切り後、その作品がSNSで再評価され、別出版社で続編の連載が始まった。: After the cancellation, the work was re-appreciated on social media, and a sequel serial began at another publisher.
打ち切り最終回に描いた1ページが切り抜かれ、10万リツイートされた。: One page from the cancelled final chapter was clipped and retweeted 100,000 times.
Web漫画のプラットフォームから、縦読み漫画の制作を誘われた。: A webcomic platform invited me to make a vertical-scroll comic.
海外で読まれ、印税が月50万円になった。: It was read overseas, and royalties reached ¥500,000 a month.
フルカラーの作業量に圧倒され、半年で降りた。: Overwhelmed by the workload of full color, I quit after six months.

作業量を減らすためAIを使ったら炎上し、謝罪動画を出した。: I used AI to cut down the workload, got flamed online, and posted an apology video.
持ち込みが通らない日々が続いた。: Day after day, my pitches got rejected.
雑誌の新人賞の審査員を任され、自分が新人時代に描いた作品のファンだった若手を見出: Asked to judge the magazine's newcomer award, I discovered a young artist who was a fan of the work I drew as a rookie.
紙の雑誌が休刊し、結局Web版に移った。: The print magazine ceased publication, and I ended up moving to the web edition.

行列のできる店になり、3年で2号店を出した。: It became a place with lines out the door, and I opened a second location within three years.
客足が伸びず、2年で閉店した。: Customers never came, and I closed after two years.
開業した店がミシュランのビブグルマンに選ばれた。: My restaurant was selected for the Michelin Bib Gourmand.
開業初日、ガス管の工事ミスで営業できず、1週間で300万円の損を出した。: On opening day, a gas line construction error kept us from operating, and we lost ¥3 million in a week.
雇われで腕を磨く: Hone my skills as an employee
オーナーが店を畳み、職を失った。: The owner shut down the restaurant, and I lost my job.
修業先で知り合った人と結婚し、二人で店を始めた。: Married someone I met during my training, and we started a restaurant together.
料理長の座を争った同僚が独立し、5年後に自分を料理長として引き抜いた。: The colleague who competed with me for head chef went independent, and five years later recruited me as his head chef.
常連客が、大手チェーンの商品開発の仕事を紹介してくれた。: A regular customer introduced me to a product development job at a major chain.
開発したメニューが全国の店舗で販売された。: The menu item I developed was sold at stores nationwide.
コスト優先で、作りたい味にならなかった。: Cost came first, and it never turned into the flavor I wanted.
開発した冷凍ギョーザが年間1億個売れ、社長賞の金一封100万円をもらった。: The frozen gyoza I developed sold 100 million pieces a year, and I received a ¥1 million cash prize with the President's Award.
商品開発の会議が毎日4時間あり、包丁を握る時間がなくなった。: Product development meetings ran four hours a day, and I no longer had time to hold a knife.
断って店に専念する: Decline and focus on the restaurant
常連さんとの関係が深まった。: My bond with the regulars deepened.
後で話題の商品を見て、少し後悔した。: Later I saw the hit product and felt a twinge of regret.
断った話を常連客が笑い、毎年誕生日に花を贈ってくれるようになった。: The regular laughed about my turning it down, and began sending me flowers every birthday.
店が地元テレビで紹介され、客が3倍になった。: The restaurant was featured on local TV, and customers tripled.
怪しい美容サプリのPR案件。報酬は100万円だ。: A promo job for a dubious beauty supplement. The fee is ¥1 million.
何事もなく報酬を受け取った。: Received the fee without any trouble.
商品が問題になり、紹介した投稿が大炎上した。: The product became a scandal, and my promotional post was torched online.
報酬で買った車が1年後に事故で廃車になり、保険金で同じ車が買えた。: The car I bought with the fee was totaled in an accident a year later, and the insurance money bought me the same car again.
サプリのメーカーが行政処分を受け、紹介したことで訴訟の対象になった。: The supplement maker was hit with an administrative penalty, and because I promoted it, I became the target of a lawsuit.
他のインフルエンサーが受けて、報酬で車を買っていた。: Another influencer took the job and bought a car with the fee.
断ったことを動画で語ったら30万回再生され、誠実なブランドから年間契約が来た。: I talked about turning it down in a video, which got 300,000 views, and an honest brand offered me an annual contract.
断ったPRの代わりに、地元の農家の野菜を無償で紹介したら、売上が10倍になったと: Instead of the promo I declined, I introduced a local farmer's vegetables for free, and he thanked me for a tenfold jump in sales.
SNS疲れがひどい。フォロワー50万人のアカウントをしばらく休むか迷っている。: Social media fatigue is severe. I'm wondering whether to take a break from my 500,000-follower account.
1か月休んで、心が回復した。: After a month off, my mind recovered.
戻ったら、フォロワーが10万人減っていた。: When I came back, I had lost 100,000 followers.

心身を壊し、結局長期休止になった。: My mind and body broke down, and I ended up on a long hiatus anyway.
毎日投稿の記録が1000日を超え、テレビの情報番組に出演した。: My daily-posting streak passed 1,000 days, and I appeared on a TV information show.
フォロワー100万人達成の日、スマホを落として画面が割れた。: On the day I hit 1 million followers, I dropped my phone and cracked the screen.
過激な企画をすれば再生数が伸びそうだ。: A more extreme stunt would probably boost views.
バズって再生数が200万回を超えた。: It went viral, passing 2 million views.
炎上し、スポンサーが離れた。: It blew up, and sponsors walked away.
企画が海外でも話題になり、外国人ファンが30万人増えた。: The stunt got attention overseas too, and I gained 300,000 foreign fans.
企画中に骨折し、入院中の動画が一番再生された。: I broke a bone during the stunt, and the video from my hospital stay got the most views.
コツコツ伸び、固定ファンがついた。: Grew steadily and built a loyal fan base.
地道な投稿が実を結び、10年後に登録者100万人を達成した。: My steady posting paid off, and ten years later I reached 1 million subscribers.
同じ路線の大手チャンネルが引退し、そのファンがまるごと流れてきた。: A major channel in the same niche retired, and its fans all flowed over to mine.
会社員とYouTuberを兼業している。収益は月20万円になった。: I'm working a day job and YouTube at the same time. Earnings have reached ¥200,000 a month.
会社を辞めて専業になる: Quit the job and go full-time
投稿ペースが上がり、年収1000万円を超えた。: My posting pace picked up, and annual income passed ¥10 million.
収益が下がり、貯金を切り崩した。: Earnings dropped, and I dipped into my savings.
専業初年度、企業案件が月5本入り、法人化した。: In my first full-time year, I landed five brand deals a month and incorporated.
専業になったら撮るネタが会社員時代の話しかなく、1年で行き詰まった。: Once full-time, all I had to film were stories from my office-worker days, and I ran dry within a year.
安定した生活のまま、趣味として楽しめた。: Kept a stable life and enjoyed it as a hobby.
寝不足が続き、動画のクオリティが落ちた。: Chronic lack of sleep dragged down my video quality.

兼業疲れで寝坊し、会社の会議に20分遅刻した。: Worn out from juggling both, I overslept and was 20 minutes late to a company meeting.

チームが大会で優勝し、年俸が倍になった。: The team won the tournament, and my salary doubled.
ベンチ入りが続き、引退を考え始めた。: Stuck on the bench match after match, I started thinking about retiring.

配信が当たり、プレイヤー時代より稼げた。: Streaming took off, and I earned more than in my player days.
視聴者が集まらず、バイトを始めた。: Viewers never showed up, so I took a part-time job.
配信者として成功し、自分のチームを立ち上げた。: Succeeded as a streamer and founded my own team.
配信の視聴者に元チームメイトの母親がいて、毎日長文のコメントをくれた。: One of my stream viewers was a former teammate's mother, who left long comments every day.

正々堂々と戦い、勝った。: Fought fair and square, and won.
負けたが、胸を張れた。: Lost, but I could hold my head high.
情報を見なかったことを試合後に明かし、フェアプレー賞を受賞した。: After the match I revealed I hadn't looked at the information, and received the Fair Play Award.
決勝の相手チームが不正で失格になり、不戦勝で優勝した。喜び方がわからなかった。: The finals opponent was disqualified for cheating, and I won the title by default. I didn't know how to celebrate.
後で発覚し、出場停止処分を受けた。: It came to light later, and got a suspension.
見たことを正直に運営に報告し、相手チームが失格。自分も処分を受けたが減免された。: Honestly reported what I saw to the organizers; the opposing team was disqualified. I was penalized too, but the penalty was reduced.
見た情報はすべて嘘だった。相手が流したフェイクに乗せられ、惨敗した。: All the information I saw was false. Fell for a fake the opponent leaked and lost badly.
トライアウトを受けたが、どこからも声がかからない。独立リーグから誘いが来た。: Took the tryout, but no team called. An independent league made an offer.

独立リーグの監督に認められ、メジャーリーグのスカウトの目に留まった。: Won over the independent league manager and caught the eye of a Major League scout.

球団職員として採用され、裏方で野球に関わった。: Hired as a team staff member and stayed involved in baseball behind the scenes.
野球以外の仕事に慣れず苦労した。: Struggled to get used to work outside baseball.
引退後に始めた野球塾が繁盛し、教え子がプロ入りした。: The baseball school I started after retiring thrived, and a student turned pro.
就職先の会社の野球部で、全国大会に出場した。: Played in the national tournament with my company's baseball team.
FA権を取得した。今の球団に残るか、移籍するか。: Earned free agency. Stay with the current team, or move?
4年総額8億円の契約を結んだ。: Signed a four-year contract worth ¥800 million in total.
新天地で不振に陥り、ブーイングを浴びた。: Slumped with the new team and got booed.
移籍先で日本一になり、ビールかけで目が開かなくなった。: Won the Japan Series with the new team; the beer shower left my eyes stinging shut.
移籍1年目でケガをし、4年間でほとんど試合に出られなかった。: Got injured in the first year after the move and barely played in four years.
ファンから「残ってくれてありがとう」と横断幕が掲げられた。: Fans raised a banner reading “Thank you for staying.”
残留した年に日本一になり、球団の永久欠番になった。: Won the Japan Series the year I stayed, and my number was retired by the club.
残留したが、翌年監督が代わり、二軍で1年過ごした。: Stayed, but the manager changed the next year and I spent a year in the minors.
海外2部リーグのクラブからオファーが来た。年俸は今より下がる。: A club in an overseas second division made an offer. The salary would be lower than now.
活躍が認められ、1部のクラブに移籍した。: My performances got noticed and I moved to a top-division club.
言葉の壁に苦しみ、1年で帰国した。: Struggled with the language barrier and came home after a year.
海外2部で得点王になり、プレミアリーグのクラブから声がかかった。: Became top scorer in the overseas second division and got a call from a Premier League club.
現地の言葉を覚えて、引退後に日本人選手の代理人になった。: Learned the local language and, after retiring, became an agent for Japanese players.
チームの主力として定着した。: Established myself as a core player on the team.
あの時行っていたら、と思う夜があった。: Some nights I wondered what if I had gone.
国内で長くプレーし、地元クラブのアンバサダーになった。: Played in Japan for many years and became an ambassador for my hometown club.
国内残留を選んだ翌年、日本代表に初選出された。: The year after choosing to stay in Japan, got called up to the national team for the first time.
30歳。出場機会が減ってきた。下部リーグのクラブからは主力として誘われている。: Age 30. Playing time is shrinking. A lower-division club wants me as a core player.
キャプテンとしてチームを昇格に導いた。: As captain, led the team to promotion.
給料が下がり、生活が苦しくなった。: My salary dropped and life got tough.
下部リーグで10年プレーし、クラブの社長に就任した。: Played ten years in the lower division, then became the club's president.
移籍先のクラブが2年で経営破綻し、給料が3か月未払いになった。: The new club went bankrupt in two years, and my pay went unpaid for three months.

指導者ライセンスを取り、ユースのコーチになった。: Earned a coaching license and became a youth team coach.
何をしたらいいか分からず、半年ぼんやりした。: Didn't know what to do and spent half a year in a daze.

引退会見の日、なぜか最も話題になったのは隣に座った子どもだった。: On the day of the retirement press conference, strangely, the child sitting next to me got the most attention.
試合残り5秒、1点ビハインド。ボールは自分の手にある。: Five seconds left, down by one. The ball is in my hands.
決まった。逆転勝利のヒーローになった。: It went in. Became the hero of a comeback win.
外れた。SNSで叩かれた。: Missed. Got slammed on social media.
決めたシュートがシーズン最優秀プレーに選ばれた。: The shot I made was voted play of the season.
外したシュートの映像が、翌年の自チームのCMで「ここから始まった」と使われた。: Footage of the shot I missed was used in my own team's commercial the next year, with the line “It all started here.”
味方が決め、チームが勝った。: My teammate scored and the team won.
味方が外し、ベンチで二人で黙り込んだ。: My teammate missed, and the two of us sat silent on the bench.
パスを受けた選手が、後に自分の結婚式で「あのパスがなかったら今の自分はない」とス: The player who got my pass later said in his wedding speech, “Without that pass, I wouldn't be who I am today.”
パスが相手に読まれ、カットされて終了。監督に「なぜ打たない」と言われた。: The pass was read and intercepted, and the game ended. The coach asked, “Why didn't you shoot?”
海外のリーグからトライアウトの誘いが来た。: An overseas league invited me to a tryout.
不合格だったが、刺激をもらって帰国した。: Didn't make it, but came home inspired.
海外で3年プレーし、帰国後に日本代表のキャプテンになった。: Played three years abroad and became captain of the national team after returning home.
トライアウトで知り合った海外選手と友人になり、帰国後に二人でバスケ用品店を開いた: Became friends with an overseas player I met at the tryout, and after returning home we opened a basketball gear shop together.
チームの顔として長くプレーした。: Played for many years as the face of the team.
けがが増え、出場時間が減った。: Injuries piled up and my minutes dropped.
国内リーグのMVPを2回受賞した。: Won the domestic league MVP twice.

間に合い、工務店から次の仕事をもらった。: Made it in time and got the next job from the contractor.

無理をしたせいで腰を痛め、3か月現場に立てなかった。: Overdoing it hurt my back, and I couldn't work on site for three months.
