一人親方として独立するか迷っている。: Torn about going independent as a solo craftsman.
仕事が途切れる時期があり、不安な日々を過ごした。: There were stretches with no work, and I spent anxious days.
一人親方として建てた古民家再生が雑誌に載り、依頼が2年待ちになった。: An old farmhouse restoration I built as a solo craftsman was featured in a magazine, and requests booked up two years out.
独立した最初の現場で、施主が実は昔の同級生だった。: At my first site after going independent, the homeowner turned out to be an old classmate.
棟梁として現場を任された。: Was put in charge of the site as head carpenter.
給料の頭打ちを感じた。: Felt my pay had hit a ceiling.
工務店の後継者に指名された。: Was named successor to the contractor.
定年まで工務店で働き、退職祝いに自分で建てた家に住んだ。: Worked at the contractor until retirement and lived in the house I built myself as a retirement present.
高齢者の家で、ついでに不要な工事を勧めれば儲かると先輩に言われた。: A senior colleague told me I'd make money by pushing unnecessary work on elderly customers' homes while I'm there.
お客さんに信頼され、次の工事も頼まれた。: The customer trusted me and asked me to do the next job too.
先輩との関係が悪くなった。: My relationship with my senior colleague soured.
断ったお客さんが地元の老人会に話し、高齢者の家から依頼が年50件来るようになった: The customer I'd been honest with told the local senior club, and requests from elderly homes grew to 50 a year.
先輩も後に考えを改め、二人で地域の水道相談会を始めた。: My senior colleague later changed his mind, and the two of us started a community plumbing consultation event.
売上が上がり、褒められた。: Sales went up and I was praised.
消費者センターに通報された。: Reported to the consumer affairs center.
売上トップになり、社長賞をもらったが、その工事の家の人が亡くなった後に罪悪感が湧: Became top in sales and won the president's award, but felt guilty after the person in that house passed away.
先輩が勧めた不要工事が原因で、自分も一緒に会社をクビになった。: Because of the unnecessary work my senior colleague pushed, I got fired from the company along with him.
独立して自分の設備会社を立ち上げるか迷っている。: Torn about going independent and starting my own plumbing and equipment company.
地域の工務店と組み、安定した仕事が入るようになった。: Teamed up with local contractors and began getting steady work.
資金繰りに苦しみ、2年で廃業した。: Struggled with cash flow and closed the business in two years.
独立5年目に従業員10人の会社になった。: By the fifth year of being independent, the company had ten employees.
独立初日、自分の家のトイレが詰まった。: On my first day as an independent, the toilet at my own house clogged.
若手が育たず、仕事が増えた。: The young staff didn't develop, and my workload grew.
社長が引退し、会社を継いだ。: The president retired and I took over the company.
会社に残って30年、取引先の若手から「配管の神様」と呼ばれた。: After 30 years with the company, young people at client firms called me the “god of piping.”
工期に追われる中、上司から「検査は通るだろうから、多少手を抜け」と言われた。: Under schedule pressure, my boss told me, “The inspection will probably pass, so cut some corners.”
品質の高さが評価され、重要な仕事を任された。: My high quality was recognized and I was given an important job.
上司と衝突し、現場の空気が悪くなった。: Clashed with my boss and the mood on site turned bad.
その現場が大地震に耐え、自分の溶接がニュースで紹介された。: That site withstood a major earthquake, and my welding was featured on the news.
上司とぶつかった後、上司も自分の意見を聞くようになり、良いコンビになった。: After we clashed, my boss started listening to my opinions, and we became a good team.
何事もなく工期内に終わった。: Finished within the schedule without incident.
後で不具合が見つかり、責任を問われた。: Defects were found later and I was held responsible.
手を抜いた箇所が10年後に破断し、大規模な補修工事に発展した。: The part I'd cut corners on broke ten years later and led to major repair work.
手を抜いた直後に上司が異動し、新しい上司から「やり直し」と言われた。: Right after I cut corners, my boss was transferred, and the new boss told me to “redo it.”
海外の造船所から、高給で溶接工を募集している。: An overseas shipyard is recruiting welders at high pay.
年収が倍になり、技術も上がった。: My annual income doubled and my skills improved.
生活環境が合わず、1年で帰国した。: Couldn't adapt to the living environment and came home after a year.
海外で現地の溶接技術者と結婚し、そのまま住み着いた。: Married a local welding engineer abroad and settled there.
帰国後、海外経験を買われて大手造船所の主任に抜擢された。: After returning home, my overseas experience got me promoted to a supervisor at a major shipyard.
職長に昇格し、若手の指導を任された。: Promoted to foreman and put in charge of training younger workers.
景気が悪化し、仕事が減った。: The economy worsened and work decreased.
溶接技能競技会で全国1位になった。: Took first place nationwide at the welding skills competition.
定年後、地元の工業高校で溶接の非常勤講師になった。: After retirement, became a part-time welding instructor at a local technical high school.
見積もりで、塗料のグレードを下げれば利益が増える。施主は気づかないだろう。: In the estimate, lowering the paint grade would boost profit. The homeowner probably won't notice.
10年後もきれいなままで、施主から紹介が来た。: It still looked good ten years later, and the homeowner sent me referrals.
利益が減り、その月は赤字だった。: Profit shrank and that month ran at a loss.
正直な施工が口コミで広まり、地元で一番予約の取れない塗装屋になった。: Word of my honest work spread, and I became the hardest-to-book painter in town.
赤字を出した月、施主が差し入れに持ってきたのが高級メロンだった。: In the month I ran a loss, the homeowner brought a premium melon as a gift.
何事もなく利益を得た。: Pocketed the profit without any trouble.
3年で塗膜が剥がれ、無償でやり直した。: The paint film peeled in three years, and I redid it for free.
グレードを下げた外壁が、なぜか一番長持ちした。: Oddly enough, the wall with the downgraded paint lasted the longest.
施主が建築士で、塗料の缶を見られて全て見抜かれた。: The homeowner was an architect, saw the paint cans, and figured it all out.
知り合いから、外壁塗装の訪問販売会社に誘われた。歩合は大きい。: An acquaintance invited me to join a door-to-door exterior painting sales company. The commission is large.
営業成績トップになり、年収が倍になった。: Became the top salesperson and my annual income doubled.
強引な営業が嫌になり、半年で辞めた。: Grew sick of the pushy sales and quit after six months.
訪問販売の会社が行政処分を受け、自分も事情聴取を受けた。: The door-to-door company received an administrative penalty, and I was questioned as well.
営業で覚えた話術を活かして、自分の塗装会社を立ち上げた。: Put the sales talk skills I'd picked up to use and started my own painting company.
体力の限界を感じ始めた。: Began to feel the limits of my stamina.
親方の技術を受け継ぎ、文化財の塗り直しを任された。: Inherited the master's skills and was entrusted with repainting a cultural property.
長男が職人を継ぐと言い出した。: My eldest son said he'd take over as a craftsman.
解体中、壁の中から古い現金の入った封筒が出てきた。: During demolition, an envelope of old cash turned up inside a wall.
施主に深く感謝され、謝礼をもらった。: The homeowner thanked me deeply and gave me a reward.
施主に「もっとあったはずだ」と疑われた。: The homeowner suspected me, saying “There must have been more.”
届けた現金が施主の亡き父の遺品で、手紙も添えられていた。施主は泣いて喜んだ。: The cash I delivered was a keepsake of the homeowner's late father, with a letter attached. The homeowner wept with joy.
届けた封筒は全部で80万円。施主はその全額を地元の児童養護施設に寄付した。: The envelope held ¥800,000 in all. The homeowner donated the entire amount to a local children's home.
誰にもバレなかったが、ずっと気まずかった。: No one found out, but I felt uneasy the whole time.
同僚にバレて会社をクビになった。: A coworker found out and I was fired.
黙っていた金の存在が、10年後に施主の親族から問い合わせられた。: Ten years later, the homeowner's relatives asked about the money I'd kept quiet about.
封筒の中身は昭和の旧札で、使うに使えず押し入れにしまった。: The envelope held old Showa-era bills; I couldn't spend them, so I stuffed them in a closet.
アスベスト除去の専門資格を取れば、日給が上がる。: Getting the specialist qualification for asbestos removal would raise my daily pay.
日給が5000円上がった。: My daily pay went up by ¥5,000.
体への負担が気になり始めた。: Began to worry about the strain on my body.
資格を活かして独立し、アスベスト除去の会社を作った。: Used the qualification to go independent and founded an asbestos removal company.
資格を取った後、現場が学校の体育館ばかりで、子どもたちに手を振られた。: After qualifying, my sites were mostly school gymnasiums, and kids waved at me.
後輩に先を越され、少し悔しかった。: A junior colleague got ahead of me, and it stung a little.
定年まで現場で無事故を貫き、会社から表彰された。: Kept an accident-free record on site until retirement and was commended by the company.
後輩に先を越されたが、後輩から「先輩の仕事を見て覚えた」と言われた。: A junior colleague got ahead of me, but he told me, “I learned by watching your work.”
深夜、明らかに泥酔した客が乗り込んできた。行き先も言えない状態だ。: Late at night, an obviously dead-drunk passenger got in. He can't even say where he's going.
乗せて交番に向かう: Take him to the police box
警察に保護してもらい、後で家族から感謝された。: The police took him into protective custody, and his family thanked me later.
車内で吐かれ、清掃で営業が1日潰れた。: He threw up in the car, and cleaning wiped out a whole day of business.
その客が実は大企業の社長で、後日お礼に100万円の寄付を職場に申し出た。: The passenger turned out to be the president of a major company, and later offered ¥1 million to my workplace as thanks.
その客が翌週、素面で同じタクシー会社を指名し、常連になった。: The following week, that passenger, sober this time, requested the same taxi company and became a regular.
何事もなく次の客を乗せた。: Picked up the next passenger without incident.
その客が倒れていたというニュースを翌朝見た。: The next morning I saw news that the passenger had been found collapsed.
乗車拒否が社内で問題になり、始末書を書いた。: The refused ride became an issue within the company, and I wrote a letter of apology.
断った客を別のタクシーが乗せ、その運転手が新聞で表彰された。: Another taxi picked up the passenger I turned away, and that driver was honored in the newspaper.
個人タクシーの資格要件を満たした。独立するか迷っている。: Met the requirements for an individual taxi license. Torn about going independent.
自分のペースで働け、手取りが増えた。: Could work at my own pace, and my take-home pay rose.
車両代の返済に追われた。: Chased by payments on the vehicle.
個人タクシーで観光ガイドも始め、外国人客から年間200件の予約が入った。: Started offering sightseeing guide service with my taxi and got 200 bookings a year from foreign tourists.
個人になった初日、車にカラスのフンが3回落ちた。: On my first day on my own, crows dropped poop on my car three times.
ノルマに追われ、腰痛が悪化した。: Pressed by quotas, my back pain got worse.
会社の教育担当になり、新人50人を育てた。: Became the company's trainer and raised 50 new hires.
会社が配車アプリと提携し、売上が1.5倍になった。: The company partnered with a ride-hailing app and sales rose 1.5 times.
乗客の一人が車内で倒れた。次のバス停まであと2分だ。: A passenger collapsed on board. The next stop is two minutes away.
すぐ停車して救護する: Stop at once and give aid
救急車が来るまで心臓マッサージをし、乗客は助かった。後日表彰された。: Gave chest compressions until the ambulance arrived, and the passenger survived. Later received a commendation.
他の乗客から「遅れる」と文句を言われた。: Other passengers complained that we'd be late.
助けた乗客が地元の議員で、路線バスの増便が決まった。: The passenger I saved was a local legislator, and more bus runs were approved.
救護の様子を他の乗客が撮影していて、SNSで「神運転手」と呼ばれた。: Another passenger filmed the rescue, and I was called a “god driver” on social media.
次の停留所まで走る: Drive on to the next stop
停留所で救急車を呼び、無事搬送された。: Called an ambulance at the stop, and the passenger was safely transported.
判断の遅れを指摘され、会社に注意された。: Was criticized for the delayed decision and warned by the company.
停留所で待機していた医師が偶然乗り合わせて救護し、二人で表彰された。: A doctor who happened to be on board gave aid at the stop, and the two of us were commended.
次の停留所に着いた時、倒れた乗客は寝ていただけだった。: When we reached the next stop, the “collapsed” passenger had just been asleep.
観光バス会社から、高い給料で誘われている。: A tour bus company is courting me with a high salary.
全国を走り回り、各地のサービスエリアに詳しくなった。: Drove all over the country and got to know service areas everywhere.
長距離の夜行運転がきつく、体を壊した。: Long overnight drives were punishing, and my health broke down.
観光バスで出会ったツアーガイドと結婚した。: Married a tour guide I met on the tour bus.
高い給料に誘われて転職したが、会社が1年で倒産した。: Lured by the high salary I switched jobs, but the company went bankrupt within a year.
地元の顔なじみが増え、町の一部になった気がした。: Met more familiar local faces and felt like part of the town.
運転手不足で勤務がさらに過酷になった。: A driver shortage made the work even harsher.
地元の小学生から感謝の寄せ書きが届き、運転席に貼った。: Local elementary school kids sent a group thank-you card, and I put it up by the driver's seat.
定年まで路線バスに乗り、最後の便に常連客30人が乗ってきた。: Drove the local route until retirement, and 30 regulars rode my final run.
ドライバー仲間に、個人事業主として独立しないかと誘われた。: A fellow driver asked if I wanted to go independent as a sole proprietor.
1個150円の委託単価。: The contract rate is ¥150 per package.
1日200個さばいて月収が60万円を超えた。体はボロボロだった。: Handled 200 packages a day and my monthly income topped ¥600,000. My body was wrecked.
単価が120円に下がり、ガソリン代で赤字の月が出た。2年で会社員に戻った。: The rate dropped to ¥120, and some months ran at a loss after fuel costs. Went back to being a salaried employee in two years.
3年後、軽貨物の会社を立ち上げ、ドライバー8人を抱える社長になった。: Three years later, started a light-cargo delivery company and became a boss with eight drivers.
初日にナビが壊れ、80個中30個を持ち戻った。妻に「向いてない」と笑われ、1週間: On day one the GPS broke and I brought 30 of 80 packages back. My wife laughed and said, “You're not cut out for it,” and I went back to being an employee within a week.
ボーナスで家族旅行に行けた。: Went on a family trip with my bonus.
独立した仲間が新車のハイエースで遊びに来た。少しうらやましかった。: A friend who'd gone independent came by in a brand-new Hiace van. I was a little envious.
社員のまま10年勤め、地区の配送センター長になった。月給が8万円上がった。: Stayed an employee for ten years and became head of the district distribution center. Monthly pay rose by ¥80,000.
誘ってきた仲間が半年で廃業し、なぜか自分が200万円の借金の保証人になっていた。: The friend who'd invited me closed shop in six months, and somehow I'd become the guarantor for a ¥2 million debt.
配達先で、荷物を受け取りに出てこない高齢者の家から異臭がした。: At a delivery stop, an elderly resident didn't come out for the package, and a strange smell came from the house.
倒れていたおじいさんが一命を取り留めた。後日、警察から感謝状が届いた。: The old man who had collapsed pulled through. Later, a letter of appreciation arrived from the police.
ただのぬか漬けだった。おじいさんに笑われて、漬物をもらった。: It was just rice-bran pickles. The old man laughed at me and gave me some pickles.
通報が地元紙に載り、配達エリアの30軒から「うちも見回って」と頼まれるようになっ: The report made the local paper, and 30 households in my delivery area began asking me to “check on us too.”
中で倒れていた猫が保護された。そのまま自分が引き取ることになった。: A cat that had collapsed inside was rescued. I ended up taking it home.
不在票を入れて去る: Leave a missed-delivery slip and go
何もなかった。でも次の週まで気になった。: Nothing was wrong. But it nagged at me until the next week.
翌週、その家に救急車が止まっていた。ずっと引きずった。: The next week, an ambulance was parked at that house. It stayed with me for a long time.
半年後、その家の息子さんが会社に来て「父が無事だったのは別の配達員のおかげ」と礼: Six months later, the son from that house came to the company and thanked a delivery driver, saying, “My father is safe thanks to another driver.” It wasn't me.
その日以来、異臭のする家の前では必ずインターホンを3回押す癖がついた。: Since that day, I've had a habit of always pressing the intercom three times in front of any house with a strange smell.
会社が自動倉庫ロボットを導入する。リーダーになってロボットの管理を覚えないかと言: The company is introducing automated warehouse robots. I was asked to become a leader and learn to manage them.
ロボット相手の仕事に慣れ、月給が4万円上がった。: Got used to working with robots, and my monthly pay rose by ¥40,000.
ロボットが毎晩止まり、深夜3時に呼び出される日々が続いた。: The robots stopped every night, and I kept getting called in at 3 a.m.
ロボット管理の資格を3つ取り、5年後にメーカーへ年収650万円で引き抜かれた。: Earned three robot-management qualifications, and five years later was headhunted by the manufacturer at ¥6.5 million a year.
ロボットに名前をつけて可愛がっていたら、社内報の表紙を飾った。: I named the robots and doted on them, and ended up on the cover of the company newsletter.
人手が減って、仲のいい3人とのんびり働けた。: With fewer staff, I got to work at a relaxed pace with three close coworkers.
2年後、人員削減の対象になった。: Two years later, I was targeted for staff cuts.
ロボットの不具合を誰より早く見抜けるようになり、手作業の「最後の砦」として時給が: I became faster than anyone at spotting robot glitches, and as the manual work's “last bastion” my hourly pay rose by ¥300.
腰を痛めて半年休職し、復帰したら持ち場がロボットに置き換わっていた。: Hurt my back and took six months off; when I returned, my post had been replaced by a robot.
同僚がこっそり商品を持ち帰っているのを見た。: Saw a coworker secretly taking merchandise home.
同僚は解雇になった。職場の空気が少し冷たくなった。: The coworker was fired. The mood at work turned a little cold.
実は他にも被害が多く、上司に感謝されて班長になった。: It turned out there was much more loss than that; my boss thanked me and I was made team leader.
実は自分の勘違いで、同僚は廃棄品を許可を得て持ち帰っていた。気まずさが1年続いた: It was my mistake: the coworker had permission to take home discarded items. The awkwardness lasted a year.
報告が評価され本社の監査チームに抜擢された。年収が50万円上がった。: My report was valued and I was picked for the head office audit team. Annual income rose by ¥500,000.
同僚は泣いて謝り、二度としなかった。その後、一番の飲み仲間になった。: The coworker apologized in tears and never did it again. Later, we became the best of drinking buddies.
逆恨みされ、ロッカーに嫌がらせをされた。: Resented unfairly, I had my locker harassed.
同僚の家庭が苦しいと知り、自分が3万円を貸した。2年後、利子つきで返ってきた。: Learned the coworker's family was struggling and lent them ¥30,000. Two years later it came back with interest.
注意した翌月、同僚は別の倉庫に移った。理由は誰も知らなかった。: The month after I warned them, the coworker moved to another warehouse. Nobody knew why.
正社員登用試験の案内が来た。受かれば安定だが、今の期間工の手当はなくなる。: Notice arrived for the permanent-employee promotion exam. Passing means stability, but the current fixed-term worker allowances would be lost.
合格した。両親が赤飯を炊いてくれた。: Passed. My parents cooked sekihan, the celebratory red rice.
面接で落ちた。来年また受けると決めた。: Failed the interview. Decided to try again next year.
合格後、改善提案が年間最優秀に選ばれ、報奨金30万円をもらった。: After passing, my improvement proposal was chosen best of the year and I received a ¥300,000 reward.
正社員になった直後に工場の閉鎖が発表され、200km離れた工場へ転勤になった。: Right after becoming a permanent employee, the factory's closure was announced, and I was transferred to a plant 200 km away.
期間工で稼いで辞める: Earn as a fixed-term worker, then quit
2年で300万円貯めて、専門学校に入り直した。: Saved ¥3 million in two years and went back to school at a vocational college.
貯金はパチンコに半分消えた。: Half my savings vanished into pachinko.
3年貯めた500万円で地元に小さなラーメン屋を開き、夜は行列ができた。: With ¥5 million saved over three years, opened a small ramen shop in my hometown, and lines formed at night.
期間満了で辞めた翌年、同じ工場が期間工を正社員に一斉登用した。: The year after my contract ended and I left, that same factory promoted all its fixed-term workers to permanent staff at once.
手袋の巻き込みでヒヤリとした。安全装置の手順を飛ばすのが現場の慣習になっている。: My glove got caught in the machine and gave me a scare. Skipping the safety device procedure has become the norm on the floor.
班長に改善を訴える: Appeal to the team leader for improvement
手順が見直され、ラインに安全カバーがついた。: The procedure was revised and a safety cover was added to the line.
「お前のせいで遅れる」と嫌味を言われた。: Got snide remarks like “You're making us late.”
提案が全社の安全大会で表彰され、ライン長に昇格した。: My proposal was recognized at the company-wide safety convention and I was promoted to line chief.
安全カバーのせいで作業が1日30分遅れ、残業代で月2万円多くもらえた。: The safety cover slowed work by 30 minutes a day, and the overtime pay brought me ¥20,000 more a month.
指を挟んで3針縫った。労災の書類が面倒だった。: Caught my finger and needed three stitches. The workers' comp paperwork was a hassle.
隣のラインで同じ事故が起き、現場が一斉に手順を守り始めた。複雑な気持ちになった。: The same accident happened on the next line over, and everyone started following the procedure at once. I felt mixed emotions.
10年間何も起きないまま定年まで勤め上げ、送別会で「運がいい男」と呼ばれた。: Nothing happened for ten years and I served until retirement; at the farewell party I was called “a lucky man.”
清掃会社から、現場責任者として新人10人のまとめ役を頼まれた。: The cleaning company asked me to be site supervisor and lead ten newcomers.
時給が200円上がり、新人に慕われた。: My hourly pay rose by ¥200 and the newcomers looked up to me.
新人が次々辞め、穴埋めで週6勤務になった。: Newcomers quit one after another, and covering the gaps put me on a six-day week.
3年後、新人だった1人と結婚した。: Three years later, married one of the former newcomers.
現場の評価が上がり、エリアマネージャーとして月給30万円になった。: My standing on site rose and, as area manager, I earned ¥300,000 a month.
新人同士の喧嘩の仲裁に追われ、胃薬が手放せなくなった。: Kept busy mediating fights between new hires; stomach medicine became a staple.
マイペースに続けられた。: Kept going at my own pace.
断った2年後、自分で清掃会社を開業し、10件の契約を取った。: Two years after declining, started my own cleaning company and landed 10 contracts.
代わりに引き受けた後輩が上司になった。指示を出される日々が始まった。: The junior who took the job instead became my boss. Days of taking orders began.
空いた時間で資格を取り、ビルクリーニング技能士になった。手当が月1万円ついた。: Studied in my spare time and became a certified building cleaning technician. Got a 10,000 yen monthly allowance.
清掃中、会議室に財布が落ちていた。中に現金20万円が入っていた。: While cleaning, found a wallet on the floor of a meeting room. It held 200,000 yen in cash.
警備室に届ける: Turn it in to the security office
持ち主の社長から1割のお礼を受け取った。: The owner, a company president, gave me 10% as a reward.
お礼はなかったが、気分はよかった。: There was no reward, but I felt good.
持ち主は清掃会社の大口取引先の社長で、契約額が年間300万円増えた。社長賞をもら: The owner was the president of a major client of the cleaning company, and the contract grew by 3 million yen a year. Received the President's Award.
その財布は落とし物ではなく、社長が社員の正直さを試すための仕掛けだった。: The wallet wasn't lost at all; the president had set it up to test his employees' honesty.
後で「清掃の人が盗った」と疑われた。防犯カメラで潔白が証明された。: Later, I was suspected: “The cleaner took it.” Security cameras proved my innocence.
翌日、財布は持ち主に戻っていた。誰も何も言わなかった。: The next day, the wallet was back with its owner. Nobody said a word.
疑いが晴れた後、謝罪に来た総務部長と仲良くなり、釣り仲間になった。: After I was cleared, the general affairs manager came to apologize, and we became friends and fishing buddies.
疑われたことが悔しく、その現場の担当を外してもらった。: Being suspected stung, so I asked to be taken off that site.
局長に、保険の営業成績を上げるよう強く求められた。親戚にも声をかけろと言う。: The postmaster pushed me hard to raise my insurance sales numbers. He told me to ask relatives, too.
ノルマを達成し、ボーナスが増えた。お正月に親戚の目が冷たかった。: Met the quota and my bonus grew. At New Year's, my relatives were cold to me.
契約した叔母が1年後に解約し、30万円の違約金でもめて親戚付き合いが途絶えた。: My aunt cancelled a year later, we argued over a 300,000 yen penalty, and the family ties broke off.
営業成績全国上位になり、表彰旅行でハワイに行った。: Ranked among the top sales performers nationwide and went to Hawaii on a commendation trip.
評価は下がったが、心は軽かった。: My rating dropped, but my heart felt light.
異動で山奥の局に飛ばされた。空気はおいしかった。: Transferred to a post office deep in the mountains. The air was delicious.
3年後、過剰な営業ノルマが全国ニュースになり、断った自分の判断が正しかったとわか: Three years later, the excessive sales quotas made national news, and I knew refusing had been the right call.
局長に睨まれ続け、5年後に退職して地元の運送会社に移った。: The postmaster kept glaring at me; five years later I quit and joined a local trucking company.
配達中、自転車とぶつかりそうになってカブで転んだ。相手はそのまま走り去った。: While delivering, I nearly hit a bicycle and fell off my Cub scooter. The other rider just rode away.
事故報告書を5枚書いた。でも膝のケガは労災になった。: Wrote five accident reports. But my knee injury was covered by workers' compensation.
走り去った自転車の相手が、翌日菓子折りを持って局に謝りに来た。: The cyclist who rode off came to the post office the next day with a gift of sweets to apologize.
報告書をきっかけにその交差点にカーブミラーがついた。地域の人に感謝された。: Thanks to the report, a curve mirror was installed at that intersection. The locals thanked me.
膝の治療で通った整形外科の理学療法士と仲良くなり、2年後に結婚した。: Became close with the physical therapist at the orthopedic clinic where I was treated for my knee, and we married two years later.
膝が腫れて3日休んだ。: My knee swelled up and I took three days off.
1年後、膝の古傷が悪化して手術になり、3か月休職した。: A year later, my old knee injury flared up, required surgery, and I took three months of leave.
隠したことが後でバレ、始末書を書かされた。: The cover-up came out later and I had to write a letter of apology.
ある受刑者から、家族に手紙をこっそり渡してほしいと頼まれた。: An inmate asked me to secretly pass a letter to his family.
規則通り断った。受刑者は「わかってた」と笑った。: I refused, following the rules. The inmate laughed and said, “I knew you would.”
逆恨みされ、しばらく嫌がらせが続いた。: He held a grudge, and the harassment went on for a while.
その受刑者が出所後、まっとうに働き始めたと風の便りで聞いた。: I heard through the grapevine that after his release, that inmate started working an honest job.
実は所内の規律を試す内部監査だったと後で知った。上司から評価された。: I later learned it was an internal audit testing discipline at the facility. My boss praised me.
正式な手続きで手紙が送られた。受刑者に頭を下げられた。: The letter was sent through proper procedures. The inmate bowed his head to me.
その受刑者が出所後、手紙を受け取った家族と和解したと便りが届いた。: After his release, word came that he had reconciled with the family who received the letter.
相談したことで上司に信頼され、教育担当に抜擢された。手当が月2万円ついた。: Because I consulted my boss, he came to trust me and I was picked as a training instructor. Got a 20,000 yen monthly allowance.
正式手続きの書類が2か月滞り、受刑者からは「結局同じだ」と恨まれた。: The formal paperwork stalled for two months, and the inmate resented me: “It's the same in the end.”
刑務官を続けるか、昇任試験を受けるか迷った。: Torn between staying a correctional officer and taking the promotion exam.
合格して看守部長になった。: Passed and became a correctional sergeant.
3年連続で落ちた。: Failed three years in a row.
15年後、刑務所長になった。: Fifteen years later, became warden of a prison.
試験勉強中の夜勤で体調を崩し、1か月入院した。: Night shifts while studying for the exam wrecked my health, and I was hospitalized for a month.
警備会社に転職し、夜はよく眠れるようになった。: Switched to a security company and began sleeping well at night.
給料が下がり、少し後悔した。: My pay dropped and I felt a little regret.
転職先の警備会社で、出所した元受刑者と同僚になった。普通に仲良くなった。: At the new security company, a former inmate who had been released became my coworker. We got along just fine.
転職後、元刑務官の経験を書いた本が5,000部売れた。: After changing jobs, a book about my experience as a former correctional officer sold 5,000 copies.
海外の寿司店から、年収1,200万円で板長として来ないかと誘われた。: An overseas sushi restaurant invited me to come as head chef for 12 million yen a year.
現地で大人気になり、3年で自分の店を出した。: Became hugely popular there and opened my own restaurant in three years.
言葉と文化の壁で1年で帰国した。英語だけは上達した。: Language and cultural barriers sent me home after a year. At least my English improved.
ニューヨークでの評判を聞いた投資家から出資を受け、5年で全米に7店舗を展開した。: Investors who heard of my reputation in New York backed me, and in five years I expanded to seven restaurants across the U.S.
現地の客に巻き寿司ばかり頼まれ、握りの腕がなまって帰国後に親方に叱られた。: Local customers mostly ordered rolls, my nigiri skills dulled, and my master scolded me after I returned to Japan.
10年後、のれん分けで自分の店を持った。: Ten years later, my master let me branch off and open my own shop.
親方とは今も厳しいままだった。: My master was still as strict as ever.
断った後、ニューヨークの店は半年で潰れたと聞いた。: After I declined, I heard the New York restaurant went under within six months.
親方が倒れ、急に店を任されることになった。常連の3割が離れた。: My master collapsed and I was suddenly put in charge of the shop. Thirty percent of the regulars left.
親方の目を盗んで、SNSで握りの動画を投稿してみないか、と後輩に言われた。: A junior suggested we post sushi-making videos on social media behind my master's back.
動画が200万回再生され、店に行列ができた。親方も満更でもなさそうだった。: The video got 2 million views and lines formed outside the shop. My master didn't seem to mind.
親方に「職人は黙って握れ」と叱られ、アカウントを消した。: My master scolded me, “A craftsman shuts up and makes sushi,” and I deleted the account.
動画の外国人視聴者が来店し、1年で客の4割が海外からになった。: Foreign viewers of the video came to the shop, and within a year 40% of customers were from overseas.
動画で握り方を真似した後輩が先に独立した。: A junior who copied my technique from the video went independent before me.
淡々と修業を続けた。: Kept up my training without fuss.
10年後、親方が自分から「動画をやってみろ」と言い出した。: Ten years later, my master himself said, “Try making videos.”
後輩が単独で投稿した動画がバズり、後輩だけテレビに出た。: A video my junior posted on his own went viral, and only he appeared on TV.
修業に集中した結果、全国の若手寿司コンクールで優勝した。: Focusing on training paid off: I won a national young sushi chefs' competition.
自分のパン屋を開業するチャンスが来た。開業資金は1,000万円。: A chance came to open my own bakery. Startup funds: 10 million yen.
地元の人気店になり、行列が毎朝できた。: It became a popular local shop, with a line every morning.
睡眠3時間の日々が続き、3年で閉店した。: Days of three hours of sleep went on, and I closed the shop in three years.
カレーパンが全国ランキング1位になり、通販で月500万円売れた。: My curry bread hit No. 1 in the national rankings and sold 5 million yen a month online.
開店初日、オーブンが故障して1個も焼けなかった。そのエピソードで地元テレビに出て: On opening day, the oven broke and I couldn't bake a single loaf. That story got me on local TV and made me famous instead.
給料は少ないが、夜はちゃんと眠れた。: The pay is low, but I slept soundly at night.
いつも買いに来る常連さんに頼まれ、仕事を辞めてその人の店で働くことになった。: A regular customer who always came to buy asked me to quit and work at his shop.
雇われのまま20年勤め、オーナーから店を無償で譲り受けた。: Worked as an employee for 20 years, then the owner handed the shop over to me for free.
オーナーが新しいフランチャイズに乗り換え、自分のレシピが全部使えなくなった。: The owner switched to a new franchise, and none of my recipes could be used anymore.
コンテストに出るため、休みを全部使って試作したいと思った。: Wanted to use all my days off to develop prototypes for a contest.
全国大会で入賞し、店の看板商品になった。: Placed at the national finals, and it became the shop's signature product.
予選落ちだった。でも新しいパンが一つ生まれた。: Eliminated in the preliminaries. But one new bread was born.
試作品を食べすぎて体重が8kg増えた。: Ate too many prototypes and gained 8 kg.
優勝したパンのレシピを大手メーカーが500万円で買い取った。: A major manufacturer bought the winning bread's recipe for 5 million yen.
休日は家族とピクニックに行った。: Spent the day off on a picnic with the family.
休日に家族とピクニックしたとき、子どもが「パパのパンが世界一」と言った。: On a family picnic on my day off, my child said, “Daddy's bread is the best in the world.”
翌年、同僚がコンテストで優勝し、店の看板職人の座を奪われた。: The next year, a coworker won the contest and took my place as the shop's star baker.
休んだおかげで腱鞘炎が治り、仕事のミスが減った。: Thanks to the rest, my tendonitis healed and I made fewer mistakes at work.
跡継ぎがいない老舗の主人から、店を継がないかと言われた。: The owner of an old established shop with no heir asked if I would take over.
伝統を守りながら新商品を出し、売上が1.3倍になった。: Kept tradition alive while launching new products, and sales rose 1.3 times.
継いだ老舗: The old established shop I took over
借金も一緒に継いでいた。: I had inherited the debts along with it.
店の100周年記念に皇族ゆかりの茶会へ菓子を納め、全国から注文が殺到した。: For the shop's 100th anniversary, I delivered sweets to a tea ceremony tied to the Imperial family, and orders poured in from across the country.
継いだ直後、先代の主人が「やっぱり自分がやる」と言い出し、2年間二人体制になった: Right after I took over, the previous owner said, “I'll do it myself after all,” and we ran the shop together for two years.
店はその後閉店した。少し胸が痛んだ。: The shop closed afterward. It hurt a little.
断った翌年、その店のレシピ帳だけが自分のもとに届いた。主人からの手紙が添えられて: The year after I declined, only that shop's recipe book arrived at my door, with a letter from the owner.
主人の孫が東京から戻って店を継いだ。自分は技術指導を頼まれた。: The owner's grandchild returned from Tokyo and took over the shop. I was asked to teach technique.
断ったことを地元の和菓子組合に知られ、しばらく陰口を言われた。: The local wagashi guild found out I had declined, and people talked behind my back for a while.
洋菓子とのコラボ商品を作らないかと、パティシエの友人に誘われた。: A pastry chef friend invited me to create a collaboration with Western confectionery.
抹茶とマスカルポーネの大福がヒットした。: The matcha and mascarpone daifuku became a hit.
コラボ大福が全国のコンビニで発売され、ロイヤリティで年300万円入った。: The collaboration daifuku went on sale at convenience stores nationwide, bringing in 3 million yen a year in royalties.
パティシエの友人と仲違いし、5年間口をきかなかった。: Fell out with my pastry chef friend and didn't speak to him for five years.
試作のしすぎでバターと餡の配合を間違え、店の看板菓子の味が一時おかしくなった。: Overdid the test batches, mixed up the butter and bean paste ratio, and the taste of the shop's signature sweet went off for a while.
3年後、友人のコラボ商品が大ヒットし、断ったことを少し後悔した。: Three years later, my friend's collaboration product became a huge hit, and I regretted declining a little.
伝統の上生菓子が品評会で金賞を取った。: My traditional jo-namagashi won a gold medal at a competition.
その後、別の和菓子職人とのコラボが1,000万円の売上を出したと聞いた。: Later I heard that a collaboration with another wagashi artisan brought in 10 million yen in sales.
海外の日本庭園から、職人として3年間来てほしいと依頼された。: A Japanese garden overseas asked me to come as a craftsman for three years.
現地で日本庭園の弟子を育て、新聞に載った。: Trained Japanese garden apprentices there and was featured in the newspaper.
気候が違いすぎて木が根付かず、苦労した。: The climate was so different that the trees wouldn't take root, and it was a struggle.
現地の庭園で出会った人と結婚し、そのまま現地に住むことになった。: Married someone I met at the garden there and ended up settling abroad.
3年の契約が終わった後、日本の大手造園会社に年収800万円で迎えられた。: After the three-year contract ended, a major Japanese landscaping company welcomed me with a salary of 8 million yen a year.
地元の庭を守った。: Looked after the gardens at home.
地元の古い庭を残すため市役所と掛け合い、庭が文化財になった。: To preserve an old local garden, I negotiated with city hall, and the garden was designated a cultural property.
断った仕事を受けた同業者がテレビの密着番組に出た。: A fellow gardener who took the job I turned down appeared on a TV documentary.
地元の常連の家が次々と代替わりし、3年で顧客が半分になった。: Local regular customers' homes changed hands one after another, and my clients were cut in half in three years.
脚立に乗った高所作業。命綱をつけるのが面倒な場所だった。: High work on a stepladder. A spot where putting on a lifeline was a hassle.
時間はかかったが無事に終わった。: It took longer, but it finished safely.
命綱を外す作業を見た同業者が「慎重すぎる」と笑ったが、翌月その人が落ちた。: A fellow tradesman who saw me handling my lifeline laughed, “You're too cautious,” but the next month he fell.
命綱の安全手順を地域の組合で講習するようになり、講師料で年20万円入った。: I began teaching lifeline safety procedures at the local guild, earning 200,000 yen a year in lecture fees.
命綱に慎重な姿勢を見た施主から、5年分の剪定契約をまとめてもらった。: A client who saw my careful approach to lifelines gave me a five-year pruning contract all at once.
落ちて腕を骨折した。2か月仕事ができなかった。: Fell and broke my arm. Couldn't work for two months.
落ちたが植え込みに着地して無傷だった。施主が大笑いしていた。: Fell, but landed in a hedge and was unhurt. The client roared with laughter.
足を滑らせ、腰を強打して3か月入院した。仕事に戻れなかった。: Slipped, hit my lower back hard, and was hospitalized for three months. Never made it back to work.
自分で林業会社を立ち上げないかと、先輩に誘われた。: A senior colleague invited me to start a forestry company together.
木材価格が上がり、5年で社員10人の会社になった。: Timber prices rose, and in five years it grew into a company of 10 employees.
機械のローンが重く、3年で廃業した。: The machinery loans were heavy, and the company folded in three years.
立ち上げた会社が森林認証を取り、外国の家具メーカーとの年間契約で年商1億円になっ: The company I founded earned forest certification, and a yearly contract with a foreign furniture maker brought annual sales to 100 million yen.
誘った先輩が開業前日にやめると言い出し、ひとりで始めることになった。: The senior who invited me backed out the day before opening, so I had to start alone.
雇われのまま、山で働き続けた。: Stayed an employee and kept working in the mountains.
断った後、先輩の会社に転職して所長になった。: After declining, I switched to the senior's company and became branch head.
チェーンソーの腕を磨き、全国大会で入賞した。: Honed my chainsaw skills and placed at a national competition.
断った翌年、林業の人手不足で給料が2割上がった。: The year after I declined, a labor shortage in forestry raised my pay by 20%.
台風の後、倒木が道をふさいでいる。危険だが、早く撤去してほしいと住民に頼まれた。: After a typhoon, a fallen tree is blocking the road. It's dangerous, but residents asked me to clear it quickly.
道が開通し、住民から差し入れが山ほど届いた。: The road reopened, and residents sent piles of treats.
作業中に足をケガした。: Injured my foot during the work.
撤去作業の様子が地域のSNSで拡散し、村長に表彰された。: Footage of the clearing spread on the local social media, and the village mayor honored me.
撤去後に住民から「ついでに庭の木も」と頼まれ、5軒分の伐採で20万円の副収入にな: After clearing, residents asked, “While you're at it, our garden trees too,” and cutting for five homes brought in a side income of 200,000 yen.
翌日、安全に撤去した。住民からは少し文句を言われた。: The next day, I cleared it safely. Residents grumbled a little.
待っている間に別の業者が勝手に撤去した。住民はその業者に感謝した。: While I waited, another contractor cleared it on their own. The residents thanked them instead.
安全確認中に2本目の木が倒れ、待ったおかげで巻き込まれずに済んだ。: While the safety check was underway, a second tree fell. Because I waited, I wasn't caught in it.
安全手順を守ったことが評価され、班長に昇格した。: My adherence to safety procedures was recognized and I was promoted to team leader.
2店舗目を出さないかと本部に言われた。: Headquarters asked if I'd open a second store.
2店舗とも黒字になり、年収が900万円になった。: Both stores turned a profit, and my annual income reached 9 million yen.
人手不足で両方回らず、毎日18時間働いた。: Short-staffed, I couldn't keep both running and worked 18 hours a day.
3店舗目、4店舗目と増やし、10年で8店舗のオーナーになった。: Added a third and fourth store, and in ten years became the owner of eight stores.
2店舗目の向かいに競合店ができ、1年で撤退した。: A competitor opened across from the second store, and I pulled out within a year.
断ったら本部の担当者に冷たくされ、売れない商品ばかり押し付けられた。: After I declined, the HQ rep gave me the cold shoulder and pushed only unsellable products on me.
浮いた時間で地域の子ども食堂に廃棄前の弁当を届け始めた。新聞に載った。: With the time I saved, I began delivering unsold lunch boxes to a local children's cafeteria. It made the newspaper.
アルバイトの大学生が卒業後に本部に就職し、何かと助けてくれるようになった。: A part-time college student joined HQ after graduating and kept helping me out in all sorts of ways.
契約更新の時期が来た。この10年、休みはほとんどなかった。: Time to renew the contract. For these ten years, I'd barely had a day off.
もう10年頑張ることにした。: Decided to push on for another ten years.
体を壊して入院した。: Ruined my health and was hospitalized.
更新した翌年、自動レジ導入で人手が半分で済み、初めて週2日休めるようになった。: The year after renewing, automatic checkouts halved the staffing I needed, and for the first time I got two days off a week.
契約更新の日に本部の担当者から店長会の会長を頼まれた。: On renewal day, the HQ rep asked me to serve as chair of the store managers' association.
店を閉めた。最後の日、常連さんが花束をくれた。: Closed the store. On the last day, a regular gave me a bouquet.
店を閉めた後、常連さんたちと立ち上げた地域の喫茶店が繁盛した。: After closing the store, a community café I started with the regulars thrived.
10年分の疲れが一気に出て、半年間寝込んだ。: Ten years of fatigue hit all at once, and I was bedridden for six months.
閉店後、旅行に出たら40か国を回っていた。貯金が300万円減った。: After closing, I went traveling and ended up visiting 40 countries. My savings dropped by 3 million yen.
店長候補として、研修を受けないかと言われた。: Offered a training course as a store manager candidate.
店長になり、年収が600万円になった。: Became store manager, and my annual income reached 6 million yen.
業界の縮小で、店が閉店した。: The industry shrank and the store closed.
研修で知り合った他店の店長候補と結婚した。: Married a manager candidate from another store whom I met at training.
店長になった後、閉店寸前の店を2年で黒字化し、エリア長になった。: After becoming manager, turned a nearly closed store profitable in two years and was promoted to area manager.
耳鳴りがなくなった。: The ringing in my ears went away.
辞めた後、ホールの経験を活かしてゲームセンターの店長になった。: After quitting, I used my floor experience to become manager of an arcade.
辞めた翌年、景品交換所のおばちゃんから「戻っておいで」と手紙が来た。: The year after I quit, the lady at the prize exchange counter sent me a letter: “Come back.”
転職先が倒産し、半年間アルバイトで食いつないだ。: My new employer went bankrupt, and I scraped by on part-time jobs for six months.
常連さんが生活費まで使い込んでいるようだ。顔色が悪い。: A regular seems to be spending even his living expenses here. He looks unwell.
相談窓口のチラシを受け取ってくれた。半年後、元気な顔で挨拶に来た。: He accepted a flyer for a counseling service. Half a year later, he came by to greet me looking well.
声をかけたことで常連さんの奥さんから感謝の電話が来た。家族が立ち直ったと聞いた。: Because I spoke up, the regular's wife called to thank me. I heard the family got back on its feet.
その常連さんが実は店の大口のオーナーの親戚で、本部に苦情が入った。: That regular turned out to be a relative of one of the shop's major owners, and a complaint went to headquarters.
その人はいつの間にか来なくなった。: Before I knew it, he stopped coming.
1年後、その常連さんが店の前で倒れ、救急車で運ばれた。自分を責めた。: A year later, that regular collapsed in front of the store and was taken away by ambulance. I blamed myself.
何も言わなかったが、ジュースを1本おごった。それだけで彼は少し笑った。: I said nothing, but I bought him a can of juice. That alone made him smile a little.
その人が宝くじで1,000万円当て、店に来なくなったと噂で聞いた。: I heard through rumors that he won 10 million yen in the lottery and stopped coming to the store.
家族葬専門の小さな葬儀社を開業しないかと、先輩に誘われた。: A senior colleague invited me to open a small funeral home specializing in family funerals.
地域の評判になり、年100件を担当した。: It earned a good local reputation, and I handled 100 funerals a year.
大手の価格に負けて、2年で閉業した。: Lost out to the big chains on price and closed in two years.
開業10年で地域シェア3割を取り、大手から5億円で買収の話が来た。: Ten years after opening, I held a 30% local market share, and a major company offered to buy me out for 500 million yen.
開業初日に初めての依頼が来たのが、誘ってくれた先輩の父親の葬儀だった。: The first request on opening day was the funeral of the father of the senior who had invited me.
安定した給料で続けた。: Carried on with a steady salary.
会社に残ったら、先輩の開業した葬儀社が大手に吸収された。自分の判断は正しかった。: After I stayed, the funeral home my senior opened was absorbed by a big company. My decision was right.
会社に残ったら社内の葬祭ディレクター1級に合格し、部長になった。: After staying, I passed the company's Grade 1 funeral director exam and became a department head.
残った会社が業績悪化でリストラを始め、自分も対象になった。: The company I stayed at hit hard times, started layoffs, and I was on the list.
遺族から、予算がないので最低限でいいと言われた。会社は追加プランを売れと言う。: The bereaved family said they had no budget and just wanted the bare minimum. The company told me to sell add-on plans.
遺族に感謝され、後日お菓子が届いた。: The family thanked me, and sweets arrived later.
その遺族が知人10人に紹介してくれ、営業成績が上がった。: That family referred me to ten acquaintances, and my sales numbers improved.
遺族の希望を優先したことが社内で問題になり、3か月の減給処分になった。: Putting the family's wishes first became an internal issue, and my pay was cut for three months.
売上は上がったが、後味が悪かった。: Sales went up, but it left a bad taste.
売上を上げた月の表彰で、遺族からのクレームの手紙が読み上げられた。: At the award ceremony for the month I boosted sales, a complaint letter from a bereaved family was read aloud.
追加プランを売った遺族から、後日「父が喜んでいたと思う」とお礼を言われた。: A family I sold the add-on plan to later thanked me: “I think my father would have been happy.”
毎月の追加売上がトップになり、ボーナスが50万円増えた。: Monthly add-on sales ranked first, and my bonus rose by 500,000 yen.
販売店の店主が引退する。店を継がないかと言われた。: The newspaper dealership owner is retiring. He asked if I'd take over the shop.
ポスティング事業も始めて、なんとか黒字を保った。: Also started a flyer-distribution business and somehow stayed in the black.
部数が減り続け、5年で廃業した。: Circulation kept falling, and the shop closed in five years.
店を継いだ後、高齢者の見守りサービスを始め、市の委託事業で年間500万円の収入に: After taking over the shop, I started a watch-over service for the elderly, and a city-commissioned project brought in 5 million yen a year.
継いだ店に昔の常連さんが訪ねてきて、ずっと気にかけてくれていた叔父だとわかった。: An old regular came to the shop I took over, and he turned out to be the uncle who had always looked out for me.
別の仕事を探し始めた。: Started looking for a different job.
断った後、配達で鍛えた早起きを活かしてパン屋に就職した。: After declining, I used the early rising I'd built up from deliveries to get a job at a bakery.
断った店を大手が買収し、配達先の契約が切れた。失業手当で半年過ごした。: A big company bought the shop I turned down, and my delivery contracts were cut. I lived on unemployment benefits for six months.
断ったら店主が泣いて引き止め、結局給料2割アップで残ることになった。: When I declined, the owner broke down in tears and begged me to stay, and in the end I stayed with a 20% raise.
配達中に雪で滑ってバイクごと転んだ。新聞が道路に散らばった。: While delivering, I slipped on snow and fell with the bike. Newspapers scattered across the road.
全部拾って配る: Pick them all up and deliver
30分遅れで配り終えた。クレームは2件だった。: Finished delivering 30 minutes late. Only two complaints.
足を痛めていて、翌日歩けなかった。: I had hurt my foot and couldn't walk the next day.
拾い集めているとき通りがかった高校生5人が手伝ってくれた。翌年、その1人が配達員: Five high school students passing by helped me pick them up. The next year, one of them became a delivery person.
新聞の束を拾った隣の住民が「雪の日の配達ご苦労さま」と温かいお茶をくれた。: A neighbor who picked up the bundle of newspapers gave me hot tea, saying, “Thanks for delivering on a snowy day.”
店主が軽トラで助けに来てくれた。: The owner came to help in his mini truck.
店主がバイクを新しいものに替えてくれた。: The owner replaced my bike with a new one.
連絡したら店主に「なぜ拾わない」と怒鳴られた。: When I called, the owner yelled, “Why aren't you picking them up?”
1年後、店主が引退し、残った配達員5人で協同組合を作ることになった。: A year later, the owner retired, and the five remaining carriers formed a cooperative.
作業中、お客さんの高価な花瓶を割ってしまった。: While working, I broke a customer's expensive vase.
保険で弁償し、お客さんも許してくれた。: Paid for it through insurance, and the customer forgave me.
お客さんがものすごく怒り、会社に何度も電話が来た。: The customer was furious and called the company again and again.
お客さんが「正直に言ってくれたから」と次の引越しも指名してくれた。: The customer said, “Because you told me honestly,” and requested me for their next move too.
割れた花瓶は実は100円ショップの品だった。お客さんも笑っていた。: The broken vase turned out to be from a 100-yen shop. The customer laughed about it.
後でバレて、会社をクビになった。: It came out later, and I was fired from the company.
隠した花瓶は実は割れていても価値が変わらない骨董品だった。罪悪感だけが残った。: The vase I hid was actually an antique whose value didn't change even broken. All I was left with was guilt.
隠したことを同僚に気づかれ、5年間その同僚に頭が上がらなかった。: A coworker noticed I'd hidden it, and for five years I couldn't stand up to that coworker.
隠したまま誰にも気づかれなかった。それから10年間、花瓶を見るたび胸が痛んだ。: I hid it and nobody noticed. For the next ten years, my chest ached every time I saw a vase.
独立して軽トラ1台で引越し業を始めないかと考えた。: Thought about going independent and starting a moving business with a single mini truck.
単身者向けで評判になり、月収50万円になった。: Gained a reputation among people living alone, and my monthly income reached 500,000 yen.
腰を痛めて、半年で休業した。: Hurt my back and had to suspend business after six months.
3年後、軽トラを5台に増やし、従業員12人の会社にした。: Three years later, I grew to five mini trucks and a company of 12 employees.
初回の依頼主が大御所芸能人で、口コミがSNSで1万件拡散された。: My very first client was a big-name celebrity, and word of mouth spread to 10,000 posts on social media.
会社員として続けた。: Carried on as a company employee.
独立を諦めたかわりに会社で役職がつき、月給が5万円上がった。: Having given up on going independent, I was given a title at the company, and my monthly pay rose by 50,000 yen.
独立しなかった同僚が先に独立して成功した。: A coworker who didn't go independent at the time went independent first and succeeded.
会社の人手不足が深刻化し、毎日20件の引越しをこなす日々が続いた。: The company's labor shortage got worse, and days of handling 20 moves a day went on.
新しいアトラクションのリーダーに推薦された。: Was recommended as leader of a new attraction.
オープン初日、行列が3時間待ちになった。: On opening day, the line grew to a 3-hour wait.
トラブルが続き、責任を問われた。: Trouble kept piling up, and I was held responsible.
アトラクションのアナウンスが話題になり、SNSで100万回再生された。: The attraction's announcement went viral and got 1 million views on social media.
リーダーとしてまとめた新人のひとりと結婚した。: Married one of the newcomers I led as team leader.
今の持ち場で楽しく働いた。: Enjoyed working at my current post.
断った持ち場が翌年廃止になり、人気アトラクションに異動になった。: The post I turned down was shut down the next year, and I was transferred to a popular attraction.
断った新アトラクションが1年で閉鎖になり、ほっとした。: The new attraction I turned down closed within a year. What a relief.
着ぐるみの中の人に抜擢された。夏は地獄だった。: Was picked to be the person inside the mascot suit. Summer was hell.
お客さんが列に割り込み、他のお客さんと口論になった。: A guest cut in line and got into an argument with other guests.
うまく収めて、両方に笑顔で帰ってもらえた。: Smoothed it over, and both parties went home smiling.
怒りの矛先が自分に向き、30分怒鳴られた。: The anger turned on me, and I got yelled at for 30 minutes.
割り込みの客が実は人気YouTuberで、仲裁シーンの動画が200万回再生された: The line-cutter turned out to be a popular YouTuber, and the video of me mediating got 2 million views.
仲裁した二組が意気投合し、一緒にパレードを見ていた。: The two parties I mediated hit it off and ended up watching the parade together.
警備員がすぐに来て対応してくれた。: Security came right away and handled it.
警備員が来るまでの3分間、両方からにらまれ続けた。: For the 3 minutes until security arrived, both sides glared at me.
警備員の対応が丁寧すぎて口論が倍に長引いた。: Security was so overly polite that the argument dragged on twice as long.
警備を呼んだ判断が評価され、接客マニュアルに事例として載った。: My decision to call security was praised and added to the customer service manual as a case study.
外資系ホテルから、年収1.5倍でヘッドハンティングされた。: Was headhunted by a foreign-owned hotel for 1.5 times my salary.
英語力が伸び、5年後に支配人になった。: My English improved, and five years later I became a manager.
成果主義が厳しく、2年で燃え尽きた。: The performance-based system was brutal, and I burned out in two years.
転職先で出会った外国人のゲストと親しくなり、その人の会社に年収2,000万円で引: Became close with a foreign guest I met at my new job and was poached by their company for 20 million yen a year.
転職して半年で外資系ホテルが日本から撤退した。: Six months after I switched jobs, the foreign-owned hotel pulled out of Japan.
今のホテルで信頼を積み上げた。: Built up trust at my current hotel.
残ったホテルで総支配人になり、ホテルの売上を2倍にした。: Became general manager of the hotel I stayed at and doubled its sales.
残った直後にホテルが買収され、結局外資系の傘下になった。: Right after I decided to stay, the hotel was acquired and ended up under foreign ownership anyway.
残ったことでベテランのコンシェルジュから技を全部教わり、国際大会で入賞した。: By staying, I learned every trick from a veteran concierge and placed at an international competition.
VIPのお客さんから、無理な要求をされた。深夜に高級寿司を部屋に届けてほしいと言: A VIP guest made an unreasonable demand: he wanted high-end sushi delivered to his room in the middle of the night.
知り合いの店に頼み込んで届けた。後日、チップで3万円もらった。: Begged a shop I knew and delivered it. Later received a 30,000 yen tip.
届けたが「遅い」と怒られた。: Delivered it, but got scolded for being “too slow.”
そのVIPが有名企業の会長で、退職後に顧問として迎えられた。: That VIP was the chairman of a famous company, and after I retired he brought me on as an advisor.
深夜に寿司を届けた店の大将と仲良くなり、毎週飲みに行く仲になった。: Became friends with the owner of the sushi shop that delivered at midnight, and we now go drinking every week.
断ったらVIPが本国の口コミサイトに星1をつけた。総支配人に呼び出された。: After I declined, the VIP gave us 1 star on a review site back in his home country. I was summoned by the general manager.
VIPは丁寧な断り方を気に入り、翌年から毎年30泊予約してくれるようになった。: The VIP liked how politely I declined and began booking 30 nights every year from the following year.
代わりに出したルームサービスのおにぎりが大好評で、翌月から正式メニューになった。: The rice balls I offered through room service were a huge hit and became an official menu item the next month.
製薬会社の治験コーディネーターに転職しないかと誘われた。: Was invited to switch careers to become a clinical trial coordinator at a pharmaceutical company.
年収が100万円上がった。患者さんと話す時間が増えた。: My salary rose by 1 million yen. I got to spend more time talking with patients.
営業的な仕事が合わず、戻りたくなった。: The sales-like work didn't suit me, and I wanted to go back.
治験コーディネーターとして実績を積み、5年後に製薬会社のマネージャーになった。年: Built a track record as a clinical trial coordinator and became a manager at a pharmaceutical company five years later. Salary: 9 million yen.
担当した治験の薬が承認され、ニュースで見て鳥肌が立った。: A drug from a trial I worked on was approved. Seeing it on the news gave me goosebumps.
残った検査室で新しい遺伝子検査を立ち上げ、学会で表彰された。: Launched a new genetic test in the lab I stayed in and was honored at an academic conference.
誘ってくれた先輩が転職先で大成功し、時々うらやましくなった。: The senior colleague who invited me was a huge success at the new job, and I sometimes felt envious.
検査機器の自動化で人員が3割減らされた。: Automation of the testing equipment cut staff by 30 percent.
検体のラベルが取り違えられている可能性に気づいた。結果はもう医師に送ってある。: Noticed that the specimen labels might have been mixed up. The results have already been sent to the doctor.
再検査で取り違えが判明し、誤診を防げた。: A retest confirmed the mix-up, and a misdiagnosis was prevented.
取り違えではなかった。でも上司は「よく言った」と褒めてくれた。: It wasn't a mix-up after all. But my boss praised me, saying “Good call speaking up.”
報告したことで病院の検体管理システムが一新された。院長賞をもらった。: My report led to a complete overhaul of the hospital's specimen management system. I received the Director's Award.
報告書の書き方で上司ともめたが、最終的に半年後に師長に昇進した。: Clashed with my boss over how to write the report, but was ultimately promoted to head technologist six months later.
後日、取り違えが発覚し、大問題になった。: The mix-up came to light later and became a major problem.
取り違えではなく、ラベル印字のずれだった。何事もなかった。: It wasn't a mix-up, just a misaligned label print. Nothing came of it.
他の技師が気づいて報告し、自分は気づいていたのに言わなかったと責められた。: Another technologist noticed and reported it, and I was blamed for knowing and saying nothing.
様子を見ている間に夢に毎晩検体が出てきて、結局3日後に報告した。: While I waited and watched, specimens showed up in my dreams every night, and I ended up reporting it three days later.
放射線治療専門の技師になるため、資格を取るか迷った。: Wavered over whether to earn the certification to become a radiation therapy specialist.
合格し、治療部門に異動した。: Passed and transferred to the therapy department.
勉強が大変で、2回落ちた。: Studying was brutal, and I failed twice.
資格取得後、がん治療の専門病院に引き抜かれ、年収が150万円上がった。: After getting certified, I was recruited by a cancer treatment hospital, and my salary rose by 1.5 million yen.
治療部門で担当した患者さんが完治し、毎年年賀状をくれるようになった。: A patient I treated in the therapy department fully recovered and now sends me a New Year's card every year.
診断部門で経験を積んだ。: Gained experience in the diagnostic department.
診断部門で被ばく低減のプロトコルを作り、全国の学会で発表した。: Developed a radiation dose reduction protocol in the diagnostic department and presented it at national conferences.
資格を取った同期が先に主任になった。: A peer who got certified was promoted to chief before me.
取らずに浮いた時間でダイビングを始め、インストラクターの資格を取った。: With the time I saved by not studying, I took up diving and earned an instructor certification.
医師が不要と思えるCT検査を連発する。患者さんの被ばくが気になる。: The doctor keeps ordering CT scans that seem unnecessary. I'm worried about the patients' radiation exposure.
医師が検査を減らしてくれた。: The doctor cut back on the scans.
「技師は黙って撮れ」と言われた。: Was told, “Technologists should just shut up and take the images.”
意見したことがきっかけで、病院全体の検査適正化委員会に入った。: Speaking up led me to join the hospital-wide committee for appropriate testing.
意見した医師と後に同じ趣味の釣りで仲良くなり、今は飲み仲間だ。: The doctor I spoke up to and I later bonded over our shared hobby of fishing, and now we're drinking buddies.
10年後、被ばく線量を減らす装置の導入が決まり、少し気が晴れた。: Ten years later, a device that reduces radiation dose was adopted, and I felt a little better.
黙っていた検査が後に医療監査で指摘された。技師も事情聴取された。: The scans I stayed quiet about were later flagged in a medical audit. The technologists were questioned too.
もやもやが溜まって転職した。: The unease built up, and I changed jobs.
訪問リハビリの事業所から、給料1.3倍で誘われた。: A home-visit rehabilitation agency offered me 1.3 times my salary.
運転時間が長く、思ったより大変だった。: The long driving hours made it harder than expected.
訪問先の利用者さんの紹介で、別の事業所から所長として招かれた。: Through a client I visited, I was invited by another agency to be its director.
訪問中に車をぶつけ、修理代20万円を自腹で払った。: Crashed the car during a visit and paid 200,000 yen for repairs out of pocket.
病院でリハビリ部門の主任になった。: Became chief of the rehabilitation department at the hospital.
誘いを断った事業所が地域で1番の規模になった。: The agency whose offer I turned down grew to be the largest in the region.
病院のリハビリ部門で、患者さんが作った陶芸作品の展示会を企画し、500人が来た。: In the hospital's rehabilitation department, I organized an exhibition of pottery made by patients, and 500 people came.
患者さんが「もうリハビリしたくない」と言った。: A patient said, “I don't want to do rehab anymore.”
結果的に回復し、感謝された。: In the end the patient recovered and thanked me.
関係が悪くなり、担当を外された。: The relationship soured, and I was taken off the case.
無理に続けた患者さんが後でクレームを入れ、リハビリ方針の見直し会議に呼ばれた。: The patient I pushed later filed a complaint, and I was called to a meeting to review rehab policy.
無理に続けた結果、患者さんが自力で歩いて退院した。最後に握手を求められた。: After I pushed on, the patient walked out of the hospital on their own. At the end, they asked to shake my hand.
園芸をきっかけに、リハビリに前向きになってくれた。: Gardening got the patient to take a more positive attitude toward rehab.
結局、気持ちは戻らなかった。: In the end, the patient's motivation never came back.
園芸で育てたトマトを病棟全員にふるまってくれた。: The patient treated the whole ward to tomatoes grown through gardening.
好きなことから始める手法を論文にまとめ、学会で賞をもらった。: Wrote up the approach of starting with what patients like in a paper and won an award at a conference.
ことばの教室を自分で開こうか考えた。: Thought about opening my own speech therapy classroom.
口コミで広がり、予約が半年先まで埋まった。: Word of mouth spread, and bookings filled up six months ahead.
集客に苦労し、2年で病院勤務に戻った。: Struggled to attract clients and went back to hospital work after two years.
教室の卒業生のひとりが、10年後に弁論大会で全国優勝したと連絡をくれた。: One of the classroom's graduates contacted me ten years later to say they had won a national speech contest.
教室の家賃が上がり、月10万円の赤字が1年続いた。: The classroom's rent went up, and I ran a 100,000 yen monthly deficit for a year.
病院でSTの主任になり、後輩を5人育てた。: Became chief speech therapist at the hospital and trained five juniors.
開業を諦めた分、ことばの教室を手伝うボランティアを週1で始めた。: Having given up on opening my own, I started volunteering once a week at a speech therapy classroom.
同期が開業して大成功し、少しうらやましかった。: A peer opened a practice and was hugely successful. I was a little envious.
患者さんの家族が、食べられないのに好物を食べさせたいと言う。: A patient's family wants them to eat their favorite food, even though they can't eat.
形態を工夫して実現する: Adjust the texture to make it happen
ペースト状のお寿司を一口食べて、患者さんが笑った。: The patient took a bite of pureed sushi and smiled.
むせてしまい、ヒヤッとした。: The patient choked, and it gave me a scare.
その患者さんの最期の食事が好物のお寿司になった。家族から手紙が届いた。: Sushi became that patient's last meal. A letter arrived from the family.
工夫したペースト食のレシピが病院の正式メニューになった。: The pureed-meal recipe I devised became an official hospital menu item.
リスクを説明して止める: Explain the risks and say no
家族は納得したが、少し寂しそうだった。: The family understood, but looked a little sad.
家族の不満が募り、病院にクレームが入った。: The family's dissatisfaction grew, and a complaint was lodged with the hospital.
1か月後、嚥下機能が回復し、本物の好物を食べられた。: A month later, the patient's swallowing recovered, and they could eat their real favorite food.
リスクを説明する資料を作り、病院全体で使われるようになった。: Made materials explaining the risks, and they came to be used throughout the hospital.
海外で歯科技工士として働かないかと誘われた。給料は2倍。: Was invited to work abroad as a dental technician. Double the pay.
技術が評価され、10年で独立した。: My skills were recognized, and I went independent in ten years.
言葉が通じず、1年で帰国した。: Couldn't communicate in the language and returned home after a year.
現地で出会った歯科医と結婚し、二人で歯科医院を開いた。: Married a dentist I met there, and we opened a dental clinic together.
海外で覚えたデジタル技工の技術で帰国後に独立し、年収1,000万円になった。: After returning home, I went independent with the digital dental technology I learned abroad, and my income reached 10 million yen a year.
日本で技術を磨き続けた。: Kept honing my skills in Japan.
日本で技工所を開業し、10人の技工士を雇った。: Opened a dental laboratory in Japan and hired ten technicians.
海外に行った同期が帰国後、自分の上司になった。: A peer who went abroad came back and became my boss.
残った技工所が人手不足で、月300時間働いた。: The lab I stayed at was short-staffed, and I worked 300 hours a month.
取引先の歯科医院が、技工料を2割下げてくれと言ってきた。: A client dental clinic asked me to cut my lab fees by 20 percent.
仕事は続いたが、さらに忙しくなった。: The work continued, but I got even busier.
2割下げた分を補おうと夜中まで働き、腱鞘炎になった。: Worked until midnight to make up for the 20 percent cut and developed tendonitis.
値下げを受け入れた見返りに、その医院から別の3医院を紹介された。: In return for accepting the price cut, that clinic introduced me to three other clinics.
3年後、同じ医院がさらに1割下げてくれと言ってきた。: Three years later, the same clinic asked for another 10 percent cut.
別の医院から高単価の仕事が入った。: A high-paying job came in from another clinic.
取引が打ち切られた。: The business relationship was cut off.
断った医院が後で「やはり君の技工でなければ」と元の値段で戻ってきた。: The clinic I turned down came back later at the original price, saying, “It has to be your work after all.”
断ったことが業界団体の会合で話題になり、「値下げに応じない技工士の会」が発足した: My refusal became a talking point at an industry association meeting, and a “Society of Technicians Who Won't Cut Prices” was formed.
自分の接骨院を開業するチャンスが来た。: A chance came to open my own bonesetting clinic.
地域の人気院になり、月商200万円になった。: It became a popular local clinic, with monthly sales of 2 million yen.
近所に3軒の接骨院ができ、競争に負けて閉院した。: Three bonesetting clinics opened nearby, and I lost the competition and closed.
開業した接骨院がプロ野球選手の御用達になり、テレビで紹介された。: The clinic I opened became a favorite of professional baseball players and was featured on TV.
開業初日、来院者は大家さん1人だけだった。: On opening day, the only visitor was my landlord.
勤めていた院で分院長に昇格した。: Was promoted to branch director at the clinic where I worked.
開業した同期の院が潰れ、その患者さんたちが自分のところに流れてきた。: A peer's newly opened clinic went under, and its patients came over to mine.
院長が引退し、店をそのまま安く譲り受けた。: The director retired, and I took over the clinic as is at a low price.
院長から、保険の不正請求に加担するよう言われた。: The director told me to take part in fraudulent insurance billing.
院長と険悪になり、退職した。: Relations with the director turned ugly, and I quit.
院長が改心した。: The director had a change of heart.
断ったことを他の職員にも話し、全員で労働基準監督署に相談した。院長は処分を受けた: I told the other staff about my refusal, and we all consulted the Labor Standards Inspection Office together. The director was disciplined.
院長に「もう二度と頼まない」と言われ、その後は普通に働けた。: The director said, “I'll never ask you again,” and after that I could work normally.
数年後に発覚し、資格停止になった。: It came to light a few years later, and my license was suspended.
院長の指示に従ったまま数年が過ぎた。毎晩眠れなかった。: Years passed as I kept following the director's orders. I couldn't sleep at night.
不正に加担した分の報酬で車を買ったが、良心の呵責で1年で売った。: Bought a car with the money from the fraud, but guilt drove me to sell it within a year.
監査で発覚し、院長だけでなく自分も返還金300万円を求められた。: The fraud was uncovered in an audit, and not just the director but I too was ordered to repay 3 million yen.
SNSで話題になり、予約が3か月先まで埋まった。: It took off on social media, and bookings filled up three months ahead.
美容鍼が雑誌で特集され、年収が800万円になった。: Cosmetic acupuncture was featured in a magazine, and my income rose to 8 million yen a year.
美容鍼で内出血を起こし、お客さんに訴えられた。: A cosmetic acupuncture session caused bruising, and the customer sued me.
地域のお年寄りの間で評判になり、毎日20人が来院するようになった。: Word spread among the local elderly, and 20 people began visiting every day.
美容鍼に特化した同期の店が流行り、比べられることが増えた。: A peer's cosmetic acupuncture clinic became trendy, and I was compared to it more often.
今のままでいたら、腰痛のプロスポーツ選手が偶然来院し、専属契約を結んだ。: Staying as I was, a pro athlete with back pain happened to visit, and I signed an exclusive contract.
海外のスポーツチームから、専属鍼灸師にならないかと誘われた。: A foreign sports team invited me to become its team acupuncturist.
チームが優勝し、選手たちに感謝された。: The team won the championship, and the players thanked me.
監督が変わって契約が切れた。: The coach changed, and my contract ended.
チームのスター選手の口利きで、海外のセレブ専門クリニックに招かれた。: Through a word from the team's star player, I was invited to an overseas clinic for celebrities.
現地の言葉が話せず、選手と身振り手振りでやりとりする日々だった。: I couldn't speak the local language, so my days were spent communicating with the players through gestures.
断った後、そのチームのライバルチームから同じ誘いが来た。: After I declined, that team's rival sent the same offer.
断ったチームが優勝し、テレビで見ていて少し悔しかった。: The team I turned down won the championship, and watching it on TV, I felt a little regretful.
地元の高校サッカー部のトレーナーを無償で引き受け、全国大会に出場した。: Volunteered as trainer for a local high school soccer team, and they made it to the national tournament.
出張トリミングの車を買って独立しないかと考えた。: Thought about buying a mobile grooming van and going independent.
高齢の飼い主さんに喜ばれ、予約が埋まった。: Elderly pet owners were delighted, and my schedule filled up.
車のローンが重く、苦しい日々が続いた。: The van loan weighed heavily, and hard days dragged on.
出張トリミングがテレビで紹介され、予約が半年先まで埋まった。: Mobile grooming was featured on TV, and bookings filled up six months ahead.
車で犬を運ぶ途中、犬が車酔いして車内が大惨事になった。: While driving a dog, it got carsick and the inside of the van became a disaster.
お店で店長になり、トリミングのコンテストで全国3位になった。: Became shop manager and placed third nationally in a grooming contest.
お店のオーナーが引退し、店を引き継いだ。: The shop owner retired, and I took over the shop.
独立した同期が予約で埋まり、自分の常連さんも何人か移っていった。: A peer who went independent got fully booked, and some of my regulars moved over to them.
トリミング中、犬の体にしこりを見つけた。: While grooming, I found a lump on a dog's body.
早期の腫瘍で、手術で治った。飼い主さんから手紙が来た。: It was an early-stage tumor and was cured by surgery. A letter came from the owner.
ただの脂肪腫だった。でも感謝された。: It was just a harmless fatty lump. But the owner thanked me anyway.
その飼い主さんが動物病院の院長で、病院のトリミング部門を任された。: That owner was the director of an animal hospital, and I was entrusted with the hospital's grooming department.
しこりの話をしたら飼い主さんが動揺し、それ以来来なくなった。: When I mentioned the lump, the owner was shaken and never came back.
後で気になって眠れなかった。: It bothered me afterward, and I couldn't sleep.
次のトリミングの時、しこりが大きくなっていた。今度はすぐに伝えた。: At the next grooming, the lump had grown. This time I told them right away.
他のトリマーが気づいて伝えた。飼い主さんは店を移った。: Another groomer noticed and told the owner. The owner switched shops.
半年後、飼い主さんが自分で気づいて病院に行った。無事だった。: Six months later, the owner noticed it themselves and went to the vet. The dog was fine.
ペット保険会社から、年収1.4倍で誘われた。: A pet insurance company offered me 1.4 times my salary.
給料は上がったが、動物に触れる時間はなくなった。: My pay went up, but I no longer had time to touch animals.
現場が恋しくて、1年で戻った。: I missed working on the floor and went back after a year.
ペット保険の商品開発に関わり、全国の飼い主が使う保険を作った。: Took part in developing pet insurance products and created a policy used by pet owners nationwide.
転職先の同僚と結婚した。: Married a coworker from my new job.
残った動物病院で主任になった。: Became chief at the animal hospital I stayed at.
院長が引退し、新しい院長と方針が合わずにもめた。: The director retired, and I clashed with the new director over policy.
担当していた犬が20歳の長寿で表彰され、飼い主さんと一緒に泣いた。: A dog I looked after was honored for living to age 20, and I cried together with its owner.
保護猫を1匹、家に連れて帰りたくなった。: Felt like taking one rescue cat home.
一緒に暮らし始め、毎日が少し楽しくなった。: We started living together, and every day became a little more fun.
アレルギーが出て、知人に譲った。: I developed an allergy and gave the cat to an acquaintance.
その猫が猫のモデルとしてスカウトされ、CMに出た。: The cat was scouted as a cat model and appeared in a TV commercial.
猫がすぐに子猫を5匹産んだ。: The cat soon gave birth to five kittens.
いい里親が見つかった。: A good foster family was found.
見送った猫が数年後、里親さんと一緒に動物病院に来て元気な姿を見せてくれた。: A few years later, the cat I let go came to the animal hospital with its adoptive family and showed me it was doing well.
次に入ってきた保護猫を家に連れて帰った。: Took the next rescue cat that came in home with me.
見送った後、自分で保護猫カフェを始めた。: After letting it go, I started my own rescue cat cafe.
自宅サロンを開業しようか考えた。: Thought about opening a home salon.
常連さんがついてきてくれ、月収40万円になった。: My regulars followed me, and my monthly income reached 400,000 yen.
集客に苦労し、SNSに張り付く日々が続いた。: Struggled to find clients and spent my days glued to social media.
自宅サロンにアイドルが来店し、その様子がSNSで拡散された。: An idol visited my home salon, and word of it spread on social media.
自宅サロンで子どもが走り回り、お客さんにジェルを付けてしまった。: My kid ran around the home salon and got gel on a customer.
お店で指名1位になり、全国コンテストで入賞した。: Became the shop's top-requested nail artist and placed in a national contest.
お店で新人に教える立場になり、後輩が10人育った。: Became a trainer for newcomers at the shop and brought up ten juniors.
お店の経営者が変わり、指名料が廃止された。: The shop's management changed, and the request fee was abolished.
お客さんに、爪の状態が悪いのにジェルを続けてほしいと頼まれた。: A customer asked me to keep doing gel on her nails even though they were in bad shape.
お客さんは納得して、爪がきれいに戻った。: The customer understood, and her nails returned to health.
断ったお客さんが半年後に戻ってきて、それ以来常連になった。: The customer I turned away came back six months later and has been a regular ever since.
爪のケア講座を始めたら人気になった。: I started a nail care class, and it became popular.
爪がさらに傷んでしまった。: Her nails got even more damaged.
そのお客さんが爪のトラブルでSNSにサロンの悪評を書いた。: That customer, over her nail trouble, wrote bad reviews of the salon on social media.
言われたとおりにしたら、お客さんが友人を5人紹介してくれた。: I did as she asked, and she introduced five friends to me.
爪の病気が悪化し、皮膚科に通うことになったお客さんに謝った。: Her nail condition worsened, and she had to start seeing a dermatologist. I apologized to her.
高額コースを渋るお客さんに、店長が「もっと押せ」と言う。: For a customer hesitating over the expensive course, the manager says, “Push harder.”
契約が取れ、店長に褒められた。: Closed the deal and was praised by the manager.
お客さんが消費者センターに相談し、大問題になった。: The customer consulted a consumer affairs center, and it became a major problem.
契約で店舗の売上が月100万円上がり、店長に昇格した。: The contract raised the store's monthly sales by 1 million yen, and I was promoted to manager.
契約したお客さんが後日感謝の手紙をくれた。肌がきれいになったという。: The customer who signed sent me a thank-you letter later. She said her skin had become beautiful.
お客さんとの信頼関係は続いた。: My trust-based relationship with the customer continued.
押さなかったお客さんが3年通ってくれ、総額で高額コースを上回った。: The customer I didn't push kept coming for three years, and her total spending exceeded the cost of the expensive course.
押さなかったことで店長に怒られ、地方の店舗に異動になった。: The manager was angry that I didn't push, and I was transferred to a rural branch.
押さなかった姿勢が口コミで広がり、指名が月50件になった。: My no-pressure approach spread by word of mouth, and requests reached 50 a month.
自分のサロンを開きたいと思った。: Wanted to open my own salon.
口コミで人気になった。: Became popular by word of mouth.
資金繰りに苦しみ、2年で閉めた。: Struggled with cash flow and closed after two years.
開業したサロンが美容雑誌で特集され、予約が3か月先まで埋まった。: The salon I opened was featured in a beauty magazine, and bookings filled up three months ahead.
開業1年目は毎月赤字で、親から300万円借りた。: The first year after opening ran at a loss every month, and I borrowed 3 million yen from my parents.
雇われのまま技術を磨き、業界のコンテストで優勝した。: Stayed an employee and honed my skills, then won an industry contest.
雇われ先が倒産し、別のサロンに移った。: My employer went bankrupt, and I moved to another salon.
雇われのまま、オーナーから店舗の共同経営を持ちかけられた。: While still an employee, the owner proposed that we co-manage the shop.
フランスへ修業に行くチャンスが来た。費用は自己負担。: A chance came to go train in France. Costs out of pocket.
本場の技術を身につけ、帰国後に引き抜かれた。: Mastered authentic techniques and was poached after returning home.
言葉の壁で苦労したが、一生の思い出になった。: The language barrier was tough, but it became a memory for life.
フランスでの修業中に作ったケーキが現地のコンクールで優勝した。: A cake I made while training in France won a local competition.
フランスで恋人ができ、10年住み続けた。: Got a partner in France and ended up living there for ten years.
日本で腕を磨き、地元の有名店のシェフになった。: Honed my skills in Japan and became chef at a famous local shop.
フランス帰りの同僚にシェフの座を取られた。: A coworker back from France took the chef position from me.
日本の素材にこだわったケーキが、海外のコンクールで入賞した。: A cake made with a focus on Japanese ingredients placed at an overseas competition.
SNSでバズったケーキの注文が、1日300件来た。: A cake that went viral on social media brought in 300 orders a day.
徹夜で作り、売上が過去最高になった。: Baked all night, and sales hit an all-time high.
品質が落ちてクレームが殺到した。: Quality dropped, and complaints flooded in.
300件全部作り切った後、3日間眠り続けた。: After finishing all 300 orders, I slept for three days straight.
そのケーキが雑誌の表紙を飾り、店の売上が年1億円になった。: That cake made a magazine cover, and the shop's sales reached 100 million yen a year.
予約は半年待ちになったが、品質は守れた。: Reservations had a six-month wait, but I kept the quality up.
絞った結果、希少価値が上がり、1個5,000円でも売れるようになった。: By limiting supply, the rarity value rose, and it sold even at 5,000 yen each.
絞ったことで「感じが悪い」とSNSで叩かれた。: Limiting orders got me bashed on social media as “unfriendly.”
予約待ちの人の中に、10年前に別れた恋人の名前があった。: Among the people on the waiting list was the name of a partner I broke up with ten years ago.
有名アーティストの専属にならないかと誘われた。: Was invited to become the exclusive artist's personal staff for a famous musician.
全国ツアーに同行し、名前が業界に知られた。: Went along on a national tour, and my name became known in the industry.
アーティストのわがままに振り回され、1年で辞めた。: Was run ragged by the artist's whims and quit after a year.
ツアー先で知り合った俳優の専属にもなり、年収が1,200万円になった。: Also became the personal makeup artist of an actor I met on tour, and my annual income reached 12 million yen.
アーティストが活動休止し、半年で仕事がなくなった。: The artist went on hiatus, and within six months the work dried up.
いろんな現場で経験を積んだ。: Gained experience at all kinds of sets.
フリーで撮影現場を回り、映画のメイク監督に抜擢された。: Worked film sets as a freelancer and was picked as head makeup artist for a movie.
断ったアーティストが大ブレイクし、少し悔しかった。: The artist I turned down became a huge star, which stung a little.
フリーの現場で知り合ったカメラマンと結婚した。: Married a photographer I met on a freelance job.
YouTubeでメイク講座を始めようか考えた。: Considered starting a makeup tutorial channel on YouTube.
登録者が30万人になり、コスメのコラボ商品を出した。: Reached 300,000 subscribers and released a collaboration cosmetics line.
再生数が伸びず、半年でやめた。: Views never took off, and I quit after six months.
YouTubeのメイク動画をきっかけに化粧品会社のアンバサダーになった。年間契約: My YouTube makeup videos led to becoming a brand ambassador for a cosmetics company. A yearly contract worth 5 million yen.
動画の撮影で自分の顔にメイクした回だけが1,000万回再生された。: Of all my videos, only the one where I did makeup on my own face hit 10 million views.
YouTubeを始めた後輩が大成功し、仕事を回してもらうようになった。: A junior who started on YouTube became hugely successful and began passing work my way.
現場の仕事に集中した結果、業界の賞を取った。: Focusing on work on set paid off with an industry award.
YouTubeをやらなかったが、現場で撮った写真をInstagramに載せたら1: Didn’t do YouTube, but photos from the set posted on Instagram gained 10,000 followers.
新郎が式の3日前に逃げた。新婦から連絡が来た。: The groom ran off three days before the wedding. The bride contacted me.
キャンセルの手続きを一緒にした。半年後、新婦から感謝の手紙が届いた。: Went through the cancellation procedures together. Half a year later, a thank-you letter arrived from the bride.
新婦が1年後、別の相手との結婚式を自分に依頼してくれた。: A year later, the bride asked me to plan her wedding to someone else.
逃げた新郎が後日戻ってきて、2人は同じ式場で式を挙げた。: The groom who ran off came back later, and the two held their wedding at the same venue.
キャンセル料の説明をした。重い気持ちになった。: Explained the cancellation fees. It left me feeling heavy.
キャンセル料を払った新婦から、会社宛てにクレームが入った。: The bride who paid the cancellation fee sent a complaint to the company.
規定通りに対応した姿勢を評価され、社内研修のお手本にされた。: My by-the-book handling was praised and used as a model in internal training.
その後、新婦が友人の結婚式場で自分を見つけ、笑顔で挨拶してくれた。: Later, the bride spotted me at a friend’s wedding venue and greeted me with a smile.
フリーランスのプランナーとして独立しないかと考えた。: Thought about going independent as a freelance planner.
集客に苦しみ、副業を始めた。: Struggled to find clients and took up a side job.
独立後、有名人の結婚式を担当し、SNSで話題になった。: After going independent, I handled a celebrity’s wedding, and it became a hot topic on social media.
独立して1年目、依頼は3件だけだった。: In my first year on my own, I got only three jobs.
会社に残り、10年後に支店長になった。: Stayed with the company and became a branch manager ten years later.
残った会社が別の会社と合併し、プランナーの数が半分になった。: The company I stayed with merged with another, and the number of planners was cut in half.
会社に残ったまま、担当した夫婦の子どもの結婚式も担当した。: Stayed with the company and even planned the wedding of a couple’s child whose own wedding I had handled.
海外ツアー中、お客さんが急病で倒れた。: During an overseas tour, a customer suddenly fell ill and collapsed.
お客さんは回復し、帰国後に感謝の手紙が届いた。: The customer recovered, and a thank-you letter arrived after they returned home.
残りのツアー客から「ほったらかしだ」とクレームが来た。: The rest of the tour group complained, saying “You neglected us.”
回復したお客さんが大手企業の社長で、社員旅行の幹事を毎年任された。: The recovered customer was the president of a major company, and I was entrusted with organizing its company trip every year.
