2年目に病院が経営難で閉院し、北海道で職探しをする羽目になった。: In my second year the hospital closed due to financial trouble, and I ended up job hunting in Hokkaido.
気心の知れた職場で続けた。収入は相変わらずだが、相談者は待っていてくれた。: Kept going at workplaces I knew well. Income stayed the same, but my clients were waiting for me.
翌年、1か所の契約が打ち切られ、月収が8万円減った。: The next year, one of my contracts was terminated and my monthly income fell by 80,000 yen.
非常勤先の一つで研修講師を頼まれ、1回5万円の講演依頼が年10本来るようになった: One of my part-time workplaces asked me to be a training instructor, and soon I was getting ten lecture requests a year at 50,000 yen each.
気づけば10年非常勤のまま。同業の後輩に常勤ポストを先に取られた。: Before I knew it, ten years had passed as a part-timer. A junior in my field landed a full-time post before me.
新生児訪問で、母親が明らかに疲れ切っていて「大丈夫です」としか言わない。: On a newborn home visit, the mother was clearly exhausted and would only say, “I’m fine.”
3回目の訪問で母親が泣き出し、産後うつの治療につながった。1年後、笑顔で健診に来: On the third visit the mother broke down in tears, which led to treatment for postpartum depression. A year later, she came to the checkup smiling.
「監視されてるみたい」と苦情が入り、上司に注意された。: A complaint came in saying “It feels like I’m being watched,” and my boss warned me.
1年後、その母親が子育てサークルを立ち上げ、毎月15組の親子が集まるようになった: A year later, that mother started a parenting circle, and 15 parent-child pairs now gather every month.
毎週通ううちに自分の睡眠が削れ、3か月で体重が4kg落ちた。: Going every week ate into my own sleep, and I lost 4 kg in three months.
電話では明るかった。たぶん大丈夫だったと思う。: She sounded cheerful on the phone. I think she was probably fine.
半年後、別ルートで深刻な状態が分かった。もっと行けばよかったと何年も思った。: Six months later, I learned through another channel that her condition was serious. For years I wished I had gone more.
母親が電話口で突然「実は」と話し始め、2時間の電話で支援につながった。: The mother suddenly began with “Actually...” on the phone, and a two-hour call led to support.
電話がつながらなくなり、転居したことを3か月後に知った。: The phone stopped connecting, and three months later I learned she had moved away.
民間企業の産業保健師に転職しないかと誘われた。年収は+100万円、土日休み確定。: I was invited to switch to a private company as an occupational health nurse. Pay up 1 million yen a year, with weekends guaranteed off.
大手メーカーの健康管理室に移った。災害対応の夜間呼び出しがなくなり、よく眠れるよ: Moved to the health management office of a major manufacturer. The nighttime disaster call-outs ended, and I slept well again.
大手メーカーの健康管理室: Health management office of a major manufacturer
ストレスチェック集計とメンタル休職者の面談ばかりで、地域が恋しくなった。: It was all stress-check tabulations and interviews with employees on mental health leave, and I began to miss the community.
健康施策が評価され、社長表彰で金一封30万円をもらった。: My health initiatives were recognized, and I received a 300,000 yen cash prize from the president.
半年で会社が健康管理室を外注化し、契約社員に切り替えられた。: Within six months the company outsourced the health management office, and I was switched to a contract employee.
係長に昇進した。地域の顔なじみも増えた。: Was promoted to section chief. I also came to know more familiar faces in the community.
大雨災害で避難所に2週間詰めた。腰を痛めた。: After heavy-rain disasters, I was stationed at an evacuation shelter for two weeks. I hurt my back.
感染症流行時に保健所の司令塔になり、地元紙に「町を守った人」と載った。: During an infectious disease outbreak, I became the command center of the health center, and the local paper called me “the person who protected the town.”
同期が民間に移って年収で150万円差がつき、飲み会で話題を避けるようになった。: A peer moved to the private sector and our annual incomes diverged by 1.5 million yen, so I began avoiding the topic at drinking parties.
病院を辞めて、助産院を開業しないかという話が出た。開業資金は800万円。: There was talk of leaving the hospital and opening a midwifery clinic. Startup costs: 8 million yen.
口コミで年間60件のお産を扱う人気助産院になった。休みは消えたが、誇らしかった。: Through word of mouth it became a popular midwifery clinic handling 60 births a year. My days off vanished, but I felt proud.
嘱託医が見つからず、2年で閉院した。借金が残った。: Couldn’t find a consulting physician and closed after two years. Debt remained.
助産院で生まれた子が10年後に職業体験で訪ねてきて「ここで生まれました」と言った: Ten years later, a child born at the clinic came for a job-experience program and said, “I was born here.”
開業1年目は月の休みが2日しかなく、腰を痛めて整体に月3万円使った。: In the first year after opening, I got only two days off a month, hurt my back, and spent 30,000 yen a month on chiropractic care.
主任助産師になった。後輩の育成が楽しくなってきた。: Became a head midwife. Training junior staff started to be enjoyable.
夜勤続きで体を壊し、日勤のみの外来に移った。: Back-to-back night shifts wrecked my health, so I moved to a day-shift-only outpatient clinic.
病院の院内助産を立ち上げ、年間100件のお産を任されるようになった。: Launched the hospital’s in-house midwifery program and came to be entrusted with 100 births a year.
病院が分娩取扱いをやめ、婦人科病棟の看護に回された。: The hospital stopped handling deliveries, and I was reassigned to nursing in the gynecology ward.
分娩中、ベテラン医師の判断に違和感を覚えた。言えば角が立つ。: During a delivery, I felt uneasy about a veteran doctor’s judgment. Speaking up would cause friction.
医師が方針を変え、緊急帝王切開で母子とも無事だった。後で医師に「助かった」と言わ: The doctor changed course and an emergency C-section left mother and baby safe. Later the doctor said, “You saved us.”
結果的に問題はなく、医師との関係がぎくしゃくした。: In the end there was no problem, and things got awkward with the doctor.
後日、医師から「あのとき言ってくれて助かった」と飲みに誘われ、以後チームの雰囲気: Later the doctor invited me for a drink, saying, “Thanks for speaking up back then.” The team's atmosphere changed after that.
師長に呼ばれ「医師に意見するなら手順を踏め」と始末書を書かされた。: The head nurse called me in, said, “If you question a doctor, follow procedure,” and made me write an apology report.
何事もなく生まれた。心配しすぎだったようだ。: The baby was born without incident. I seem to have worried too much.
赤ちゃんがNICUに入った。あのとき言えばよかったと何日も考えた。: The baby went into the NICU. For days I kept thinking I should have said something.
医師が自分で方針を変え、後で「君も気づいてた？」と聞かれて正直に答えた。笑われた: The doctor changed course on his own, and later asked, “Did you notice too?” I answered honestly. He laughed, but I earned his respect.
同じ医師で2度目のヒヤリハットが起き、病院が事故調査委員会を開いた。: The same doctor had a second near-miss, and the hospital convened an accident investigation committee.
役員が「売上が伸びた」と言える分析結果を求めてきた。データを素直に見ると、施策の: An executive wanted analysis results that would let him say “sales grew.” Read honestly, the data shows the campaign had almost no effect.
役員は不機嫌だったが、CFOに「信頼できる」と評価された。: The executive was in a bad mood, but the CFO said I could be trusted.
次のプロジェクトから外された。: I was taken off the next project.
1年後、施策の失敗を見抜いた分析が評価され、データ部門の部長に抜擢された。: A year later, the analysis that saw through the campaign's failure was recognized, and I was promoted to head of the data department.
役員が別の分析会社に依頼し、その会社は300万円で「効果あり」と報告した。: The executive hired another analytics firm, which reported “effective” for 3 million yen.
都合のいい切り口で見せる: Present it from a convenient angle
会議は円満に終わり、評価も上がった。少しだけ自分が嫌になった。: The meeting ended smoothly and my evaluation went up. I disliked myself a little.
翌年、同じ施策に5億円投資されて失敗し、元の分析が掘り返された。: The next year, 500 million yen was invested in the same campaign and it failed, and the original analysis was dug up.
その切り口が社内のテンプレートになり、自分の名前のついた分析手法が5年使われた。: That angle became an in-house template, and an analysis method bearing my name was used for five years.
社内監査で分析の恣意性を指摘され、評価が2段階下がった。: An internal audit pointed out that my analysis was arbitrary, and my rating dropped two grades.
外資テック企業から年収1400万円のオファーが来た。今は700万円。: A foreign tech company offered 14 million yen a year. I make 7 million now.
年収は倍になったが、英語の会議と成果主義で毎日胃が痛い。: My income doubled, but English meetings and performance-based pay give me a stomachache every day.
1年半後、レイオフで部署ごと消えた。: A year and a half later, layoffs wiped out the entire department.
英語が伸び、3年後にシンガポール拠点のリードとして年収2000万円になった。: My English improved, and three years later I became lead of the Singapore office at 20 million yen a year.
入社直後にRSU（株）を受け取り、株価が4倍になって1500万円の含み益が出た。: Right after joining I received RSUs (stock), the share price quadrupled, and I had 15 million yen in unrealized gains.
社内で唯一データが分かる人として、居心地はよかった。: As the only person in the company who understood data, I was comfortable there.
同期が年収2000万円になったと聞いて、しばらくもやもやした。: I heard a peer from my cohort hit 20 million yen a year, and it bugged me for a while.
社内で育てた後輩5人がデータチームを作り、自分は課長として率いることになった。: Five juniors I had trained formed a data team, and I ended up leading it as section chief.
社内でAIツールが導入され、自分の仕事の半分が自動化された。: The company introduced AI tools, and half of my work was automated.
社内でAIエージェントを使った業務自動化を任されたが、締め切りまで1か月しかない: I was put in charge of automating operations with AI agents, but there's only one month until the deadline.
2週間で動くものができ、社長賞をもらった。: Had something working in two weeks and received the President's Award.
API料金が想定の10倍かかり、経理から呼び出された。: API fees came to ten times the estimate, and accounting summoned me.
社内発表がバズり、他部署から10件の依頼が殺到して半年残業が月60時間になった。: My internal presentation went viral, 10 requests poured in from other departments, and for six months I worked 60 hours of overtime a month.
APIの仕様変更で一晩で全部止まり、元に戻すのに2週間かかった。: An API spec change stopped everything overnight, and it took two weeks to restore.
自社モデルを作り込む: Build our own model in depth
締め切りは過ぎたが、性能は段違いで特許も出せた。: We missed the deadline, but the performance was in a different league and we could even file a patent.
間に合わず、プロジェクトは外部ベンダーに回された。: We didn't make it, and the project was handed to an outside vendor.
作った仕組みをOSSで公開したら、GitHubのスターが3000を超え、転職の誘: I released the system as open source, got over 3,000 stars on GitHub, and received job offers from 10 companies.
GPUの電気代で月80万円かかり、プロジェクトごと凍結された。: GPU electricity costs hit 800,000 yen a month, and the whole project was frozen.
友人から、AIスタートアップの共同創業者に誘われた。給料は半分、株は15%。: A friend invited me to be a co-founder of an AI startup. Half the salary, 15% of the shares.
3年後、大手に買収された。株で人生が変わった。: Three years later, a major company acquired it. The shares changed my life.
資金調達に失敗し、2年で解散した。経験だけが残った。: Fundraising failed and the company dissolved in two years. Only the experience remained.
会社が倒産しかけたが、最後の1か月で大型契約を取って生き延びた。今は社員40人だ: The company nearly went under, but a big contract in the final month saved it. Now we have 40 employees.
共同創業者と方針で揉め、株を手放して出ていくことになった。: I clashed with my co-founder over direction and had to give up my shares and leave.
安定した給料で、家を買う頭金ができた。: With a steady salary, I saved up a down payment for a house.
その会社が上場したニュースを見て、スマホを置いた。: I saw the news that the company had gone public, and put my phone down.
社内のAI推進室長になり、年収が200万円上がった。: Became head of the in-house AI promotion office, and my income rose by 2 million yen.
誘ってきた友人と疎遠になり、結婚式にも呼ばれなかった。: I drifted apart from the friend who had invited me, and wasn't even invited to the wedding.
台湾の大手ファウンドリから、年収1.5倍で引き抜きの声がかかった。: A major Taiwanese foundry tried to recruit me at 1.5 times my salary.
仕事は激務だったが、夜市と同僚に助けられ、5年で一人前になった。: The work was brutal, but night markets and my colleagues helped me through, and in five years I became fully competent.
言葉と働き方が合わず、1年で帰国した。: The language and work style didn't suit me, and I returned to Japan after a year.
台湾で出会った人と結婚し、家族ぐるみで向こうに住むことになった。: I married someone I met in Taiwan, and our whole family ended up living there.
地震でラインが3日止まり、24時間体制の復旧で倒れかけた。: An earthquake halted the line for three days, and round-the-clock recovery work nearly made me collapse.
国内の新工場で中核メンバーになった。: Became a core member at the new domestic plant.
会社が事業売却され、待遇が大きく変わった。: The company sold off the business, and my terms of employment changed drastically.
熊本の新工場立ち上げで手腕を買われ、年収が300万円上がった。: My skill in launching the new plant in Kumamoto was recognized, and my income rose by 3 million yen.
台湾に行った同期が日本法人の上司として帰ってきた。: A peer who had gone to Taiwan came back as my boss at the Japanese subsidiary.
量産直前に、ごくまれに起きる不良の兆候を見つけた。報告すれば出荷が2週間遅れる。: Just before mass production, I spotted signs of a defect that happens very rarely. Reporting it would delay shipment by two weeks.
原因が見つかり、大規模リコールを防いだ。: The cause was found, and a large-scale recall was prevented.
結局問題はなく、営業部から1か月恨まれた。: In the end there was no problem, and the sales department held a grudge against me for a month.
その報告がきっかけで社内表彰され、海外顧客から指名で仕事が来るようになった。: That report earned me an internal commendation, and overseas customers began requesting me by name.
2週間の遅れで競合に先を越され、大口顧客を1社失った。: The two-week delay let a competitor get ahead, and we lost one major customer.
何も起きなかった。でもしばらく夢に出た。: Nothing happened. But it haunted my dreams for a while.
出荷後に不良が発覚し、顧客対応で半年潰れた。: The defect came to light after shipment, and handling customers consumed half a year.
別の工場で同じ兆候が見つかり、自分のメモが原因究明の決め手になった。: The same signs turned up at another plant, and my notes were the key to finding the cause.
社内調査で「気づいていた」ことが分かり、降格になった。: An internal investigation revealed I “had noticed,” and I was demoted.
納期1週間前、自分の設計で試作機が振動トラブルを起こした。: One week before delivery, the prototype built on my design developed a vibration problem.
徹夜で設計を見直す: Pull an all-nighter to rework the design
補強リブを足して解決した。顧客から感謝の電話が来た。: Adding reinforcing ribs solved it. The customer called to thank me.
直したら別の場所が壊れた。納期は2週間遅れた。: After the fix, something else broke. Delivery was two weeks late.
その補強構造で特許を取り、社内の発明報奨金を50万円もらった。: I patented that reinforcement structure and received a 500,000 yen in-house invention reward.
徹夜明けに車で帰る途中、居眠りで縁石に乗り上げた。修理代15万円。: Driving home after the all-nighter, I dozed off and hit a curb. Repairs cost 150,000 yen.
ベテランの一言で原因が分かった。もっと早く聞けばよかった。: A single remark from a veteran revealed the cause. I should have asked sooner.
「設計者だろ」と突き放され、結局一人でやった。: “You're the designer, aren't you?” I was brushed off and ended up doing it alone.
相談したベテランが定年前の最後の仕事として一緒に直してくれ、師弟関係になった。: The veteran I consulted helped fix it as his last job before retirement, and we became master and apprentice.
上司が勝手に顧客に謝罪し、自分の責任ということになった。: The boss apologized to the customer on his own, and it was pinned on me.
ベンチャーのロボット会社から、設計リーダーで来ないかと誘われた。: A robotics venture company asked me to join as design lead.
自分の設計した配膳ロボが全国のファミレスで走り出した。: A serving robot I designed started running in family restaurants nationwide.
資金難で給料が3か月遅れた。: Short on funds, salaries were three months late.
会社が上場し、ストックオプションで1000万円手に入れた。: The company went public, and I got 10 million yen from stock options.
3年後、大手に買収されて設計部ごと元の会社の下請けになった。笑うしかなかった。: Three years later, a major company acquired us and the whole design department became a subcontractor of my old company. All I could do was laugh.
課長になり、設計審査をする側になった。: Became a section chief, now on the side that reviews designs.
会社が海外に設計拠点を移し、仕事が減った。: The company moved its design base overseas, and my work dwindled.
定年まで勤め、若手設計者30人を育てた。送別会で花束を3つもらった。: Worked until retirement and trained 30 young designers. At the farewell party I received three bouquets.
誘ったベンチャーが成功し、後任の人がメディアに出ていた。: The venture that had invited me succeeded, and my replacement appeared in the media.
地震で被災した町の道路復旧に、応援で3か月派遣される話が来た。: An offer came to be dispatched for three months to help restore roads in a town hit by an earthquake.
1か月で仮復旧させた。避難所のおばあちゃんにおにぎりをもらった。: Got temporary repairs done in a month. An elderly woman at the shelter gave me a rice ball.
過労で倒れ、途中で帰された。: Collapsed from overwork and was sent home partway through.
派遣先の町で知り合った人と、3年後に結婚した。: Three years later, I married someone I met in the town where I was dispatched.
戻ったら自分の現場の担当が替わっていて、居場所がなかった。: When I got back, someone else had taken over my site, and there was no place for me.
自分の現場は予定通り完成した。: My site was completed on schedule.
同期の活躍をニュースで見て、少し後悔した。: I saw a peer's achievements on the news and felt a little regret.
その現場が土木学会の賞を取り、名前が銘板に刻まれた。: That site won an award from the Japan Society of Civil Engineers, and my name was engraved on the plaque.
同じ時期に自分の現場で大雨被害があり、復旧で結局3か月帰れなかった。: Around the same time my site suffered heavy rain damage, and in the end I couldn't go home for three months because of the recovery.
発注者から、工期短縮のために安全手順を一部省略してくれと言われた。: The client asked me to skip part of the safety procedures to shorten the construction period.
工期は延びたが、無事故で竣工した。: The schedule ran long, but the project was completed without accidents.
次の入札で外された。: I was dropped from the next bidding.
断った件が業界紙に載り、安全重視のゼネコンからヘッドハンティングされた。: The refusal was covered in an industry paper, and a safety-focused general contractor headhunted me.
工期遅延の違約金500万円を会社が負担し、ボーナスがゼロになった。: The company paid a 5 million yen penalty for the delay, and my bonus went to zero.
作業員がケガをして、労基署の調査が入った。: A worker was injured, and the Labor Standards Inspection Office launched an investigation.
発注者に気に入られて次の大型案件を指名で受注した。: The client took a liking to me and gave me the next big project by direct request.
作業員が辞めてしまい、残りの工期を人手不足で乗り切ることになった。: Workers quit, and we had to get through the rest of the schedule short-handed.
出荷前の検査データが基準をわずかに外れた。上司は「誤差だから合格にしろ」と言う。: The pre-shipment inspection data fell slightly outside the standard. The boss says, “It's within margin of error, so pass it.”
再検査で本当に不良だった。上司は何も言わなかったが、工場長に褒められた。: The retest showed it really was defective. The boss said nothing, but the plant manager praised me.
再検査で問題なしだった。上司との関係が冷えた。: The retest found no problem. My relationship with the boss cooled.
不良品流出を防いだことで取引先から感謝状が届き、課長に昇進した。: Preventing defective products from getting out earned a letter of thanks from the client, and I was promoted to section chief.
ライン停止の損失が1200万円と計算され、社内で「止めた人」として有名になった。: The loss from halting the line was calculated at 12 million yen, and I became known in the company as “the one who stopped it.”
何も起きなかった。でもその記録を見るたび胸が痛んだ。: Nothing happened. But every time I saw that record, my chest ached.
数年後、データ改ざんとして報道され、自分も聴取された。: Years later it was reported as data falsification, and I was questioned too.
その上司が翌年昇進し、自分を引き上げてくれた。気まずいままだった。: That boss was promoted the next year and pulled me up with him. It stayed awkward.
内部告発しようか半年悩み、胃薬が手放せなくなった。: I agonized for six months over whether to blow the whistle, and became unable to do without stomach medicine.
顧客から大型クレーム。現地に謝罪に行くか、データで原因究明を優先するか。: A major complaint from a customer. Go apologize on site, or prioritize finding the cause through data?
誠意が伝わり、取引は続いた。: My sincerity came across, and business continued.
原因を聞かれて答えられず、かえって怒らせた。: Asked about the cause, I couldn't answer, which only made them angrier.

事務所の代表になり、20人の鑑定士を率いた。: Became head of the office and led 20 appraisers.
後輩が独立して成功し、飲み会で年収の話になって黙った。: A junior colleague went independent and succeeded, and when income came up at a drinking party, I fell silent.
証拠は不十分だが、世間の注目が高く、有罪を求める声が強い事件を担当した。: Presided over a case with insufficient evidence, but with intense public attention and strong calls for a guilty verdict.
疑わしきは被告人の利益に: When in doubt, rule in favor of the accused
SNSで批判されたが、高裁でも支持された。法律家としての誇りを感じた。: Criticized on social media, but the High Court upheld it too. I felt pride as a jurist.
検察が控訴し、高裁で有罪になった。自分の判断は何だったのかと考えた。: Prosecutors appealed, and the High Court found the defendant guilty. I wondered what my judgment had meant.
その判決が司法試験の判例教材に載り、10年後も大学で教えられていた。: That ruling made it into bar exam case-law materials and was still taught at universities 10 years later.
自宅住所がネットに晒され、半年間警察の巡回がついた。: My home address was exposed online, and police patrolled my area for half a year.
10年後、真犯人が見つかり、再審で無罪になった。: 10 years later the real culprit was found, and a retrial ended in acquittal.
有罪判決の被告から刑務所から手紙が届いた。「真実は違う」と書かれていた。: A letter arrived from the convicted defendant in prison. It said, “The truth is different.”
世論が収まり、上司から「よくやった」と言われた。だが自分では納得できなかった。: Public opinion calmed, and my superior said, “Well done.” But I couldn't convince myself.
退官して弁護士になれば、年収が倍以上になると誘われた。: I was told that if I left the bench and became a lawyer, my income would more than double.
大手事務所に入り、年収3000万円になった。法廷の反対側に立つのは不思議な気分だ: Joined a major firm and earned 30 million yen a year. Standing on the other side of the courtroom felt strange.
営業が苦手で、なかなか依頼が取れなかった。: Bad at sales, I struggled to win cases.
元判事の肩書で大企業の社外取締役も兼任し、年収が4000万円を超えた。: With the title of former judge, I also served as an outside director at large companies, and my income exceeded 40 million yen a year.
弁護士として初めて負けた相手が、かつての部下の裁判官だった。笑い話になった。: The first time I lost as a lawyer, the judge was my former subordinate. It became a funny story.
地裁の所長になった。: Became chief of a district court.
また転勤で、子どもが転校を嫌がった。: Transferred again, and my child hated changing schools.
最高裁の調査官に抜擢され、全国から判決例を読み込む日々になった。: Was picked as a Supreme Court research official, and spent my days reading precedents from across the country.
転勤先で地元の祭りに誘われ、太鼓チームに入って家族ぐるみで溶け込んだ。: At my new posting I was invited to the local festival, joined the taiko team, and my whole family blended in.
上から「この事件は必ず起訴しろ」と言われたが、証拠に弱さを感じる。: My superiors said, “Be sure to indict this case,” but I feel the evidence is weak.
上司は渋々了承した。後に真犯人が別にいたと分かった。: My boss reluctantly agreed. Later it turned out the real culprit was someone else.
出世コースから外され、地方に異動になった。: Taken off the fast track and transferred to a provincial post.
不起訴の判断が後に「冤罪を防いだ」と報道され、司法修習生の講義に呼ばれた。: The decision not to prosecute was later reported as having “prevented a wrongful conviction,” and I was invited to lecture legal trainees.
上司と口をきかない状態が1年続いた。: For a year, I and my boss didn't speak to each other.
有罪判決が出た。: A guilty verdict was handed down.
法廷で証拠の弱さを突かれ、無罪判決。報道で叩かれた。: The weakness of the evidence was exposed in court, resulting in an acquittal. The press tore into me.
有罪後、新証拠が出て再審請求が始まり、法廷で証言を求められた。: After the conviction, new evidence emerged, a retrial petition began, and I was asked to testify in court.
起訴した件の被害者遺族から感謝の手紙が届いた。複雑な気持ちで保管した。: A thank-you letter came from the bereaved family of a victim in a case I prosecuted. I kept it with mixed feelings.
ヤメ検として大手法律事務所から年収2500万円で誘われた。: As an ex-prosecutor, a major law firm offered me 25 million yen a year.
企業の不祥事対応で引っ張りだこになった。: Became in high demand for handling corporate scandals.
守る側に回る違和感が消えなかった。: The strangeness of now being on the defending side never went away.
5年で事務所のパートナーになり、年収が5000万円に届いた。: In 5 years I became a partner at the firm, and my income reached 50 million yen a year.
初めての案件で、かつての同僚検事と法廷で対峙した。気まずくて胃が痛くなった。: In my first case, I faced a former fellow prosecutor in court. It was so awkward my stomach hurt.
特捜部に配属され、大型事件を手がけた。: Was assigned to the Special Investigation Department and handled a major case.
仕事に追われ、家族と過ごす時間がなかった。: Swamped with work, I had no time to spend with my family.
定年後、地方で公証人になり、穏やかに過ごした。: After retirement, I became a notary in the provinces and lived peacefully.
大型事件が政治的圧力で不起訴になり、退職を考えた。: A major case ended in non-prosecution due to political pressure, and I thought about resigning.
赴任国で政情不安が起き、本省は撤退を検討している。大使館に残る人員を募っている。: Political unrest broke out in the country of my posting, and the home ministry is considering withdrawal. The embassy is seeking staff to remain.
最後の日本人退避まで見届けた。後に感謝状が届いた。: Stayed until the last Japanese national was evacuated. A letter of appreciation arrived later.
銃声の夜を過ごし、帰国後もしばらく眠れなかった。: Spent nights under gunfire, and for a while after returning home I couldn't sleep.
退避した邦人の一人が後に国会議員になり、演説で自分の話をした。: One of the evacuated Japanese later became a member of the Diet and told my story in a speech.
通信が途絶えた3日間、家族は自分が死んだと思っていた。: For 3 days with communications cut off, my family thought I was dead.
家族と一緒に無事帰国した。: Returned home safely with my family.
残った同僚の苦労を聞き、申し訳なさが残った。: Hearing of the hardships of the colleagues who stayed, I was left with a sense of guilt.
帰国後、日本で政情不安の解説役としてテレビに呼ばれた。: After returning, I was invited onto TV in Japan as a commentator on the political unrest.
帰国便で隣の席の人と意気投合し、1年後に結婚した。: Hit it off with the person in the next seat on the flight home, and married a year later.
国際機関（国連）への出向の話が来た。給料は上がるが、キャリアは本省から外れる。: An offer came for a secondment to an international organization (the UN). The pay rises, but the career leaves the home ministry track.
ジュネーブで働き、世界中の友人ができた。: Worked in Geneva and made friends from all over the world.
官僚的な組織に戸惑い、2年で戻った。: Bewildered by the bureaucratic organization, I returned after 2 years.
ジュネーブで出会った各国の同僚が、後の交渉で何度も助けてくれた。: Colleagues from various countries I met in Geneva helped me again and again in later negotiations.
出向中に本省の人事で同期に大きく差をつけられた。: During the secondment, personnel decisions at the ministry left me far behind my peers.
国会対応で連日徹夜だった。: Pulling all-nighters day after day for Diet duties.
40代で大使に任命された。小国だったが、首脳会談を成功させた。: Was appointed ambassador in my forties. It was a small country, but I made a summit a success.
深夜の国会答弁作成で、2年で白髪が一気に増えた。: Drafting Diet replies late at night, my hair turned gray fast within 2 years.
2機の接近が迫る中、新人が交信でもたついている。: With two aircraft about to come close, the rookie is fumbling on the radio.
間隔を確保した。新人は落ち込んだが、後で「ありがとうございました」と言ってきた。: Separation was secured. The rookie was dejected, but later came and said, “Thank you.”
新人はショックで翌月訓練を辞めた。: The rookie, shocked, quit training the next month.
その新人が10年後、管制塔の主任になり、自分を「師匠」と呼んだ。: 10 years later, that rookie became a senior controller in the tower and called me “master.”
交信を代わったことで手順違反とされ、始末書を書いた。: Taking over the radio was deemed a procedural violation, and I wrote a letter of apology.
新人がぎりぎりで指示を出した。一皮むけた。: The rookie gave instructions at the last moment. They grew from it.
ニアミスとして報告書を書くことになった。: It ended up as a near miss, and I had to write a report.
その新人がのちに羽田の主任になり、表彰式で自分の名前を出した。: That rookie later became a senior controller at Haneda and mentioned my name at an award ceremony.
新人が辞め、その分自分の夜勤が月に5回増えた。: The rookie quit, and my night shifts increased by 5 a month.
地方の小さな空港への異動の打診が来た。のんびりできるが、技術は鈍る。: I was approached about a transfer to a small regional airport. I could relax, but my skills would dull.
1日20便の静かな空港で、家族との時間が増えた。: At a quiet airport with 20 flights a day, I had more time with my family.
物足りなくなり、2年で都会に戻った。: It felt unfulfilling, and I returned to the city after 2 years.
空港近くに古民家を買い、週末は畑で野菜を育てた。: Bought an old farmhouse near the airport and grew vegetables in the field on weekends.
地方空港が廃港の議論にかけられ、身の振り方に迷った。: The regional airport came under discussion for closure, and I was unsure what to do next.
主任管制官になった。: Became a senior air traffic controller.
ストレスで胃潰瘍になった。: Developed a stomach ulcer from stress.
国際会議で日本代表として新しい管制システムを発表した。: Presented a new air traffic control system at an international conference as Japan's representative.
燃え尽きて、3か月の休職を取った。: Burned out and took 3 months of leave.
自治体の予算削減で、企画展を1本削るか、教育普及の予算を削るか選べと言われた。: Due to municipal budget cuts, I was told to choose between cutting one special exhibition or cutting the education outreach budget.
子ども向けプログラムは続けられ、地元の学校から感謝された。: The children's programs continued, and local schools thanked us.
来館者数が減り、さらに予算を削られた。: Visitor numbers fell, and the budget was cut even further.
教育プログラムに来た小学生の一人が、20年後に学芸員として同じ館に就職した。: One of the elementary school students who came to the education program joined the same museum as a curator 20 years later.
展示がない年、地元紙に「やる気のない博物館」と書かれた。: In the year with no exhibition, the local paper called us a “museum with no drive.”
話題の企画展が大成功した。: The much-talked-about special exhibition was a big success.
学校との関係が切れた。: Ties with the schools were severed.
企画展の図録が5000部売れ、増刷になった。: The exhibition catalog sold 5,000 copies and went to a reprint.
学校側が独自に他館と連携し、自分の館は外された。: The schools partnered with other museums on their own, and mine was left out.
大学から、准教授として来ないかと声がかかった。: A university invited me to join as an associate professor.
研究の時間が増え、念願の本を出版した。: Had more time for research and published the book I had long wanted to write.
大学の雑務と会議で、研究時間は増えなかった。: Between university chores and meetings, my research time didn't increase.
NHKのドキュメンタリーで解説者として出演し、本が1万部売れた。: Appeared as a commentator in an NHK documentary, and my book sold 10,000 copies.
大学のポストが任期付きで、5年後に契約が切れた。: The university post was fixed-term, and the contract expired after 5 years.
自分が企画した展覧会が全国巡回することになった。: An exhibition I planned was set to tour the whole country.
指定管理者制度で、運営会社が変わった。: Under the designated manager system, the operating company changed.
展示で見つかった古文書が新発見とされ、全国ニュースになった。: An old document found during the exhibition was recognized as a new discovery and made national news.
館長に昇進したが、仕事は予算と人の調整ばかりになった。: Promoted to director, but the job became all about juggling budgets and people.
プロデューサーから、ヤラセぎりぎりの演出を台本に入れてほしいと言われた。: The producer asked me to put a staging that borders on fakery into the script.
代わりの案が通り、評判も良かった。: My alternative idea was accepted and was well received.
次の改編で番組から外された。: At the next lineup revamp, I was dropped from the show.
代案が「斬新な演出」として業界誌に取り上げられ、他局から声がかかった。: The alternative was covered in an industry magazine as a “fresh staging,” and other networks came calling.
プロデューサーと冷え込み、同期作家の名前ばかりが番組に並ぶようになった。: Relations with the producer chilled, and only my peers' names began to appear on the show.
放送後にヤラセとして炎上し、番組が打ち切られた。: After airing, it blew up online as fakery, and the show was canceled.
番組が大ヒットし、自分の名前で本を出す話が来た。: The show became a huge hit, and I was offered a book deal under my own name.
BPOの審議が入り、関係者全員が報告書を書いた。: The BPO launched a review, and everyone involved had to write a report.
人気YouTuberから、専属の構成作家として来ないかと誘われた。: A popular YouTuber invited me to join as an exclusive scriptwriter.
再生数が伸び、月収が80万円になった。: Views grew, and my monthly income reached 800,000 yen.
そのYouTuberが炎上して活動休止した。: That YouTuber got caught in a firestorm and went on hiatus.
YouTuberと立ち上げた企画が書籍化され、印税で300万円入った。: A project I launched with the YouTuber became a book, and royalties brought in 3 million yen.
アルゴリズム変更で再生数が半分になり、報酬が月30万円減った。: An algorithm change halved views, and my pay dropped by 300,000 yen a month.
ゴールデン番組のメイン作家になった。: Became the head writer of a prime-time show.
制作費削減で仕事が減った。: Production budget cuts reduced my work.
テレビ番組の映画化が決まり、脚本のクレジットに名前が載った。: The TV show was adapted into a movie, and my name appeared in the screenplay credits.
番組が打ち切られ、40代で次の仕事を探すことになった。: The show was canceled, and in my forties I had to look for my next job.
大型の撮影案件の直前、メインのカメラが故障した。: Right before a big shoot, my main camera broke.
性能は劣ったが、腕でカバーして納品できた。: The performance was inferior, but I covered it with skill and delivered.
画質が落ちてクレームが来た。: Image quality dropped, and complaints came in.
予備機の荒い画質が逆に「エモい」と言われ、それが代名詞になった。: The backup camera's rough image quality was oddly praised as “emotional,” and it became my trademark.
撮影後に予備機も壊れ、データの一部が消えた。: After the shoot the backup broke too, and some of the data was lost.
慣れない操作に苦戦したが、素晴らしい写真が撮れた。: Struggled with the unfamiliar controls, but got wonderful photos.
操作に戸惑い、肝心のシーンを逃した。: Fumbled with the controls and missed the crucial scene.
レンタル店の店長と仲良くなり、機材の割引と仕事の紹介をもらえるようになった。: Became friendly with the rental shop manager, who began giving me equipment discounts and job referrals.
レンタル機材を落として、修理代40万円を請求された。: Dropped the rental equipment and was billed 400,000 yen for repairs.
ウェディング専門のスタジオから、正社員の誘いが来た。給料は安定するが、自由な作品: A wedding-specialist studio offered me a full-time position. The pay would be steady, but I'd lose the freedom to make my own work.
毎月の給料に安心し、結婚もできた。: Reassured by a monthly salary, I was able to marry too.
同じような写真ばかりで、カメラが嫌になりかけた。: Shooting nothing but similar photos, I nearly came to hate cameras.
スタジオの社長が引退し、そのまま経営を引き継いだ。: The studio president retired, and I took over management.
年間200組の結婚式を撮り、週末がなくなって自分の家族と過ごせなかった。: Shot 200 weddings a year, lost my weekends, and couldn't spend time with my own family.
写真集を出版し、個展が話題になった。: Published a photo book, and my solo exhibition drew attention.
仕事が途切れ、バイトを掛け持ちした。: Work dried up, and I juggled several part-time jobs.
撮った写真が海外のコンテストで入賞し、賞金100万円を得た。: A photo I took won a prize at an overseas contest, earning 1 million yen in prize money.
フリーの収入が年150万円まで落ち、実家に戻った。: My freelance income fell to 1.5 million yen a year, and I moved back to my parents' home.
大手企業から多額の寄付の申し出があったが、その企業は環境問題で批判されている。: A major corporation offered a large donation, but that company is criticized over environmental issues.
事業が拡大し、支援できる人が倍になった。: The program expanded, and the number of people we could support doubled.
SNSで「グリーンウォッシュに加担」と叩かれ、他の寄付者が離れた。: Slammed on social media for “complicity in greenwashing,” other donors walked away.
企業の社員がボランティアで100人来るようになり、団体の雰囲気が明るくなった。: Company employees began coming as 100 volunteers, and the group's atmosphere brightened.
寄付企業の不祥事が報道され、団体名まで記事に載った。: A scandal at the donor company was reported, and even our organization's name appeared in the articles.
理念は守れたが、事業の一部を縮小した。: Our principles were kept, but part of the program was scaled down.
その話を聞いた個人寄付者が増え、意外にも資金が集まった。: Individual donors who heard the story increased, and funds unexpectedly came in.
その判断がメディアに取り上げられ、全国から月300人の新しい寄付者が集まった。: The decision was covered by the media, and 300 new donors a month gathered from across the country.
スタッフ2人の給料が払えず、退職してもらうことになった。: We couldn't pay the salaries of 2 staff members and had to let them go.
給料が上がらず、生活が苦しい。民間企業への転職を考えた。: My pay doesn't rise and life is hard. I thought about switching to a private company.
年収は200万円上がった。週末にボランティアとして関わり続けた。: My income rose by 2 million yen. I kept volunteering on weekends.
仕事に意味を見いだせず、半年でNPOに戻りたくなった。: Unable to find meaning in the work, after half a year I wanted to go back to the NPO.
企業のCSR部門に配属され、NPOとの橋渡し役として前より大きな仕事ができた。: Assigned to the company's CSR department, I served as a bridge to NPOs and could do bigger work than before.
転職先がブラック企業で、月100時間残業になった。: My new employer was an exploitative company, and I worked 100 hours of overtime a month.
事務局長になり、行政と組んで大きな事業を回すようになった。: Became executive director and began running large projects in partnership with the government.
貯金が尽きて、親に借金をした。: My savings ran out, and I borrowed money from my parents.
理事長に推され、団体の活動が国の補助事業に採択された。: Was elected chairperson, and the group's activities were selected for a national subsidy program.
同じ志の仲間と結婚し、共働きでなんとか暮らしを回した。: Married a colleague with the same aspirations, and we made ends meet as a dual-income couple.
地元の有力者から、特定の業者に公共工事を回すよう頼まれた。次の選挙での支援が条件: A local power broker asked me to steer a public works contract to a particular contractor. Support in the next election is the condition.
支援は失ったが、若い世代の票が増えて再選した。: I lost their support, but votes from the younger generation grew and I was re-elected.
組織票を失って落選した。: Lost the organized vote and lost the election.
その件を公開したら全国ニュースになり、市長選に推された。: Going public with the matter made national news, and I was urged to run for mayor.
選挙カーに生卵を投げられた。: Raw eggs were thrown at my campaign car.
後に口利きが発覚し、議員辞職に追い込まれた。: The favor-peddling later came to light, and I was forced to resign my seat.
業者から毎年のお歳暮が届くようになった。それが一番気持ち悪かった。: Year-end gifts from the contractor began arriving every year. That was the creepiest part.
新聞記者に嗅ぎつけられ、半年間取材に追い回された。: A newspaper reporter sniffed it out, and I was chased for interviews for half a year.
県議会議員選挙に出ないかと党から打診された。: The party asked whether I would run in the prefectural assembly election.
当選し、県政で仕事ができるようになった。: Won, and was able to work in prefectural government.
落選し、市議の席も失った。: Lost the election, and lost my city council seat too.
県議の後に国政に出て、当選した。: After the prefectural assembly, I ran in national politics and won.
選挙費用で自己資金300万円を使い、落選後は借金返済に追われた。: Spent 3 million yen of my own money on the campaign, and after losing I was chased by debt repayments.
地元に根ざした活動を続け、議長になった。: Kept up grassroots local activities and became council chair.
後輩が県議になり、少し複雑だった。: A junior colleague became a prefectural assemblyman, and I felt a bit conflicted.
地元の子ども食堂を立ち上げ、毎週50人が来るようになった。: Launched a local children's cafeteria, and 50 people came every week.
党の公認が外れ、無所属で戦うことになった。: Lost the party's endorsement and had to run as an independent.
檀家が減り、お寺の維持が苦しい。永代供養のお墓を作って新しい人を呼び込むか迷った: Parishioner households are declining and keeping the temple going is hard. Torn over whether to build perpetual-memorial graves to draw in new people.
都市部から申し込みが相次ぎ、お寺の財政が持ち直した。: Applications poured in from urban areas, and the temple's finances recovered.
永代供養の申し込みが300件を超え、本堂を建て替えられた。: Perpetual-memorial applications exceeded 300, and we were able to rebuild the main hall.
墓じまいした檀家が多く、結局財政は横ばいだった。: Many parishioners closed their family graves, and in the end finances stayed flat.
お寺の屋根が雨漏りしたまま、修理できなかった。: The temple roof kept leaking, and we couldn't afford to repair it.
地元の大学生がお寺の歴史をSNSで紹介し、若い参拝者が増えた。: Local university students introduced the temple's history on social media, and young visitors increased.
後継ぎがおらず、70歳を超えても一人で寺を守ることになった。: With no successor, I ended up guarding the temple alone even past 70.
檀家の若い遺族から、悩み相談を受けるようになった。カウンセリングの勉強を始めるか: Young bereaved family members of parishioners began coming to me with their troubles. Torn over whether to start studying counseling.
お寺で「お悩み相談会」を開き、毎月20人が来るようになった。: Held a “troubles consultation session” at the temple, and 20 people came each month.
専門的すぎて手に負えないケースに出会い、無力感を覚えた。: Met cases too specialized to handle, and felt powerless.
お悩み相談会がテレビで紹介され、YouTubeチャンネルを開いたら登録者10万人: The consultation session was featured on TV, and when I opened a YouTube channel it reached 100,000 subscribers.
カウンセリングの勉強費用に2年で150万円かかった。: Studying counseling cost 1.5 million yen over 2 years.
静かにお経を読む日々が続いた。: Days of quietly chanting sutras continued.
相談に来た人が来なくなり、気になり続けた。: A person who had come for advice stopped coming, and it kept weighing on my mind.
読経の声がよいと評判になり、法事の依頼が他寺からも来るようになった。: My sutra-chanting voice became well known, and requests for memorial services came even from other temples.
相談者が別の宗教団体に入ったと聞いた。: I heard that the person who had sought advice had joined another religious group.
SNSでバズった御朱印目当てに参拝客が急増したが、転売も横行している。: Visitors surged for the goshuin (temple stamps) that went viral on social media, but resale is also rampant.
静けさが戻り、地元の人に喜ばれた。: Quiet returned, and the locals were pleased.
収入が減り、修繕の計画が先送りになった。: Income fell, and repair plans were postponed.
地元の子どもたちと手作りの御朱印を作るイベントが始まり、毎回50人が集まった。: An event making handmade goshuin with local children began, and 50 people gathered each time.
御朱印目当ての客が来なくなり、境内の売店を閉めた。: Visitors who came for goshuin stopped coming, and we closed the shop on the temple grounds.
年間500万円の収入になり、社殿を修繕できた。: It brought in ¥5 million a year, and the shrine buildings were repaired.
海外からの参拝客が増え、英語で神社案内をする日々が始まった。: Visitors from abroad increased, and I began giving shrine tours in English.
転売業者から脅迫まがいの電話がかかってきた。: Got threatening phone calls from resellers.
後継ぎのいない近隣の小さな神社を、さらに3社兼務してほしいと頼まれた。: Was asked to take on three more small neighboring shrines that had no successors.
どの神社のお祭りも途絶えずに済んだ。氏子さんたちが泣いて喜んだ。: None of the shrines’ festivals died out. The parishioners wept with joy.
忙しすぎて体調を崩した。: Got too busy and fell ill.
4社の祭りを一つにまとめた合同祭が話題になり、県の文化事業に選ばれた。: A joint festival combining the four shrines’ festivals became a hit and was chosen as a prefectural cultural project.
4社の行き来で車を年3万km走らせ、2年で買い替えた。: Driving between the four shrines racked up 30,000 km a year, and I replaced the car in two years.
自分の神社に集中できた。: Could focus on my own shrine.
そのうち1社が廃社になった。: One of them was eventually abolished.
断った神社の氏子から恨まれ、自分の神社の祭りに協力してもらえなくなった。: Parishioners of the shrine I turned down held a grudge and stopped helping with my own shrine’s festival.
家族と過ごす時間が増え、子どもが神職を継ぐと言い出した。: Spent more time with family, and my child said they would take over as a Shinto priest.
編集者から「売れ筋の異世界ものを書いてほしい」と言われた。本当は純文学が書きたい: My editor said, “Write a bestselling isekai novel.” What I really want to write is literary fiction.
シリーズが10巻続き、アニメ化された。: The series ran for 10 volumes and got an anime adaptation.
全く筆が乗らず、1巻で打ち切られた。: The writing wouldn’t flow, and it was cancelled after one volume.
異世界ものの中に純文学のテーマを潜ませたら評論家に絶賛された。: I slipped literary themes into the isekai story, and critics raved.
ネットで「テンプレ作家」と叩かれ、しばらくSNSを見られなかった。: Got slammed online as a “formula writer” and couldn’t look at social media for a while.
文学賞を受賞し、一気に注目された。: Won a literary prize and suddenly drew attention.
評価はされたが売れず、バイトを続けた。: Critically acclaimed but didn’t sell, so I kept my part-time job.
受賞作が映画化され、原作料で500万円入った。: The winning work was adapted into a film, and the rights fee brought in ¥5 million.
10年書き続けて、初めて書いた家族の話がやっと重版になった。: After ten years of writing, my first family story finally got a reprint.
会社員との兼業か、専業作家になるか迷った。: Couldn’t decide whether to keep my day job or become a full-time writer.
書く時間が増え、毎年2冊出せるようになった。: More time to write; I could now publish two books a year.
収入が不安定で、2年で貯金が尽きかけた。: Income was unstable, and my savings nearly ran out in two years.
専業2年目に書いた作品が直木賞の候補になった。: A work written in my second full-time year was nominated for the Naoki Prize.
締め切りに追われて昼夜逆転し、体重が10kg増えた。: Chased by deadlines, my sleep schedule flipped and I gained 10 kg.
会社の経験がネタになり、お仕事小説がヒットした。: My office experiences became material, and my workplace novel was a hit.
疲れて、1年間1行も書けなかった。: Exhausted, I couldn’t write a single line for a year.
会社の同僚が読者になり、社内に読書会ができた。: Coworkers became readers, and a book club started at the company.
会社にバレて副業規定違反で注意された。: The company found out and warned me for violating the side-job policy.
クライアントから、有名な曲にそっくりな曲を作ってほしいと頼まれた。: A client asked me to write a song that sounds just like a famous one.
オリジナルで提案した曲が気に入られ、継続案件になった。: They liked my original proposal, and it turned into ongoing work.
提案曲がCMに使われ、年間で200万円の使用料が入った。: My proposed song was used in a commercial, earning ¥2 million in fees that year.
その後、同じクライアントから二度と連絡はなかった。: After that, I never heard from the same client again.
盗作疑惑で炎上し、名前に傷がついた。: Plagiarism accusations blew up online and damaged my name.
「そっくり」と言われた曲が予想外にヒットし、元の曲の作者からも面白がられた。: The song called a “dead ringer” unexpectedly became a hit, and even the original composer was amused.
訴訟になり、和解金100万円を払った。: It went to court, and I paid ¥1 million in a settlement.
自分の名義でアルバムを出すか、裏方の作曲家に徹するか迷った。: Couldn’t decide between releasing an album under my own name and staying a behind-the-scenes composer.
1曲がSNSでバズり、ストリーミングで1億回再生された。: One song went viral on social media and hit 100 million streams.
売れずに、自主制作費200万円が赤字になった。: It didn’t sell, and the ¥2 million self-production cost became a loss.
バズった曲が海外ドラマに使われ、ロイヤリティで年300万円入るようになった。: The viral song was used in an overseas TV drama, bringing in ¥3 million a year in royalties.
ライブで客が7人しか来ず、その日のうちに配信を消した。: Only seven people came to the live show, and I deleted the stream that same day.
自分の名前を誰も知らないことが寂しくなった。: It began to feel lonely that nobody knew my name.
提供したアイドルの曲が紅白で歌われ、テレビの前で泣いた。: A song I wrote for an idol was sung on Kohaku, and I cried in front of the TV.
発注元のレコード会社が倒産し、未払い80万円が戻らなかった。: The record label that commissioned the work went bankrupt, and the ¥800,000 owed to me was never paid.
大手事務所からオーディション合格の連絡が来た。個人勢として続けるか迷った。: A major agency told me I passed their audition. Couldn’t decide whether to keep going as an independent streamer.
事務所の方針と合わず、2年で卒業した。: Didn’t fit the agency’s direction and graduated after two years.
同期デビューの4人と仲良くなり、オフラインでも旅行に行くようになった。: Became close with the four others who debuted with me, and we even started taking trips together offline.
事務所の配信スケジュールで1日8時間配信し、喉を痛めて2週間休んだ。: The agency’s schedule had me streaming 8 hours a day; I hurt my throat and took two weeks off.
自由に配信し、ファンとの距離が近くて楽しかった。: Streamed freely and had fun, close to my fans.
伸び悩み、バイトを続けながら配信した。: Growth stalled, so I kept streaming alongside a part-time job.
個人勢のまま企業案件が年10件来るようになり、月収50万円になった。: Even as an independent, I got 10 corporate gigs a year, reaching ¥500,000 a month.
配信機材に100万円かけたが、同接は20人のままだった。: Spent ¥1 million on streaming gear, but concurrent viewers stayed at 20.
過去のSNSアカウントが特定され、身バレの危機が迫った。: My old social media account was identified, and I was at risk of being outed.
アンチが増え、配信が荒れた。: Haters multiplied, and my streams turned chaotic.
身バレをネタにした雑談配信が話題になり、登録者が2万人増えた。: A chat stream joking about being outed went viral, adding 20,000 subscribers.
家族に配信のことが知られ、実家で気まずい正月を過ごした。: My family found out about the streaming, and New Year’s at my parents’ place was awkward.
数年後、別の名前で転生し、また人気になった。: Years later, I was reborn under a different name and became popular again.
引退後、ファンから届いた手紙を全部読み、500通あった。: After retiring, I read every letter from fans. There were 500.
引退後も特定スレが動き続け、仕事先で噂された。: Even after retiring, the doxxing threads kept going, and rumors spread at my workplace.
SGの優勝戦。スタートでフライング覚悟で踏み込むか迷った。: The final of an SG race. Couldn’t decide whether to risk a flying start and go all-in at the start.
トップスタートを決めて優勝した。賞金3900万円。: Nailed the best start and won. Prize money: ¥39 million.
フライングした。長期の出場停止で、収入が途絶えた。: Jumped the start. A long suspension cut off my income.
優勝賞金で母に家を建てた。: Built a house for my mother with the prize money.
大観衆の前でフライングし、その映像がネットで100万回再生された。: Jumped the start in front of a huge crowd, and the footage got 1 million views online.
3着だった。それでも賞金は大きかった。: Finished third. The prize money was still substantial.
出遅れて6着だった。: Got a slow start and finished sixth.
慎重なスタートが評価され、若手の手本として講習会で教えるようになった。: My careful starts were praised, and I began teaching at workshops as a role model for young racers.
優勝戦後、ファンに「攻めろよ」とヤジられ、夜眠れなかった。: After the final, fans heckled, “Be aggressive!” and I couldn’t sleep that night.
減量がきつくなってきた。体重を落とし続けるか、ペナルティ覚悟で少し増やすか。: Weight cutting was getting harsh. Keep dropping weight, or gain a little and accept the penalty?
減量のノウハウを本にまとめたら、ボートレーサー志望者の教科書になった。: I compiled my weight-cutting know-how into a book, and it became a textbook for aspiring boat racers.
骨密度が落ち、30代で骨折した。: My bone density dropped, and I broke a bone in my thirties.
体調が安定し、レーサー人生が長くなった。: My health stabilized, and my racing career grew longer.
重さが響いて、勝率が下がった。: The extra weight told, and my win rate dropped.
体重が戻って体力がつき、年間100走を休みなく走れた。: My weight came back, my stamina improved, and I ran 100 races a year without a break.
重量調整のおもりが外れる珍事で失格になり、珍プレー番組に流された。: A freak accident — my weight-adjustment ballast fell off — got me disqualified, and it aired on a blooper show.
レースの最終周、ラインの先輩を守るか、自分が勝ちに行くか迷った。: On the final lap, I couldn’t decide whether to protect my senior in the line or go for the win myself.
先輩が1着になり、後で深く感謝された。地元での信頼が増した。: My senior took first and thanked me deeply afterward. My standing back home grew.
先輩も負け、自分も負けた。: My senior lost, and so did I.
先輩が引退するときに地元のライン全員から花束を受け取り、自分が後継者として指名さ: When my senior retired, I received bouquets from the whole local line and was named as the successor.
先輩が自分の頑張りを当然と思っていて、次からも盾役を任された。: My senior took my effort for granted, and I was assigned the shield role again from then on.
1着になった。でも先輩との関係は冷えた。: Took first. But things turned cold with my senior.
失速して、二人とも着外だった。: I faded, and both of us finished out of the places.
その1勝が初のG1優勝になり、賞金で家を建てた。: That win became my first G1 title, and I built a house with the prize money.
SNSで「裏切り者」と叩かれ、地元の練習会に呼ばれなくなった。: Slammed on social media as a “traitor,” and I stopped being invited to local practice sessions.
ケガが続き、引退を考え始めた。: Injuries kept piling up, and I started thinking about retiring.
地元で自転車店を開き、子どもたちに教えた。: Opened a bicycle shop in my hometown and taught the kids.
何をすればいいか分からず、しばらく落ち込んだ。: Didn’t know what to do with myself and was down for a while.
自転車店の教え子が競輪学校に合格し、引退レースで3着になった。: A student from my bicycle shop got into keirin school, and I finished third in my farewell race.
元選手のYouTubeを始め、登録者5万人になった。: Started a YouTube channel as a former racer and reached 50,000 subscribers.
ケガから復帰し、地元記念で優勝した。: Came back from injury and won the local commemorative race.
50歳まで現役を続け、最年長勝利記録をつくった。: Kept racing until 50 and set the record for the oldest winner.
練習中に転倒し、鎖骨を2本折った。: Crashed during practice and broke both collarbones.
有力馬の騎乗依頼が2つ重なった。長年の恩がある調教師の馬か、勝てそうな人気馬か。: Two offers came in to ride top horses. The horse of a trainer I owe for years of support, or the favorite likely to win?
恩のある馬に乗る: Ride the horse of the trainer I owe
人気薄ながら2着に入り、調教師が泣いて喜んだ。: Though a long shot, it finished second, and the trainer wept with joy.
大敗し、人気馬は別の騎手で勝った。: Lost badly, and the favorite won with another jockey.
その馬が翌年G1を勝ち、調教師に「お前の騎乗で育った」と言われた。: That horse won a G1 the next year, and the trainer told me, “You raised him with your riding.”
調教師が引退を決め、最後のレースを一緒に戦った。泣いた。: The trainer decided to retire, and we fought his last race together. I cried.
負けたうえ、恩のある調教師から依頼が来なくなった。: Not only did I lose, the trainer I owe stopped sending me rides.
人気馬のオーナーに気に入られ、海外遠征に連れて行ってもらえた。: The favorite’s owner took a liking to me and brought me along on an overseas trip.
人気馬が故障して、レースを走れなかった。: The favorite got injured and couldn’t run the race.
海外（フランス）で修行しないかと誘われた。: Was invited to train abroad in France.
現地で重賞を勝ち、帰国後は依頼が殺到した。: Won a graded stakes race there, and requests poured in after I returned home.
言葉の壁で騎乗機会が少なく、1年で帰国した。: The language barrier meant few rides, and I came home after a year.
フランスで知り合った調教師の娘と結婚した。: Married the daughter of a trainer I met in France.
落馬して骨折し、現地の病院で2か月入院した。: Fell from a horse, broke a bone, and spent two months in a local hospital.
地道に勝ち星を重ね、通算500勝を達成した。: Steadily piled up wins and reached 500 career victories.
若手の台頭で、騎乗依頼が減った。: Young riders rose, and my ride requests dwindled.
重賞を初勝利し、地元の祭りで表彰された。: Won my first graded stakes race and was honored at the local festival.
落馬事故で長期休養し、引退を考えた。: A fall kept me out for a long recovery, and I considered retiring.
怪我の膝が治りきっていないが、出場しないと幕下に落ちる。: My injured knee hasn’t fully healed, but if I don’t compete I’ll drop to makushita.
勝ち越して番付を守った。: Finished with a winning record and kept my rank.
怪我が悪化し、長期休場になった。: The injury got worse, and I was out for a long time.
勝ち越しで大関昇進の可能性も見え、地元で後援会が倍になった。: With a winning record, promotion to ozeki came into view, and my local supporters’ association doubled.
勝ち越したが、膝の手術が必要になり、1年後の場所を棒に振った。: Won more than I lost, but my knee needed surgery, and I wrote off the tournament a year later.
番付は下がったが、復帰後に優勝争いに絡んだ。: My rank dropped, but after returning I got into the title race.
番付が下がりすぎて、引退を考えた。: My rank fell so far that I considered retiring.
休場中にちゃんこの腕を磨き、部屋の料理番として若手に慕われた。: While sitting out, I sharpened my chanko skills and became the stable’s cook, adored by the younger wrestlers.
復帰したら若手に番付を抜かれ、ついていけなかった。: After I returned, younger wrestlers overtook my rank, and I couldn’t keep up.
引退後、親方として残るか、ちゃんこ屋を開くか迷った。: After retiring, I couldn’t decide whether to stay on as a stablemaster or open a chanko restaurant.
年寄株を取得し、弟子が関取になった。: Acquired an elder stock, and my disciple became a sekitori.
弟子が横綱に昇進し、テレビで「親方に育ててもらった」と言った。: My disciple was promoted to yokozuna and said on TV, “My stablemaster raised me.”
年寄株の取得に1億円かかり、借金を背負った。: Acquiring the elder stock cost ¥100 million, and I took on debt.
現役時代のファンが通い、繁盛した。: Fans from my wrestling days came, and the place thrived.
コロナ禍で客足が途絶え、閉店した。: Customers vanished during the COVID pandemic, and I closed the restaurant.
ちゃんこ屋が雑誌で紹介され、2号店を出した。: The restaurant was featured in a magazine, and I opened a second location.
仕込みと営業で毎日16時間働き、体を壊した。: Prep and service meant 16-hour days, and I ruined my health.
勝てば昇級の大一番。AIで研究した奇襲戦法を使うか迷った。: A crucial game: win and I get promoted. Couldn’t decide whether to spring the surprise strategy I’d researched with AI.
相手が対応できず完勝した。昇級した。: My opponent couldn’t respond, and I won decisively. Got promoted.
相手も研究済みで、完敗した。: My opponent had prepared for it too, and I was crushed.
奇襲戦法に自分の名前がつき、「〇〇流」として本が出た。: The surprise strategy was named after me, and a book came out on the “○○ style.”
奇襲がネットで「AI頼み」と叩かれた。: The surprise strategy got slammed online as “relying on AI.”
最後までもつれ、粘り勝った。: It went down to the wire, and I won by sheer persistence.
終盤でミスして負けた。: Made a mistake in the endgame and lost.
粘り勝ちの一局が年間最優秀対局に選ばれた。: The hard-fought win was chosen as game of the year.
勝ったものの終盤の悪手を解説で散々指摘された。: I won, but the commentary kept pointing out my bad move in the endgame.
テレビや講演の仕事が増えてきた。対局の研究時間が減るのが心配だ。: TV and speaking jobs are increasing. I worry about losing time to study for my games.
人気が出て、収入は倍になった。: I became popular, and my income doubled.
成績が落ち、ファンにも心配された。: My results slipped, and fans were worried.
将棋の子ども教室を開いたら、生徒が200人になった。: I opened a shogi class for kids, and it grew to 200 students.
テレビの撮影中に失言し、謝罪会見を開いた。: Made a gaffe during a TV shoot and held an apology press conference.
研究会仲間とタイトルを争う関係になり、親友兼ライバルになった。: A study-group friend and I ended up competing for a title, becoming best friends and rivals.
研究しすぎて睡眠不足が続き、対局中に倒れた。: Overstudying left me chronically sleep-deprived, and I collapsed during a game.
船外活動中、予定外のトラブルが発生した。: During a spacewalk, an unexpected problem occurred.
時間を延長して修理: Extend the time and repair it
修理を完了し、ミッションを救った。: Completed the repair and saved the mission.
酸素の残量が危なくなり、管制に怒られた。: Oxygen ran dangerously low, and mission control scolded me.
修理中に見た地球の景色が忘れられず、写真集を出したら10万部売れた。: I couldn’t forget the view of Earth I saw during the repair; I published a photo book, and it sold 100,000 copies.
船外活動の負担で腰を痛め、帰還後半年リハビリした。: The strain of the spacewalk hurt my back, and I did six months of rehab after returning.
翌日、別の飛行士が修理した。: The next day, another astronaut made the repair.
ミッションが一部失敗に終わった。: The mission ended in partial failure.
戻る判断が後に「理想的なリスク管理」として訓練教材になった。: The decision to come back later became training material as “ideal risk management.”

カーブで滑って転んだ。右手首を痛め、2週間シャーペンが持てなかった。: Slipped on a curve and fell. Hurt my right wrist and couldn't hold a mechanical pencil for two weeks.
びしょぬれで塾に着いた。講師にタオルを借りた。: Arrived at cram school soaking wet. Borrowed a towel from an instructor.
バスの30分で、単語を50個覚えた。それから毎日バスで行くようになった。: Memorized 50 words in those 30 minutes on the bus. After that, I took the bus every day.
受験生向けの「合格祈願パフェ」が駅前のカフェで売られている。: A café by the station is selling a “Pass-Prayer Parfait” for exam takers.
パフェを食べた。てっぺんの「合格」と書いたクッキーを、最後まで残した。: Ate the parfait. Saved the cookie on top that said “Pass” for last.
家でキットカットとアイスで再現: Recreate it at home with Kit Kats and ice cream
家でパフェを再現した。妹に「なにそれ」と笑われたが、一緒に食べた。: Recreated the parfait at home. My little sister laughed, “What is that?” but we ate it together.
オンライン家庭教師の先生が、画面越しにずっとカップ麺を食べている。: My online tutor keeps eating cup noodles through the screen the whole time.
指摘したら、先生は「ごめん、夜勤明けで」と言った。それから、その先生を少し好きに: When I pointed it out, the tutor said, “Sorry, I just got off a night shift.” After that, I liked them a little.
先生を変えた。新しい先生は、厳しすぎて泣いた。成績は上がった。: Switched tutors. The new one was so strict I cried. My grades went up.
父が「俺も一緒に勉強する」と言い出し、リビングで宅建の勉強を始めた。: Dad announced, “I'll study with you,” and started studying for the real estate licensing exam in the living room.
毎晩、父とリビングで勉強した。父も宅建に合格した。合格祝いは2人分だった。: Studied with Dad in the living room every night. Dad passed his real estate exam too. The celebration was for two.
父は2週間で寝落ちするようになった。いびきがうるさくて部屋に戻った。: After two weeks, Dad started falling asleep mid-study. His snoring was so loud I went back to my room.
自分の部屋で勉強した。リビングから、父が問題を読み上げる声が聞こえてきた。: Studied in my own room. From the living room, I could hear Dad reading out practice questions.
受験期の家族ルールで、「落ちる」「滑る」が禁句になった。: Under our exam-season family rules, “fall” and “slip” became forbidden words.
家で「落とした」を「ごはんが床に旅立った」と言うようになった。: At home, I started saying “the rice set off for the floor” instead of “I dropped it.”
「気にしすぎ」と言った次の日、玄関で盛大に滑って転んだ。家族は誰も何も言わなかっ: The day after I said “You're overthinking it,” I slipped and fell spectacularly in the entryway. Nobody in the family said a word.
大手予備校の特待生テストを受けないかと声をかけられた。: A major prep school asked if I'd take their scholarship test.
受かれば授業料が全額免除になる。: If I pass, tuition is waived in full.
特待生になった。授業料は0円になったが、毎回最前列に座らされた。: Became a scholarship student. Tuition dropped to zero yen, but I was made to sit in the front row every time.
特待生テストに落ちた。その日、本番もダメな気がした。: Failed the scholarship test. That day, I had a feeling the real exam would go badly too.
受けなかった。今の塾で最後までやった。: Didn't take it. Stuck it out to the end at my current cram school.
教室の机に、前の学年の先輩の落書きを見つけた。「あと少し、がんばれ」: Found graffiti from a senior of a previous year on a classroom desk: “Almost there, hang in there.”
「がんばります」と書き足した。卒業前、その下にもう一言書いた。「次の人もがんばれ: Added “I'll do my best.” Before graduating, I wrote one more line beneath it: “To the next person, hang in there too.”
消しゴムで消した。消したあとも、なんとなく覚えている。: Erased it with an eraser. Even after erasing it, I somehow still remember it.
総合型選抜の志望理由書。締め切りは明日。: The statement of purpose for comprehensive selection admissions. The deadline is tomorrow.
AIに「志望理由書 1200字 熱意あふれる感じで」と打ち込めば、3秒で終わる。: If I type “statement of purpose, 1,200 characters, passionate tone” into an AI, it's done in three seconds.
面接で「この“知の地平を切り拓く”とは具体的に？」と聞かれ、自分の書いた文章の意: In the interview, I was asked, “What exactly does ‘opening new horizons of knowledge’ mean here?” and I didn't understand my own writing.
書類審査で、他の受験生と一字一句同じ段落があると指摘された。不合格だった。: In the document screening, it was pointed out that one paragraph was word-for-word identical to another applicant's. Rejected.
そのまま提出して、通った。: Submitted it as is, and it passed.
徹夜で書いた。下手な文章だったが、面接では全部自分の言葉で話せた。: Wrote all night. The writing was clumsy, but in the interview I could speak entirely in my own words.
推薦の書類に書く「課外活動」が何もない。: I have no “extracurricular activities” to put on my recommendation application.
友だちが「ボランティアは1回行けば“継続的に参加”って書いていい」と言う。: A friend says, “If you go to a volunteer event just once, you can write ‘participated continuously.’”
「地域清掃ボランティアに3年間継続して参加」と書いた。実際に行ったのは1回だった: Wrote “Participated continuously in community cleanup volunteering for three years.” In reality, I went once.
何も書かなかった。代わりに、その月から本当に毎週ボランティアに通った。卒業までに: Wrote nothing. Instead, from that month on, I really did volunteer every week. By graduation I'd gone 40 times.
頭のいい自分に、浪人中の先輩が頼んできた。「俺の代わりに受けてくれ。50万払う」: A senior who's a ronin came to me, the smart one, with a request: “Take the exam for me. I'll pay you 500,000 yen.”
替え玉受験をする: Take the exam as a stand-in
試験当日、受験票の写真と顔が違うと監督者に止められた。その場で警察が呼ばれた。: On exam day, a proctor stopped me because my face didn't match the photo on the exam ticket. The police were called on the spot.
替え玉受験として、自分も先輩も偽計業務妨害で逮捕された。ニュースでは実名こそ出な: For the stand-in exam, both the senior and I were arrested for obstruction of business by fraudulent means. My name wasn't in the news, but I was expelled from high school.
先輩の代わりに受けた。先輩は合格し、自分は50万円を受け取った。: Took the exam in the senior's place. The senior passed, and I received 500,000 yen.
断った。翌年、先輩は別の人に頼んで捕まったと、地元のニュースで知った。: Refused. The next year, I learned from the local news that the senior had asked someone else and got caught.
合格発表の日。親が仕事中に「どうだった？」とLINEしてきた。: Results day. My parent texted me on LINE from work: “How did it go?”
まだ結果は見ていない。: I haven't looked at the result yet.
結果を開いたら、番号はなかった。親はもう親戚中に電話していた。夜、祖母から合格祝: When I opened the results, my number wasn't there. My parent had already called all the relatives. That night, an envelope with a congratulatory gift arrived from Grandma.
結果を開いたら、本当に受かっていた。冷や汗が止まらなかった。: When I opened the results, I had really passed. The cold sweat wouldn't stop.
深呼吸して、結果を開いた。: Took a deep breath and opened the result.
高3の冬、志望校はE判定のまま。: Winter of senior year, and my target school is still rated E.
「浪人すればいける」と、心のどこかで思っている。: Somewhere in my heart, I think, “If I take a year off to retake it, I can make it.”
最初から浪人前提でいく: Plan on a ronin year from the start
今年は記念受験: Just a try for the experience this year
今年は記念受験と決めた。冬、同級生が必死な横で、少しだけ余裕だった。: Decided to treat this year as a just-for-the-experience attempt. That winter, I had a bit of breathing room next to my desperate classmates.
今年で決めると親に宣言した。そこから毎日、学校の自習室が閉まるまで残った。: Declared to my parents that I'd settle it this year. From then on, I stayed at the school study room every day until it closed.
全国模試の数学の問題が、試験前日にネットに流出しているのを見つけた。: I found the math questions of a national mock exam leaked online the day before the test.
見た。数学は偏差値78だった。本番の共通テストでは、偏差値52だった。: Looked. Got a deviation score of 78 in math. On the real Common Test, it was 52.
見なかった。模試の数学は散々だった。本番では、模試より20点高かった。: Didn't look. Did terribly in math on the mock exam. On the real one, I scored 20 points higher than the mock.
英単語帳の1ページ目「abandon」しか覚えていない。: All I remember from my English vocab book is “abandon” on page 1.
1日100語を毎日続けた。単語帳は3冊目でボロボロになった。: Kept up 100 words a day, every day. By the third vocab book, it was falling apart.
「長文で覚えればいい」: “I'll just learn words from reading passages”
単語帳を捨てた。共通テストの英語で、知らない単語が1ページに12個あった。: Threw away the vocab book. On the Common Test English section, there were 12 words I didn't know on a single page.
第一志望に届きそうにない。「とりあえず受かったところに入って、仮面浪人すればいい: My first choice looks out of reach. A senior says, “Just go wherever you get in and secretly study for a retake.”
仮面浪人を前提に、受験校を決めた。: Chose which schools to apply to on the assumption of a hidden retake year.
受かった大学で頑張る: Do my best at the school I get into
受かった大学で4年間やりきると決めた。: Decided to see through all four years at the university I got into.
合格祈願で神社に行った。お賽銭はいくら入れる？: Went to a shrine to pray for success. How much should I put in the offering box?
財布には5円玉と1万円札しかない。: All I have in my wallet is a 5-yen coin and a 10,000-yen bill.
1万円を入れた。おみくじは「大凶」だった。神主さんが気まずそうに目をそらした。: Put in the 10,000 yen. My fortune slip said “Great Misfortune.” The priest awkwardly looked away.
1万円を入れた。おみくじは「大吉・学問：思うままなり」。その日から無敵の気分にな: Put in the 10,000 yen. My fortune slip said “Great Blessing. Studies: all goes as you wish.” From that day on, I felt invincible.
1万円を入れたのを、横で見ていた知らないおじいさんに「若いのにえらい」と褒められ: A stranger, an old man, saw me put in the 10,000 yen and praised me, “Good for one so young,” and for some reason gave me three mandarin oranges.
ご縁がありますように: May fate be on my side
5円玉を投げたら、跳ね返って自分の足元に戻ってきた。もう一度投げる勇気はなかった: Threw in the 5-yen coin, and it bounced back to my feet. I didn't have the nerve to throw it again.
5円玉を入れた。おみくじは「末吉・学問：油断するな」。ちょうどいい現実だった。: Put in the 5-yen coin. My fortune slip said “Small Blessing. Studies: don't let your guard down.” A fitting dose of reality.
共通テスト1日目。マークシートの塗りつぶしの途中で、ふと気づいた。: Day one of the Common Test. Partway through filling in the answer sheet, I suddenly noticed something.
1問ずれている気がする。残り時間は8分。: I think my answers are off by one question. Eight minutes left.
消しゴムをフル稼働させて、残り10秒で全部塗り直した。手が震えて、消しカスが机か: Put my eraser to work at full speed and redid everything with 10 seconds left. My hands shook, and eraser shavings fell off the desk like snow.
全部塗り直したら、ずれていなかった。正解を全部消して、全部ずらしていた。: After redoing it all, I found it hadn't been off at all. I'd erased all the correct answers and shifted every one of them.
自己採点で、大問2から最後まで1つずつずれていたとわかった。数学IA：18点。: Scoring myself, I found everything from section 2 to the end was off by one. Math I-A: 18 points.
共通テスト当日の朝。目覚ましが鳴らなかった。: The morning of the Common Test. My alarm didn't go off.
時計は8時。集合は8時50分。: The clock says 8:00. Assembly is at 8:50.
タクシーの運転手に「受験生です」と言ったら、運転手が「任せろ」と言った。信号を全: Told the taxi driver, “I'm a test taker,” and the driver said, “Leave it to me.” We hit every light green.
タクシーで会場に着いたら、隣の大学のキャンパスだった。全力で走って、着席は8時4: When the taxi dropped me off, it was the campus of the university next door. I sprinted and took my seat at 8:49.
パジャマの上にコートを着ただけで会場に着いた。トイレの鏡を見て、寝ぐせが天井を向: Arrived at the venue wearing just a coat over my pajamas. Looking in the restroom mirror, my bed head was pointing at the ceiling.
パトカーで送ってもらう: Get a ride in a patrol car
交番に駆け込んだら、パトカーで会場まで送ってもらえた。到着の様子がテレビのニュー: Ran into a police box and got driven to the venue in a patrol car. Footage of my arrival aired on the TV news. The whole class found out.
共通テストのお昼。母が作ってくれた弁当を開けた。: Lunchtime at the Common Test. I opened the bento Mom made for me.
弁当のふたを開けたら、海苔で「合格」と書いてあった。周りの3人がちらっと見て、目: When I lifted the bento lid, “Pass” was spelled out in seaweed. Three people around me glanced over and looked away.
弁当の真ん中に、カツが4枚重なっていた。午後の試験、ずっと胃もたれしていた。: Four cutlets were stacked in the middle of the bento. I felt queasy from heavy food the entire afternoon exam.
弁当箱の中身が、空だった。母のメモに「ごめん、お父さんのと間違えた」。: The bento box was empty. Mom's note read, “Sorry, I mixed it up with Dad's.”
弁当を開けたら、おかずが全部「キットカット」だった。: When I opened the bento, every side dish was a Kit Kat.
コンビニで買う: Buy something at a convenience store
コンビニに行ったら、受験生が全員カツサンドを持っていた。カツサンドだけ売り切れて: At the convenience store, every test taker was holding a katsu sandwich. The katsu sandwiches alone were sold out.
試験の休み時間、隣の受験生が急にこっちを見て言った。「それ、ゴミですか？」: During a break between exams, the test taker next to me suddenly looked over and said, “Is that trash?”
自分の机の上には、消しカスの山がある。: There's a pile of eraser shavings on my desk.
「ゴミです」と答えたら、その人は自分の消しカスもこっちの山に足して去っていった。: I answered, “It's trash,” and they added their own eraser shavings to my pile and walked off.
「アートです」と答えた。その人は少し笑った。合格後、大学の入学式でその人と再会し: I answered, “It's art.” They smiled a little. After getting in, we met again at the university entrance ceremony, and they said, “You're the art person.”
受験の朝、母が玄関で言った。「何があっても、あんたは、あんたよ」: On exam morning, Mom said at the front door, “No matter what happens, you're still you.”
「ありがとう」と言った。電車の中で、少し泣いた。: Said “Thank you.” Cried a little on the train.
「縁起でもない」と言ったら、母が「確かに」と言い直した。「あんたは受かる」。それ: When I said, “Don't jinx it,” Mom corrected herself: “Right. You'll pass.” That was its own kind of pressure.
二次試験の会場。周りが全員スーツか私服なのに、自分だけ高校の制服だった。: At the secondary exam venue. Everyone else was in suits or casual clothes, and I was the only one in a high school uniform.
堂々としていたら、隣の浪人生に「現役ですか。いいですね」とため息をつかれた。: While I was holding my head high, the ronin next to me sighed, “You're straight out of high school? Lucky you.”
上着で制服を隠したら、暖房が効きすぎていて汗だくになった。: Hid the uniform under a jacket, but the heating was too strong and I ended up drenched in sweat.
試験会場に向かう途中、頭に鳥のフンが落ちてきた。: On the way to the exam venue, bird droppings fell on my head.
「ウンがついた」と喜んだ。その日の試験は、本当によくできた。: Rejoiced, “Luck has landed on me!” (a pun: “poop” and “luck” sound alike in Japanese). The exam that day really went well.
「ウンがついた」と喜んでいたら、もう1羽に落とされた。: While rejoicing, “Luck has landed on me!”, another bird dropped one on me.
トイレで洗う: Wash it off in the restroom
トイレで髪を洗った。ハンドドライヤーで頭を乾かしている姿を、同じ高校の子に見られ: Washed my hair in the restroom. A kid from my own high school saw me drying my head under the hand dryer.
受験期のバレンタイン。気になる人に渡すか迷っている。: Valentine's Day during exam season. Torn about whether to give chocolate to the person I like.
二次試験まであと2週間。: Two weeks until the secondary exam.
渡した。「受験終わったら、お礼させて」と言われた。3月、本当にデートに行った。: Gave it to them. They said, “Let me thank you once the exams are over.” In March, we really went on a date.
渡そうとしたら、相手が「今日は受験だから」と学校に来ていなかった。チョコは自分で: When I tried to give it, they weren't at school because they had an exam that day. I ate the chocolate myself.
渡した。翌日、相手から「キットカット」1枚が机に置いてあった。意味は今もわからな: Gave it to them. The next day, a single Kit Kat had been left on my desk from them. I still don't know what it means.
合格したら渡すと決めて、チョコを冷蔵庫に入れた。3月、チョコは父に食べられていた: Decided to give it once I passed, and put the chocolate in the fridge. In March, Dad had eaten the chocolate.
占い師に「あなたの守護霊は、受験の神様です」と言われた。: A fortune-teller told me, “Your guardian spirit is the god of exams.”
信じたら、本当に自信がついて成績が上がった。プラシーボ効果だと、後で知った。: I believed it, and I really gained confidence and my grades went up. I later learned it was the placebo effect.
信じて油断した。守護霊は、二次試験の日、休みだったらしい。: I believed it and let my guard down. Apparently my guardian spirit had the day off on the day of the secondary exam.
信じなかった。8,000円で参考書を2冊買えた、と30分くらい後悔した。: Didn't believe it. For about 30 minutes I regretted that 8,000 yen could have bought two study guides.
推しゲームで「合格祈願ガチャ」が始まった。: A “Pass-Prayer Gacha” started in my favorite game.
SSRは「合格」と書かれたハチマキを巻いたキャラ。: The SSR is a character wearing a headband that says “Pass.”
天井まで回して、3万円使った。SSRのキャラは受験期間中、ずっとスマホの壁紙だっ: Pulled until the pity cap and spent 30,000 yen. The SSR character was my phone wallpaper for the entire exam period.
1回目でSSRが出た。運をここで使い切った気がして、試験前日まで震えていた。: Got the SSR on the first pull. I felt like I'd used up all my luck there and trembled right up to the day before the exam.
天井まで回したら、ガチャの結果画面を見た母に、スマホを取り上げられた。: After I pulled until the pity cap, Mom saw the gacha results screen and confiscated my phone.
合格したら回すと決めた。合格発表の日、ガチャは終わっていた。: Decided to pull once I passed. By results day, the gacha had ended.
試験中、静まり返った会場で、くしゃみが出そうになった。: During the exam, in the dead-silent hall, I felt a sneeze coming.
全力でこらえる: Hold it in with all my might
全力でこらえたら、「ふごっ」という音が鼻から出た。会場の何人かの肩が震えていた。: I held it in with all my might, and a “fugo!” sound came out of my nose. The shoulders of several people in the venue were shaking.
思いきりくしゃみをした。会場の向こうで、誰かが「お大事に」と小声で言った。少し泣: Sneezed with full force. From across the venue, someone whispered, “Bless you.” I almost teared up a little.
試験会場に向かう満員電車。目の前のおじさんが、自分の受験票を見て言った。「その大: On the packed train to the exam venue, the middle-aged man in front of me looked at my exam ticket and said, “That university? It's my alma mater.”
おじさんは学食の唐揚げの話を15分した。試験には1ミリも関係なかったが、緊張がほ: The man talked about the fried chicken in the cafeteria for 15 minutes. It had nothing to do with the exam, but it eased my nerves.
おじさんは降りぎわに「赤本の2009年、やっとけよ」と言った。家に帰って解いたら: As he got off, he said, “Do the 2009 edition of the past exam book.” When I got home and solved it, it was nearly identical to the questions that came up.
おじさんは、その大学の教授だった。試験会場で、監督者として再会した。: The man was a professor at that university. We met again at the exam venue, where he was a proctor.
イヤホンをつけたら、おじさんはそのまま隣の受験生に話しかけ始めた。: When I put in my earphones, the man simply started talking to the test taker next to me.
試験会場が寒い。カイロを貼る場所を決めなきゃ。: The exam venue is cold. I need to decide where to stick my heat pack.
背中に貼った。暖房が入って、背中だけ灼熱になった。: Stuck it on my back. Then the heating came on, and only my back became scorching hot.
お腹に3枚貼ったら、低温やけどで、試験中ずっとお腹がヒリヒリしていた。: Three heat pads on my stomach gave me a low-temperature burn. My belly stung through the whole exam.
県外受験の前泊。ホテルの部屋の隣から、夜中まで騒ぐ声がする。: Staying the night before an out-of-prefecture exam. The room next door is noisy until late.
フロントに電話したら、隣の部屋は同じ大学を受ける受験生のグループで、合格祈願の円: The front desk said the next room was a group taking exams at the same university, huddled in a circle praying for success.
フロントに電話したら、スタッフが「受験生の方ですね」と、別の階の部屋に移してくれ: The staff said, “You must be an exam taker,” and moved me to a room on another floor. They even gave me earplugs.
壁を叩いたら、叩き返された。そこからなぜかリズムが合ってしまい、セッションになっ: I banged on the wall and they banged back. Somehow we fell into rhythm and it turned into a jam session. I didn't sleep.
試験中。監督者の革靴が、通路を歩くたびに「キュッ、キュッ」と鳴る。: During the exam. The proctor's leather shoes squeak with every step down the aisle.

知らない人たちが、自分の名前を書いてくれた。: Strangers wrote their name for them.
自分の看板を掲げた。重さも、自分で背負った。: Hung out their own sign. Carried its weight alone, too.
何人の最期に立ち会ったか、途中から数えなくなった。: Somewhere along the way, they stopped counting how many final moments they had been present for.
何百人もの「先生」になった。覚えているのは、ほんの何人か。: Became a “teacher” to hundreds. Remembered only a handful.
天気予報を、誰よりも真剣に見ていた。: Watched the weather forecast more seriously than anyone.
家族の毎日は、この人の手でできていた。: The family’s everyday life was made by this person’s hands.
誰も知らないことを、一つだけ知っていた。: Knew just one thing that no one else knew.
みんなが眠っている時間に、誰かのそばにいた。: Was at someone’s side while everyone else slept.
何も起きなかった日が、いちばんの仕事だった。: The days when nothing happened were the best work.
救えた人の顔より、救えなかった人の顔を覚えていた。: Remembered the faces of those they could not save more than those they could.
窓口の向こうの人生を、毎日見ていた。: Saw, every day, the lives on the other side of the counter.
使いきれなかった。使い方を、誰も教えてくれなかった。: Could not spend it all. No one ever taught them how to use it.
特別なことは何も起きなかった。それを続けるのが、いちばん難しかった。: Nothing special happened. Keeping that up was the hardest part.
誰にも頼らなかった。誰かに頼ればよかった日も、少しだけあった。: Relied on no one. There were a few days when leaning on someone would have been better.
数字は増えた。何に使えばよかったのかは、最後までわからなかった。: The numbers grew. What to spend them on, they never figured out.
うまくいかない年のほうが多かった。それでも、毎朝起きた。: Most years did not go well. Still, they got up every morning.
何度も底を見た。そのたびに、もう一日だけ生きた。: Hit rock bottom many times. Each time, lived one more day.
取り返せないことをした。残りの人生で、それを抱えて生きた。: Did something that could not be undone. Carried it for the rest of their life.
表の道が、最初から用意されていなかった。: The front road was never laid out for them in the first place.
あの日、手を伸ばしたことだけは、後悔していない。: The one thing they do not regret is reaching out that day.
短かった。それでも、確かにここにいた。: It was short. Still, they were here, truly.
名前をもらい、抱かれて、それで終わった。それでも、生まれてきた。: Given a name, held in arms, and that was all. Still, they were born.
一世紀ぶんの朝を迎えた。: Greeted a century’s worth of mornings.
最後に握られた手は、小さくて温かかった。: The hand that held theirs at the end was small and warm.
一度目でわかったことを、二度目に生かした。: Used in the second round what they learned in the first.
食卓はいつも、椅子が足りなかった。: The dining table never had enough chairs.
働かなかった。働けなかった日も、たしかにあった。: Did not work. There were also days when they truly could not.
どこにも属さなかった。そのぶん、どこへでも行けた。: Belonged nowhere. For that very reason, could go anywhere.
一瞬でも、何万人の前に立った。: Even if only for a moment, stood before tens of thousands.
頂点から見た景色を、一生覚えていた。: Remembered the view from the top for the rest of their life.
教科書に名前が載った。本人はそれを照れくさがった。: Their name appeared in textbooks. They were embarrassed by it.
それなりに笑い、それなりに泣いた。: Laughed a fair amount, cried a fair amount.
選べなかったことと、選んだことでできた一生だった。: A life made of what they could not choose and what they chose.
大きな記録は残らなかった。小さな記憶はたくさん残った。: No great records remained. Many small memories did.
うまくいったことも、いかなかったことも、全部この人のものだった。: What went well and what did not, all of it belonged to this person.

貸した金は、結局返ってこなかった。: The money I lent was never paid back.
母は最後まで何も言わなかった。: Mother never said a word to the very end.
合格したら渡すと決めて、チョコを冷蔵庫に入れた。: Decided to give it to them if they passed, and put the chocolate in the fridge.
ネットで「テンプレ作家」と叩かれ、しばらくネットを見られなかった。: Slammed online as a “formulaic writer,” I couldn’t look at the internet for a while.
センター試験のリスニングで、ICプレーヤーの音が途中で途切れた。: During the Center Test listening section, the sound on the IC player cut out partway through.
受験の時の単語帳のページが、頭に浮かんだ。: A page from my vocabulary book from exam days came to mind.
15歳で東京都府中市を出て、奈良県の西大和学園高校の寮に入った。: Left Fuchu, Tokyo at 15 and moved into the dorm at Nishiyamato Gakuen High School in Nara.
「2030年問題」。人手が約640万人足りないと推計された年になった。求人の貼り: The “2030 problem” arrived: a year when the labor shortage was estimated at about 6.4 million workers. Shops without a help-wanted sign were the rarity.
「2040年問題」。65歳以上が約3,900万人でピークになり、働き手は約1,1: The “2040 problem”: people aged 65 and over peaked at about 39 million, and the workforce was estimated to fall short by about 11 million.
今人が住んでいる地域のおよそ2割が、誰も住まない土地になると言われていた年が来た: The year came when about 20% of the areas now inhabited were said to become land where no one lives.
日本の人口が、推計どおり1億人を割った。: Japan’s population fell below 100 million, just as projected.
人口は約8,700万人。4割近くが65歳以上で、10人に1人が外国から来た人にな: The population was about 87 million. It was projected that nearly 40% would be 65 or older, and 1 in 10 people would be from abroad.
人口は約5,000万人。明治の終わりごろと同じ人数まで減ると推計されていた年だっ: The population was about 50 million, projected to shrink to the level of the late Meiji era.

子どもの小学校が隣の学区と統合された。通学路が倍の長さになり、朝はスクールバスの: My child’s elementary school was merged with the neighboring district’s. The route to school doubled in length, and every morning I started driving my child to the school bus stop.
町でその年に生まれた赤ちゃんが10人を切ったと広報に載った。お産ができる病院は、: The town newsletter reported that fewer than 10 babies were born in town that year. To give birth at a hospital, you had to go to the next city.
近所の公園から子どもの声がほとんど消えた。夕方のブランコは、風で揺れているだけだ: Children’s voices nearly vanished from the neighborhood park. In the evening the swings moved only with the wind.
入学した高校は1学年2クラスしかなかった。部活は人数が足りず、サッカー部は近くの: The high school I entered had only two classes per grade. Clubs lacked members, and the soccer club became a joint team with a nearby school.
担任するクラスの児童が8人になった。複式学級になり、二学年分の授業計画を毎週立て: My homeroom class shrank to 8 pupils. It became a combined-grade class, and every week I had to plan lessons for two grades.
駅前の子ども用品店が撤退した。甥への誕生日プレゼントは、結局ネットで選ぶしかなか: The children’s goods store in front of the station closed. In the end I had no choice but to pick my nephew’s birthday present online.
近所の保育園が定員割れで閉園した。数年前までは待機児童で入れなかったのに、と町内: The neighborhood nursery school closed for lack of enrollment. At the neighborhood association, people said that just a few years ago kids were on waiting lists and couldn’t get in.
勤め先の社員の平均年齢が50歳を超えた。新卒の採用枠は毎年埋まらず、若手がやるは: The average age of employees at my company went past 50. The new-graduate hiring quota went unfilled every year, and work meant for young staff landed on me too.
もう一人子どもを、と夫婦で話した夜があった。教育費の見積もりを並べて計算し、二人: One night my spouse and I talked about having another child. We lined up the estimated education costs and did the math, and we both fell silent.
地域の祭りの子ども神輿が、担ぎ手不足で中止になった。昔は担ぐ子を選ぶほどいたのに: The children’s portable shrine at the local festival was canceled for lack of bearers. There used to be so many kids we had to choose who carried it, and it felt lonely.
勤めていた病院の産科が分娩の取り扱いをやめた。お産が少なすぎて、医師も助産師も確: The maternity ward at the hospital where I worked stopped handling deliveries. There were too few births, and they couldn’t secure doctors or midwives.
地元の成人式の会場が小さな公民館に変わったと聞いた。出席したのは、地元に残った十: I heard the venue for the local Coming-of-Age Day ceremony had been changed to a small community hall. Only a dozen or so who had stayed in town attended.
推計では2070年に出生数が年50万人ほどになると言われた。ニュースのグラフは、: Projections said births would fall to about 500,000 a year by 2070. The graph on the news was a single line sloping down to the right.
市内から小児科のある病院がなくなった。夜に子どもが熱を出した近所の家は、1時間か: The last hospital with a pediatrics department in the city was gone. I heard that a neighbor whose child ran a fever at night drove an hour to the next prefecture.
子ども会が会員不足で解散した。夏休みのラジオ体操もなくなり、子どもは朝から家で画: The children’s association disbanded for lack of members. The summer-vacation morning exercises disappeared too, and kids spent mornings at home looking at screens.
担当していたベビー用品の売り場が縮小され、介護用品の棚に置き換わった。客層の変化: The baby goods section I managed was scaled down and replaced with shelves of nursing-care products. The sales figures laid the change in customers bare.
同い年の人口が親の世代の半分ほどしかないとニュースで知った。自分たちが将来支える: I learned from the news that my age group is only about half the size of my parents’ generation. Thinking of how many people we would have to support, I felt a little afraid.
経営していた学習塾の生徒が年々減り、教室を一つ閉めた。看板を下ろした日は雨だった: The number of students at the cram school I ran fell year after year, and I closed one classroom. The day I took down the sign, it rained.
住宅街から子どもが減り、町内の見守り当番のなり手もいなくなった。結局、毎月のよう: Children dwindled in the residential area, and no one was left to take the neighborhood watch duty. In the end it came around to me almost every month.
役所で少子化対策の担当になった。給付を増やしても下げ止まらない出生数のグラフを前: I was assigned to the declining-birthrate measures at city hall. Facing the birth-count graph that kept falling no matter how much we raised benefits, every meeting felt heavy.
子ども向けの事業を柱にする銘柄が軒並み値を下げた。人口の推計を見れば当然だと、誰: Stocks of companies built around children’s businesses all dropped. Someone on a message board wrote that it was only natural given the population projections.
同窓会の出席者の半分以上が独身だった。誰も結婚の話題を出さず、話は親の介護と健康: More than half of those at the class reunion were single. No one brought up marriage; the talk was all about caring for parents and health checkup numbers.
休日に誰とも話さずに一日が終わった。最後に声を出したのは、コンビニのレジで袋を断: A day off ended without speaking to anyone. The last time I used my voice was declining a bag at the convenience store register.
推計では2040年ごろ、50歳時点で一度も結婚していない男性が約3割になると言わ: Projections said that around 2040, about 30% of men would reach age 50 never having married. Looking around, it was no longer unusual.
保証人を頼める身内がいなくなった。賃貸の更新のたびに、保証会社へ手数料を払うこと: There was no relative left I could ask to be my guarantor. Every rental renewal meant paying a fee to a guarantor company.
入院の手続きで「緊急連絡先」の欄を埋められなかった。病院の窓口で、しばらくペンが: During hospital admission paperwork I couldn’t fill in the “emergency contact” field. At the hospital counter, my pen stopped for a while.
職場の外で人と知り合う機会がなかった。登録した結婚相談所の月会費だけが、毎月口座: I had no chance to meet people outside work. Only the monthly fee for the matchmaking agency I registered with was deducted from my account every month.
職場の飲み会も送別会もなくなった。帰りの電車で、今日誰と話したかを思い出せなかっ: Even the work drinking parties and farewell parties were gone. On the train home, I couldn’t remember who I had talked to that day.
一人分の食材を買う生活が二十年続いた。スーパーの小分け惣菜の棚は、年々広くなって: Twenty years of buying groceries for one. The supermarket’s shelf of small-portion prepared dishes grew wider year by year.
マンションの隣に誰が住んでいるか知らないまま十年が過ぎた。郵便受けの名札は、どこ: Ten years passed without my knowing who lived next door in my apartment building. The nameplates on the mailboxes were blank everywhere.
