独身のまま定年を迎えた同級生から、年賀状じまいの便りが届いた。「これで最後です」: A classmate who reached retirement still single sent word that they were ending their New Year’s cards. The line “This is the last one” weighed heavily.
一人で受けた人間ドックで要精密検査になった。結果を一緒に聞いてくれる人がいないこ: My solo full medical checkup said I needed a detailed follow-up exam. On the way home I realized there was no one to hear the results with me.
自治体に孤独・孤立対策の窓口ができたが、担当は自分ひとりだった。相談の電話は、い: The municipality set up a loneliness and isolation support desk, but I was the only one staffing it. Calls for help always came in at night.
友人の結婚式に呼ばれる回数が、ここ十年でゼロになった。代わりに届くのは、誰かの親: In the past ten years, invitations to friends’ weddings dropped to zero. What arrived instead was news of someone’s parent passing away.
新しく建つのは単身向けの小さな部屋ばかりだった。ファミリー向けの物件は、街から少: Everything newly built was small units for single people. Family-sized housing gradually disappeared from the city.
親が亡くなり、実家に一人残った。部屋の数だけが多く、どの部屋にも明かりをつける理: My parents died, and I was left alone in the family home. There were many rooms, but no reason to turn on the light in any of them.
収入が不安定で、結婚は最初から選択肢に入れていなかった。届いた年金の見込み額を見: My income was unstable, and I had never counted marriage as an option. After seeing the projected pension amount that arrived, I thought about it even less.
推計では2050年に一人暮らしの世帯が全体の4割を超えると言われた。近所のスーパ: Projections said that by 2050, single-person households would exceed 40% of all households. At the nearby supermarket, single-serving bento boxes took up most of the shelves.
料理を作っても「おいしい」と言う相手がいないので、作らなくなった。夕食はいつも、: With no one to say “delicious,” I stopped cooking. I always finished dinner standing up.
自治体の婚活イベントに参加したが、集まった男女の人数が大きく偏っていた。会話は半: I attended a municipal matchmaking event, but the numbers of men and women were badly lopsided. Not even half the conversations could happen.
在宅勤務が続き、一週間で口にした言葉はオンライン会議の「聞こえますか」くらいだっ: Working from home dragged on, and the only words I said in a whole week were things like “Can you hear me?” in online meetings.
単身高齢と孤独死: Elderly living alone and solitary deaths
同じ団地の一人暮らしの人が、亡くなって十日後に見つかった。それから、隣同士で新聞: A person living alone in the same housing complex was found ten days after dying. After that, neighbors began checking each other’s newspaper boxes every morning.
見守りセンサーを部屋につけた。トイレのドアが一日開かないと、遠方の親族に通知が届: I installed a monitoring sensor in my home. If the bathroom door stayed unopened for a whole day, a notification would go to a relative far away.
遠くで一人暮らしをする親に、毎晩電話するようになった。呼び出し音が五回鳴っても出: I started calling my parent, who lives alone far away, every night. If it rang five times without an answer, my hands shook.
推計では2050年に一人暮らしの高齢者が1,000万人を超えると言われた。近所を: Projections said that by 2050, elderly people living alone would exceed 10 million. Looking around my neighborhood, it had already come true.
高齢を理由に、賃貸の入居審査に三件続けて落ちた。不動産屋は「もしものときが」と言: Because of my age, I failed rental screening three times in a row. The real estate agent trailed off, saying something about “in case something happens.”
配偶者を見送ってから、夕食は毎日同じ時間に一人で食べた。部屋にあるのは、テレビの: After seeing my spouse off to the other side, I ate dinner alone at the same time every day. The only sound in the room was the TV.
貸していたアパートの一室で、一人暮らしの入居者が亡くなっていた。清掃と改装に費用: A tenant living alone had died in one of the apartment units I rented out. Cleaning and renovation costs piled up, and no next tenant was found.
訪問介護で担当していた一人暮らしの利用者が、自分の休みの日に亡くなっていた。週一: A client living alone whom I cared for on home visits died on my day off. I kept thinking that once a week hadn’t been enough.
引き取り手のない遺骨が、役所の保管庫に増え続けた。棚が足りず、別の倉庫を借りるこ: Unclaimed cremated remains kept piling up in the city office’s storage. With not enough shelves, we had to rent another warehouse.
回覧板を回す相手がいなくなった。両隣も向かいの家も、いつの間にか空き家になってい: There was no one left to pass the neighborhood circular to. The houses on both sides and across the street had all become vacant before I knew it.
終活の講座で身元保証サービスを勧められた。月々の費用を聞き、年金の振込額と何度も: At an end-of-life planning seminar, I was pitched an identity guarantee service. After hearing the monthly cost, I compared it with my pension deposit again and again.
配達先の玄関に新聞が何日分も溜まっていた。警察に連絡すると、その家への配達はそれ: Several days’ worth of newspapers had piled up at a delivery address’s front door. I contacted the police, and that was the last delivery to that house.
冬の風呂場で倒れたが、腕の見守り端末が自動で通報してくれた。救急隊員に「お一人で: I collapsed in the bathroom in winter, but the monitoring device on my wrist called for help automatically. The paramedics asked me three times, “Do you live alone?”
自分が倒れたら誰が気づくのかと考え、友人と「既読がつかなかったら様子を見に行く」: Wondering who would notice if I collapsed, I made a pact with a friend: “If the message isn’t marked read, go check on each other.”
大きな団地の住民の半分以上が65歳以上になった。夜になっても明かりのつかない窓が: More than half the residents of the large housing complex became 65 or older. Windows that stayed dark even at night increased year by year.
葬儀を頼める身内がいないので、自分の葬儀を生前に契約した。担当者は「最近はこうい: With no relatives to ask to arrange a funeral, I contracted my own funeral while still alive. The representative said, “Lately it’s all people like you.”
配偶者の遺品を一人で片づけきれず、整理業者を呼んだ。見積もりは、思っていた額の三: I couldn’t finish sorting my spouse’s belongings alone, so I called a cleanout company. The estimate was three times what I had expected.
孫は遠くに住み、会えるのは年に一度のビデオ通話だけになった。画面越しの顔が、毎年: My grandchild lives far away, and all I get is one video call a year. Through the screen, the face grew a little more grown-up each year.
電気代を惜しんで、エアコンをつけずに夏を越そうとした。熱中症で倒れ、隣の人が気づ: Trying to save on electricity, I tried to get through the summer without the air conditioner. I collapsed from heatstroke, and a neighbor noticed and saved me.
何年も会っていなかった叔父が一人で亡くなり、警察から連絡が来た。手続きは、なぜか: An uncle I hadn’t seen for years died alone, and the police contacted me. For some reason, all the procedures fell to me.
地元の高校が統廃合で閉校になった。新しい学校までバスで1時間かかり、朝6時に家を: My local high school was closed in a consolidation. The new school took an hour by bus, so I started leaving home at 6 a.m.
教員の欠員が埋まらず、専門外の教科も受け持つことになった。夜遅くまで教科書を読み: Teaching vacancies went unfilled, and I ended up taking on subjects outside my specialty. Day after day I read textbooks late into the night.
子どもの担任が年度の途中で休職し、代わりの先生は見つからなかった。数か月間、教頭: My child’s homeroom teacher took leave mid-year, and no replacement could be found. For several months, the vice principal taught the class.
志望していた地方の私立大学が、学生の募集を停止すると発表した。進路指導室の資料が: The regional private university I had hoped to attend announced it would stop admitting students. One less brochure sat in the career guidance room.
閉校になった小学校の校舎が、何年も放置された。体育館の窓は割れたまま、校庭に雑草: The building of the closed elementary school was left abandoned for years. The gym windows stayed broken, and weeds grew across the schoolyard.
推計では18歳人口が2040年ごろに約80万人まで減ると言われた。それでも、大学: Projections said the 18-year-old population would fall to about 800,000 around 2040. Even so, the number of universities had hardly decreased.
部活動が地域に移されたが、地域の指導者が見つからなかった。いくつかの部は、そのま: School club activities were handed over to the community, but no local instructors could be found. Some clubs were simply shut down.
住んでいる町に塾がなく、受験勉強はオンライン授業だけで乗り切った。都会の友人との: My town had no cram school, so I got through exam prep with online lessons alone. I felt the gap with my city friends in my mock-exam results.
大学の学費が上がるというニュースを見て、子どもの教育費の積立を増やした。外食の回: Seeing news that university tuition was going up, I increased my savings for my child’s education. I cut back on eating out once more.
奨学金を借りて進学することになった。返し終わるのは40代になると、書類の返済表で: I decided to go on to college with a student loan. The repayment table in the paperwork showed I wouldn’t finish paying it off until my forties.
母校の小学校が閉校し、最後の記念式典に招かれた。校歌を歌ったのは、白髪の卒業生ば: My old elementary school closed, and I was invited to the final commemorative ceremony. The ones singing the school song were all gray-haired alumni.
閉校した校舎の使い道を任されたが、手を挙げる事業者は現れなかった。机には解体費の: I was put in charge of finding a use for the closed school building, but no business stepped forward. All that remained on my desk was the demolition cost estimate.
先生が足りず、一部の授業が別の学校からのオンライン配信になった。画面の向こうの先: With too few teachers, some classes became online broadcasts from another school. It was hard to ask questions of a teacher on the other side of a screen.
都心の中学受験の塾はどこも満員だった。子どもの数は減っても、一人にかける教育費は: Every cram school for middle-school entrance exams in central Tokyo was full. Even as the number of children fell, the education spending per child kept rising.
教員採用試験の倍率が1倍台まで下がったと聞いた。新任の同僚は、着任した次の日から: I heard the competition ratio for the teacher hiring exam had dropped to around 1x. A new colleague was given a homeroom class the day after arriving.
町に一つだけあった高校が、生徒数の基準を下回って募集停止になった。中学の卒業生は: The town’s only high school fell below the enrollment threshold and stopped admitting students. Every middle-school graduate went on to school outside town.
学童保育の指導員が辞め、受け入れ人数が減らされた。夏休みの昼間、子どもの預け先が: The after-school care staff quit and the intake was cut. During the summer vacation days, I couldn’t find anywhere to leave my child.
学校の図書室が司書不在で、週に二日しか開かなくなった。読みたい本は、自分で取り寄: With no librarian, the school library opened only two days a week. If I wanted a book, I had to order it myself.
大学で学んだ知識が、入社数年で通用しなくなった。会社の補助はなく、自腹で夜間の講: The knowledge I gained at university stopped being useful within a few years of joining the company. With no company support, I paid out of pocket for evening courses.
出身大学で学部の統合が発表された。自分が卒業した学科の名前が、カタログから消える: My alma mater announced a merger of faculties. The name of the department I graduated from would disappear from the catalog.
教育実習生が何年も来なくなった。後輩に教え方を伝える機会もないまま、職員室の平均: No student teachers came for years. With no chance to pass my teaching methods on to younger colleagues, the only thing that rose was the staff room’s average age.
保育園の送迎に車で片道30分かかるようになった。近くの園は保育士が足りず、0歳児: Dropping off and picking up at nursery school now took 30 minutes each way by car. The nearby nursery lacked staff and had closed its infant class.
電車で泣く赤ちゃんを抱えた親が、ずっと周りに頭を下げていた。乗客のほとんどは年配: A parent holding a crying baby on the train kept bowing in apology to everyone around. Most of the passengers were elderly.
保育の現場で人が足りず、一人で見る子どもの数が増えた。昼寝の時間も、連絡帳を書く: With too few staff at the nursery, the number of children each of us watched grew. Even during naptime, I couldn’t stop writing in the parent contact notebooks.
夜中に子どもが高熱を出したが、近くの小児救急は閉鎖されていた。電話相談は、つなが: My child ran a high fever in the middle of the night, but the nearby pediatric emergency service had been closed. The phone consultation line took 30 minutes to connect.
子どもの迎えのために勤務時間を短くした。その分、昇給の査定が一段下がった。: I shortened my working hours to pick up my child. As a result, my raise evaluation dropped a notch.
共働きの子ども夫婦に頼まれ、毎日孫の保育園の迎えに行くようになった。腰の痛みが少: Asked by my working child and their spouse, I started picking up my grandchild from nursery school every day. My back pain grew little by little.
子どもの習い事の教室が、講師の高齢化で次々に閉じた。残ったのは、隣町のスイミング: Classes for my child’s lessons closed one after another as the instructors aged. All that remained was the swimming school in the next town.
公園の遊具が老朽化で撤去され、新しいものは置かれなかった。子どもは、すべり台の跡: The park’s playground equipment was removed for aging, and nothing new was installed. The kids kicked a ball where the slide used to be.
町が子育て世帯に家賃補助と医療費の無料化を始めた。それでも、移り住んでくる家族は: The town began offering rent subsidies and free medical care to families raising children. Even so, only a few families moved in each year.
育休に入った同僚の仕事が、そのまま自分に回ってきた。補充の人は来ず、残業時間だけ: The work of a colleague who went on parental leave simply landed on me. No replacement came, and only my overtime hours grew.
物価が上がり続け、給食費と教材費の請求が毎年増えた。家計簿の「子ども」の欄だけが: Prices kept rising, and the bills for school lunches and teaching materials grew every year. Only the “children” line in the household ledger kept swelling.
同じ学年の子どもがいる家が、町内に一軒もなかった。子育ての悩みを話せる相手は、画: There wasn’t a single household in the neighborhood with a child in the same grade. The only people I could talk to about parenting worries were on the other side of a screen.
児童相談所の職員が足りず、一人で何十件もの案件を抱えた。電話が鳴るたびに胃が痛ん: The child guidance center was short-staffed, and I handled dozens of cases alone. My stomach hurt every time the phone rang.
小児科の予約がネットで取れず、朝7時から病院の前に並んだ。並んでいた親たちは皆、: I couldn’t get a pediatrics appointment online, so I lined up in front of the hospital from 7 a.m. All the parents in line looked exhausted.
近所の子どもに声をかけたら、その親に不審そうな目を向けられた。子どもと話す機会は: When I spoke to a neighborhood child, the parent gave me a suspicious look. My chances to talk with children ended right there.
子育ての給付金が増えた。ありがたかったが、同じ月に社会保険料の値上げの通知も届い: Child-rearing benefits increased. I was grateful, but that same month a notice of higher social insurance premiums also arrived.
子どもの塾の送迎と、親の通院の付き添いが同じ曜日に重なった。ダブルケアという言葉: Driving my child to cram school and accompanying my parent to the hospital fell on the same day of the week. The term “double care” became about me.
非正規の同僚が、育休の条件を満たせず出産を機に退職した。代わりの人は、いつまでも: A non-regular colleague couldn’t meet the conditions for parental leave and quit when she gave birth. Her replacement never came.
閉園した保育園の解体工事を請け負った。園庭の遊具を重機で崩すとき、現場の誰もが黙: I took on the demolition of a closed nursery school. When the heavy machinery brought down the playground equipment, everyone on site fell silent.
ファミリー向けの賃貸が見つからず、子ども部屋のない狭い部屋で家族が暮らした。宿題: I couldn’t find a family-sized rental, so we lived in a cramped place with no children’s room. The kids did their homework at the kitchen table.
田舎の実家を相続したが、買い手も借り手もつかなかった。固定資産税と草刈りの費用だ: I inherited the family home in the countryside, but found neither a buyer nor a tenant. Only property tax and weeding costs piled up every year.
先祖代々の墓を墓じまいした。遠方の寺に何度も足を運び、話し合いがまとまるまで半年: I closed down the ancestral grave. After many trips to a distant temple, it took half a year to reach an agreement.
推計では2030年代後半に空き家が2,000万戸を超えると言われた。自分の家の行: Projections said vacant homes would exceed 20 million in the late 2030s. The fate of my own house was part of that number.
祖父名義のままの山林の相続登記をすることになった。戸籍をたどると、相続人は親戚中: I had to register the inheritance of forestland still in my grandfather’s name. Tracing the family registers, there were more than twenty heirs among the relatives.
所有者のわからない土地が道路の予定地にかかり、工事が何年も止まった。登記簿の名義: Land with an unknown owner fell within a planned road site, and construction stalled for years. The name on the land register belonged to someone born in the Meiji era.
駅に納骨堂の広告が並ぶようになった。墓地はどこも空きがなく、ビルの中の納骨堂が当: Ads for columbariums began lining the station. With no vacancies in any cemetery, indoor columbariums inside buildings had become the norm.
自分が入るはずの墓を守る人がいないことに気づいた。永代供養の合同墓の資料を、何度: I realized there was no one to look after the grave I was meant to enter. I reread the brochure on a perpetual-care communal grave again and again.
配偶者の遺骨を、しばらく家に置いたままにした。墓をどうするか、親族との話がまとま: I kept my spouse’s ashes at home for a while. Talks with relatives about what to do about the grave didn’t come together.
集落の共同墓地を管理していた人が亡くなった。お盆に行くと、草が腰の高さまで伸びて: The person who had looked after the village’s communal cemetery died. When I went at Obon, the grass had grown waist high.
相続した土地は評価額がつくのに、売ろうとしても買い手がいなかった。相続税を払うた: The inherited land had an assessed value, yet when I tried to sell it there were no buyers. I drew down my savings to pay the inheritance tax.
配偶者の実家の空き家を誰が管理するかで、きょうだいの間がこじれた。年末の帰省は、: Who would manage the empty house of my spouse’s family home soured relations among the siblings. Our year-end visits home ended after that.
残る人に迷惑をかけたくないと、遺言書を書いて法務局に預けた。書き終えると、少しだ: Not wanting to burden those left behind, I wrote a will and deposited it with the Legal Affairs Bureau. When I finished, a little of the weight lifted from my shoulders.
相続した田んぼの借り手が見つからず、耕作放棄地になった。周りの田からも、苗の緑が: I couldn’t find anyone to rent the inherited rice paddy, and it became abandoned farmland. The green of rice seedlings also disappeared from the surrounding paddies year by year.
親から「この家をどうするか決めておいて」と言われた。きょうだいは全員都会に住み、: My parent told me, “Decide what to do with this house.” My siblings all lived in the city, and none of them intended to come back.
空き家になった実家について、自治体から管理を求める通知が届いた。草刈りと屋根の修: The municipality sent a notice demanding that I manage the family home that had become vacant. I hurriedly called contractors for weeding and roof repairs.
解体の依頼は増えたのに、相続人全員の同意が取れず着工できない現場が続いた。重機を: Demolition requests increased, but sites kept stalling because consent couldn’t be obtained from all the heirs. More days passed with the heavy machinery sitting idle.
営んでいた葬儀社は、家族葬と火葬だけの依頼ばかりになった。一件あたりの売上は、以: At the funeral home I ran, requests became nearly all small family funerals and cremation-only services. Sales per job fell to less than half of what they used to be.
孫に「お墓って何のためにあるの」と聞かれ、うまく答えられなかった。墓じまいの話は: My grandchild asked me, “What are graves for?” and I couldn’t answer well. The talk of closing down the grave was put off until next year.
推計では2040年ごろ、年間の死亡数が約170万人でピークになると言われた。近く: Projections said annual deaths would peak at about 1.7 million around 2040. The nearby crematorium was booked solid for days ahead.
相続した株を売るか迷っているうちに、相続税の納付期限が来た。結局、相場の底で手放: While I was hesitating over whether to sell the inherited shares, the inheritance tax payment deadline arrived. In the end I had to let them go at the bottom of the market.
配偶者名義の銀行口座が凍結され、戸籍を何通も取り寄せた。窓口で同じ説明を三度繰り: My spouse’s bank account was frozen, and I had to request copy after copy of family registers. At the counter I repeated the same explanation three times.
勤めている介護施設で、海外から来た同僚が半数近くになった。申し送りは、やさしい日: Nearly half of my colleagues at the care facility came from abroad. It became the rule to write handover notes in plain Japanese.
近所のコンビニの店員が、ほとんど外国から来た人になった。名札の名前を覚えて、あい: Most of the clerks at the neighborhood convenience store became people from abroad. I memorized the names on their name tags and started greeting them.
クラスに日本語を学び始めたばかりの転校生が来た。翻訳アプリを間に置いて、休み時間: A transfer student who had just started learning Japanese joined the class. We talked during breaks with a translation app between us.
畑の収穫は、新しい就労制度で海外から来た若い人たちが支えていた。彼らが帰国した年: The farm harvest was supported by young people who came from abroad under a new work program. The year they went home, only half the harvest got done.
推計では2070年に人口の約1割が外国から来た人になると言われた。駅前の案内板に: Estimates said that by 2070 about one in ten people would be from abroad. The signs in front of the station began to line up in many languages.
担任するクラスに日本語の指導が必要な児童が五人いた。支援の先生が来るのは、週に一: My class had five children who needed Japanese language support. The support teacher came only once a week.
物流センターの夜勤は、半分以上が外国から来た人だった。休憩室の掲示は四つの言語で: More than half of the night shift at the distribution center were people from abroad. Notices in the break room were posted in four languages.
現場の職人の多くが外国から来た人になった。安全教育の動画は、何種類もの言語で作り: Most of the craftsmen on site became people from abroad. The safety training video was remade in many languages.
役所の窓口に通訳用のタブレットが置かれた。それでも、制度の細かい説明は伝わりきら: Interpreter tablets were placed at the city hall counter. Even so, the finer points of the procedures often didn't get across.
町の人口に占める外国人の割合が一割を超えた。自治会の回覧板に、初めていくつかの言: Foreign residents passed ten percent of the town's population. For the first time, the neighborhood association's circular came with translations in several languages.
人手が足りず、店で海外からの留学生を雇った。在留資格の更新の書類を、初めて自分で: Short on staff, I hired an international student at my shop. I looked up the residence status renewal paperwork on my own for the first time.
住んでいる団地の住民の多くが、外国から来た家族になった。ゴミ出しのルールの説明書: Most residents of the housing complex I live in became families from abroad. Together we made a sheet explaining the rules for taking out the trash.
働き手の取り合いで、賃金の高い他の国へ移る外国人が増えた。職場の欠員は、いつまで: With countries competing for workers, more foreigners moved to countries with higher wages. Vacancies at my workplace stayed unfilled forever.
一緒に働いていた海外出身の看護師が、待遇のいい別の国へ移った。送別会で、引き留め: A nurse from abroad who had worked with me moved to another country with better pay. At the farewell party, I couldn't find the words to ask her to stay.
訪問介護のヘルパーが、海外から来た若い人に替わった。郷土料理の作り方を教えると、: My home-visit caregiver was replaced by a young person from abroad. When I taught them how to make a local dish, they listened happily.
子どもの学校の保護者会で、通訳を介した話し合いが増えた。会は長くなったが、行事の: Discussions through interpreters increased at my child's school parent meetings. The meetings got longer, but there were certainly more hands to help with events.
アパートの隣に外国から来た家族が越してきた。生活の時間帯の違いに戸惑い、管理会社: A family from abroad moved in next door. Unsure how to deal with the difference in daily rhythms, I consulted the management company.
取引先との会議が、日本語より英語の方が多くなった。慣れない英語のメールに、毎晩時: Meetings with clients came to be held more in English than in Japanese. Unfamiliar English emails ate up my evenings every night.
地元の選挙で外国人住民の受け入れ方が争点になった。家族の間でも意見が分かれ、食卓: How to accept foreign residents became an issue in the local election. Opinions split even within my family, and the mood at the dinner table turned heavy.
地域の日本語教室でボランティアを始めた。教えるつもりが、相手の国の話を聞く時間の: I started volunteering at a local Japanese language class. I meant to teach, but I ended up spending more time listening to stories about their home countries.
正月が明けて帰省していた若者がいなくなると、町は急に静かになった。駅のホームには: After New Year, once the young people home for the holidays left, the town suddenly fell quiet. Only elderly people remained on the station platform.
地元に就職先がなく、仲のよかった先輩が進学と同時に都会へ出た。駅のホームで見送っ: There were no jobs in my hometown, so a close senior went off to the city when starting college. I saw them off on the station platform.
都会に出たまま、地方の親が一人きりになった。帰省のたびに、実家の電球の切れた部屋: Having stayed on in the city, my parents in the countryside ended up alone. Each time I visited, there were more rooms at my parents' house with burnt-out light bulbs.
地元で営む商店から若い客がいなくなった。売れるのは、高齢の人向けの品ばかりになっ: Young customers vanished from the local shop I run. All that sold were goods for the elderly.
推計では全国の自治体の4割ほどが「消滅の可能性」があると言われた。発表された一覧: Estimates said about 40 percent of municipalities nationwide faced a “possibility of disappearing.” My own town's name was on the published list.
町役場の新規採用に応募がなく、退職した職員の再任用でしのいだ。窓口に並ぶ職員は、: No one applied for new positions at the town office, which got by by rehiring retired staff. The employees lined up at the counter were all older.
地元のバス路線が廃止された。運転手のなり手が町にいないことが理由だった。: The local bus route was discontinued. The reason was that the town had no one willing to become a driver.
地元に残りたいと言うと、先生にも親にも「もったいない」と言われた。結局、都会の大: When I said I wanted to stay in my hometown, both my teacher and my parents said, “What a waste.” In the end, I took the entrance exams for a university in the city.
漁協の組合員の平均年齢が70歳を超えた。港で見かける若い人は、週末の釣り客だけに: The average age of fishing cooperative members passed 70. The only young people seen at the harbor were weekend anglers.
地方から出てきた若者で、都心のシェアハウスはどこも満室だった。家賃の高さに、誰も: With so many young people arriving from the regions, every share house in the city center was full. With rents so high, everyone had a side job.
町の消防団が団員不足で隣の分団と統合された。火事のときに駆けつけるのは、60代以: The town's volunteer fire corps merged with the neighboring unit for lack of members. The ones rushing to fires were all members in their 60s or older.
地元にUターンしたが、求人は夜勤の工場と介護ばかりだった。都会で積んだ経歴は、ほ: I returned to my hometown, but the job listings were nothing but night-shift factory work and caregiving. The career I'd built in the city was almost useless.
夏祭りの担い手がいなくなり、何百年も続いた行事が休止になった。最後の太鼓を叩いた: With no one left to carry on the summer festival, an event that had lasted hundreds of years was suspended. The last person to beat the drum was in their 70s.
スーパーが撤退し、一番近い店まで車で20分になった。移動販売のトラックが、週に二: The supermarket pulled out, and the nearest store was now a 20-minute drive away. A mobile sales truck came only twice a week.
地元の友だちの大半が都会へ出た。同級生のグループチャットは、都会での集まりの誘い: Most of my friends from home left for the city. My classmates' group chat became nothing but invitations to get-togethers in the city.
推計では2050年に、今人が住んでいる地域の半分ほどで人口が半分以下になると言わ: Estimates said that by 2050, the population would fall to half or less in about half of the areas where people now live. The local elementary and junior high schools were merged into one.
地方の支社が閉鎖されることになり、本社への転勤か退職かを迫られた。同じ支社の半分: The regional branch office was to be closed, and I was forced to choose between transferring to headquarters or quitting. Half of that branch's staff left town.
生まれた町の人口が、自分が子どもの頃の半分になっていた。通った駄菓子屋の場所は、: The population of the town where I was born had fallen to half of what it was in my childhood. I could no longer remember where the old candy shop I used to go to had been.
仕事を求めて都会に出たが、正社員の口は見つからなかった。家賃を払うため、アルバイ: I went to the city looking for work but couldn't find a full-time position. To pay rent, I juggled three part-time jobs.
人手の足りない職場が、都会に住む人をリモート勤務で採用した。一度も会ったことのな: A short-staffed workplace hired someone living in the city to work remotely. Colleagues I'd never met made up half the team.
住んでいる地域から若い世帯が減り続けた。家の売却査定は、買ったときの半値以下だっ: Young households in my area kept dwindling. The appraisal for selling my house came in at less than half of what I paid.
夫婦それぞれの勤務地が離れ、週末だけ同じ家に帰る暮らしになった。日曜の夜は、いつ: My spouse and I ended up working in different places, so we lived as a couple who only came home to the same house on weekends. On Sunday nights, we always said goodbye at the station.
クラスの半分以上が一人っ子だった。きょうだいげんかの話をすると、珍しがられた。: More than half the class were only children. When I talked about fights with my siblings, they found it unusual.
親の介護のために仕事を辞めて実家に戻った。収入はなくなり、親の年金で二人が暮らし: I quit my job and moved back home to care for my parent. With no income, the two of us lived on my parent's pension.
子ども世帯との同居を考えたが、家の広さが足りなかった。結局、近くのアパートに一人: I considered living with my children's household, but their home wasn't big enough. In the end, I moved alone into an apartment nearby.
親戚が集まる法事や正月が、十年ほど前から途絶えていた。いとこの顔も名前も、もう思: Family gatherings for memorial services and New Year had stopped about ten years earlier. I could no longer recall my cousins' faces or names.
夫婦二人だけの暮らしが長く続いた。どちらかが先に逝ったらどうするか、休日に話し合: We lived as just the two of us for a long time. On days off, we began to talk about what to do if one of us went first.
ひとり親になり、仕事と家事を一人で回した。休みが取れず、子どもの学校行事の欠席が: I became a single parent and juggled work and housework alone. Unable to take time off, I kept missing my child's school events.
保護犬を家族として迎えた。動物病院の診療費が、自分の医療費より高くつく月もあった: I took in a rescue dog as part of the family. Some months, the vet bills came to more than my own medical expenses.
配偶者を亡くし、契約の名義を一つずつ変えていった。どの窓口でも「お一人ですか」と: After my spouse died, I changed the name on each contract one by one. At every counter, I was asked, “Are you here alone?”
家族の誰も近くに住んでいなかった。役所から届く書類の意味がわからず、民生委員に読: None of my family lived nearby. I couldn't understand the documents from the city office, so a local welfare volunteer read them to me.
同僚の多くが共働きで、家事代行を頼むのが普通になった。夕食はほぼ毎日、買ってきた: Most of my coworkers were in dual-income households, and hiring housework help was the norm. Dinner was almost every day something bought ready-made.
介護の仕事を続けながら、自分の親の介護も始まった。職場でも家でも、誰かの体を支え: While continuing my caregiving job, care for my own parent began. At work and at home, I was always supporting someone's body.
クラスで、親と離れて暮らす友だちや、祖父母に育てられている友だちが珍しくなくなっ: In class, it was no longer unusual to have friends living apart from their parents or being raised by their grandparents.
共働きで、家事の分担を細かく決めた表を作った。どちらかが残業すると、表は一日で崩: As a dual-income couple, we made a chart with a detailed division of housework. Whenever either of us worked overtime, the chart fell apart in a day.
月に二度、新幹線で親の家に通う遠距離介護が始まった。交通費だけで、月に十万円近く: Long-distance caregiving began, commuting to my parent's home by bullet train twice a month. Transportation alone cost nearly 100,000 yen a month.
知人が長年連れ添った相手と離婚し、年金分割の手続きの話を聞かされた。自分の家の家: An acquaintance divorced after many years together, and I was told all about the pension-splitting procedures. It made me review my own household budget too.
きょうだいのグループチャットが、親の通院と薬の話ばかりになった。誰が付き添うかで: The siblings' group chat turned into nothing but our parent's hospital visits and medication. When it came to who would accompany them, the replies stopped.
生活費を切り詰めるため、大人になったきょうだいと二人で部屋を借りた。家賃を割り勘: To cut living costs, I rented a place with my grown sibling. Splitting the rent in half, we were finally able to save.
近所には事実婚の夫婦や三世代の家族、同性のカップルが暮らしていた。一つの表札に、: My neighbors included common-law couples, three-generation families, and same-sex couples. More houses had two surnames side by side on a single nameplate.
孫の運動会に行くと、祖父母席はがらがらだった。来ていたのは、自分を含めて数人だけ: When I went to my grandchild's sports day, the grandparents' section was nearly empty. Only a handful of us, myself included, had come.
後継ぎが見つからず、親の代から続けてきた店を閉めた。閉店の貼り紙の前で、常連客が: With no successor in sight, I closed the shop that had run since my parents' time. Regulars took photos in front of the closing notice.
町で一軒だけの豆腐屋が、後継ぎがいなくて店を閉めた。朝のラッパの音が聞こえなくな: The town's only tofu shop closed for lack of a successor. The sound of the morning horn was no longer heard.
体力の衰えを感じ、田んぼを集落の営農組合に預けた。その組合も、人手不足で次の春が: Feeling my strength decline, I entrusted my rice fields to the village farming cooperative. Even that cooperative, short of workers, couldn't be sure of seeing next spring.
取引先の町工場が、後継ぎのいないまま廃業した。替えのきかない部品が手に入らず、職: A supplier's small factory closed down with no successor. We couldn't get an irreplaceable part, and the production line at my workplace stopped.
町に一軒だけ残っていた酒蔵が、杜氏の引退で酒造りをやめた。祭りの振る舞い酒も、よ: The last sake brewery in town stopped brewing when its master brewer retired. Even the sake served at the festival came from another town.
会社を買い手に譲ることにした。社名は残ったが、社員の顔ぶれは一年で半分入れ替わっ: I decided to hand the company over to a buyer. The company name stayed, but within a year half the staff had changed.
腕のいい宮大工の親方が引退し、技術を継ぐ者がいなかった。修理を頼まれた寺の屋根は: The master of a skilled temple carpenter workshop retired, and no one inherited the skills. The temple roof I'd been asked to repair was put on a waiting list for years.
漁船を継いでくれる人が見つからなかった。中古で売りに出したが、買い手も現れなかっ: I couldn't find anyone to take over my fishing boat. I put it up for sale as a used boat, but no buyer appeared.
長年通った床屋が、店主の引退で閉店した。新しい店を探すと、予約はスマホからしか取: The barbershop I had gone to for years closed when the owner retired. When I looked for a new one, reservations could only be made from a smartphone.
事業承継の補助金を申請しようとしたが、書類の多さに途中で手が止まった。自分の代で: I tried to apply for a business succession subsidy, but the sheer amount of paperwork stopped me partway. I decided to close the shop in my generation.
知人から、ある会社を買い取らないかと持ちかけられた。帳簿を見ると、後継ぎがいない: An acquaintance proposed that I buy a certain company. Looking at the books, it was a profitable company whose only problem was having no successor.
商店街の老舗の和菓子屋が閉店し、跡地はコインパーキングになった。季節ごとの楽しみ: A long-established Japanese confectionery shop in the shopping street closed, and the site became a coin parking lot. One of the seasonal pleasures was gone.
地元の商店主から「うちを継がないか」と声をかけられた。悩んだ末に断ったが、店はそ: A local shopkeeper asked me, “Why don't you take over my shop?” After agonizing, I turned him down, and the shop closed within the year.
地元の運送会社が、社長の高齢化と後継ぎ不在で廃業した。その荷物の分まで、自分のル: A local trucking company shut down because its president was aging and had no successor. Even that company's cargo ended up added to my route.
長年通っていた歯医者が閉院した。紹介された先の医院は、予約が二か月先まで埋まって: The dentist I had gone to for years closed. The clinic I was referred to was booked up two months ahead.
後継ぎにと考えていた従業員が、都会の会社に引き抜かれた。事業の引き継ぎ計画を、一: The employee I had in mind as my successor was poached by a company in the city. I rebuilt the business handover plan from scratch.
商工会で廃業の相談を受ける担当になった。相談に来る人の多くは黒字なのに、継ぐ人が: I became the person handling closure consultations at the chamber of commerce. Many of the people who came were profitable, with just no one to take over.
町で唯一のガソリンスタンドが、経営者の引退で閉まった。家の車の給油は、隣町まで往: The town's only gas station closed when its owner retired. Filling up my car now meant a 40-minute round trip to the next town.
行きつけの喫茶店の店主が亡くなり、店は閉じたままになった。仲間と集まる場所が、町: The owner of my favorite coffee shop passed away, and the shop stayed closed. One more place where friends gathered vanished from town.
担当していた老舗の取引先が、後継ぎ不在で廃業した。年に一度の挨拶回りの名簿から、: A long-established client I was in charge of closed for lack of a successor. I crossed one name off the list for my annual greeting rounds.
孫が家の農園を継ぎたいと言い出した。うれしかったが、古い機械と借入金のことを思う: My grandchild said they wanted to take over the family farm. I was happy, but thinking of the old machinery and the loans, I couldn't simply be glad.
年金の振込通知が届いた。物価は上がったのに、額はマクロ経済スライドでほとんど増え: The pension deposit notice arrived. Prices had gone up, but the amount had barely increased because of macroeconomic slide adjustments.
ねんきん定期便の見込み額を見た。今の物価のまま暮らすには、月に数万円足りない計算: I looked at the projected amount on my pension statement. By my calculation, living at current prices would leave me tens of thousands of yen short each month.
自分が受け取るころの年金は、今の高齢者より目減りすると授業で習った。グラフが映る: In class, I learned that pensions at the time I receive them will be worth less than the elderly get now. When the graph appeared, the classroom went quiet.
国民年金だけの見込み額は月6万円台だった。家賃を払えば何も残らない数字を、スマホ: The projected amount from the basic national pension alone was in the 60,000-yen range per month. I kept looking again at the figure on my phone, which left nothing after paying rent.
厚生年金のない自営業で、老後の受取額を試算した。店をたたんだ後の暮らしが、うまく: As a self-employed person with no employees' pension, I estimated what I'd receive in old age. I could no longer picture life after closing the shop.
独身のまま老後を迎える前提で年金を試算した。ひとり分の年金でひとり分の家賃を払う: I estimated my pension on the assumption of reaching old age unmarried. Paying one person's rent on one person's pension was cutting it very close.
年金だけでは足りず、貯金を毎月取り崩した。通帳の残高が減る速さを、自分の寿命と見: My pension alone wasn't enough, so I drew down my savings every month. I began comparing how fast my balance was shrinking against my own lifespan.
配偶者が亡くなり、受け取る年金が遺族年金に切り替わった。世帯の入りが大きく減り、: After my spouse died, the pension I received switched to a survivors' pension. Household income dropped sharply, and I held back on heating in winter.
年金の実質的な目減りが続き、近所のスーパーで見切り品が並ぶ時間を覚えた。: As pensions kept losing real value, I memorized the hours when discounted items appeared at the neighborhood supermarket.
2029年、年金の財政検証の結果が発表された。将来の給付水準の見通しは、前回より: In 2029, the results of the pension fiscal review were announced. The outlook for future benefit levels had dropped a little more than the last time.
給料明細の厚生年金保険料の欄を見た。払っている額のほうが、将来もらえる見込みより: I looked at the employees' pension insurance premium line on my pay slip. What I was paying felt heavier than what I could expect to receive in the future.
夫婦ふたりの年金見込みを合算した。どちらかが先に亡くなった後の生活費は、どう計算: I added up the projected pensions for the two of us. No matter how I calculated, living expenses after one of us died weren't covered.
年金の受け取りを70歳まで繰り下げるため、パートを続けた。体はきついが、増える額: To defer my pension to age 70, I kept working part-time. It was hard on my body, but thinking of the increased amount, I couldn't quit.
年金だけでは足りないと考え、積立投資を続けた。相場が下がった月は、老後の見通しご: Thinking my pension alone wouldn't be enough, I kept up my investment plan. In months when the market fell, my outlook for old age wobbled along with it.
持ち家のないまま年金生活に入る見込みになった。家賃を払い続ける老後を想像して、公: I was heading into retirement without owning a home. Imagining an old age spent paying rent, I started looking into public housing openings.
近所の農家のおばあさんは、国民年金だけで暮らしていた。畑の野菜でしのげるうちはい: The old farming woman next door lived on the basic national pension alone. She laughed and said it was fine as long as she could get by on the vegetables from her field.
退職手当と年金の見込みが、先輩たちの代より減っていた。定年後も働き続けることが前: The projected retirement allowance and pension were lower than for my seniors' generation. Working even after mandatory retirement became the assumption.
保険料の免除期間が長く、年金の見込み額は暮らせる水準に届かなかった。追納の案内を: Because of a long period of exempted premiums, my projected pension fell short of a livable level. Seeing the notice about making up the payments, I sighed.
年金の支給開始年齢を引き上げる案がニュースに出た。食卓で、大人たちが自分は何歳か: A proposal to raise the age at which pensions start appeared in the news. At the dinner table, the adults were deep in conversation about what age they would start receiving theirs.
親の年金だけでは施設の費用を払えず、毎月の差額を自分が出すことになった。: My parent's pension alone couldn't cover the facility fees, so I ended up paying the monthly difference.
孫へのお年玉を、年金の額に合わせて減らした。手渡すとき、少しだけ申し訳ない気持ち: I cut my New Year gifts to my grandchildren to match my pension. Handing them over, I felt a little sorry.
村に一軒だけの診療所の医師が引退し、後任が来なかった。月に一度の通院のため、バス: The doctor at the village's only clinic retired, and no successor came. For my monthly checkup, I transferred between buses to reach the next town.
子どもが夜に熱を出したが、近くの病院の小児科は医師不足で夜間を閉めていた。隣の市: My child ran a fever at night, but the pediatrics department at the nearby hospital was closed at night due to a doctor shortage. I drove to the next city.
紹介された専門外来は3か月待ちと言われた。痛みを抱えたまま、カレンダーの受診日に: I was told the specialist clinic I was referred to had a three-month wait. Living with the pain, I circled the appointment date on the calendar.
職場で辞めた人の補充が来ず、ひとりで受け持つ人数が増えた。休みの日は一日中眠って: No replacement came for a coworker who quit, so the number of people I handled alone grew. On my days off, I slept the whole day away.
駅前のクリニックの予約枠は、朝7時の受付開始から数分で埋まった。目覚ましを6時5: The appointment slots at the clinic in front of the station filled up within minutes of opening at 7 a.m. I set my alarm for 6:59.
地域の病院が統合され、近くの病院は外来だけになった。入院するなら山を越えた市の病: The local hospitals were consolidated, and the nearby hospital became outpatient-only. I was told that for admission, it would be the hospital in the city over the mountains.
健康診断で再検査になったが、近くの病院の予約が取れたのは2か月後だった。: My health checkup called for a retest, but the earliest appointment I could get at a nearby hospital was two months away.
オンライン診療を勧められたが、タブレットの操作が分からなかった。結局、半日かけて: I was recommended online consultations, but I couldn't figure out how to use the tablet. In the end, I spent half a day going to the hospital.
地方では医師が足りない地域がこの先も残ると言われた。町の診療所の「医師募集」の張: I was told that areas short of doctors would remain in rural regions for the foreseeable future. The “Doctors wanted” notice at the town clinic stayed there, faded.
医学部の地域枠の説明会に出た。卒業後は決められた地域で何年か働く条件がついていた: I attended an information session on the regional quota for medical schools. It came with the condition of working for several years in a designated region after graduation.
通っている病院の担当医が数か月ごとに替わった。そのたびに、はじめから病歴を説明し: The doctor in charge at the hospital I went to changed every few months. Each time, I had to explain my medical history from the beginning.
近くの産院が分娩の受け入れをやめた。出産できる病院は、車で1時間先にしかなくなっ: The nearby maternity clinic stopped accepting births. I learned that the only hospital where I could give birth was an hour away by car.
通っていた歯医者が後継ぎがいなくて閉院した。新しい歯医者を探すのに、口コミを何時: The dentist I had gone to closed for lack of a successor. I spent hours reading reviews to find a new one.
通院のために仕事を半日休んだ。待合室で3時間待ち、診察は5分で終わった。: I took half a day off work to go to the hospital. I waited three hours in the waiting room, and the exam took five minutes.
会社の産業医は何社もかけもちしていて、面談の枠は月に一度しかなかった。相談したい: The company's occupational physician worked for several companies at once, and there was only one consultation slot a month. What I wanted to discuss got carried over to the next month.
病院へ行く路線バスが減便になった。通院の日は、診察より帰りのバスを待つ時間のほう: The local bus to the hospital had its service cut back. On clinic days, I spent more time waiting for the return bus than seeing the doctor.
同僚が、より条件のいい都市部の職場へ移っていった。残った者で回すシフト表は、毎月: My coworkers moved on to better-paying jobs in urban areas. The shift schedule we managed with those left was always stretched to the limit each month.
窓口での支払いが気になり、具合が悪くても受診を先延ばしにした。結局、こじらせてか: Worried about the cost at the counter, I put off seeing a doctor even when I felt unwell. In the end, I went to the hospital only after it had gotten worse.
大学病院の受付に、紹介状のない初診には追加の費用がかかると大きく掲示されていた。: At the university hospital reception, a large notice said first-time patients without a referral letter would be charged an extra fee. I looked for a nearby clinic first.
県内の病院の再編が決まり、町の病院が診療所に縮小された。救急車の行き先は、いつも: The prefecture decided to reorganize its hospitals, and the town hospital was downsized into a clinic. Ambulances always headed for the next city.
付き添う人がいなくなり、診察室でひとりで説明を聞いた。メモを取る手が追いつかなか: With no one left to accompany me, I listened to the explanation alone in the exam room. My hand couldn't keep up with taking notes.
親の特別養護老人ホームの入所を申し込んだ。順番待ちは100人を超えていると言われ: I applied for my parent's admission to a special nursing home for the elderly. I was told the waiting list had passed 100 people.
推計では、2040年度に介護職員が約57万人足りなくなると言われた。近所のデイサ: Estimates said Japan would be short about 570,000 care workers by fiscal 2040. The day service center near me cut back to three days a week due to staff shortages.
入っている施設の職員が足りず、入浴が週2回から週1回に減った。: The facility I live in didn't have enough staff, and baths dropped from twice a week to once a week.
近所の訪問介護事業所が閉鎖した。ヘルパーの来る日が減り、買い物は自分で何とかする: The home-visit care agency near me shut down. Visits from the helper became less frequent, and I had no choice but to manage the shopping myself.
町の介護施設が職員を集められず、ベッドの半分を閉めた。入所を待つ家族は、町の外の: The town's care facility couldn't recruit staff and closed half of its beds. Families waiting for admission went searching for facilities outside the town.
都市部の高齢者の急増で、施設の空きが足りないと言われた。見学した有料老人ホームの: With the sharp rise in elderly people in urban areas, there weren't enough openings in facilities, I was told. The entrance fee for a paid nursing home I toured was several million yen.
職場に外国から来た仲間が増えた。休憩室で、互いの国の言葉を少しずつ教え合った。: More colleagues from abroad joined my workplace. In the break room, we taught each other bits of our languages.
物価と人件費の上昇で、親が入っている施設の月額費用が値上げされた。差額の振込額を: Rising prices and labor costs led to an increase in the monthly fee at the facility where my parent lives. I reviewed the amount I transfer to cover the difference.
見守りセンサーや介護ロボットを入れた施設がニュースになった。それでも夜の職員は1: A facility that introduced monitoring sensors and care robots made the news. Even so, I heard there was still only one staff member at night.
ひとり暮らしが難しくなり、年金で入れる施設を探した。空いているのは費用の高い所ば: Living alone became difficult, so I looked for a facility I could afford on my pension. The only ones with openings were expensive.
配偶者の要介護度が上がったが、施設に空きがなかった。在宅介護のまま、夜中に何度も: My spouse's level of care needs went up, but no facility had a vacancy. Continuing to provide care at home, I got up many times during the night.
駅の求人誌は介護の仕事で埋まっていた。時給を見比べると、近くのコンビニとほとんど: The job listings at the station were full of caregiving work. Compared hourly wages, they were barely different from the nearby convenience store.
介護の資格を取ろうと講座を調べた。夜勤の手当を足しても、今の暮らしが楽になるとは: Looked into courses to get a caregiving qualification. Even with the night-shift allowance, I couldn't see life getting any easier.
身寄りがないため、将来の施設入所で保証人をどうするか調べた。どの施設の書類にも、: With no relatives, I looked into who could act as guarantor when I eventually enter a care facility. Every facility's paperwork had that line.
孫が介護の仕事に就いた。腰を痛めた話を聞くたびに、何と声をかければいいか分からな: My grandchild became a caregiver. Every time I hear about their bad back, I don't know what to say.
デイサービスの送迎車の運転手が見つからず、送迎が止まった。利用者の家族が車で送り: Couldn't find a driver for the day-service shuttle, so pick-ups stopped. Users' families ended up driving them back and forth themselves.
大口の取引先だった介護事業所が、人手不足で廃業した。売上の柱がひとつ消えた。: A care provider that was a major client closed due to staff shortages. One of our pillars of sales vanished.
親の担当のケアマネジャーが退職し、後任が決まるまで1か月かかった。その間、ケアプ: My parent's care manager quit, and it took a month to find a replacement. In the meantime, the review of the care plan stalled.
介護職員の高齢化が進み、70代の職員が80代の入居者を支える施設もあると報じられ: It was reported that caregiver ranks were aging, with some facilities having staff in their 70s supporting residents in their 80s.
入居していた施設が、運営会社の撤退で閉鎖されることになった。次の行き先が決まるま: The facility I lived in was to close after its operator pulled out. I lay awake night after night until my next place was decided.
親の介護が始まり、毎週末に実家へ通うようになった。往復の交通費だけで、月に数万円: My parent's care began, and I started going to my parents' home every weekend. Round-trip fares alone ate up tens of thousands of yen a month.
同僚が家族の介護を理由に退職した。介護離職は年に約10万人と言われていたが、身近: A coworker quit to care for a family member. Care-related resignations were said to number about 100,000 a year, but it was my first time seeing one up close.
家族の介護のため、在宅勤務と通院の付き添いを行き来した。オンライン会議の最中に、: To care for a family member, I shuttled between working from home and accompanying them to the hospital. In the middle of an online meeting, the facility called.
推計では、働きながら家族を介護する人は2030年に約318万人になると言われた。: It was estimated that about 3.18 million people would be working while caring for family by 2030. I became one of them.
家族の介護のため介護休暇を申請した。人の少ない部署で、引き継ぎだけに3日かかった: I applied for caregiver leave to care for a family member. In a short-staffed department, the handover alone took three days.
家族の介護と担任を両立できず、学年の途中で担任を外してもらった。教室を出るとき、: Unable to balance caring for a family member with being a homeroom teacher, I asked to be taken off homeroom duty mid-year. Leaving the classroom, I couldn't look at the students.
家族の介護のため、長距離の運行を断って近場の仕事に変えてもらった。手取りは大きく: To care for a family member, I turned down long-haul runs and switched to local jobs. My take-home pay dropped sharply.
家族の介護で現場を早上がりする日が増えた。日当が減り、親方に頭を下げ続けた。: Caring for a family member meant leaving the site early more and more often. My daily pay shrank, and I kept bowing my head to the boss.
家族の介護に時間を取られ、田んぼの一部を作れなくなった。耕さなくなった田に、夏草: Caring for a family member took my time, and I could no longer farm part of my rice fields. Summer grass grew in the fields I stopped tilling.
家族の介護のため、店の営業時間を短くした。閉店時間の張り紙を見た常連客に、体を心: To care for a family member, I shortened my shop's hours. Regulars who saw the notice about the closing time worried about my health.
家族の介護に合わせられるのは、シフトの融通がきく仕事だけだった。正社員の求人は、: The only jobs that fit around caring for a family member were ones with flexible shifts. Full-time listings became something I only looked at.
独り身で、家族の介護を頼める相手はいなかった。休みの日はすべて通院の付き添いで埋: Single, with no one to turn to for help caring for family. Every day off was filled with accompanying them to the hospital.
家族の介護が始まり、配偶者と交代で付き添う日が続いた。ふたりで出かける休日は、い: Care for a family member began, and my spouse and I took turns at their side day after day. Before I knew it, our days off together had disappeared.
子育てと家族の介護が同時に来た。子どもの行事と介護の予定が、手帳の同じ日に重なっ: Raising kids and caring for a family member hit at the same time. My children's school events and care appointments landed on the same days in my planner.
家族の介護を手伝うため、部活をやめた。同級生には、本当の理由を言えなかった。: I quit my club to help care for a family member. I couldn't tell my classmates the real reason.
仕事で人のケアをして、帰ってからは家族のケアをした。気を休められる場所が、どこに: I cared for people at work, then cared for family when I got home. There was nowhere I could rest.
家族の介護のため、仕事を辞めた。収入が途絶え、貯金を切り崩す暮らしが始まった。: I quit my job to care for a family member. My income stopped, and I began living off my savings.
推計では、仕事と介護の両立による経済損失は2030年に約9兆円と言われた。ニュー: The economic loss from balancing work and caregiving was estimated at about 9 trillion yen by 2030. Watching the news, my family's faces came to mind.
家族の介護に、保険外の民間サービスを足した。月の出費は数十万円になり、資産が目に: I added private, non-insured services to my family member's care. Monthly expenses rose to hundreds of thousands of yen, and my assets visibly shrank.
実家は遠い地方にあった。家族の介護のため、月に2回、新幹線で往復するようになった: My parents' home was in a faraway region. To care for a family member, I started making round trips by bullet train twice a month.
推計では、2040年に認知症の高齢者は約584万人になると言われた。回覧板に、認: It was estimated that the number of elderly people with dementia would reach about 5.84 million by 2040. A flyer for a dementia supporter course was tucked into the neighborhood circular.
親が同じ話を何度も繰り返すようになった。病院で軽度認知障害と言われ、帰りの車は無: My parent started repeating the same story over and over. The hospital said it was mild cognitive impairment, and the ride home was silent.
通帳と印鑑をしまった場所が思い出せなかった。家じゅうを探し、冷蔵庫の中で見つけた: I couldn't remember where I'd put the bankbook and seal. I searched the whole house and found them in the refrigerator.
孫の名前が、とっさに出てこなかった。笑ってごまかしたが、帰ったあとで急に不安にな: My grandchild's name wouldn't come to me at first. I laughed it off, but after leaving I was suddenly anxious.
運転免許の更新で認知機能検査を受けた。結果が出るまでのあいだ、手のひらに汗をかい: Took a cognitive function test for my driver's license renewal. My palms were sweating while I waited for the results.
認知症と診断された家族が免許を返納した。買い物と通院の送迎は、すべて自分の役目に: A family member diagnosed with dementia gave up their driver's license. Driving them to shopping and hospital visits all became my job.
駅で行き先が分からなくなった高齢者に声をかけた。家族の連絡先は、首から下げたカー: I spoke to an elderly person who'd lost track of where they were going at the station. Their family's contact number was written on a card hanging from their neck.
町の防災無線で、行方の分からない高齢者を探す放送が流れた。週に何度も聞くようにな: The town's disaster-prevention loudspeaker broadcast a search for a missing elderly person. I started hearing it several times a week.
推計では、認知症の人が持つ金融資産は2030年に200兆円を超えると言われた。資: It was estimated that financial assets held by people with dementia would exceed 200 trillion yen by 2030. I went to consult about a family trust to manage assets.
認知症と診断された親の預金を下ろすのに、成年後見の手続きが必要になった。家庭裁判: To withdraw the savings of my parent, who was diagnosed with dementia, I needed adult guardianship procedures. I went to the family court again and again.
配偶者が夜中に起きて外へ出ようとするようになった。玄関に鈴をつけ、浅い眠りの日が: My spouse started getting up in the middle of the night and trying to go outside. I hung a bell on the front door and spent my nights sleeping lightly.
ひとり暮らしで物忘れが増え、認知症になったら誰が気づくのかと考えた。見守りサービ: Living alone and growing more forgetful, I wondered who would notice if I developed dementia. I signed up for a monitoring service.
ひとりになってから、カレンダーの予定を忘れることが増えた。地域包括支援センターに: Since being on my own, I'd been forgetting calendar appointments more often. I called the community comprehensive support center.
若年性認知症と診断された同僚が働き続けられるよう、部署で仕事の分担を組み直した。: So a coworker diagnosed with early-onset dementia could keep working, our department reorganized how tasks were divided.
認知症の人への接し方の研修が、職場で必修になった。ロールプレイで、相手を否定しな: Training on how to interact with people with dementia became mandatory at work. In role-play, I practiced ways of speaking that don't deny the other person.
訪問販売で高い布団を契約していたことに、家族に言われて初めて気づいた。契約書の字: Only when my family pointed it out did I realize I'd signed a contract for an expensive futon from a door-to-door seller. The handwriting on the contract was indeed mine.
学校で認知症サポーターの講座を受けた。オレンジ色のリングをもらい、祖父母の顔が浮: Took a dementia supporter course at school. I was given an orange ring and thought of my grandparents.
持ち主の家族が認知症になり、実家を売ることも貸すこともできなくなった。空き家の固: The owner's family developed dementia, and I could neither sell nor rent out the family home. I just kept paying property tax on the vacant house.
認知症と診断された。医師は淡々と説明し、隣に座った家族は何度もうなずいていた。: Diagnosed with dementia. The doctor explained it matter-of-factly, while the family member beside me nodded again and again.
受け持つ生徒が、認知症の祖父の世話で夜まで家事を担っていると知った。面談の帰り道: I learned that a student in my class was handling housework until late at night to look after a grandfather with dementia. On the way home from the meeting, I couldn't find the words.
認知症の新しい薬が承認されたと報じられた。ただ、使えるのは初期の一部の人に限られ: A new dementia drug was reported to have been approved. But I heard it could only be used by some people in the early stages.
社会保険料と手取り: Social Insurance Premiums and Take-Home Pay
給料は上がったのに、手取りはほとんど増えなかった。明細の社会保険料の欄が、また少: My pay went up, but my take-home barely rose. The social insurance line on my payslip had grown a little fatter again.
賞与の明細を見た。額面と振込額の差が大きく、思わず電卓を叩き直した。: Looked at my bonus statement. The gap between the gross amount and what was deposited was big, and I instinctively redid the math on a calculator.
勤め先で社会保険の適用が広がり、パートでも保険料が引かれるようになった。手取りが: Social insurance coverage expanded at my workplace, and premiums started being deducted even from part-timers. My take-home fell by nearly 20,000 yen a month.
医療保険料に上乗せされる子ども・子育て支援金が、また引き上げられた。明細に見慣れ: The child and childcare support levy added on top of medical insurance premiums was raised again. An unfamiliar new line had appeared on my payslip.
国民健康保険料の通知が届いた。売上が伸びなかった年なのに、保険料は去年より上がっ: The National Health Insurance premium notice arrived. It was a year when sales hadn't grown, yet the premium was higher than last year's.
後期高齢者医療の保険料が値上げされ、年金から天引きされる額が増えた。: Premiums for the late-stage elderly medical system were raised, and the amount deducted from my pension grew.
介護保険料の基準額がまた上がった。推計では、2040年度には月9,000円前後に: The base amount for long-term care insurance premiums rose again. It was estimated to reach around 9,000 yen a month by fiscal 2040.
推計では、社会保障給付費は2040年度に約190兆円になると言われた。数字が大き: Social security benefit spending was estimated to reach about 190 trillion yen by fiscal 2040. The number was so big that I couldn't connect it to my own wallet.
共働きの手取りを計算し直した。配偶者の年収が壁を越えた分は、保険料に消えて世帯の: Recalculated our dual-income take-home pay. The amount my spouse's income went over the threshold just vanished into premiums, and the household's take-home barely changed.
年収の壁を越えないよう、12月のシフトを減らした。店長は、年末なのに人が足りない: To stay under the income threshold, I cut my December shifts. The store manager held their head over being short-staffed at year-end.
株の配当などの金融所得も保険料の計算に入れる案が議論された。証券口座の画面を見な: A proposal to include financial income such as stock dividends in premium calculations was debated. Looking at my brokerage account screen, I rethought how to receive my returns.
手取りが増えないまま家賃と保険料が上がった。更新のたびに、少しずつ安い部屋へ移っ: With take-home pay flat, rent and premiums rose. At each renewal, I moved to a slightly cheaper room.
共済の掛金が上がり、手取りが去年より減った。給与改定のニュースは、明細の上では見: Mutual aid contributions rose, and my take-home dropped below last year's. The news about pay revisions was nowhere to be seen on my payslip.
運賃の見直しで給料は少し上がったが、保険料と税の天引きでほとんど消えた。: A fare revision raised my pay slightly, but deductions for premiums and taxes ate up nearly all of it.
処遇改善で給料が上がると聞いていたが、明細を見ると手取りは数千円しか増えていなか: I'd heard that improved working conditions would raise my pay, but on the payslip my take-home had risen by only a few thousand yen.
国民健康保険料の滞納が続き、督促の封筒が届いた。病院に行くのが、少し怖くなった。: I kept falling behind on National Health Insurance premiums, and a reminder envelope arrived. I became a little afraid of going to the hospital.
推計では、2065年ごろには現役世代約1.3人で高齢者1人を支えると言われた。社: It was estimated that around 2065, about 1.3 working-age people would support each elderly person. I saw that chart in social studies class.
会社の健康保険組合が赤字で解散し、協会けんぽに移った。保険料率が上がり、手取りが: My company's health insurance association dissolved in the red, and we moved to the national association plan. Premium rates rose, and my take-home fell again.
孫の学費を援助すると約束していたが、天引きの増えた年金では無理だった。約束の額を: I'd promised to help with my grandchild's tuition, but with more deducted from my pension, it wasn't possible. I told them I'd reduce the amount I'd promised.
国民負担率が5割近くになったと報じられた。財布の中身が軽い理由が、数字で分かった: It was reported that the national burden rate had neared 50 percent. The numbers seemed to explain why my wallet felt so light.
固定資産税と保険料の通知が同じ月に重なって届いた。春は、出ていくお金の季節になっ: The property tax and premium notices arrived in the same month. Spring became the season when money flows out.
電気代の請求を見て、冬なのに暖房を切った。重ね着したまま布団に入った。: Seeing the electricity bill, I turned off the heater even in winter. I went to bed in layers of clothes.
生活保護を受ける世帯の半分以上が高齢者だと報じられた。近所のひとり暮らしの人は、: It was reported that over half of households receiving public assistance were elderly. A neighbor living alone shook their head, saying applying was shameful.
年金だけでは家賃が払えず、生活保護を申請した。窓口で、これまでの暮らしを一から説: My pension alone couldn't cover rent, so I applied for public assistance. At the counter, I explained my life so far from the beginning.
推計では、2050年に65歳以上のひとり暮らしは約1,080万人になると言われた: It was estimated that about 10.8 million people aged 65 or older would be living alone by 2050. I vividly imagined myself as one of them.
給食のない夏休み、子どもの昼ごはん代が家計を圧迫した。そうめんの日が続いた。: During summer break with no school lunches, the cost of my child's midday meals strained the household budget. Days of somen noodles went on.
契約が更新されず、次の仕事が決まるまでに貯金が尽きかけた。: My contract wasn't renewed, and my savings were nearly gone before my next job was decided.
更新のときに家賃が上がり、払えずに引っ越した。新しい部屋は駅から遠く、日当たりも: Rent went up at renewal and I couldn't pay, so I moved. The new place was far from the station and got little sunlight.
借りた奨学金の返済額を計算した。社会に出てから15年以上、毎月払い続ける見込みだ: Calculated the repayments on my student loan. I'd be paying every month for more than 15 years after entering the workforce.
近所にフードバンクの配布所ができた。土曜日の朝、そこに長い列ができるようになった: A food bank distribution site opened in the neighborhood. On Saturday mornings, long lines began to form there.
葬儀の費用を払うと、手元にほとんど残らなかった。社会福祉協議会の貸付の窓口を訪ね: After paying for the funeral, almost nothing was left. I visited the loan counter at the social welfare council.
近所の古いアパートが取り壊され、住んでいた高齢者たちは家賃の安い郊外へ散っていっ: An old apartment building nearby was torn down, and the elderly residents scattered to cheaper rent in the suburbs.
町のスーパーが撤退し、移動販売車が週に一度来るだけになった。値段は高かったが、ほ: The town's supermarket pulled out, leaving only a mobile sales truck once a week. Prices were high, but there was nowhere else to buy.
同世代の知人が、非正規のまま50代を迎えていた。老後は生活保護しかない、と冗談め: An acquaintance my age had reached their 50s still in irregular employment. They said, half-joking, that public assistance was all that awaited them in old age.
スマホの料金を払えず、回線を止められた。求人に応募するための連絡手段もなくなった: I couldn't pay my phone bill, and my line was cut off. I lost my means of contact for job applications, too.
物価が上がり続け、食事を一日二食にした。夕方になると、決まってふらついた。: Prices kept rising, so I cut down to two meals a day. Every evening, I'd feel unsteady on my feet.
子どもを塾に通わせる余裕がなくなった。やめると告げると、子どもは黙ってうなずいた: I could no longer afford cram school for my child. When I told them we'd stop, my child silently nodded.
子どもの約9人に1人が相対的貧困だと報じられた。学校の近くに子ども食堂ができ、夕: It was reported that about 1 in 9 children lives in relative poverty. A children's cafeteria opened near the school, and lines formed in the evening.
物価は上がったが給料は据え置きだった。昼食を家から持っていく日が増えた。: Prices rose, but my pay stayed the same. I packed my lunch from home more and more often.
仕事を失い、貯金も尽きて生活保護を申請した。車は手放すよう言われ、駅まで歩く生活: I lost my job, my savings ran out, and I applied for public assistance. I was told to give up my car, and life became walking to the station.
福祉事務所のケースワーカー一人あたりの担当世帯が増えていると報じられた。窓口の待: It was reported that caseworkers at welfare offices were handling more households each. The wait at the counter always exceeded an hour.
住宅ローンの金利が上がり、毎月の返済額が増えた。食費を削って返済に回した。: Mortgage interest rates rose and my monthly payment increased. I cut back on food to put toward repayment.
薬局で、いつもの薬が出荷調整で入らないと言われた。在庫のある薬局を探して3軒回っ: At the pharmacy, I was told my usual medicine was unavailable due to shipping restrictions. I went around to three pharmacies looking for one with stock.
子どもの咳止めが品薄で、どこの薬局にもなかった。夜通し続く咳を、隣で聞いているし: Cough medicine for my child was in short supply, and no pharmacy had any. All I could do was listen beside them to the coughing that lasted all night.
救急車を呼んだが、受け入れてくれる病院が決まるまで40分かかった。車内でサイレン: I called an ambulance, but it took 40 minutes for a hospital to agree to take us. Inside, the siren stayed off the whole time.
救急車を呼んでから現場に着くまで、30分近くかかった。いちばん近い消防署が統合で: It took nearly 30 minutes from calling the ambulance to its arrival. The nearest fire station had been merged and was now farther away.
軽い症状で救急車を使うと費用がかかる地域が増えた。夜中の腹痛で、119番を押すか: More areas began charging for ambulances used for minor symptoms. With stomach pain in the middle of the night, I hesitated over whether to dial 119.
救急車の出動件数が過去最多を更新したと報じられた。夜のあいだに、サイレンの音が何: It was reported that ambulance dispatches had hit a record high. Through the night, I heard sirens over and over.
飲んでいる薬が7種類になった。朝昼晩の仕分けを間違えないよう、箱に曜日を書いた。: I was now taking seven kinds of medicine. I wrote the days of the week on the box so I wouldn't mix up morning, noon, and night doses.
ジェネリックが手に入らず、処方が先発品に変わった。薬局の窓口で払う額が増えていた: Generic drugs were unavailable, and my prescription switched to the brand-name drug. I was paying more at the pharmacy counter.
長く使われてきた先発薬を希望すると、追加の負担がかかるようになった。迷った末、い: Choosing a long-used brand-name drug began to cost an extra charge. After hesitating, I switched my usual medicine.
救急隊は一晩に何度も出動していて、休む間もないと聞いた。近所の消防署の車庫は、夜: I heard ambulance crews were dispatched many times a night with no time to rest. The garage at the nearby fire station was nearly empty even at night.
配偶者が夜中に倒れ、救急相談の#7119に電話した。話し中が続き、結局119番を: My spouse collapsed in the middle of the night, and I called the emergency consultation line, #7119. The line stayed busy, so I ended up dialing 119.
熱中症で運ばれた人の数がニュースで流れた。部活の練習が、日が傾いてからに変わった: The news reported the number of people taken to hospital with heatstroke. Club practice moved to after the sun had gone down.
真夏、電気代を気にしてエアコンを我慢した。めまいがして、床に座り込んだ。: In midsummer, worried about the electricity bill, I held off on using the air conditioner. I felt dizzy and sank down onto the floor.
薬代の自己負担が重く、もらった薬を少しずつ飲んで日数を延ばした。症状はなかなか良: The out-of-pocket cost of medicine was heavy, so I took my pills a little at a time to stretch out the days. My symptoms were slow to improve.
市販の風邪薬の値段が上がっていた。箱を手に取って値札を見て、そっと棚に戻した。: Over-the-counter cold medicine had gone up in price. I picked up the box, looked at the price tag, and quietly put it back on the shelf.
救急で運ばれた病院は満床だった。空きが出るまで、処置室のベッドで一晩を過ごした。: The hospital I was taken to by ambulance was full. I spent the night on a bed in the treatment room until a bed opened up.
ドクターヘリが町の運動場に降りた。近所の人が運ばれたと聞き、大きな病院までの距離: The medical helicopter landed on the town's athletic field. Hearing that a neighbor had been airlifted, I was struck by how far away the big hospital was.
授業中に生徒が倒れた。救急車を待つあいだ、研修で習ったAEDの手順を必死に思い出: A student collapsed during class. While waiting for the ambulance, I desperately tried to recall the AED steps I'd learned in training.
孫が高熱を出し、夜間の救急外来に付き添った。待合室は、子どもを抱いた家族でいっぱ: My grandchild ran a high fever, and I accompanied them to the night emergency room. The waiting room was packed with families holding children.
薬の原料の多くを海外に頼っていると報じられた。薬局の棚には「入荷未定」の札が増え: It was reported that we depend on other countries for much of the raw material for medicine. The “out of stock, no date” signs on pharmacy shelves kept increasing.
ひとり暮らしの夜中に胸が苦しくなった。誰にも気づかれないまま朝を待つのが、ひどく: Alone in the middle of the night, my chest tightened. Waiting for morning with no one noticing was terrifying.
平均寿命は延びたが、健康寿命との差は約10年のままだと言われた。介護が必要な10: Average life expectancy had risen, but the gap with healthy life expectancy was said to remain about 10 years. I couldn't tell who would support those 10 years of needing care, or how.
人生100年と言われたが、膝が痛んで散歩の距離が半分になった。坂の上の神社には、: They said we'd live to 100, but my knees ached and my walks got half as long. I could no longer make it to the shrine at the top of the hill.
健康診断で血糖値が引っかかり、生活習慣病の予備群と言われた。夜のラーメンをやめた: My blood sugar was flagged at my checkup, and I was told I was at risk for lifestyle disease. I gave up late-night ramen.
長時間のデスクワークで腰を痛めた。整形外科の待合室は、同じような年代の人で埋まっ: Long hours at a desk hurt my lower back. The orthopedic clinic's waiting room was full of people around my age.
画面を見続ける時間が長くなり、視力検査の数字が年々下がった。眼鏡の度を、また強く: With more time spent staring at screens, my eye test numbers dropped year after year. I made my glasses prescription stronger again.
70歳まで働けるよう職場の制度が変わった。体が動くうちは働き続けるのが、当たり前: The workplace system changed so we could work until 70. Working as long as the body can move became the default assumption.
フレイル予防の体操教室に通い始めた。参加者の中で、自分がいちばん若かった。: I started going to a frailty-prevention exercise class. I was the youngest participant there.
公民館の健康体操が、教える人の高齢化で休止した。集まる場所がなくなり、近所の人と: The community center's health exercise class was suspended because the instructors were aging. With no place to gather, I saw my neighbors less and less.
夏の暑さが年々厳しくなり、昼間の外出を控えるようになった。歩く量が減り、階段で息: Summers grew harsher year by year, and I started avoiding going out in the daytime. I walked less, and climbing stairs left me out of breath.
職場で健康診断を受ける機会がないまま、数年が過ぎた。体の不調は、気のせいにしてや: Several years passed without a chance for a health checkup at work. I brushed off my body's troubles as nothing and carried on.
ひとり暮らしで食事が偏り、コンビニの弁当ばかりが続いた。健康診断の数値が、少しず: Living alone, my diet was lopsided, and it was convenience-store bento after bento. My checkup numbers worsened little by little.
夫婦そろって長生きする前提で、老後資金を計算し直した。95歳まで生きたら、貯金が: Assuming we'd both live long, we recalculated our retirement funds. If we lived to 95, our savings fell short.
長生きに備えて資産を残そうとして、行きたかった旅行を先延ばしにし続けた。: Trying to leave assets behind in case of a long life, I kept putting off the trip I'd wanted to take.
長生きしてお金が尽きる不安から、終身で受け取れる年金保険の資料を取り寄せた。: Anxious about running out of money after a long life, I sent for brochures on lifetime annuity insurance.
子どもの体力の低下が報じられた。体育の授業で、外で遊ぶ時間の少なさを先生に指摘さ: A decline in children's physical fitness was reported. In gym class, the teacher pointed out how little time kids spent playing outside.
歯が弱り、硬いものが食べられなくなった。好きだったせんべいを、もう買わなくなった: My teeth weakened and I couldn't eat hard foods. I stopped buying the rice crackers I used to love.
2070年、推計どおり人口の約4割が65歳以上になったと言われた。病院の待合室も: In 2070, as estimated, about 40 percent of the population was 65 or older. Hospital waiting rooms and bus seats alike were full of white-haired people.
骨粗しょう症と言われ、転ばないよう家の段差を減らす工事をした。廊下には手すりがつ: I was told I had osteoporosis, so I had work done to reduce steps in the house to avoid falls. Handrails were added in the hallway.
長生きに備えて自宅をバリアフリーに改修した。浴室と段差の工事だけで、費用は想像の: To prepare for a long life, I renovated my home to be barrier-free. The bathroom and step work alone cost twice what I'd expected.
子どもの運動不足が気になり、休日に公園へ連れ出した。ボール遊び禁止の看板が、入口: Worried about my child not getting enough exercise, I took them to the park on my days off. A “no ball games” sign stood at the entrance.
推計では、年間の死亡者数は2040年ごろに約170万人でピークになると言われた。: It was estimated that annual deaths would peak at about 1.7 million around 2040. Crematorium reservations were reported to be booked up several days ahead.
親の最期をどこで迎えるか決められなかった。病院も施設も在宅も、空きか人手のどちら: I couldn't decide where my parent should spend their final days. Hospitals, facilities, and home care were each short on either openings or staff.
火葬場が混み合い、家族の葬儀まで10日待つことになった。その間の安置料が日ごとに: Crematoriums were crowded, and the funeral for my family member had to wait 10 days. The storage fees over that time added up day by day.
延命治療を望むかどうか、主治医に聞かれた。家に帰って、エンディングノートの空欄を: My doctor asked whether I wanted life-prolonging treatment. At home, I filled in the blanks of my ending note.
配偶者を自宅で看取った。訪問看護師が来る日以外は、ひとりで長い夜を越えた。: I saw my spouse through their final days at home. Except on the days the visiting nurse came, I got through the long nights alone.
近所の在宅医が高齢で引退した。家で最期を迎えたいという希望を、引き受けてくれる医: The home-visit doctor in the neighborhood retired due to age. There was no longer any doctor willing to take on my wish to die at home.
町の葬儀場が閉鎖し、葬儀は隣の市で行うのが当たり前になった。参列者の送迎の手配に: The town's funeral hall closed, and holding funerals in the next city became the norm. I was swamped arranging rides for the attendees.
自分が亡くなった後の手続きを誰に頼むか考え、身元保証サービスの契約書を読んだ。費: I thought about whom to ask to handle procedures after my death, and read a contract for an identity guarantor service. The fee was several hundred thousand yen.
入院中の家族の延命治療をどうするか、親族の意見が割れた。病院の談話室で、話し合い: Relatives were split on whether to continue life-prolonging treatment for a hospitalized family member. The talk in the hospital lounge went on until night.
自分が亡くなった後、この家を誰が継ぐのか決まらなかった。空き家にしたくないと、遺: It was undecided who would inherit this house after I was gone. Not wanting to leave it empty, I looked up how to write a will.
孫たちに負担をかけたくないと、墓じまいを決めた。遠方の墓から遺骨を移す費用は、思: Not wanting to burden my grandchildren, I decided to close up the family grave. Moving the remains from the distant grave cost more than I expected.
子や親族に迷惑をかけまいと、葬儀の費用を年金から少しずつ積み立て始めた。: Not wanting to trouble my children or relatives, I began setting aside funeral costs little by little from my pension.
主治医から、治療よりも穏やかに過ごすことを考える時期だと言われた。窓の外の桜を、: My doctor said it was time to think less about treatment and more about living peacefully. I gazed at the cherry blossoms outside the window for a long time.
ひとり暮らしの高齢者が亡くなり、何日も気づかれないことがあると報じられた。集合住: News reported that elderly people living alone sometimes die and go unnoticed for days. A notice about a check-in service was posted on the apartment building’s bulletin board.
部屋の契約更新で、亡くなった後の家財の片付けを誰がするのか確認された。書類の欄を: At the lease renewal, I was asked who would clear out my belongings after I died. I sat frozen for a while in front of the blank on the form.
親と人生会議をした。最期にどこで過ごしたいかを初めて聞き、答えは「家」だった。: I had an end-of-life planning talk with my parent. I asked for the first time where they wanted to spend their final days, and the answer was “home.”
お墓を継ぐ人がいない家が増え、お寺の掲示板に合葬墓の募集が貼られていた。: More families had no one to take over the grave, and a call for shared-grave applicants was posted on the temple’s bulletin board.
どちらが先に逝っても困らないよう、夫婦で口座とパスワードを紙に書き出した。: So that neither of us would be stranded if the other went first, my spouse and I wrote down our accounts and passwords on paper.
自分に何かあったときの店の始末を考えたが、継いでくれる人は見つからなかった。: I thought about what would happen to my shop if something happened to me, but found no one to take it over.
町の成人式は、新成人が5人しかいないので隣町と合同になった。: The town’s Coming-of-Age Day ceremony was merged with the neighboring town’s, since only 5 people were turning twenty.
町に一つだけの高校が閉校した。近所の中学生は朝6時台のバスで町外の高校へ通うこと: The town’s only high school closed. Local junior high students now take a bus before 7 a.m. to attend high school outside town.
町が隣の市に吸収合併され、役場は支所になった。窓口の職員は3人に減った。: The town was absorbed into the neighboring city, and the town hall became a branch office. Staff at the counter dropped to 3.
推計では2050年までに今人が住む地域の約2割が無人になると言われた。その地図に: Projections said that by 2050 about 20% of currently inhabited areas would become uninhabited. My own village’s name was on that map.
町の人口が1万人を割った年、駅前に最後まで残っていた書店が閉店した。: The year the town’s population fell below 10,000, the last bookstore in front of the station closed.
地元の同級生30人のうち、町に残っているのは自分を含めて3人だけになった。: Of my 30 classmates from back home, only 3 of us, including me, were still living in town.
近所の小学校の全校児童が12人になり、運動会は町内会の行事と合同で開かれるように: The neighborhood elementary school was down to 12 pupils in total, and its sports day was now held together with the neighborhood association’s event.
ふるさとと呼んでいた町が地図から名前を消し、隣の市の一地区になったと知らせが来た: I got word that the town I used to call my hometown had vanished from the map and become a district of the neighboring city.
地方の取引先が後継ぎがいないまま次々と廃業し、担当エリアの出張先は3年で半分にな: Clients in the regions closed one after another with no successors, and the places I traveled to in my territory halved in 3 years.
町役場の職員採用が止まり、ひとりで三つの課の仕事を兼ねるようになった。残業の明か: Hiring at the town office stopped, and I ended up covering the work of three departments alone. The only light left on during overtime was at my desk.
商店街で店を続けてきたが、常連客の多くが亡くなるか施設に入り、売上は10年で半分: I kept my shop going in the shopping street, but many regulars passed away or moved into care facilities, and sales halved over 10 years.
老人会の会員は自分より年上ばかりになり、新しく入る人のいないまま会は解散した。: Everyone left in the senior citizens’ club was older than me, and with no new members joining, the club disbanded.
推計どおり、2050年代半ばに総人口が1億人を割ったと報じられた。テレビの特集は: As projected, it was reported that the total population fell below 100 million in the mid-2050s. The TV special quickly moved on to the next topic.
町の祭りは担ぎ手が足りず、神輿を軽トラックの荷台に載せて回るようになった。数年後: The town festival lacked bearers, so the portable shrine was carried around on the back of a small truck. A few years later it was cancelled.
春の駅で、就職で町を出る若者を親たちが見送っていた。戻ってくる人は、ほとんどいな: At the station in spring, parents saw off young people leaving town for jobs. Hardly any of them ever came back.
住んでいる町が「消滅可能性自治体」の一覧に入っていると、地元紙の一面で知った。: I learned from the front page of the local paper that my town was on the list of “municipalities at risk of disappearing.”
家の周りの田んぼが耕作されなくなり、夏の夜にはイノシシが庭先まで降りてくるように: The rice fields around my house were no longer farmed, and on summer nights wild boars began coming down right up to the yard.
地方で一人暮らしをする親に同居を勧めたが、「この町で最後まで暮らす」と断られた。: I urged my parent, who lives alone in the countryside, to move in with me, but was turned down: “I’ll live out my days in this town.”
地方出身の同僚の多くが、もう帰る実家はないと言った。どの家も、売れずに取り壊した: Many coworkers from the countryside said they had no family home left to return to. Every one had been torn down after failing to sell.
地方都市の賃貸物件に投資したが、人口が減って入居者が見つからず、評価額は買値の半: I invested in a rental property in a regional city, but with the population shrinking I couldn’t find tenants, and its appraised value fell to half of what I paid.
配偶者の故郷の村が隣の市に合併され、年賀状に書いてきた住所の表記が変わった。: My spouse’s home village was merged into the neighboring city, and the address we had always written on New Year’s cards changed.
近所の家が次々と空き家になり、気がつけば自分の家の両隣とも雨戸が閉まったままにな: Neighboring houses emptied out one after another, and before I knew it the storm shutters on both sides of my home stayed closed.
親が施設に入り、実家が空き家になった。月に一度、風を通すために片道2時間かけて通: My parent moved into a care facility, and the family home became vacant. Once a month I made a 2-hour trip each way to let air through it.
相続した実家の解体に200万円かかると言われ、手をつけられないまま固定資産税だけ: I was told demolishing the inherited family home would cost 2 million yen, so I left it untouched and just kept paying the property tax.
隣の空き家の瓦が台風で飛び、自分の車がへこんだ。持ち主には最後まで連絡がつかなか: Roof tiles from the vacant house next door blew off in a typhoon and dented my car. I never managed to reach the owner.
町の空き家バンクに実家を登録したが、3年たっても問い合わせは1件もなかった。: I registered the family home with the town’s vacant-house bank, but after 3 years there hadn’t been a single inquiry.
子どもに「この家は相続したくない」とはっきり言われた。住み慣れた家の行き先は決ま: My child told me plainly, “I don’t want to inherit this house.” What would become of the home I was so used to stayed undecided.
相続登記が義務になり、名義が祖父のままだった土地の手続きに、親戚を探して半年かか: Inheritance registration became mandatory, and sorting out land still in my grandfather’s name took half a year of tracking down relatives.
住んでいる古いアパートの半分が空室になり、管理会社から取り壊しを理由に退去を求め: Half of the units in the old apartment building where I lived were empty, and the management company asked me to move out because it would be demolished.
都市の住宅街にも空き家が増え、夜道には明かりのついていない家が何軒も続くようにな: Vacant houses increased even in city residential areas, and on night streets many dark houses stood in a row.
一人で暮らす家の2階は、もう10年以上使っていない部屋ばかりになった。: The second floor of the house I live in alone had become nothing but rooms unused for over 10 years.
夫婦で建てた家に一人で残された。広すぎる家の掃除と庭の草むしりが、日ごとに重荷に: I was left alone in the house we had built together. Cleaning the far-too-large house and weeding the garden became a heavier burden each day.
自分がいなくなった後、この家を誰が片付けるのかと考えた。頼める相手は思い浮かばな: I wondered who would clear out this house after I was gone. I couldn’t think of anyone I could ask.
現場の仕事は新築より解体のほうが多くなった。仕事は途切れなかったが、壊すばかりの: On-site work became more about demolition than new construction. The jobs never dried up, but every day was just tearing things down.
相続した地方の空き家が管理不全と判断され、土地の固定資産税が大きく上がるという通: The inherited rural vacant house was deemed poorly maintained, and a notice arrived saying the land’s property tax would rise sharply.
いらない土地を国に引き取ってもらう制度を調べたが、負担金と条件が重く、あきらめた: I looked into the system for handing unwanted land over to the state, but the fees and conditions were too steep, so I gave up.
空き家に住みついたハクビシンが、隣の自分の家の屋根裏にまで入りこんできた。: A masked palm civet that had settled in the vacant house next door crept into the attic of my own home.
子どもの通学路に崩れかけた空き家があり、毎朝、塀が倒れないかと気になった。: A half-collapsed vacant house stood along my child’s route to school, and every morning I worried its wall might fall.
地方の空き家を安く借りて手を入れたが、冬の寒さと修繕費に耐えられず、2年で出た。: I rented a cheap rural vacant house and fixed it up, but couldn’t bear the winter cold and repair costs, and left after 2 years.
空き家を改装して小さな店を開いた。客は週末に少し来るだけだったが、通りに一つ明か: I renovated a vacant house and opened a small shop. Customers only trickled in on weekends, but the street gained one more light.
転勤が決まったが、地元の持ち家は売れず、空き家のまま家賃と二重の住居費を払った。: I was transferred, but my house back home wouldn’t sell, so I left it vacant and paid for housing twice over, rent included.
近所の空き家から火が出て、自分の家の外壁まで焦げた。中には誰も住んでいなかった。: A fire broke out in a vacant house nearby and even scorched the outer wall of my home. No one had been living inside.
推計では、2040年代には水道料金が今より4割以上高くなる地域が多いと言われた。: Projections said that in the 2040s, water bills in many areas would be over 40% higher than today. Looking at the bill that arrived, I remembered that.
町の水道料金が隣の市のほぼ2倍になった。使う人が減っても、水道管の長さは変わらな: The town’s water rates became nearly double those of the neighboring city. Even as users decreased, the length of the pipes stayed the same.
道路の下の古い水道管が破裂し、近所一帯が半日断水した。コンビニの水はすぐに売り切: An old water main under the road burst, and the whole neighborhood lost water for half a day. The convenience store sold out of bottled water right away.
断水の日、給水車の列に並び、満杯のポリタンクを抱えて坂を上った。翌日は腰が痛んだ: On the day of the outage, I lined up at the water truck and climbed the hill hugging a full jerrycan. My back ached the next day.
配管工として古い水道管の取り替えに追われたが、人手が足りず、計画の半分も進まなか: As a plumber I was swamped replacing old water pipes, but with too few hands, we didn’t get even half of the plan done.
水道課の技術職員が自分ひとりになり、真夜中の漏水の呼び出しにも一人で駆けつけた。: I became the only technical staff member in the waterworks section, and I rushed out alone even for midnight leak calls.
町の水道事業が県の広域事業に統合され、問い合わせ窓口が車で1時間の場所に移った。: The town’s water service was merged into a prefecture-wide operation, and the inquiry desk moved to a place an hour away by car.
蛇口から赤い水が出た朝、子どもの水筒には買い置きのペットボトルの水を入れた。: The morning red water came out of the tap, I filled my child’s water bottle with water from the plastic bottles I had stocked.
昭和に埋められた水道管の多くが、耐用年数の40年を過ぎたまま使われているとニュー: I kept hearing on the news that many water pipes laid in the Showa era were still in use past their 40-year service life.
真冬に水道管が凍って破裂したが、修理の業者が来るまで4日かかった。: A water pipe froze and burst in midwinter, and it took 4 days for a repairman to come.
大雨の日、古い下水管が水をさばききれず、家の前の道路があふれて床下まで水が入った: On a day of heavy rain, the old sewer pipes couldn’t handle the water, the road in front of my house flooded, and water seeped under the floor.
浄化槽の点検を頼んでいた業者が廃業し、遠くの業者に頼むと費用は倍になった。: The company I used for septic tank inspections went out of business, and hiring one from farther away doubled the cost.
住んでいる古い集合住宅で給水管の交換工事があり、1週間、昼間は水が使えなかった。: The old apartment complex where I lived had its water supply pipes replaced, and for a week there was no water during the day.
集落の簡易水道を住民で守ってきたが、管理できる人がいなくなり、古い井戸を掘り直す: The villagers had kept the small village waterworks running themselves, but with no one left to manage it, some households started digging their old wells anew.
店の水道代の値上げが続き、メニューの値段を2度上げた。常連客の足が少し遠のいた。: Water rates for the shop kept rising, so I raised menu prices twice. Some regulars began coming a little less often.
一人暮らしを始めて最初に届いた水道の請求に、聞いていた額の倍近い数字が書いてあっ: The first water bill after I started living alone showed a figure nearly double what I had been told to expect.
夏の渇水と古い管からの漏水が重なり、市内で時間を区切った給水が始まった。風呂は2: A summer drought and leaks from old pipes combined, and the city began supplying water only at set hours. Baths dropped to once every two days.
用水路を守る人が減って補修が追いつかず、田植えの時期に田に水が届かない年があった: With fewer people tending the irrigation canals, repairs couldn’t keep up, and one year water didn’t reach the paddies in rice-planting season.
水道料金の通知に「料金改定のお知らせ」が同封されてくるのが、毎年のことになった。: A “notice of rate revision” arriving with the water bill had become a yearly occurrence.
夫婦で話し合い、断水に備えて家に2週間分の水を備えるようになった。押し入れの半分: My spouse and I talked it over and began stocking two weeks’ worth of water at home in case of outages. Half the closet became water.
毎日通る橋に「通行止め」の看板が立った。点検で修繕が必要と判定され、通勤は20分: A “Road Closed” sign went up on the bridge I crossed every day. An inspection found it needed repairs, and my commute grew by 20 minutes.
集落へ続く古い橋が、直す予算がないとして撤去されることになった。町へ出るには山を: The old bridge leading to the village was to be removed because there was no budget to fix it. Getting into town now meant a long detour around the mountain.
