町道の補修予算がつかず、アスファルトの穴には砂利が詰められただけだった。: No budget was approved for town road repairs, and potholes in the asphalt were simply filled with gravel.
割れて盛り上がった歩道の継ぎ目につまずいて転び、手首の骨を折った。: I tripped on a cracked, raised joint in the sidewalk, fell, and broke my wrist.
重量制限のかかる橋が増え、大型トラックで通れる道が減った。毎朝の配送ルートを組み: More bridges got weight limits, and fewer roads were open to large trucks. I struggled every morning to rework the delivery route.
橋の点検ができる技術者が足りず、自分が受け持つ橋は年に80本を超えた。: With too few engineers qualified to inspect bridges, the number I was responsible for exceeded 80 a year.
直さなければならない橋の一覧を前に、今年の予算で手をつけられるのは1割だと上司に: Facing the list of bridges that needed fixing, my boss told me this year’s budget could cover only 10% of them.
トンネルの点検で通行止めが続き、ニュースで「インフラの老い」という言葉をよく聞く: Tunnel inspections kept roads closed, and on the news I started hearing the phrase “aging infrastructure” often.
都市高速の補修工事で車線の規制が何年も続き、朝夕の渋滞が当たり前になった。: Repair work on the urban expressway kept lanes restricted for years, and morning and evening traffic jams became the norm.
通学路の橋が通行止めになり、自転車で回り道をするため毎朝15分早く家を出た。: The bridge on my school route was closed, so I left home 15 minutes earlier every morning to take a detour by bicycle.
除雪車を動かせる人がいなくなり、大雪の朝、家の前の道は2日間開かなかった。: With no one left who could operate the snowplow, the road in front of my house stayed unplowed for 2 days after a heavy snowfall.
家の前の街灯が切れたまま半年直らず、夕方からは外を歩かなくなった。: The streetlight in front of my house stayed out for half a year, and I stopped walking outside after dusk.
家の前の生活道路のひび割れの補修を役所に頼んだが、「優先順位が低い」と5年待たさ: I asked the city office to repair the cracks in the residential road in front of my house, but was told it was “low priority” and made to wait 5 years.
子どもを乗せて走る道のガードレールが、錆びて根元から折れているのが目に入った。: I noticed the guardrail along the road where I drove with my child had rusted through and snapped off at its base.
客が通る山道が土砂崩れで閉鎖され、復旧のめどが立たないまま宿の予約が途絶えた。: The mountain road our guests used was closed by a landslide, and with no prospect of reopening, reservations at the inn dried up.
高速道路の無料化の時期が2115年まで先送りされたと聞き、生きているうちに無料に: I heard that making expressways toll-free had been postponed to 2115, and realized it wouldn’t happen in my lifetime.
教習所で習った道とは違い、地元の道は継ぎはぎと穴だらけで、ハンドルを取られそうに: Unlike the roads I learned on at driving school, the local roads were all patches and potholes, and the wheel nearly got yanked from my hands.
古い歩道橋が撤去されたが横断歩道はつくられず、遠くの信号まで歩くようになった。: The old pedestrian overpass was removed but no crosswalk was built, so I had to walk to a distant traffic light.
農道の小さな橋が崩れ落ち、トラクターで畑へ行くのに大きく回り道をするようになった: A small bridge on the farm road collapsed, and getting to my field by tractor now required a long detour.
配偶者の実家へ向かう峠道のトンネルが点検で危険と判定され、閉鎖された。帰省は片道: The tunnel on the mountain pass to my spouse’s family home was judged dangerous in an inspection and closed. Visits home took an hour longer each way.
2040年代、建設から50年を超えた橋が全国の約4分の3になったと報じられた。: In the 2040s, it was reported that about three-quarters of the nation’s bridges had passed 50 years since construction.
町を通るローカル線が廃止された。代わりに走り始めたバスは1日5本だった。: The local rail line through town was discontinued. The replacement bus ran only 5 times a day.
通学の路線バスが運転手不足で減便され、部活を途中で抜けて帰るようになった。: The school commute bus service was cut due to a driver shortage, and I started leaving club activities early to get home.
病院へ行くバスがなくなり、往復のタクシー代が月に2万円を超えるようになった。: The bus to the hospital stopped running, and round-trip taxi fares came to over 20,000 yen a month.
運転免許を返納したが、乗れるのは週に2回の乗合タクシーだけだった。: I surrendered my driver’s license, but the only ride left was a shared taxi twice a week.
同じ営業所の運転手が辞めても補充はなく、休日の出勤が続いた。: When drivers at my depot quit, no replacements came, and I kept working on my days off.
都市部でも深夜バスと早朝便が削られ、終電を逃すと帰る手段がなくなった。: Even in the city, late-night and early-morning buses were cut, and missing the last train left no way to get home.
通勤の路線が減便され、1本逃すと次は30分後になった。朝は10分早く家を出るよう: Service on my commuter line was cut, and missing one train meant waiting 30 minutes for the next. I started leaving home 10 minutes earlier in the morning.
無人駅の木造駅舎が取り壊され、ホームには屋根のないベンチだけが残った。: The wooden building of the unstaffed station was torn down, leaving only a roofless bench on the platform.
久しぶりに生まれた町へ帰ると、駅前のバス乗り場の時刻表は、ほとんど空白になってい: Returning to my hometown after a long time, I found the timetable at the bus stop in front of the station almost entirely blank.
町のコミュニティバスの運転手が見つからず、役場の職員である自分も交代でハンドルを: The town couldn’t find drivers for its community bus, so I, a town office employee, took the wheel in rotation too.
親の通院の送り迎えのため、月に一度の休みは毎回、実家との往復で消えた。: Driving my parent to and from hospital visits meant my one day off a month vanished each time into trips to and from the family home.
自動運転のバスが町で試験運行されたが、雪の日は運休になり、結局ほとんど使われなか: A self-driving bus was trialed in town, but it was suspended on snowy days and ended up barely used.
駅が廃止され、駅前で続けてきた店の客足はさらに落ちた。: The station was closed, and foot traffic at my shop in front of it fell even further.
行きたかった高校まで通える鉄道がなくなり、寮のある学校を選ぶしかなかった。: The railway that would have taken me to the high school I wanted was gone, so I had no choice but to pick a school with a dormitory.
駅のエスカレーターが故障したまま部品待ちになり、朝のラッシュの階段に長い列ができ: The station escalator broke down and sat waiting for parts, and long lines formed on the stairs during the morning rush.
赤字路線の存廃を話し合う住民説明会に出た。集まったのは、自分と同じ年ごろの人ばか: I attended a residents’ briefing on whether to keep or scrap the money-losing rail line. Everyone who showed up was about my age.
孫の住む町へ向かう特急が減便され、会いに行くには乗り継ぎが3回必要になった。: The limited express to the town where my grandchild lives was cut back, and visiting now required 3 transfers.
地方への出張で乗っていた路線バスが廃止され、最寄り駅からタクシーで40分かかった: The local bus I used on business trips to the regions was discontinued, and it took a 40-minute taxi ride from the nearest station.
大雨で流された線路は直されることなく、そのまま廃線が決まった。: The tracks washed away by heavy rain were never repaired, and the line was simply discontinued.
早朝のシフトに間に合う始発バスがなくなり、自転車で40分かけて通うようになった。: There was no longer a first bus early enough for my morning shift, so I started biking 40 minutes to work.
車を運転していた配偶者を亡くし、買い物も病院も、バスの時刻に合わせる暮らしになっ: After losing my spouse, who used to drive, shopping and hospital visits all had to be arranged around the bus schedule.
町に一軒だけのスーパーが閉店した。次に近い店までは車で30分かかった。: The town’s only supermarket closed. The next nearest store was 30 minutes away by car.
週に一度来る移動販売車を待って、1週間分の食材をまとめて買う暮らしになった。: I waited for the mobile shop that came once a week and bought a week’s worth of groceries all at once.
推計では2030年に荷物の3割ほどが運べなくなると言われた。担当エリアの配達が翌: Projections said that by 2030 about 30% of parcels would no longer be deliverable. Deliveries in my area shifted to arriving two days later, and I took complaint calls again and again.
通販の「翌日お届け」の表示が消え、注文してから届くまで3〜4日待つのが普通になっ: The “next-day delivery” label disappeared from online shopping, and waiting 3 to 4 days from order to arrival became normal.
宅配の再配達が有料になり、置き配と宅配ボックスを頼りにする暮らしになった。: Redelivery became a paid service, and I came to rely on leave-at-door drop-offs and parcel lockers.
坂の下のスーパーまで歩くのがつらくなり、重い米や水は自分では買えなくなった。: Walking to the supermarket at the bottom of the hill became hard, and I could no longer buy heavy things like rice and water myself.
仕入れの配送が週3回から週1回に減らされ、店に生鮮品を置けなくなった。: Supply deliveries were cut from 3 times a week to once, and the shop could no longer stock fresh produce.
出荷のトラックが確保できず、収穫した野菜の一部を畑で処分した。: Unable to secure trucks for shipping, I had to dispose of part of the harvested vegetables in the field.
切らしかけた子どもの日用品を通販で頼んだが、配送の遅れで届くのは4日後と表示され: I ordered my child’s nearly-run-out daily necessities online, but because of delivery delays it showed arrival in 4 days.
夜のコンビニが無人営業になり、レジで店員の顔を見ることがなくなった。: The convenience store switched to unstaffed operation at night, and I no longer saw a clerk’s face at the register.
町のコンビニが24時間営業をやめ、夜8時には看板の明かりが消えるようになった。: The town’s convenience store stopped operating 24 hours, and its sign went dark at 8 p.m.
送料の値上げが続き、送料無料の金額に届かせるために、いらない物まで買い足した。: Shipping fees kept rising, and to reach the free-shipping threshold I ended up buying things I didn’t even need.
一人分の食材を買いに出るのがおっくうになり、届けてもらう弁当ばかりの日が続いた。: Going out to buy groceries for one became a chore, and day after day I ate nothing but delivered bento meals.
通販で選んだ家具が「配送できない地域です」と表示され、隣の市の倉庫まで自分で取り: The furniture I picked online showed “delivery unavailable in your area,” so I went to the warehouse in the neighboring city to pick it up myself.
職場の備品の配送も遅れがちになり、「明日届く」前提で仕事を組むことができなくなっ: Deliveries of office supplies also ran late, and I could no longer plan work on the assumption that things would “arrive tomorrow.”
週末に夫婦で、車で1時間かかる郊外の大型店までまとめ買いに出るのが習慣になった。: It became our habit on weekends to drive an hour to a big suburban store and stock up together.
近所の商店街から個人商店が消え、歩いて行ける店はドラッグストアだけになった。: Independent shops vanished from the neighborhood shopping street, and the only store within walking distance was a drugstore.
孫の誕生日に荷物を送ったが、届くまでに1週間かかり、誕生日には間に合わなかった。: I sent a package for my grandchild’s birthday, but it took a week to arrive and missed the day.
集落でドローンの配送が始まったが、運べるのは軽い薬ぐらいで、米や灯油は相変わらず: Drone delivery started in the village, but it could carry only light items like medicine, and rice and kerosene still didn’t arrive.
日用品の売り場に「運賃上昇のため価格を改定しました」という張り紙が目立つようにな: Notices reading “Prices revised due to higher shipping costs” became a common sight in the household goods aisles.
郵便が届くのに4日かかるようになり、役所に出す書類が期限に間に合わなかった。: Mail started taking 4 days to arrive, and the documents I had to send to the city office missed the deadline.
近くの郵便局が閉局し、窓口での手続きのたびに町の中心までバスで行かなければならな: The nearby post office closed, and every transaction at the counter meant taking a bus to the center of town.
役所の窓口が予約制になり、予約の電話がつながらないまま1週間が過ぎた。: The city office counter switched to appointments only, and a week passed with the reservation line never connecting.
ほとんどの手続きがスマホでの申請に変わり、画面の操作がわからず近所の人に頼みこん: Nearly all procedures moved to smartphone applications, and unable to work the screen, I begged a neighbor for help.
職員が足りなくなり、窓口業務の半分を近隣の市と共同で行うことになった。: Staff ran short, and half of the counter services came to be run jointly with the neighboring city.
保育園の申し込みがオンラインだけになったが、締め切りの前夜にシステムが止まり、申: Daycare applications became online-only, but the system went down the night before the deadline and I couldn’t apply.
町の図書館が閉館し、本を借りられるのは月に一度来る移動図書館の車だけになった。: The town library closed, and the only way to borrow books was the mobile library van that came once a month.
近所のポストが撤去され、手紙を出すには歩いて15分先のポストまで行くようになった: The neighborhood mailbox was removed, and to send a letter I had to walk 15 minutes to the next one.
配偶者を亡くした後の手続きのため、統合されて遠くなった庁舎まで3回通った。: For the paperwork after my spouse’s death, I made 3 trips to the government office, now farther away after its merger.
学校の統廃合で異動の範囲が広がり、次の勤務先は車で1時間半かかる学校になった。: School consolidations widened the range of transfers, and my next posting was a school an hour and a half away by car.
住民票を取るために休みを取ったが、近くの出張所は週に2日しか開いていなかった。: I took time off to get a residence certificate, but the nearby branch office was open only 2 days a week.
投票所が統合され、投票に行くには車で20分かかるようになった。: Polling places were consolidated, and voting now meant a 20-minute drive.
町の消防署が隣の市と統合され、救急車が着くまでの時間が以前の倍近くになったと聞い: The town’s fire station was merged with the neighboring city’s, and I heard the time for an ambulance to arrive had nearly doubled.
年賀状を出す人はほとんどいなくなり、それでも郵便料金は数年おきに値上げされた。: Hardly anyone sent New Year’s cards anymore, yet postage was still raised every few years.
一人暮らしの見守りを、郵便の配達員から自治体の配るセンサー機器に切り替えるという: A notice arrived saying the check-ins on people living alone would switch from mail carriers to sensor devices distributed by the municipality.
生活の相談窓口に行きたかったが、統合された市役所まで往復のバス代が重く、足が向か: I wanted to go to the livelihood counseling desk, but the round-trip bus fare to the merged city hall was a burden, and I never went.
郵便料金の値上げで請求書を電子化したが、紙でしか受け取れない高齢の客の分だけは郵: With postage going up, I switched invoices to electronic form, but kept mailing them for elderly customers who could only receive paper.
ごみの収集が週2回から週1回に減らされ、夏は部屋の生ごみの臭いに悩まされた。: Garbage collection was cut from twice a week to once, and in summer I was plagued by the smell of kitchen waste in my room.
市の財政が苦しくなり、通っていた市民プールと近所の公民館が同じ年に閉鎖された。: The city’s finances worsened, and the public pool I used and the nearby community center were both closed in the same year.
介護の申請がオンライン中心になり、利用者の家族の代わりに書類の入力を手伝う時間が: Care-service applications moved mainly online, and I spent more time entering paperwork on behalf of users’ families.
手続きの多くはスマホで済むようになったが、窓口でしか受け付けない書類のために半休: Most procedures could now be done on a smartphone, but I took a half day off for a document accepted only at the counter.
冬の電気代の請求が月3万円を超え、エアコンは家族のいる一部屋でしか使わなくなった: The winter electricity bill topped 30,000 yen a month, so the air conditioner only ran in the one room where the family gathered.
町に最後に残ったガソリンスタンドが閉店し、給油のたびに往復1時間かけるようになっ: The last gas station in town closed, and every fill-up became a one-hour round trip.
灯油の配達が終わり、暖房を電気に切り替えたところ、冬の電気代が倍になった。: Kerosene delivery ended. I switched the heating to electric, and the winter electricity bill doubled.
猛暑の夏、電気代を気にしてエアコンをつけずにいたら、熱中症で救急搬送された。: In the scorching summer, I held off on the air conditioner to save on electricity and was rushed to the hospital with heatstroke.
夏の電力がひっ迫し、「節電にご協力ください」という通知がスマホに何度も届いた。: Summer power supply ran tight, and my phone kept buzzing with “Please help save electricity” alerts.
店の冷蔵設備にかかる電気代がかさみ、営業時間を2時間短くした。: The electricity cost of the shop’s refrigeration piled up, so I cut opening hours by two hours.
電気工事士として古い送電設備の更新工事に駆り出された。現場の同業者は、平均すると: As an electrician, I was called in to replace aging power transmission equipment. The average age of my fellow workers on site was close to 60.
裏山の斜面に太陽光パネルが並んだ。大雨のあと、そこから流れた土砂が田んぼに入りこ: Solar panels were lined up on the slope of the hill behind the village. After a heavy rain, soil washed down from there into the rice paddies.
大規模な停電で高層マンションのエレベーターが止まり、上の階の住人は階段で水を運び: A massive blackout stopped the elevators in the high-rise, and residents of the upper floors carried water up the stairs.
古い賃貸は断熱が弱く、冬は部屋の中でも息が白かった。光熱費の補助は、もう終わって: The old rental had poor insulation, and in winter my breath showed white even indoors. The utility subsidy had already ended.
子ども部屋の暖房は削れず、自分の部屋は毛布を重ねてしのいだ。: I couldn’t cut the heating in the kids’ room, so I got through the cold in my own room by piling on blankets.
電気代を滞納して供給停止の予告が届き、食費を削ってなんとか払った。: I fell behind on the electricity bill and got a notice of impending cutoff. I cut back on food to scrape the payment together.
屋根に太陽光パネルをつけて電気代は抑えられたが、パネルの寿命と処分の費用が気にな: Solar panels on the roof kept the electricity bill down, but I began to worry about their lifespan and the cost of disposal.
台風で倒れた電柱の復旧に作業員が足りず、集落の停電は5日続いた。: There weren’t enough workers to restore the utility poles toppled by the typhoon, and the village blackout lasted five days.
ハウスを温める燃料代が上がり、冬の加温をやめて作付けを減らした。: The fuel cost of heating the greenhouses went up, so I stopped heating in winter and planted less.
電気代の高騰で、勤め先の工場が生産を海外に移すと決めた。地元に残る仕事は、ほとん: Soaring electricity costs led my employer’s factory to move production overseas. Almost no work was left locally.
一人分の暮らしでも、電気・ガス・水道の基本料金だけで月1万円近くになった。: Even living alone, the base charges for electricity, gas and water alone came to nearly 10,000 yen a month.
教室の古いエアコンが壊れたまま予算がつかず、夏の授業は扇風機の風だけで受けた。: The old air conditioner in the classroom broke and no budget came through, so we sat through summer lessons with only a fan.
地域で小さな発電所をつくる取り組みに出資した。配当はわずかだったが、停電の夜も公: I invested in a project to build a small community power plant. The dividends were tiny, but the community hall stayed lit even on blackout nights.
一人になっても光熱費はほとんど下がらなかった。基本料金と冬の暖房は、二人のときと: Even after I was left on my own, utility bills barely dropped. The base charges and winter heating were the same as when there were two of us.
集落に残ったのは自分を含めて5世帯。全員が80歳を超えていた。: Only five households remained in the village, mine included. Everyone was over 80.
集落の道の草刈りに出られる人が3人になり、夏の終わりには道の両側を草が覆った。: Only three people were left able to cut the weeds along the village roads, and by the end of summer grass covered both sides of the road.
自治会の役を全員で回しても足りず、一人で会長と会計を兼ねることになった。: Even with everyone taking turns in the neighborhood association posts, there weren’t enough hands, so I ended up serving as both chair and treasurer.
山あいの集落で一人で暮らす親から、「屋根の雪を下ろせない」と電話が来た。: My parent, living alone in a mountain village, phoned to say, “I can’t get the snow off the roof.”
山あいの集落を訪問介護で回ったが、一軒ごとに車で40分かかり、1日4件が限界だっ: I made home-care visits to mountain villages, but each house was a 40-minute drive away, and four visits a day was the limit.
集落の墓を守れる人がいなくなり、墓じまいをして街の納骨堂に移した。: No one was left to look after the village graves, so I had them closed out and moved the remains to an ossuary in town.
最後の住民が街の施設に移り、隣の集落が無人になったと、地元の新聞が小さく伝えた。: The local paper ran a small item: the last resident had moved into a care facility in town, and the neighboring village was now empty.
救急車が着くまで40分かかる集落で、毎晩、電話を枕元に置いて眠った。: In a village where an ambulance took 40 minutes to arrive, I slept every night with the phone by my pillow.
集落の水路と田を一人で守ってきたが、腰を痛め、今年は作付けをあきらめた。: I had kept up the village’s irrigation channels and paddies on my own, but I hurt my back and gave up planting this year.
集落からの移転について住民の聞き取りに回り、「ここで最期を迎えたい」と何度も言わ: I went around interviewing residents about relocating from the village, and again and again I heard, “I want to spend my last days here.”
地域おこしの隊員として集落に住んだが、任期が終わると仕事が見つからず、町を離れた: I lived in the village as a community revitalization volunteer, but when my term ended I couldn’t find work and left town.
集落の共同の消防ポンプを動かせる人がいなくなり、倉庫の中で錆びていった。: No one was left who could operate the village’s shared fire pump, and it rusted away in the storehouse.
配偶者を亡くし、集落で一人きりになった。夜は獣の声だけが聞こえた。: I lost my spouse and was left all alone in the village. At night, the only sound was animals.
夏休みに孫が遊びに来たが、集落にはほかに子どもが一人もおらず、孫はすぐに退屈した: My grandchild came to visit over summer vacation, but there wasn’t another child in the village, and they got bored right away.
集落を通るバスがなくなり、週に一度の見回りの車だけが外とのつながりになった。: The bus no longer passed through the village, and the weekly patrol car became the only link to the outside.
集落で一軒だけの商店を続けてきたが、客は十数人の常連だけになり、閉店を決めた。: I had kept the village’s only shop going, but down to a dozen or so regulars, I decided to close.
実家のある集落の共有林の管理が回ってきたが、持ち主の多くが行方知れずで手がつけら: The job of managing the shared forest in my family’s home village fell to me, but many of the owners couldn’t be traced and there was nothing I could do.
山あいに持っていた別荘の周りの家が崩れはじめ、管理を頼める人もいなくなった。: The houses around my holiday home in the mountains began to collapse, and there was no one left I could ask to look after it.
「限界集落」という言葉より、集落が丸ごと消えたという話を聞くことのほうが多くなっ: More often than the term “marginal village,” I started hearing stories of whole villages disappearing altogether.
集落の診療所が閉まり、薬は月に一度の巡回診療でまとめてもらうようになった。: The village clinic closed, and I began getting my medicine all at once during the monthly mobile clinic visit.
住んでいる大きな団地は住民の半分が高齢者になり、階段の手すりにすがって歩く人をよ: Half the residents of the big housing complex where I lived were now elderly, and I often saw people clinging to the stair railings as they walked.
エレベーターのない団地の5階に住んでいたが、膝を痛めてからは外に出るのが週1回に: I lived on the fifth floor of a walk-up housing block with no elevator, and after hurting my knee I only went out once a week.
マンションの修繕積立金が足りず、大規模修繕の一時金として100万円を求められた。: The condo’s repair reserve fund fell short, and I was asked for a one-time assessment of 1 million yen for major repairs.
築50年を超えたマンションに建て替えの話が出たが、住民の合意がまとまらず、話は立: Talk of rebuilding the condo, now over 50 years old, came up, but the residents never reached agreement and the idea fizzled out.
都市部では75歳以上の一人暮らしが大きく増えると推計され、自分の住む区も例外では: Projections said the number of people aged 75 and over living alone in cities would soar, and my ward was no exception.
マンションに20年住んでも、隣の部屋の人の名前を知らないままだった。: Even after twenty years in the condo, I still didn’t know my next-door neighbor’s name.
都市部の高齢者が急に増え、一人で受け持つ訪問先が30件を超えた。: The number of elderly people in the city jumped, and the households I covered alone grew past thirty.
都会のマンションで一人暮らしをする親と2日間連絡がつかず、駆けつけると転んで動け: I couldn’t reach my parent, who lived alone in a city condo, for two days. When I rushed over, they had fallen and couldn’t move.
打ち合わせの相手も、取引先の担当者も、気づけば60代以上ばかりになった。: Before I knew it, everyone I met with, including my contacts at client companies, was in their sixties or older.
ニュータウンの中心にあったスーパーが撤退し、坂の多い街で買い物に困る高齢者があふ: The supermarket at the heart of the new town pulled out, and in a hilly neighborhood, elderly people struggling to shop were everywhere.
投資用に買った都市のワンルームの入居者が高齢になり、家賃の滞納が始まった。: The tenant in the city studio I’d bought as an investment grew old and began falling behind on rent.
近所の区民センターが耐震性の不足で閉鎖され、建て直しの予定は示されなかった。: The local ward community center was closed for lack of earthquake resistance, and no plans for rebuilding were announced.
古い団地の学生向け格安プランで入居すると、住民の大半は祖父母の世代だった。: I moved into an old housing complex on a cheap student plan, and most of the residents were of my grandparents’ generation.
郊外の住宅地で同じ年ごろの住人が次々と施設に入り、回覧板を回す相手がいなくなった: In the suburban neighborhood, residents my age moved into care facilities one after another, until there was no one left to pass the circular to.
推計では2040年に働き手が約1,100万人足りなくなると言われた。職場では定年: Estimates said that by 2040 the workforce would be short by about 11 million people. At work, people past retirement age were still the mainstay.
年齢を理由に賃貸の入居を何度も断られ、5軒目の不動産屋でようやく部屋が見つかった: I was turned down for rentals again and again because of my age, and only at the fifth real estate agency did I finally find a place.
郊外の住宅地は夫婦二人の世帯ばかりになり、夜8時には通りの家々の明かりが消えた。: The suburban neighborhood filled up with households of just an elderly couple, and by 8 p.m. the lights in the houses along the street were out.
都会の高層マンションで一人暮らし。災害時に安否を確かめてもらう名簿に、自分の名前: Living alone in a city high-rise, I wrote my name on the list of people to be checked on in a disaster.
都心の小学校でも児童が減り、勤める学校は隣の学校との統合が決まった。: Even in the city center, the number of pupils dropped, and the elementary school where I worked was set to merge with the one next door.
古い地下街の天井から水漏れが続き、立ち入り禁止の区画が少しずつ増えていった。: Water kept leaking from the ceiling of the old underground mall, and the roped-off sections slowly grew.
いつものコンビニが深夜営業をやめた。夜中に薬や水を買える店が、駅前から消えた。: My usual convenience store stopped staying open late at night. The places where you could buy medicine or water after midnight disappeared from around the station.
荷物を積み下ろす人が足りず、一日の配達件数が増え続けた。休憩はトラックの運転席で: There weren’t enough people to load and unload, and my daily deliveries kept climbing. Taking breaks in the truck cab became the norm.
宅配の再配達が有料になった。受け取れなかった荷物は、近くの受け取りロッカーまで取: Redelivery of parcels became a paid service. Packages I couldn’t receive had to be picked up from a nearby pickup locker.
推計で働き手が約1,100万人足りなくなると言われた2040年が来た。求人の貼り: The year 2040 arrived, the year projected to leave the workforce about 11 million short. Help-wanted signs stayed up in every shop.
路線バスが運転手不足で一日3本に減った。通院の帰りは、2時間待つか、タクシー代を: Driver shortages cut the local bus to three runs a day. On the way home from the hospital, it was either wait two hours or pay for a taxi.
夜勤の人が辞めて、ひとりで30人の入所者を見る夜が続いた。朝にはふらふらだった。: The night-shift staff quit, and night after night I watched over 30 residents alone. By morning I was staggering.
現場の職人の多くが60代以上になった。誰かが休むたびに工期が延び、休日出勤が増え: Most of the craftsmen on site were now in their sixties or older. Every time someone took a day off, the schedule slipped and weekend work piled up.
保育士が足りず、定員に空きはあるのに保育園の入園を断られた。仕事への復帰を半年遅: There weren’t enough nursery teachers, so even though spots were open, I was refused a daycare place. I put off returning to work by six months.
近所の歯医者が受付の人を雇えなくなり、予約も会計も機械だけになった。: The dentist nearby could no longer hire a receptionist, and booking and payment went entirely to machines.
行きつけの定食屋が、人が雇えないと言って昼だけの営業になった。夜に一人で食べられ: My regular diner said it couldn’t hire anyone and went to lunch-only hours. One more place to eat alone at night was gone.
採用試験の倍率が1倍を切り、職場の欠員は埋まらなかった。足りない人数のまま、当直: The competition ratio for the hiring exam fell below 1, and vacancies at work stayed unfilled. With the headcount still short, only the number of night duties grew.
欠員の補充が来ないまま、隣のクラスの授業も受け持つことになった。採点は毎晩、日付: With no replacement for the vacancy, I also had to teach the class next door. Grading ran past midnight every night.
頼んでいたヘルパーの事業所が人手不足で撤退した。次の事業所が見つかるまで、ひと月: The home-helper agency I’d been using withdrew for lack of staff. It took a month to find the next one.
同僚が辞めても補充はなく、ひとりで二人分の仕事をこなす毎日になった。: When a coworker quit there was no replacement, and every day I did the work of two.
近くのガソリンスタンドが、人がいなくて閉まった。給油のたびに隣町まで20分走った: The nearby gas station closed for lack of staff. Every fill-up meant a 20-minute drive to the next town.
推計では、2030年には運べる荷物が3割ほど足りなくなると言われた。通販の「翌日: Estimates said that by 2030 about 30 percent of parcels could no longer be carried. The “arrives tomorrow” labels in online shopping began to disappear.
バイト先の店長に、試験期間でもシフトに入ってほしいと頼み込まれた。断りきれず、勉: My manager at my part-time job begged me to work shifts even during exam period. I couldn’t say no, so I studied in the middle of the night.
台所の水道管が壊れたが、修理業者の予約は3週間先までいっぱいだった。: The water pipe in the kitchen broke, but repair contractors were booked solid for three weeks.
コンビニも介護施設も、働く人の多くが外国から来た人になった。身ぶりを交えた会話に: At convenience stores and care facilities alike, most of the workers were now from abroad. I got used to conversations full of gestures.
求人を出しても半年応募がなく、店を週休3日にした。売上はそのまま減った。: Half a year of job postings brought no applicants, so I made the shop closed three days a week. Sales fell right along with it.
入っていた老人ホームが職員不足で、お風呂が週1回に減った。: The nursing home I lived in was short of staff, and baths dropped to once a week.
いつものお菓子が、値段はそのままでまた一回り小さくなった。: My usual snack got a size smaller again, at the same price.
春に給料が3%上がったが、同じ年に物価はもっと上がった。手取りで買えるものは減っ: My pay rose 3 percent in spring, but prices rose even more that year. What my take-home pay could buy shrank.
食費と教育費がそろって上がり、子どもの習い事を一つやめさせた。: Food and education costs both went up, and I had to pull my child out of one of their lessons.
家賃の更新で月8,000円の値上げを言われた。引っ越す費用もなく、そのまま判を押: At the lease renewal I was told the rent would go up 8,000 yen a month. I couldn’t afford to move, so I just signed.
年金の額は少し上がったが、物価の上げ幅には届かなかった。スーパーでは見切り品の棚: My pension went up a little, but not as much as prices. At the supermarket I started checking the markdown shelf first.
冬の電気代の請求が3万円を超えた。暖房をつけるのは夜だけにした。: The winter electricity bill topped 30,000 yen. I only ran the heating at night.
ファミレスでも1回2,000円近くかかるようになり、友達と集まるのはもっぱら誰か: Even a family restaurant now cost nearly 2,000 yen a visit, so getting together with friends meant someone’s home almost every time.
ボーナスは増えたが、社会保険料も上がって手取りはほとんど変わらなかった。: My bonus went up, but social insurance premiums rose too, and my take-home pay hardly changed.
物価が上がり続けるなか、持っていた株や不動産の値段も上がった。預金しかない知人と: As prices kept rising, the stocks and real estate I held rose in value too. I felt the gap between me and acquaintances who had only savings.
卵1パックの値段を見て、買うのをやめて棚に戻した。: I saw the price of a pack of eggs, decided against it and put it back on the shelf.
共働きでも家計が赤字になる月が出てきた。夫婦で話し合い、動画や音楽の定額サービス: Even with both of us working, some months the household budget ran in the red. We talked it over as a couple and canceled every video and music subscription.
最低賃金は上がったが、店はその分シフトを減らした。月の収入はほとんど増えなかった: The minimum wage went up, but the shop cut shifts to offset it. My monthly income barely grew.
昼に買うパンがまた値上がりし、1個で我慢する日が増えた。: The bread I buy for lunch went up again, and more days I made do with just one roll.
給料は10年前より上がっていたが、物価の上昇を差し引くと、暮らしの楽さはほとんど: My pay was higher than ten years earlier, but after subtracting the rise in prices, life was hardly any easier.
都心の新築マンションの値段は、普通の会社員の年収の15倍を超えた。住宅情報サイト: New condos in the city center cost over 15 times an ordinary salaried worker’s annual income. I stopped looking at housing listing sites.
インフレに備えて預金の一部を投資に回した。値上がり分で、ようやく物価高に追いつい: To prepare for inflation, I moved part of my savings into investments. The gains finally let me catch up with rising prices.
孫へのお年玉を、物価に合わせて増やしてやれなかった。: I couldn’t raise my grandchildren’s New Year’s money to keep up with prices.
資材と工事費が上がり、家の外壁の塗り直しを見積もりだけで先送りにした。: Material and labor costs rose, so I got a quote for repainting the exterior walls and then put the job off.
学生のころから好きだったラーメンが1杯1,500円を超え、月に1回のぜいたくにな: The ramen I’d loved since my student days passed 1,500 yen a bowl and became a once-a-month luxury.
美容院の料金が上がり、髪を切る間隔を2か月から3か月にのばした。: Hair salon prices went up, so I stretched the gap between haircuts from two months to three.
材料費が上がったのに、常連が離れるのが怖くて値上げできなかった。利益は前の年の半: Ingredient costs rose, but I was afraid of losing regulars and couldn’t raise my prices. Profit fell to half of the previous year.
国の借金がまた過去最大を更新したというニュースを、夕飯を食べながら聞き流した。毎: The news said the national debt had hit another record high, and I let it wash over me during dinner. It happened every year, and nobody was surprised.
長期金利が上がり、持っていた債券の投資信託の値段が下がった。: Long-term interest rates rose, and the price of the bond fund I held fell.
住宅ローンの変動金利が上がり、毎月の返済が2万円増えた。: The variable rate on my mortgage rose, and my monthly payment went up by 20,000 yen.
消費税の引き上げが決まった。増えた分は社会保障に使うと説明されたが、買い物のたび: A consumption tax hike was decided. We were told the extra would go to social security, but I sighed every time I shopped.
医療費の窓口負担が増える人の範囲が広がり、通院の回数を減らした。: The group of people paying a larger share of medical costs at the counter widened, and I cut down on hospital visits.
予算が削られ、職場の古いパソコンも空調も、更新されないまま何年も使い続けた。: The budget was cut, and the old computers and air conditioning at work went without replacement for years.
子育ての給付が増えたと思ったら、別の名目で保険料が上がった。差し引きいくら得なの: Just as child-rearing benefits seemed to grow, premiums rose under another name. I couldn’t tell what I came out ahead after all.
市の図書館が開館日を減らした。張り紙には、財政が厳しいためと書かれていた。: The city library cut its opening days. A notice on the door said it was due to budget constraints.
町の財政が苦しくなり、地区の公民館の雨漏りと小さな橋の補修が後回しにされた。: The town’s finances grew strained, and repairs to the leaky roof of the district community hall and to a small bridge were put off.
社会保険料の率がまた上がり、給料明細の天引きの額が少しずつ大きくなった。: Social insurance rates rose again, and the deductions on my pay stub crept up bit by bit.
相続や資産にかかる税が重くなり、税理士との相談の回数が増えた。: Taxes on inheritance and assets grew heavier, and I consulted my tax accountant more and more.
国債の入札で買い手が集まらなかったと報じられ、円と株が同時に大きく下がった。: Reports said a government bond auction failed to draw enough buyers, and the yen and stocks plunged together.
財政難で、区のごみ収集が週2回から週1回に減った。ベランダに袋を置いておく日が増: Amid fiscal trouble, the ward cut garbage collection from twice a week to once. More days went by with bags sitting out on the balcony.
国の借金を将来払うのは自分たちの世代だ、と授業で聞いた。教室が少し静かになった。: In class I was told that our generation will be the one to pay back the national debt. The room went a little quiet.
借金の利払いが国の予算の大きな割合を占めるようになった、と新聞に出ていた。研究や: The paper reported that interest payments on the debt now made up a large share of the national budget. Money for research and education was cut again.
介護保険料が上がり、年金から引かれる額がまた増えた。: Long-term care insurance premiums rose, and the amount deducted from my pension grew again.
会社が国の補助金を当てにして進めていた事業が、予算の打ち切りで中止になった。: A project my company had been pushing ahead in the expectation of government subsidies was canceled when the budget was cut off.
年金を物価ほどには上げない仕組みが続き、受け取る額の価値が毎年少しずつ目減りした: The system that raises pensions by less than prices continued, and the real value of what I received shrank a little each year.
金利の上昇で、カードローンの利息がまた上がった。返しても返しても元本が減らなかっ: Rising rates pushed up the interest on my card loan again. No matter how much I paid, the principal wouldn’t shrink.
学校の予算が減り、プリントの紙まで節約するように言われた。教材は自腹で買うことが: The school budget shrank, and we were told to economize even on printing paper. I ended up buying teaching materials out of my own pocket more and more.
借金を減らすため公共施設を減らす計画が進み、駅前の古い市民ホールが取り壊された。: A plan to cut public facilities to reduce debt moved forward, and the old civic hall by the station was torn down.
円安と国力: The Weak Yen and National Strength
海外旅行のパンフレットの値段を見て、家族旅行の行き先を国内に変えた。: I saw the prices in the overseas travel brochure and switched the family trip to somewhere in Japan.
円安で留学の費用が思っていたより大きくふくらみ、行くのをあきらめた。: The weak yen made study abroad far more expensive than I’d expected, and I gave up on going.
観光客で街はにぎわったが、昼ごはんの店はどこも観光客向けの値段になった。: Tourists filled the town with life, but every lunch place switched to tourist prices.
海外の同業者の給料が自分の2倍近いと知った。同じ仕事なのに、と思った。: I learned that peers in the same line of work abroad earned nearly double my pay. Same job, I thought.
ワーキングホリデーで海外に行った友人が、日本より稼げると言って帰ってこなかった。: A friend who went abroad on a working holiday said they could earn more there than in Japan, and never came back.
輸入の小麦や家畜のえさが高くなり、パンと牛乳がまた値上がりした。: Imported wheat and livestock feed got more expensive, and bread and milk went up in price again.
円安で、持っていた海外の株の評価額が大きく増えた。: The weak yen sharply increased the yen value of the overseas stocks I held.
輸入の肥料と燃料が円安で値上がりし、作れば作るほど赤字になる年があった。: Imported fertilizer and fuel got pricier with the weak yen, and there was a year when the more I grew, the deeper in the red I went.
年金暮らしには円安の恩恵は何もなく、輸入品の値上がりだけが届いた。: Living on a pension, I saw no benefit from the weak yen, only the higher prices of imported goods.
日本の経済の規模がまた他の国に抜かれ、順位を一つ落としたと報じられた。: It was reported that Japan’s economy had been overtaken by another country again and dropped one place in the rankings.
スマホの新機種が20万円を超え、画面の割れた古い機種を使い続けることにした。: New smartphone models passed 200,000 yen, so I decided to keep using my old one with the cracked screen.
仕入れ値が上がり、輸入雑貨を扱う店の品ぞろえを半分に減らした。: Purchase costs rose, so I cut the selection at my imported-goods shop by half.
日本の大学から研究者が海外に移るニュースが続いた。論文の数でも、日本は順位を下げ: News kept coming of researchers leaving Japanese universities for posts abroad. Japan kept sliding in the rankings for number of papers, too.
外国から来ていた介護の同僚が、もっと給料の高い国へ移っていった。: A coworker in caregiving who had come from abroad moved on to a country with higher pay.
近所のマンションを海外の投資家がまとめて買い、あたりの家賃相場が上がった。: Overseas investors bought up the neighborhood condo in bulk, and rents in the area went up.
輸入牛肉が高くなり、食卓に並ぶ肉は鶏肉ばかりになった。: Imported beef got expensive, and the meat on the table was nearly all chicken.
県に大きな工場が誘致された。地元に仕事は増えたが、作業員の多くは他県や外国から来: A big factory was attracted to the prefecture. Jobs grew locally, but many of the workers came from other prefectures or abroad.
記録的な円安になり、輸入品の値段がひと月のうちに一斉に上がった。: The yen hit a record low, and import prices all jumped within a single month.
海外出張のホテル代が会社の規定額を大きく超え、差額を自腹で払った。: Hotel costs on an overseas business trip far exceeded the company’s limit, and I paid the difference out of pocket.
日本の給料は安いからと、海外の会社にリモートで勤める人が周りで増えていった。: Because Japanese pay was low, more and more people around me took remote jobs with overseas companies.
冬の灯油が値上がりし、ストーブをつけるのは朝と晩だけにした。: Winter kerosene went up in price, so I only ran the heater morning and evening.
町の工場が海外に移り、700人の働き口が一度に消えた。: The town’s factory moved overseas, and 700 jobs vanished all at once.
勤めていた工場の生産ラインが海外に移ることになり、遠くの工場への転勤か退職かを迫: The production line at the factory where I worked was moving overseas, and I was pushed to choose between a transfer to a faraway plant or quitting.
地元の商店街は、半分以上の店がシャッターを下ろしたままになった。: In the local shopping street, more than half the shops stayed shuttered.
会社の主力製品が海外メーカーとの競争に負け、事業ごと売却された。: The company’s flagship product lost out to overseas makers, and the whole business was sold off.
家電売り場の棚の多くが、海外メーカーの製品で埋まるようになった。: Most of the shelves in the appliance section came to be filled with products from overseas makers.
腕のいい先輩の技術者が、高い給料を提示されて海外の会社に移っていった。: A skilled senior engineer was offered a high salary and moved to an overseas company.
工場の跡地が更地のまま何年も放置され、雑草が背丈ほどに伸びた。: The old factory site was left as bare ground for years, and the weeds grew as tall as a person.
地元に就職先が少なく、高校の同級生の大半は都会に出ていった。: There were few places to work locally, and most of my high school classmates left for the city.
親の住む町は工場の閉鎖から人が減り続けた。帰省するたびに、閉まった店が増えていた: The town where my parents live kept losing people after the factory closed. Each time I went home, more shops were shut.
取引先の大手工場が撤退し、部品を納めていた自分の町工場の仕事が7割消えた。: A major factory we supplied pulled out, and 70 percent of the work at my small parts factory disappeared.
工場の新設がなくなり、地元の建設会社に来る仕事は解体ばかりになった。: No new factories were being built, and the local construction company got nothing but demolition jobs.
近くの工場が閉まって運ぶ荷物が減り、会社の便が半分になった。手当が減り、給料も下: A nearby factory closed and there was less freight to haul, so the company’s runs were cut in half. Allowances shrank and my pay dropped.
薬の原料の輸入が止まり、薬局で咳止めや解熱剤が品切れのままになった。: Imports of drug ingredients stopped, and cough medicine and fever reducers stayed out of stock at the pharmacy.
町に一つだけ残っていた大きな会社が、本社を東京に移した。: The one big company left in town moved its headquarters to Tokyo.
積み立ては海外の株ばかりになった。日本の会社にお金が回らないと言われても、自分の: My savings plan ended up entirely in overseas stocks. People said money wasn’t flowing to Japanese companies, but my own retirement mattered more.
ベテランが定年で辞め、職場のある工程を誰もできなくなった。マニュアルは古くて役に: The veterans retired, and no one at work could handle a certain process anymore. The manual was outdated and useless.
国内回帰で工場が戻ってきたが、中はほとんどロボットで、雇われたのは数十人だけだっ: Reshoring brought a factory back, but it was mostly robots inside, and only a few dozen people were hired.
工業高校の先輩たちの就職先は、ほとんどが県外の会社になった。: Nearly all of the older students from the technical high school ended up working for companies outside the prefecture.
会社が研究所を海外に移した。日本に残るのは営業と管理の部門だけだと告げられた。: The company moved its research lab overseas. We were told that only sales and administration would remain in Japan.
工場の撤退で税収が減り、市役所の新しい職員の採用が止まった。: Tax revenue fell with the factory’s withdrawal, and city hall stopped hiring new staff.
近くの食品工場が閉まり、契約で作っていた野菜の出荷先がなくなった。: The nearby food factory closed, and the vegetables I grew under contract had nowhere to be shipped.
書類作りや集計の仕事がAIに置き換わり、部署ごと縮小された。別の部署への異動を言: Document preparation and tabulation work was replaced by AI, and the whole department was scaled down. I was told I was being moved to another department.
店の注文も電話の問い合わせもAIが受けるようになり、一日中だれとも話さない日が増: AI took over both the shop's orders and the phone inquiries, and I had more and more days when I spoke to no one at all.
新卒の募集が減り、簡単な仕事はAIがやるから即戦力しかいらない、と言われた。: New-graduate hiring shrank. I was told that AI handles the easy work, so they only wanted people who could contribute right away.
宿題をAIに任せる生徒が増え、授業では手書きのテストばかり出されるようになった。: More students left their homework to AI, and classes turned into nothing but handwritten tests.
AIを使いこなせるかどうかで、同じ職場の中でも評価と給料の差が開いた。: Whether you could master AI widened the gap in evaluations and pay, even within the same workplace.
コールセンターのバイトが、AIの導入で契約を打ち切られた。: My call center part-time job ended when AI was brought in and my contract was cut.
生徒がAIに書かせたレポートを見分ける作業に、毎週何時間も取られた。: Spotting reports that students had AI write took up hours of my time every week.
自動運転のトラックが高速道路の幹線を走るようになり、長距離の仕事が減った。: Self-driving trucks began running on the main expressways, and long-haul jobs dwindled.
会社でAIの研修を受けたが、若手のようにはうまく使いこなせず、会議で黙っているこ: I took AI training at work, but couldn't use it as well as the younger staff, and I fell silent in meetings more often.
介護記録をAIが書くようになり、利用者と話す時間が少しだけ増えた。: AI started writing the care records, and I got a little more time to talk with the residents.
市役所の窓口がAIの音声案内になり、何度聞き返しても話が通じなかった。: The city hall counter switched to an AI voice guide, and no matter how many times I asked again, we couldn't understand each other.
AIで作った安いデザインに客を取られ、仕事の単価が半分になった。: Customers went to cheap AI-made designs, and my rate per job was cut in half.
申請の審査にAIが入り、自分の仕事は機械の判断を確認することになった。: AI entered the application screening, and my job became checking the machine's decisions.
AI関連の株が急に上がったあと急に下がり、利益がほとんど消えた。: AI-related stocks shot up and then suddenly dropped, and nearly all my gains vanished.
求人の一次面接の相手がAIになった。画面に向かって話しただけで、不採用の通知が届: The first-round job interview was with an AI. I just talked at a screen, and a rejection notice arrived.
子どもになりたい仕事を聞かれて、それはAIに取られないかと、つい考えてしまった。: When my child told me what job they wanted, I couldn't help wondering whether AI would take it.
AIで仕事は速くなったが、浮いた時間にはすぐ別の仕事が入れられた。: AI made work faster, but the time it freed up was immediately filled with other work.
現場にもドローンや測量のAIが入ったが、最後に手を動かすのは人で、人手は足りない: Drones and surveying AI arrived on site too, but people still did the final hands-on work, and there was still a labor shortage.
無人の店が駅前に増えた。深夜でも買い物はできたが、店員に何かを聞くことはできなく: Unstaffed stores multiplied in front of the station. I could shop even late at night, but there was no clerk to ask anything.
AIが人の知能を超えると言われた2045年を過ぎた。仕事を失った人と、仕事が増え: We passed 2045, the year AI was said to surpass human intelligence. People who lost their jobs and people whose work grew split sharply apart.
契約は3か月ごとの更新で、そのたびに次はあるのかと気になって眠れなかった。: My contract was renewed every three months, and each time I lay awake wondering if there would be a next one.
同じ仕事をしている正社員にはボーナスが出たが、自分に出たのは寸志の5,000円だ: Full-time employees doing the same work got bonuses, but all I got was a token 5,000 yen.
非正規の仕事を続けたまま年を重ね、老後の蓄えはほとんどないままだった。: I kept working non-regular jobs as the years went by, and I had almost no savings for old age.
健康診断も歯医者も、お金がかかるからと何年も行かずにいた。: I skipped health checkups and the dentist for years because of the cost.
同じクラスの子は塾に通っていたが、うちは行かせてやれなかった。: Kids in my class went to cram school, but we couldn't afford to send mine.
親から受け継いだ資産で、暮らしは安定していた。同級生の生活の苦しさを聞くと、言葉: Assets inherited from my parents kept my life stable. When I heard how hard my classmates had it, I was at a loss for words.
奨学金を借りた場合の返済額を計算して、進学するかどうか迷った。: I calculated how much I'd have to repay if I took out a scholarship loan, and wavered over whether to go on to college.
奨学金の返済が毎月の給料から消えていき、完済は30代半ばになる計算だった。: Scholarship loan repayments vanished from my paycheck every month, and by my calculation I wouldn't be done until my mid-thirties.
年金だけでは足りず、朝早くからビル清掃のパートを続けた。: My pension wasn't enough, so I kept up a part-time building cleaning job starting early every morning.
保証人がいないことを理由に、部屋の申し込みを3件続けて断られた。: Three apartment applications in a row were turned down because I had no guarantor.
同じ駅の東と西にタワーマンションと古いアパートが並び、通う塾も学校も分かれていっ: On the east and west sides of the same station stood high-rise condos and old apartment buildings, and the cram schools and schools the kids attended split along that line.
食料の無料配布の列に並んだ。前にはスーツ姿の人もいた。: I stood in line for a free food handout. Some of the people ahead of me were in suits.
夫婦ともに非正規で、子どもを持つかどうか決められないまま年月が過ぎた。: Both of us were in non-regular jobs, and the years passed without our being able to decide whether to have a child.
派遣先との契約が切れ、次の仕事が見つかるまで2か月かかった。: My contract with the placement company ended, and it took two months to find the next job.
推計では男性の3割近くが生涯結婚しない時代になると言われ、周りでも珍しい話ではな: Projections said nearly 30% of men would never marry in their lifetime, and around me it had stopped being unusual.
非課税の積み立てで資産を増やす人と、投資に回すお金がない人の差が、10年で大きく: In ten years, the gap widened greatly between those growing their assets through tax-free investment accounts and those with no money to invest.
近所の子ども食堂の利用者が、前の年の倍になったと聞いた。: I heard the number of people using the neighborhood children's cafeteria had doubled from the year before.
転職先を探したが、年齢の壁で正社員の求人はほとんど残らなかった。: I looked for a new job, but the age barrier left almost no full-time openings.
就職氷河期に非正規で働き始めた世代が、そのまま年金生活に入り始めた。老後の生活保: The generation that started in non-regular work during the employment ice age began entering retirement on pensions as is. Welfare recipients in old age were said to be on the rise.
熱を出して1週間休んだら、その分の給料がまるごと減った。有給休暇は使えないと言わ: I ran a fever and took a week off, and that whole stretch came out of my pay. I was told I couldn't use paid leave.
年金だけでは暮らせず、スーパーの品出しの仕事を続けた。腰の痛みは湿布でごまかした: I couldn't live on my pension alone, so I kept stocking shelves at a supermarket. I covered up the pain in my back with medicated patches.
交通誘導の仕事で炎天下に立ち続け、熱中症で倒れかけた。: Working traffic control, I stood under the blazing sun and nearly collapsed from heatstroke.
年金の受け取りは今より遅くなるかもしれないと言われ、老後の計画を5年後ろにずらし: I was told pension payouts might start later than they do now, so I pushed my retirement plans back five years.
定年後に再雇用された元上司が、同じ席で同じ仕事なのに給料が4割下がったとこぼして: My former boss, rehired after retirement, grumbled that his pay had dropped 40% for the same work at the same desk.
80歳を過ぎても、シルバー人材センターから草刈りの仕事を受けた。: Even past eighty, I took mowing jobs from the Silver Human Resources Center.
近所のコンビニでも工事現場でも、働いているのは60代や70代の人ばかりになった。: At the local convenience store and at construction sites alike, the workers were almost all in their sixties and seventies.
仲間のドライバーの中心は60代後半になった。事故を起こさないよう、みんな毎朝血圧: The core of my fellow drivers were now in their late sixties. To avoid accidents, everyone checked their blood pressure every morning.
仕事中に段差で転び、手首の骨を折った。治るまでの2か月、収入が途絶えた。: I tripped on a step at work and broke my wrist. For the two months until it healed, my income stopped.
70代の父が、まだ働けると言ってタクシーの運転を続けた。電話で無理しないでと言う: My father, in his seventies, said he could still work and kept driving a taxi. All I could do was tell him over the phone not to push himself.
職場の平均年齢が上がり、70代の職員が80代の入所者を介助するのが当たり前になっ: The average age at the workplace rose, and it became normal for staff in their seventies to care for residents in their eighties.
旅行や趣味にあてるつもりだった老後は、週4日のパートで埋まった。: The retirement I had meant to spend on travel and hobbies got filled up with part-time work four days a week.
70代の職人が現場に欠かせなくなり、引退したい親方がなかなか辞めさせてもらえなか: Craftsmen in their seventies became indispensable on site, and the master who wanted to retire couldn't get let go.
集落で田んぼに出ているのは、70代と80代の人ばかりになった。: In the village, the only people out in the rice fields were in their seventies and eighties.
パソコンが使えないと採用されない仕事が増え、高齢者向けの講習に通った。: More jobs refused to hire anyone who couldn't use a computer, so I attended a course for seniors.
孫の学費を少しでも出してやろうと、マンションの管理人の仕事を続けた。: Hoping to chip in for my grandchild's tuition, I kept working as an apartment building caretaker.
働いて収入があるせいで、受け取るはずの年金の一部が止められた。: Because I had earnings from working, part of the pension I should have received was withheld.
会社が70歳まで働ける制度を作った。ありがたいような、終わりが見えなくなったよう: My company set up a system allowing work until age 70. It felt both welcome and like the end had slipped out of sight.
体力の落ちた体で夜間の警備を続け、帰りの電車でいつも眠り込んだ。: I kept up night security work with a body that had lost its stamina, and I always dozed off on the train home.
仕事を辞めたとたん、毎日話す相手が一気にいなくなった。: The moment I quit work, the people I talked to every day were suddenly gone.
推計で人口の3人に1人以上が65歳以上になる2040年代に入った。求人票の「年齢: We entered the 2040s, when more than one in three people were projected to be 65 or older. “Age no object” on job postings became the norm.
近所のパン屋が、後継ぎがいなくて店を閉めた。最終日には長い列ができた。: The neighborhood bakery closed because it had no successor. On its last day, a long line formed.
店を継ぐ人がおらず、70年続いた看板を自分の代で下ろすことにした。: With no one to take over the shop, I decided to take down the sign that had stood for 70 years in my own generation.
町で一軒だけの自転車屋が閉店し、パンクの修理にも隣町まで行くことになった。: The town's only bicycle shop closed, and I had to go to the next town even to fix a flat.
事業を引き継ぐ相手を探す仲介に登録したが、2年たっても買い手は現れなかった。: I registered with a matching service to find someone to take over the business, but two years passed and no buyer appeared.
親の工務店を誰が継ぐかで、兄弟の意見がまとまらなかった。: My siblings and I couldn't agree on who would take over our parents' construction firm.
勤め先が後継ぎがいないまま廃業を決め、40人の社員が一斉に職を失った。: My employer decided to close with no successor, and all 40 employees lost their jobs at once.
腕のいい親方が引退して会社をたたみ、抱えていた得意先がばらばらになった。: The skilled master retired and shut down the company, and the clients he had kept scattered.
後継ぎのいない地元の会社を買い取らないかと、銀行から持ちかけられた。: The bank asked whether I'd buy out a local company that had no successor.
地元の酒蔵が、継ぐ人がいないまま二百年の歴史を閉じると聞いた。最後の新酒を一本だ: I heard the local sake brewery would close after 200 years with no one to carry it on. I bought a single bottle of its last new sake.
子どものころから通った銭湯が、燃料代の高さと後継ぎの不在で閉業した。: The public bathhouse I'd gone to since childhood closed because of high fuel costs and the lack of a successor.
家を建ててくれた工務店が廃業し、雨どいの修理を頼める先がなくなった。: The builder who had built my house went out of business, and I had no one left to ask to fix the rain gutter.
農機具を直してくれた町の店が閉まり、壊れたトラクターを半年動かせなかった。: The town shop that used to repair my farm equipment closed, and my broken tractor sat idle for half a year.
学校の制服を扱っていた地元の店が閉まり、遠くの店まで子どもを連れて買いに行った。: The local shop that sold school uniforms closed, and I took my child to a faraway store to buy one.
事業を引き継いでくれる外部の人がようやく見つかった。従業員の雇用だけは守ることが: At last I found an outside person willing to take over the business. At least I managed to protect my employees' jobs.
長年の取引先から、黒字のまま廃業するという挨拶状が届いた。: A longtime client sent a notice saying they were closing down while still in the black.
商店街の老舗が次々に閉まり、全国チェーンの店ばかりの通りになった。: The long-established shops in the shopping street closed one after another, until the street was nothing but national chain stores.
何十年も通った床屋の主人が引退し、新しい店ではうまく注文を伝えられなかった。: The barber I'd gone to for decades retired, and at a new shop I couldn't explain what I wanted.
社長が急に倒れ、後継ぎを決めていなかった勤め先は半年で立ち行かなくなった。: The president suddenly collapsed, and my employer, which had not chosen a successor, fell apart within six months.
地元の小さな鉄工所が閉まり、祭りの山車を直せる職人がいなくなった。: The small local ironworks closed, and there was no longer any craftsman who could repair the festival floats.
銀行の担当者に、後継ぎが決まっていない会社への新しい融資は難しいと言われた。: The bank officer told me that new loans to a company with no successor decided would be difficult.
米の値段が上がり、5キロの袋に手を伸ばすのをためらった。: The price of rice rose, and I hesitated before reaching for a 5-kilo bag.
農業で働く人の平均年齢は70歳近くになった。寄り合いでは、いつまでも自分が若手と: The average age of farm workers neared 70. At community meetings, I was still called one of the young ones.
隣の田んぼが耕す人のいない荒れ地になり、家の近くにイノシシが出るようになった。: The neighboring rice field became abandoned wasteland with no one to farm it, and wild boars began appearing near the house.
食料自給率は4割に届かないままで、スーパーの棚は輸入品で埋まっていた。: Food self-sufficiency stayed below 40%, and the supermarket shelves were packed with imports.
海外の不作と輸送の混乱が重なり、スーパーからパスタや小麦粉が一時的に消えた。: Poor harvests overseas combined with shipping disruptions, and pasta and flour briefly vanished from the supermarket.
猛暑で米が白く濁り、等級が下がって買い取り価格が大きく落ちた。: The extreme heat turned the rice grains chalky white, the grade dropped, and the purchase price fell sharply.
後継ぎのいない近所の農家から田んぼを預かり、耕す面積が倍になった。休みはほとんど: I took over the rice fields of a neighboring farm with no successor, and the area I farmed doubled. I almost never had a day off.
食材費の高騰で給食の果物の回数が減った、と学校からお知らせが届いた。: The school sent a notice saying fruit would appear less often in school lunches because of soaring ingredient costs.
近くの酪農家が餌代の高さに耐えられず、牛を手放した。朝に聞こえていた鳴き声がしな: A nearby dairy farmer couldn't bear the high cost of feed and sold off his cows. The lowing I used to hear in the morning stopped.
魚が高くなり、食卓に上るのはほとんど缶詰の魚になった。: Fish became expensive, and what reached our table was mostly canned fish.
海の温度が上がり、網に入る魚の種類が変わった。値のつかない魚ばかりがとれた。: The sea warmed, and the kinds of fish in my nets changed. I caught mostly fish that fetched no price.
空きビルを使った野菜工場ができ、天気に関係なくレタスが同じ値段で買えるようになっ: A vegetable factory opened in a vacant building, and lettuce could be bought at the same price regardless of the weather.
農業法人の求人を見に行った。広い田んぼをドローンで見回る仕事で、応募者は数えるほ: I went to look at a job opening at an agricultural corporation. The work was patrolling wide rice fields by drone, and applicants could be counted on one hand.
米も野菜も高くなり、食費を削るために一日2食にした。: Rice and vegetables both got more expensive, so I cut down to two meals a day to save on food.
ウナギは高すぎて、土用の丑の日にもスーパーで眺めるだけだった。: Eel was too expensive, and even on the midsummer eel day I only looked at it in the supermarket.
見慣れた田んぼが一枚ずつ太陽光パネルと空き地に変わり、田園の風景が半分になった。: The familiar rice fields turned one by one into solar panels and vacant lots, and the countryside scenery was cut in half.
体力の限界で、耕してきた田んぼの半分を手放した。貸す相手も見つからなかった。: Reaching the limit of my strength, I gave up half of the fields I had farmed. I couldn't even find anyone to lease them to.
食料価格の上昇で持っていた食品株は上がったが、家の食費の上がり方のほうが大きかっ: Rising food prices lifted the food stocks I held, but my household grocery bill rose even more.
災害で物流が止まった時に備え、押し入れに2週間分の米と缶詰を置くようになった。: To prepare for when a disaster halts distribution, I started keeping two weeks' worth of rice and canned food in the closet.
輸入が止まったときの国の試算では、毎食いも類中心の献立になると書かれていて、思わ: A government estimate of what would happen if imports stopped said every meal would center on potatoes and other tubers, and I found myself staring at it.
家の耐震診断を頼んだら、補強に約200万円かかると言われた。見積書は引き出しにし: I had my house assessed for earthquake resistance and was told reinforcement would cost about 2 million yen. The estimate stayed shut in a drawer.
借りているアパートが旧耐震基準の建物だと知った。引っ越し費用を計算して、結局その: I learned my rented apartment was built under the old earthquake standards. I worked out the moving costs and ended up staying put.
家の防災リュックを開けたら、非常食の賞味期限が3年前に切れていた。水も半分しか入: When I opened the emergency backpack at home, the emergency food had expired three years earlier. There was only half the water it should have held.
首都直下地震の想定では、都内の帰宅困難者は約450万人と言われた。会社から家まで: Under the Tokyo inland earthquake scenario, about 4.5 million people in the city would be unable to get home. I learned that walking from the office to my house would take five hours.
自治体の避難行動要支援者名簿に名前が載った。担当の支援者は、自分より年上の近所の: My name was added to the municipality's register of people needing evacuation assistance. The neighbor assigned to help me was older than I was.
南海トラフ地震の津波想定が見直され、家のあたりは浸水深10mの区域になった。高台: The Nankai Trough earthquake tsunami projections were revised, and my neighborhood became a zone with 10 meters of flooding. The only evacuation route to high ground was one steep slope.
子どもの学校の引き渡し訓練に、仕事で間に合わなかった。本当の災害のとき迎えに行け: I couldn't make it to my child's school pickup drill because of work. I grew anxious about whether I could go get them in a real disaster.
地震保険の保険料がまた上がった。更新のたびに、補償を減らすかどうか迷うようになっ: Earthquake insurance premiums went up again. With every renewal, I found myself wondering whether to reduce the coverage.
家具の転倒防止をしようとしたが、脚立に上るのが怖くてできなかった。頼める人も近く: I tried to secure my furniture against tipping over, but I was too scared to climb the stepladder. There was no one nearby to ask.
大規模地震を想定した訓練で、災害対応にあたる職員の数がまったく足りないと分かった: A drill simulating a major earthquake showed there were nowhere near enough staff for disaster response. The report said only “handle by requesting reinforcements.”
南海トラフ地震臨時情報が出て、店の棚から水とカセットボンベが消えた。数日で棚は元: A Nankai Trough earthquake advisory was issued, and water and portable gas canisters vanished from the store shelves. Within days the shelves were restocked, and no earthquake came.
耐震補強の工事依頼が増えたが、職人が足りず半年待ちになった。断った客の顔がしばら: Requests for seismic retrofitting grew, but there weren't enough craftsmen and the wait stretched to six months. I couldn't forget the faces of the customers I turned away for a long time.
勤め先の施設で夜間の避難訓練をした。夜勤2人で利用者20人を避難させるのは無理だ: We held a night evacuation drill at the facility where I worked. Everyone silently understood that two night-shift staff could never evacuate 20 residents.
マンションの管理組合で、非常用発電機の更新費用が足りないと報告された。修繕積立金: At the condo management association, it was reported that funds to replace the emergency generator fell short. A hike in the repair reserve fund was decided.
木造住宅が密集した地域の地図で、自分の住む町が赤く塗られていた。地震のあと火災が: On the map of densely packed wooden housing areas, my town was painted red. I was told it was an area where fire spreads easily after an earthquake.
夫婦で災害時の集合場所を決めようとしたが、話し合いは5分で終わった。結局どこにも: My spouse and I tried to decide where to meet in a disaster, but the talk ended in five minutes. In the end we wrote it down nowhere.
会社の事業継続計画で、自分は「発災時出社可能者」に入れられた。家族より先に職場へ: In the company's business continuity plan, I was listed as someone “able to report to work when disaster strikes.” The rule was to head to the workplace before my family.
防災グッズを一式そろえると3万円近くかかると知った。ひとまず水だけ箱で買い、残り: I learned a full set of disaster supplies would cost nearly 30,000 yen. For now I just bought a case of water and put off the rest.
防災訓練の安否確認カードに緊急連絡先を書く欄があったが、誰の名前も書けなかった。: The safety-confirmation card at the disaster drill had a space for an emergency contact, but I couldn't write anyone's name.
孫の家が沿岸部にあると知り、避難場所を一緒に地図で確かめた。高台までは子どもの足: Learning that my grandchild's home was in a coastal area, I checked the evacuation site on a map together with them. It was a 20-minute walk for a child to reach high ground.
ハザードマップが改訂され、近くの避難所が「地震時は使用不可」に変わった。次に近い: The hazard map was revised, and the nearby shelter was changed to “unusable during earthquakes.” The next closest shelter was 2 km away.
最高気温40℃を超える日が、珍しいニュースではなくなった。夏休みの昼間、外で遊ぶ: Days above 40°C stopped being unusual news. During summer vacation, I no longer saw children playing outside in the daytime.
電気代を気にして夜はエアコンを止めて寝たら、朝、頭痛とめまいで起き上がれなかった: Worried about the electric bill, I turned off the air conditioner and slept, and in the morning I couldn't get up from a headache and dizziness.
部活の練習が熱中症警戒で中止続きになり、大会前なのにほとんど練習できなかった。: Club practices were canceled one after another because of heatstroke warnings, and I barely got to practice even right before the tournament.
現場の気温が38℃を超え、作業は早朝と夕方だけになった。工期は延び、手取りは減っ: Temperatures at the site topped 38°C, and work was limited to early morning and evening. The schedule dragged on and my take-home pay shrank.
配達の車内は50℃近くになり、保冷が追いつかない日が増えた。一日に水を2リットル: The inside of the delivery vehicle neared 50°C, and there were more days when the cooling couldn't keep up. Even drinking over two liters of water a day wasn't enough.
夏の電気代が月2万円を超えた。昼は図書館で過ごし、家のエアコンは夜だけつけること: My summer electric bill topped 20,000 yen a month. I spent the days at the library and decided to run the home air conditioner only at night.
熱中症警戒アラートが毎日のように出たが、喉の渇きをあまり感じず、水を飲むのを忘れ: Heatstroke alerts went out almost every day, but I hardly felt thirsty and tended to forget to drink water.
夏の高温で米粒が白く濁り、等級が下がった。出荷価格は前の年より大きく下がった。: The summer heat turned the rice grains chalky white and lowered the grade. The shipping price fell well below the previous year's.
公園の遊具が熱くて触れず、子どもを外で遊ばせられるのは夕方の30分だけになった。: The playground equipment in the park was too hot to touch, and the only time I could let my child play outside was 30 minutes in the evening.
夜になっても気温が30℃を下回らない日が続いた。寝不足のまま朝を迎える日がひと夏: Days when the temperature stayed above 30°C even at night kept coming. In a single summer, dozens of mornings arrived with me short on sleep.
通勤で15分歩くだけで汗だくになり、職場に着くと着替えるようになった。シャツが倍: Just a 15-minute walk to work left me drenched in sweat, so I began changing clothes on arrival. I needed twice as many shirts.
秋が短くなったと誰もが口にした。半袖をしまうのは11月になり、衣替えという言葉を: Everyone said autumn had gotten shorter. Short sleeves didn't go away until November, and the word “seasonal wardrobe change” faded from use.
体育の授業や運動会を、暑さを理由に何度も中止や短縮にした。保護者からの問い合わせ: We canceled or shortened PE classes and sports days over and over because of the heat. I was swamped answering inquiries from parents.
地域の夏祭りが熱中症の恐れから昼の行事をやめ、夜だけの短い催しになった。: Fearing heatstroke, the local summer festival dropped its daytime events and became a short evening-only affair.
自治体のクーリングシェルターに指定された公民館に、夏の昼間は毎日通うようになった: I started going every summer afternoon to the community center designated as a cooling shelter by the municipality.
訪問先の高齢者の家でエアコンが壊れていた。修理まで1週間かかると言われ、毎日様子: The air conditioner was broken at the home of an elderly person I visited. Repairs would take a week, so I stopped by every day to check on them.
西日の当たる部屋のエアコンは古く、真夏は室温が33℃までしか下がらなかった。大家: The air conditioner in my west-facing room was old, and in midsummer the room only cooled to 33°C. The landlord was reluctant to replace it.
猛暑で葉物野菜が不作になり、スーパーのキャベツがいつもの倍の値段になった。: Extreme heat ruined the leafy vegetable crops, and cabbage at the supermarket cost double the usual price.
猛暑日が続くと客足がぱったり途絶え、店の夏の売上は前の年より2割減った。: When the scorching days continued, customers stopped coming altogether, and the shop's summer sales fell 20% from the previous year.
夏の旅行先を決めるとき、条件の一番目が「涼しいところ」になった。北の宿はどこも満: When choosing a summer travel destination, the first requirement became “somewhere cool.” Every inn in the north was fully booked.
厳しい想定では、今世紀末の夏は今より4℃以上暑くなると言われた。自分が年をとるこ: Under harsh scenarios, summers at the end of this century were said to be over 4°C hotter than now. Imagining the summers of my old age, I felt a slight chill.
家が浸水想定区域に入っていて、火災保険の水災補償の保険料が上がった。: My home was in a projected flood zone, and the flood coverage premium on my fire insurance went up.
線状降水帯の予報が出て、夜中に公民館へ避難した。翌朝帰ると、裏山の土砂が庭まで流: A linear rainband forecast was issued, and I evacuated to the community center in the middle of the night. When I returned the next morning, soil from the hill behind the house had flowed into the yard.
短時間の豪雨で駅前の地下通路が水につかり、帰りは遠回りして1時間歩いた。: A short burst of heavy rain flooded the underground passage by the station, and on the way home I took a detour and walked for an hour.
「数十年に一度」のはずの大雨特別警報が、気づけば毎年どこかで出ていた。天気予報を: Heavy rain emergency warnings that were supposed to come “once in several decades” were, before I knew it, being issued somewhere every year. I spent more time watching weather forecasts.
避難指示が出たが、足が悪くて避難所まで行けなかった。2階で一晩、雨の音を聞いて過: An evacuation order was issued, but with my bad legs I couldn't get to the shelter. I spent the night on the second floor, listening to the rain.
大雨で田んぼに土砂が流れ込み、復旧に2年かかると言われた。補助金を受けても赤字が: Heavy rain washed soil into my rice fields, and recovery was said to take two years. Even with subsidies, I was left in the red.
半地下の部屋が大雨で浸水し、家具と家電をほとんど捨てた。大家からは退去を勧められ: My semi-basement room flooded in heavy rain, and I threw out nearly all my furniture and appliances. The landlord suggested I move out.
大雨で通学路の川があふれ、子どもの学校が3日休校になった。仕事を休んで家で一緒に: The river along the school route overflowed in heavy rain, and my child's school closed for three days. I took time off work and stayed home with them.
豪雨のあと避難所の運営に入り、3日間ほとんど眠れなかった。交代の職員はなかなか来: After the torrential rain, I went to run the evacuation shelter and barely slept for three days. The relief staff were slow to arrive.
豪雨で幹線道路と鉄道が同時に止まり、荷物を届けられない日が1週間続いた。: Heavy rain shut down both the main road and the railway at once, and for a week I couldn't deliver any packages.
近くの川の堤防改修は、予算の都合で「おおむね20年後」とされた。それまで毎年、梅: Reinforcing the embankment of the nearby river was put off to “roughly 20 years from now” due to budget constraints. Until then, I dreaded the rainy season every year.
台風が近づくたびに窓へ養生テープを貼り、ベランダの物を片付けるのが年に何度もの決: Every time a typhoon approached, taping the windows and clearing things off the balcony became a routine repeated several times a year.
水害のあとの修理依頼が殺到し、半年先まで予約が埋まった。休みなく働き続け、腰を痛: Repair requests poured in after the flood, and bookings filled up six months ahead. I kept working without a break and hurt my back.
床上浸水した家の片付けにボランティアが来るまで、泥のにおいの中で一週間暮らした。: I lived for a week in the smell of mud until volunteers came to help clean up my flooded house.
隣の空き家の雨どいが壊れたまま放置され、大雨のたびにうちの庭へ水が流れ込んだ。: The gutter on the empty house next door was left broken, and every heavy rain sent water flowing into my yard.
夜の大雨で駐車場の車が水につかり、廃車になった。車両保険には入っていなかった。: A heavy rain at night submerged my car in the parking lot, and it was totaled. I had no vehicle insurance.
下水があふれる内水氾濫で、家の前の道路がひざの高さまで水につかった。玄関の土のう: Sewers overflowed in an urban flood, and the road in front of my house was knee-deep in water. The sandbags at the front door were my last hope.
大雨で鉄道が止まり、定期試験が延期になった。勉強の計画を一から立て直した。: Heavy rain halted the trains, and the regular exams were postponed. I rebuilt my study plan from scratch.
店が浸水し、冷蔵庫と在庫をすべて失った。営業を再開できたのは3か月後だった。: The shop flooded, and I lost the refrigerator and all the stock. It was three months before I could reopen.
大雨警報が出た朝も「出社できる人は出社」と連絡が来た。濡れた靴のまま一日働いた。: Even on the morning a heavy rain warning was issued, word came: “Come in if you can.” I worked all day in wet shoes.
水害で出た家具や畳のごみの山が、近所の公園に1か月置かれたままだった。夏はにおい: A pile of furniture and tatami mats discarded after the flood sat in the neighborhood park for a month. The smell was awful in summer.
輸入小麦の値上がりが続き、いつも買う食パンが数年でずいぶん高くなった。: Imported wheat kept getting more expensive, and the sandwich bread I always buy got a lot pricier over a few years.
食料自給率はカロリーベースで約4割のままだと報じられた。冷蔵庫を開けると、中身の: It was reported that food self-sufficiency stayed at about 40% on a calorie basis. When I opened the fridge, most of what was inside was foreign-made.
肥料の原料はほぼ輸入頼みで、肥料代が数年で2倍近くになった。畑の作付けを一部やめ: Fertilizer ingredients are almost all imported, and fertilizer costs nearly doubled in a few years. I stopped planting part of the field.
電気代とガス代が上がり続け、冬は暖房を最小限にして厚着で過ごした。: Electricity and gas bills kept rising, and in winter I kept the heating to a minimum and bundled up.
近所のガソリンスタンドが閉店し、灯油の配達も終わった。冬の前に灯油を確保するのが: The neighborhood gas station closed, and kerosene delivery ended too. Securing kerosene before winter became a struggle.
年金は少し増えても、食料品と光熱費の値上がりに追いつかなかった。献立から肉と魚の: Even though my pension rose a little, it couldn't keep up with rising food and utility prices. Meat and fish appeared less often on the menu.
電気料金の値上げで、店の冷蔵ショーケースの電気代だけで月10万円を超えた。: After the electricity rate hike, the power bill for the shop’s refrigerated display case alone topped 100,000 yen a month.
海外の不作で輸入大豆が高くなり、豆腐と納豆の値札が書き換えられた。: Poor harvests overseas made imported soybeans more expensive, and the price tags on tofu and natto were rewritten.
給食費が値上げされ、献立から果物の日が減ったと子どもが言った。: School lunch fees went up, and my child said fruit shows up less often on the menu.
電力の需給がひっ迫し、夏と冬に節電要請が出るのが当たり前になった。駅の照明も半分: Electricity supply grew tight, and requests to conserve power in summer and winter became routine. Half the lights in the station were off too.
農業を担う人の平均年齢は70歳近くになり、近所の田んぼが次々と耕作放棄地になった: The average age of farmers approached 70, and the rice paddies in the neighborhood became abandoned farmland one after another.
エネルギー価格の急騰で相場が荒れ、運用していた資産が一時1割近く減った。: A sharp rise in energy prices roiled the market, and the assets I was investing dropped nearly 10% at one point.
屋根に太陽光パネルと蓄電池をつけた。停電への備えにはなったが、初期費用の回収には: I put solar panels and a storage battery on the roof. They prepared me for blackouts, but I was told it would take 15 years to recoup the initial cost.
円安が続き、輸入に頼る食品や日用品が軒並み値上がりした。家計簿の食費の欄は毎月予: The yen kept weakening, and imported foods and daily goods all got more expensive. The food line in my household ledger went over budget every month.
軽油の値上がり分を運賃に上乗せできず、そのしわ寄せが歩合の給料に回ってきた。: I couldn't pass the higher diesel cost on to freight rates, and the squeeze landed on my commission-based pay.
輸入飼料が高くなり、卵が「物価の優等生」と呼ばれなくなった。卵焼きの出番が減った: Imported feed got expensive, and eggs stopped being called a “price-stable staple.” Rolled omelets appeared less often.
停電に備えて石油ストーブを出したが、灯油を買いに行く手段がなかった。: I took out the kerosene heater in case of a blackout, but had no way to go buy kerosene.
電気代の高騰で、勤め先は国内の生産ラインを縮小した。自分の部署も配置換えになった: Because of soaring electricity costs, my employer scaled down its domestic production lines. My own department was reassigned too.
一人分の自炊は割高で、閉店前の値引き総菜で済ませる日が増えた。: Cooking for one costs more per serving, and I increasingly got by on discounted deli food right before closing time.
日本のエネルギー自給率は1割台だと言われた。電気の明細を見るたびに、遠い国のニュ: Japan’s energy self-sufficiency was said to be in the low teens percent. Every time I looked at my electricity statement, I thought of news from faraway countries.
息子を名乗る電話で「会社のお金をなくした」と言われ、銀行に向かいかけた。窓口の行: A call from someone claiming to be my son said, “I lost company money,” and I almost headed to the bank. The teller stopped me.
本物そっくりの宅配業者のSMSが届き、リンクを押しかけた。同じ文面のメッセージが: A text that looked exactly like a delivery company’s arrived, and I almost tapped the link. The same message had reached everyone in my family.
SNSで有名人を名乗るアカウントに投資を勧められ、少しだけ送金してしまった。お金: An account claiming to be a celebrity on social media pitched me an investment, and I sent a small amount. The money never came back.
取引先を装ったメールで、請求書の振込先の変更を指示された。経理が気づかなければ数: An email posing as a client told me to change the bank account on an invoice. If accounting hadn’t noticed, we would have lost several million yen.
勤める病院がランサムウェアに感染し、電子カルテが2週間使えなくなった。紙とペンで: The hospital where I worked was hit by ransomware, and the electronic medical records were unusable for two weeks. We ran care with paper and pens.
役所の職員を名乗る電話で還付金があると言われ、ATMへ向かいかけた。途中で近所の: A call from someone claiming to be a city hall employee said I had a refund coming, and I almost went to the ATM. A neighbor called out to me on the way.
「高収入・即日」のSNS募集に応募しかけたが、闇バイトの入り口だと気づいて連絡を: I almost answered a social media ad for “high pay, same-day cash,” but realized it was the gateway to a shady side job and cut off contact.
署で特殊詐欺の相談電話を受け続けた。手口は毎年変わり、被害額は大きくなっていった: At the station, I kept taking calls from people reporting phone scams. The methods changed every year, and the damage grew larger.
使っていた通販サイトから個人情報が流出したと通知が来た。パスワードを全部変えるの: I got a notice that personal information had leaked from the online shop I used. Changing all my passwords took an entire night.
子どものゲームのアカウントが乗っ取られ、知らないうちに課金されていた。: My child’s game account was hijacked, and purchases had been made without us knowing.
店のホームページが改ざんされ、客から「変なサイトに飛ぶ」と連絡が来た。復旧に30: The shop’s website was defaced, and customers contacted me saying, “It sends me to a weird site.” The recovery cost 300,000 yen.
一人暮らしになってから、勧誘や不審な電話が急に増えた。電話が鳴るたびに身構えるよ: Since I started living alone, solicitations and suspicious calls have suddenly increased. I began bracing myself every time the phone rang.
ネットバンキングに不正ログインされ、預金が引き出されていた。補償の手続きが終わる: My online banking was accessed without authorization, and money was withdrawn from my savings. It took three months to finish the reimbursement process.
友だちのアカウントから「電子マネーを買って」とメッセージが来た。そのアカウントは: A message came from a friend’s account saying, “Buy me some e-money.” That account had been hijacked.
会社の訓練用の偽メールに引っかかり、セキュリティ研修を受け直すことになった。: I fell for the company’s fake training phishing email and had to retake the security training.
固定電話を、登録していない番号は鳴らない設定に変えた。それ以来、古い友人からの電: I set my landline so numbers I haven’t saved won’t ring. Since then, calls from old friends no longer get through either.
本物そっくりの偽のニュース映像が動画サイトに出回った。どれが本当なのか、もう見分: Fake news footage that looked completely real circulated on video sites. I felt I could no longer tell which was true.
賃貸の初期費用を振り込んだが、物件情報そのものが偽物だった。同じ手口の被害が相次: I transferred the initial costs for a rental, but the listing itself was fake. I later learned similar cases were happening one after another.
マッチングアプリで知り合った相手に投資を勧められた。言われるままにしていたら、全: Someone I met on a dating app pushed me to invest. If I had kept doing as I was told, I would have lost everything.
役所のシステムがサイバー攻撃で止まり、住民票の発行が数日できなくなった。窓口で謝: The city hall system went down in a cyberattack, and residence certificates couldn’t be issued for several days. I kept apologizing at the counter.
特殊詐欺の被害は年に数百億円規模と報じられた。親に電話して、家族だけの合言葉を決: Damage from special fraud was reported to be in the tens of billions of yen a year. I called my parents and suggested we set a password just for family.
近くの交番が統合で無人になった。何かあれば隣町の警察署へ電話するよう張り紙がして: The nearby police box was consolidated and left unmanned. A notice said to call the police station in the next town if anything happened.
予算の都合で夜道の街灯が間引かれ、帰り道がずいぶん暗くなった。: Due to budget constraints, streetlights on night roads were thinned out, and the way home got much darker.
採用の応募が減り、署は定員割れのまま夜勤を回した。休日の呼び出しが当たり前になっ: Applications for hiring dropped, and the station ran night shifts while understaffed. Being called in on days off became normal.
地域の消防団の団員が減り、集落の消防団は60代と70代だけになった。放水訓練も年: Members of the local volunteer fire corps dwindled, and the village corps came down to people in their 60s and 70s. Water-spraying drills dropped to once a year.
救急車を呼んでから着くまで20分以上かかった。出動が重なっていると言われた。: It took more than 20 minutes for the ambulance to arrive after I called. I was told that dispatches were overlapping.
通学路の見守りボランティアが高齢で引退し、登校の付き添いが保護者の当番制になった: The volunteers who watched over the school route retired due to age, and escorting kids to school became a rotating duty for parents.
町内会長を頼まれたが、引き受けられる人が自分以外にいなかった。: I was asked to be the neighborhood association head, but no one other than me could take it on.
近所の空き家に、誰かが出入りしている形跡があった。持ち主には連絡がつかなかった。: There were signs that someone was coming and going from an empty house nearby. I couldn’t reach the owner.
警備員が集まらず、勤め先のビルの夜間警備はカメラとセンサーだけになった。: Not enough security guards could be found, so the building where I worked was guarded at night by cameras and sensors alone.
置き配の荷物が盗まれる被害が続き、再配達と弁償の手続きに追われた。: Thefts of packages left at the door kept happening, and I was swamped with redelivery requests and compensation paperwork.
家に防犯カメラとセンサーライトをつけた。見守りサービスの月額料金も払うようになっ: I installed security cameras and sensor lights at home. I also started paying the monthly fee for a monitoring service.
救急搬送の受け入れ先がなかなか決まらず、救急車の中で1時間待った。: It took a long time to find a hospital to accept the ambulance patient, and I waited an hour inside the ambulance.
近所で火事があり、消防車が着いたのは通報の15分後だった。署が統合されて遠くなっ: There was a fire in the neighborhood, and the fire engine arrived 15 minutes after the call. I heard the station had been consolidated and was now farther away.
隣の部屋の住人が何度も入れ替わり、誰が住んでいるのか分からなくなった。: The tenant next door changed again and again, until I no longer knew who lived there.
地域の見守りが減り、下校後の子どもの安全確認まで学校に頼まれるようになった。: Community watching decreased, and the school was even asked to check on children’s safety after school.
塾帰りの暗い道で、スマホの防犯アプリを起動したまま歩くのが習慣になった。: On the dark road home from cram school, I made a habit of walking with a safety app running on my phone.
一人暮らしの見守りサービスに登録した。毎朝ボタンを押して、無事を知らせるようにな: I signed up for a monitoring service for people living alone. Every morning I press a button to let them know I’m safe.
店の万引き被害が増えたが、警備員を雇う余裕はなかった。夜の営業時間を短くした。: Shoplifting at the store increased, but I couldn’t afford to hire a guard. I shortened the evening hours.
推計では2040年に働き手が約1,100万人足りなくなると言われた。地元の祭りで: Estimates said the country would be about 11 million workers short by 2040. At the local festival, they couldn’t find enough people to carry the portable shrine.
消防士の仕事に興味があったが、説明会で「人が足りず休みが取りにくい」と正直に言わ: I was interested in being a firefighter, but at the information session they honestly told me, “We’re short-staffed, so it’s hard to take days off.”
サンマの水揚げが減り続け、船を出しても燃料代すら取れない日が増えた。: Pacific saury catches kept falling, and more days I couldn’t even cover fuel costs by going out to sea.
秋の食卓からサンマが消えた。スーパーでは1尾が高級魚のような値段で売られていた。: Pacific saury disappeared from autumn tables. At the supermarket, a single fish was priced like a luxury catch.
港町の漁協が合併し、地元の魚市場が閉鎖された。朝の競りの声が聞こえなくなった。: Fishing cooperatives in the port town merged, and the local fish market closed. The sound of the morning auction was gone.
海水温の上昇で、養殖のカキが大量に死んだ。出荷できたのは例年の半分だった。: Rising sea temperatures killed off large numbers of farmed oysters. We could ship only half the usual amount.
昔は南の海にいた魚が、近くの海でとれるようになったと聞いた。魚屋の店先に見慣れな: I heard that fish that used to live in southern seas could now be caught nearby. Unfamiliar names lined the front of the fish shop.
漁師だった近所の人が引退し、跡を継ぐ人はいなかった。港には動かない船が並んだ。: A neighbor who had been a fisherman retired, and no one took over. Idle boats lined the harbor.
仕入れていた地元の魚が高くなり、定食の値段を上げるか量を減らすかで何日も迷った。: The local fish I bought became more expensive, and I agonized for days over whether to raise the set meal price or cut the portion.
海岸に流れ着くプラスチックごみが増えたが、清掃活動に来る人は年々減った。: More plastic waste washed up on the shore, but fewer people came to the cleanup drives each year.
子どもと出かけた海水浴場が、高潮対策の工事で閉鎖されていた。: The beach I took my kids to was closed for storm surge protection work.
夫婦で海辺の町への移住を考えたが、高潮の浸水想定区域を見てあきらめた。: My spouse and I considered moving to a seaside town, but gave up after seeing the storm-surge flood risk zone.
外国から来た若い人が船員の多くを占めるようになった。片言の日本語と身ぶりで網を引: Young people from abroad came to make up most of the crew. We hauled in nets with broken Japanese and gestures.
回転寿司の皿の値段が上がり、メニューから国産のネタが少しずつ減った。: The prices of plates at the conveyor-belt sushi place went up, and domestic ingredients gradually disappeared from the menu.
港の防波堤が老朽化しても、補修は後回しにされた。台風のたびに波が道路を越えた。: Even as the harbor breakwater aged, repairs were put off. Every typhoon, waves went over the road.
漁師になりたいと進路面談で話すと、先生は少し困った顔をした。: When I told my teacher in a career meeting that I wanted to be a fisherman, they looked a little troubled.
趣味の釣りで、近くの港で釣れる魚の種類がすっかり変わった。昔の仕掛けでは何もかか: For my hobby of fishing, the kinds of fish caught in the nearby harbor changed completely. My old rigs caught nothing.
魚売り場の半分が輸入の冷凍品になり、産地表示に日本の地名を探すのが難しくなった。: Half the fish section was imported frozen goods, and it became hard to find a Japanese place name in the origin labels.
燃料の重油が高騰し、漁に出る日を週3日に減らした。: Fuel oil prices soared, and I cut my fishing days to three a week.
海水温が上がり、近くの海でサンゴが見られるようになったと話題になった。喜ぶ人の横: As the sea warmed, it became a topic that corals could now be seen in nearby waters. Next to those delighted, the fishermen looked troubled.
水揚げの減った港への配送ルートが廃止され、冷凍トラックの仕事が一つなくなった。: The delivery route to the port with its reduced catch was abolished, and one refrigerated truck job disappeared.
家の裏の畑がイノシシに掘り返され、植えたばかりのジャガイモが全滅した。: Wild boars dug up the field behind my house, and the potatoes I had just planted were wiped out.
クマの出没が続き、夕方以降は外を出歩かないよう防災無線で放送が流れた。: Bear sightings continued, and the emergency radio announced that people should not go out after evening.
シカの食害で山の下草がなくなり、大雨のたびに土が田んぼへ流れ込むようになった。: Deer overgrazing wiped out the undergrowth on the mountain, and after every heavy rain, soil began washing into the rice paddies.
散歩道でクマを見たという話が近所で続き、日課の朝の散歩をやめた。: Talk of bear sightings on the walking trail kept spreading in the neighborhood, so I gave up my daily morning walk.
クマの出没で通学路が変更になり、遠回りのため毎朝30分早く家を出ることになった。: Because of bear sightings, the school route was changed, and I had to leave home 30 minutes earlier every morning for the detour.
住宅地の公園にイノシシが出たとニュースになった。都会でも油断できないと言われた。: It made the news that a wild boar appeared in a park in a residential area. They said even the city isn’t safe to be careless in.
猟師が高齢化して減り、自分で狩猟免許を取ることにした。講習と道具で思わぬ出費にな: Hunters aged and dwindled, so I decided to get a hunting license myself. The training and gear cost more than I expected.
アライグマが家の屋根裏に住みつき、駆除業者を呼んだ。天井には大きなしみが残った。: Raccoons took up residence in the attic of my house, and I called an exterminator. A large stain stayed on the ceiling.
集落の人が減ると、サルの群れが平気で家の庭先まで来るようになった。: As the number of people in the village fell, troops of monkeys began coming right up to the front yards.
子どもと予約していたキャンプ場が、クマの出没で急に閉鎖された。: The campground I had reserved with my kids was suddenly closed due to bear sightings.
庭の柿の実を放っておくとクマが来ると役場に言われた。自分では高い枝に手が届かなか: The town office told me that leaving the persimmons on my garden tree would draw bears. I couldn’t reach the high branches myself.
ジビエの加工所を始めたが、処理できる人も施設も足りず、捕れた獣の多くは埋めるしか: I started a game meat processing facility, but there weren’t enough people or facilities to handle it, and most of the animals caught had to be buried.
外来種のアリが近くの港で見つかり、公園に「素手で触らないで」という注意書きが立っ: Invasive ants were found in a nearby port, and a sign went up in the park saying, “Do not touch with bare hands.”
空き家になった隣家の庭木が伸び放題になり、うちの屋根まで枝がかかってきた。: The garden trees of the vacated house next door grew wild, and the branches began to reach over my roof.
手入れされない山のスギが育ちきり、春の花粉症が年々ひどくなった気がした。: The cedars on unmanaged mountains had fully matured, and I felt my spring hay fever worsening year after year.
山あいの道を通勤中、車がシカとぶつかった。修理に20万円かかった。: On my commute along a mountain road, my car hit a deer. The repair cost 200,000 yen.
獣よけの電気柵を畑に張ったが、毎朝の見回りが体にこたえた。: I strung an electric fence against animals around the field, but the morning rounds every day took a toll on my body.
クマの出没対応に追われ、夜中の呼び出しが月に何度もあった。: Swamped with bear-response duties, I was called in the middle of the night several times a month.
